Statement ledger

Statement ledger

This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to the manuscript revision 39f2597a, and labels are written exactly as in its LaTeX source (for example P:clock-copy-obstruction). The ledger was written and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258, 975feb3 and a284420; waves L5 and L6 were anchored to 975feb3, waves L7 to L14 to a284420. Revision 39f2597a adds front matter, appendices and figures. The appendix-local direct-bound constant C_2 of P:d1-upper, P:low-alpha-upper and C:planar-range is renamed C_dir (C_dir^gen); the intrinsic C_2(Gamma,a) is unchanged. The attribution of the quoted source result T:first is clarified (wording only; T:first is not formalized here). A front-guide paragraph pointing readers to L:white-test and P:nogo-05 is added. A readability pass adds explanatory sentences to 207 of the 249 proofs (one more proof, of P:original-signed-point-upper, changes only by an original-text correction listed below); statements, displays, labels and references are kept, and old proof lines are kept word for word except 50 reworded and 32 re-wrapped lines. Six places of the original text are corrected (two unparsable sentences, a garbled clause and three typographical errors in statements of results not formalized here). An unused setup step is removed from the proof of P:symplectic-block-mean (not formalized here). Every cited label exists exactly once at 39f2597a. TeX line numbers were moved to 39f2597a by the git diff of each file or, inside proofs rewritten by the readability pass, by the pass's per-file line maps. A range moved by the git diff has the same text at both revisions up to that rename; a range moved by a line map keeps every cited line word for word, with explanatory sentences inserted between them, except 1 range whose words are kept but re-wrapped around inserted sentences. The 1593 ranges resolved by hand were read: each cites the same object at both revisions, though its wording may have changed. The file of every locator was checked against the labels cited next to it (script checks and hand resolutions recorded in provenance/manuscript-anchor.json).

Scope

  • The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean (step modules) or StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean (library modules: whole results, narrower results, foundations and proof steps); Audit/<module>/ prints the elaborated types.
  • The rows cover every public theorem (3654) except MaskedAuxiliaryReal.Cx.ext_iff, which @[ext] generates (3653 rows), and 849 definitions whose values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 113 public definitions have no rows of their own: 107 (for example kappa, delta, gauge, counts, InventoryProduct.partialEval, OccupationPhysicalClass.volI, SpaceTimePositivity.timeMeasure, TerminalWick.chainMassReal, WaveGreenFourier.spherePhi, OccupationCeilingExact.stepG, HigherRieszTwo.dens2, FixedSplit.extTime, FockColumnBound.mulOp, TerminalWickInputs.chainMap and TerminalWickRegularization.regMap; every public definition of the wave-L12, L13 and L14 modules has a row, the compiler-generated constructor declarations without a source range excepted) only name quantities or measures used in those statements, one is the structure FockColumnBound.L2Map (a Lean-route data structure), four are the instances that make TimeCompletion.Pre a pre-inner-product space, and one is the syntax constant WhiteFour.tacticTw_close; read their bodies in the Lean source or in Audit/. Counting convention: a public definition is a non-private def, abbrev, instance, structure or inductive written in the source of the StratonovichHAMSecondMoment and StratonovichHAMAudit modules; declarations generated by Lean (structure projections, constructors, recursors, matchers, noConfusion and the instance MaskedTrigProducts.instDecidableEqTrig produced by deriving DecidableEq) are not counted. The inventory is taken from the elaborated environment (962 public definitions: 849 with rows, 100 def and 7 abbrev quantities, the structure FockColumnBound.L2Map, the four instances, and WhiteFour.tacticTw_close, the syntax constant of a local tactic macro, which has no row and no claim since release v0.10.0). Earlier versions of this page said 89 and 507: two definitions were left out of the running count, one when wave L2 was added and one when wave L5 was added.
  • The StratonovichHAMAudit modules check finite, algebraic and scalar steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates, real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional inner-product and finite-word facts. The exception is HermiteWordFock (wave L9), which applies HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw to the Fock model of FockForm and so formalizes the special case of L:finite-word-cutoff with one Gaussian coordinate per color (section "HermiteWordFock (narrower result: L:finite-word-cutoff for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)"); the multi-mode case is the library module FiniteWordCutoff (wave L11).
  • Section headings use three categories. (A) "whole result": every conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean conclusion under the manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied inputs that are disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or inputs-supplied, conclusion full); no other section carries it. (B) "narrower result: ...": a labelled result some of whose conclusions are not Lean conclusions, or are proved for a modelled object (the class O by joint representatives, the rate in Rayleigh form, the cost in integral form, an abstract structure standing for an object the manuscript constructs, an object that is not constructed) whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized; the heading names what is missing. The one exception is a registered model choice (next item): a result whose only modelled object is such a choice stays a whole result, and its section names the model. Discharging a named input in a completion module does not turn a narrower result into a whole one. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps ...": facts used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; every StratonovichHAMAudit section except HermiteWordFock is of this kind. The Index by label is a pointer table: each manuscript label (and one row for declarations with no direct label) points to the sections whose tables formalize it, each followed by the category phrase of that section's heading. It carries no per-declaration lists or qualifiers: what each declaration states and the analytic inputs it takes are stated once, in the section tables. Labelling convention: every backticked manuscript label in a section-table label cell is an assignment and creates an Index pointer; a label mentioned only as context goes in the "What it states" cell as "(Context: ...)"; a "no direct label" cell contains no manuscript label.
  • Model-choice register. A registered model choice is a documented definitional choice that is the standard construction of a manuscript object, recorded with the identification that is not formalized. M1 (wave L6, Le's decision 4): the wave Green measure in d = 3 is (s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere, Mathlib's sphere measure scaled to the radius-s sphere; its identification with the surface (Hausdorff or Riemannian) measure of the TeX is not proved. Results whose only modelled object is M1 (L:low-alpha-convolution, L:phase-contractions, L:higher-riesz and L:alpha-one-convolution, and the sections LowAlphaConvolution, PhaseContractions, L9Completed, HigherRieszThree, AlphaOneConvolution and L10Completed; and, in wave L11, L:uniform-series-tail for the constructed chain measures in TerminalWickInputs; in wave L12, L:terminal-wick in TerminalWickComplete) are whole results; L:damped-homogeneous-norms (DampedSmoothing, wave L12) uses M1 and M3 (below); LowAlphaUpper (wave L13) uses M1 with M4 in d = 3. The narrower section HigherRieszTwo also uses M1, only in the steps it shares with d = 3, and the proof-steps section TerminalWickRegularization uses M1 in d = 3. M2 (wave L11, item K10): the Gaussian space L^2(Omega; X) over finitely many independent standard Gaussian coordinates, with X a complex inner product space, is the space of normalized Hermite coefficient vectors (Fin m -> N) -> X (as in HermiteFock, FockForm and FixedSplit; the Hermite isometry HermiteFock.integral_norm_sq_iota is proved), multiplication by a coordinate acts by creation plus annihilation, and finite sums and Bochner integrals of words are taken coordinatewise in the Hermite basis; the identification of a Bochner integral in L^2(Omega; X) with the coordinatewise integral is not proved. L:finite-word-cutoff (section FiniteWordCutoff), whose only modelled object is M2, is a whole result; FockSandwichModel (wave L12) uses M2 for the cutoff Hilbert space and is narrower for another reason (the Fourier-side identification, below). M3 (wave L12, item C1; accepted by the author on 2026-11-13): the smoothed covariance p_eps * Gamma of L:damped-homogeneous-norms (lines 1052-1053, p_eps the centered Gaussian density of covariance eps I) is the measure with Lebesgue density gamma_eps(x) = int p_eps(x - y) Gamma(dy) (DampedSmoothing.smoothedCov, as the TeX defines the convolution of a density with a measure); its identification with Mathlib's Measure.conv of N(0, eps I) and Gamma is not proved. L:damped-homogeneous-norms (section DampedSmoothing), whose only modelled objects are M1 and M3, is a whole result. M4 (wave L13, item DM0; decision 2 of wave L13, accepted by the author on 2026-11-13): the two-chain diagram integrals J_(m,n,D)(t) of E:mixed-diagram (main TeX lines 808-832) are the deterministic integrals of DiagramModel: labels Fin (m+n) with a separate root for each chain, Pi_k as the fixed-point-free involutions of FiniteWick (self-pairings included), each pair evaluated once at its smaller label, the open simplices [0,t]^m_< x [0,t]^n_<, the temporal kernel in [0, infinity], and the Green factors read as measures of the increments y_l - y_(p(l)) (the TeX's generalized-kernel reading, which covers the d = 3 sphere measure of M1); for a covariance measure Gamma the TeX's J_(m,n,D)(t) is diagramLim, the limit as a common noise width eps -> 0+ of the diagrams with p_eps * Gamma (covEps). The identification of the increment form with the TeX's positions form is proved in d = 1 (DiagramBridge) and not in d = 2, 3; the identification of the TeX's joint limit at arbitrary vertexwise widths (L:joint-fixed-order) with this common-width limit is part of the model M4 and is not proved; the common-width convergence of every diagram is the named input DiagramLimits, and with the finiteness of the limit a clause of MixedMoment; convergence and finiteness are proved for white noise in d = 1 (WhiteCollapse, D1Upper.diagramLimits_white; MixedMoment itself stays supplied there), and the order-two Riesz limit is proved in RieszFourDiagrams (rieszDiagramLimit). Statements about diagram, diagramLim, coeffA or coeffALim whose only modelled objects are M4 (and M1) are whole results (L:d1-spatial in D1Spatial, P:white-four in WhiteFour); statements about the solution u or the chaos terms X_n rest on MixedMoment and are narrower (split modelled-object rule). M4 is used by DiagramModel, DiagramBridge, D1Spatial, TwoSimplexTime, D1Upper, LowAlphaUpper, OrderTwoDiagrams, RieszFourDiagrams, WhiteCollapse and WhiteFour. M5 (wave L14, items K1a and K1b; decision 4 of wave L14, "K1 as Lp G 2 completions, no tensor identification"; accepted by the author on 2026-11-13): the completion spaces of the occupation and source sections are L^2 completions, not tensor products. OccupationCompletion.HK p G, standing for H_t (x) G, is the Hausdorff completion of Bochner L^2(I; G), I = (0,1), for the kernel seminorm (int int_(I^2) |s-t|^(-a) <F(s), F(t)>_G)^(1/2), so J_G is defined on all of L^2(I; G); Ht p = HK p R stands for H_t; Hsp S is the Hausdorff completion of C_c^infinity(R^d) for B_Gamma (the TeX's own definition of H_sp); HI p S = HK p (Hsp S) stands for H_I = H_t (x) H_sp; and SourceHeatGram.HGamma mu, standing for H_Gamma, is the closure in L^2(mu; C) (as a real Hilbert space) of the transforms of the real tests, a completion of the tests for B_Gamma(f,f)^(1/2), with H_I over it HK p (HGamma mu). Not proved: the identification of HK p G with a tensor product, of Ht with the completion of C_c^infinity(I), of HI with the completion of smooth space-time tests and with the Hilbert tensor product of L:cameron-supported-tensor, and an isometry between Hsp and HGamma. M5 is used by OccupationCompletion (L:positive-raw-embedding, L:occupation-raw-square, both narrower for other reasons) and SourceHeatGram (L:source-spatial-heat, a whole result over M5, and L:positive-physical-gram, narrower for another reason), and by ClassOH1, whose two Q rows (continuous_Q, occupation_raw_square_continuous_paper, steps of L:occupation-raw-square) map into Hsp. M6 (wave L14, item O; accepted by the author on 2026-11-13): the real Sobolev space H^1(R^d; R) is ClassOH1.H1R d, the graph of the weak gradient (WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient) in L^2(R^d; R) x L^2(R^d; R^d) with the product topology, the TeX's own description in the proof of P:spatial-four-linear (integrated_spatial_occupation.tex lines 356-358); its topology is proved to be that of Mathlib's Bessel-potential space H^1 (ClassOH1.isEmbedding_toMH1, topology_eq_induced); not proved is that every real element of Mathlib's H^1 comes from H1R d. The class O of strongly H^1-measurable fields (ClassOBridge.IsClassO) is defined over this space, with a.e.-strong measurability for Lebesgue measure on (0,1). Results whose only modelled object is M6 (P:spatial-four-linear in ClassOH1; P:occupation-physical-class and P:raw-occupation-energy in ClassOBridge) are whole results; M6 is also used by OccupationCompletion (via ClassOH1) for L:occupation-raw-square. Missing constructions are not model choices: they make a result narrower (for example the noise W of P:masked-quotient-obstruction, the ground family of L:raw-block-indexed-cone, the chain measures used for L:uniform-series-tail before wave L11 (constructed in TerminalWickInputs), the operator paths of P:radius-mean-anchor, the solution moments of P:moment-growth-logconvex and C:static-moment-constant-continuity, the cutoff evolution, propagators and coefficients of L:fixed-split, and the identification of the Fourier-side operators of FockColumnBound with the physical-space operators of L:fock-form and L:interval-contractions, also for the operator form of L:fock-form in FockSandwichModel; and, from wave L13, the solution u and its chaos terms X_n of P:mixed (statements about them rest on MixedMoment), the abstract ThreeMomentModel of C:three-product-riesz and C:three-finite-images, the uniform mean T_R and the multiplier form v_L of L:positive-physical-gram, and the operator H_V and the pairing v_V of P:signed-closed-form).
  • The 115 StratonovichHAMSecondMoment modules: 40 are whole-result modules (every whole result with nothing supplied, the two named inputs of AlphaOneConvolution being discharged in L10Completed and the two of EndpointLemmas in RieszPositiveDefinite, except P:tube-rayleigh-transfer in SourceTube, a whole result with two named inputs; FiniteWordCutoff also carries a step row of P:interval-coefficients with named inputs, and ClassOH1 a step row of L:occupation-raw-square), 48 are narrower-result modules, and 27 are foundations or proof steps (WaveKernel, SpectralHomog, TimeFractional, DampedNorms, GaussianIBP, GaussianTest, WeakSobolev, VariationalFloor, SeriesType, H1Density, FiniteWick, GaussianHermite, HermiteFock, WaveGreen, WaveGreenFourier, SpaceTimePositivity, IntervalScalar, StaticPhaseCauchy, FixedSplitCore, WhiteModel, TerminalWickRegularization, and from waves L13 and L14 DiagramModel, DiagramBridge, TwoSimplexTime, WhiteCollapse, PhaseShiftControl, H1Mathlib). Some modules without a section of their own are covered in the section of the module they serve. Together they model H:homog and give, by labelled result, 44 whole results with the manuscript's hypotheses alone, one whole result with named inputs (P:tube-rayleigh-transfer, wave L12), 16 narrower results with the manuscript's hypotheses, and steps, parts or narrower forms of 34 further results with named inputs supplied (see COMPLETION.md), to the scopes specified below (the narrower conclusions are stated per result). Sixty-four (the 44 whole and 16 narrower results with the manuscript's hypotheses, and E:kappa and E:driver-parameters, E:masked-time-schur and R:gaussian-one-variance-test) need no supplied input: L:gaussian-scalar-powers is stated with the manuscript's own hypotheses. L:gram-scalar-algebra and L:tube-rayleigh-tail are proved under weaker hypotheses (no completeness or C_ij >= 0; no delta < 1) and also stated exactly as the manuscript does by the wrappers gram_scalar_algebra_paper and rayleigh_tail_paper; the Rayleigh lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is not formalized. E:kappa and E:driver-parameters are proved from the numerical part of H:homog (a generalization) and also restated under the full hypothesis H:homog, which HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance models clause by clause (covariance measure, spectral measure, evenness, temperedness, positive-definiteness, scaling, parameter ranges). L:equilibrium-gamma-beta and L:temporal-equilibrium are stated with the manuscript's own hypotheses (gamma_beta_paper, temporal_equilibrium_paper). The finite slice of S:compact-gaussian, L:gaussian-trace-bounds, P:finite-gaussian-matrix and R:gaussian-one-variance-test, is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses (independent standard Gaussians on an arbitrary probability space) on top of a finite Gaussian integration-by-parts foundation (GaussianIBP). L:variational-control-dilation is stated with the section's hypotheses (H:homog, Gamma != 0, a = alpha0) by variational_control_dilation_paper, for the cost in its integral form and the rate defined as the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum E:variational-real-rayleigh (over a weak-gradient H^1(R^d) built in WeakSobolev, identified with Mathlib's Bessel-potential H^{1,2} in H1Mathlib, wave L13); the identifications with E W(Psi)^2 and sqrt(-E_s) are not formalized. P:masked-spectral-growth is stated with the section's hypotheses (H:homog, Gamma != 0) by masked_spectral_growth_paper, and the homogeneity of the spectral measure, which the TeX derives in the proof of L:damped-homogeneous-norms, is derived from H:homog (spectralHomogeneous_of_homog). Hence P:clock-copy-obstruction and the finiteness part of L:damped-homogeneous-norms (with N_2(theta)^2 >= 0) are stated with nothing supplied by the ClockCopyHomog wrappers. The rest of L:damped-homogeneous-norms (N_0, the scaling identities, the tails E:damped-tail-norms, and the upper bounds of E:damped-multiplier-comparison, for a measurable multiplier in [0,1] on the spectral measure and measurable Laplace domains S subset S') is DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper, for an arbitrary family G with the mass identity GreenMass G as hypothesis, and is stated with H:homog alone (no Gamma != 0) and nothing supplied by WaveGreen.damped_homogeneous_norms_wave: WaveGreen builds the wave Green measures G_s for d = 1, 2, 3 (in d = 3 with Mathlib's Measure.toSphere taken as the surface measure, a definitional choice) and proves their mass G_s(R^d) = s, finiteness, support in the closed radius-s ball and the scaling G_s(sA) = sG_1(A). L:masked-time-completion is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses (0 < a < 1, T > 0; no Gamma != 0) by masked_time_completion_paper: the completion H_a is built (TimeCompletion, Mathlib's completion of L^2(0,T) under the temporal form, over C), with positive semidefiniteness, separability, the continuous extension, the complexified norm identity, interval amplitudes, and density of the real compact smooth tests on (0,T). E:masked-time-schur and L:masked-temporal-modulation are stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by time_schur_paper and masked_temporal_modulation_paper for the defining double integral, and E:masked-time-schur also for the norm of H_a (emb_norm_sq_le). L:masked-trig-products and L:masked-continuous-wave are stated in this H_a with the manuscript's hypotheses and nothing supplied (masked_trig_products_completed_paper, masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper). P:frequency-row and C:frequency-time are stated with the section's hypotheses (H:homog with a = alpha0, the range of gamma, and of beta for the corollary) by frequency_row_paper and frequency_time_paper, with the constant chosen before d, Gamma, mu, nu, C, h. L:occupation-kernel-row and L:spatial-physical-pair are stated with the section's hypotheses (H:homog, Gamma != 0, D = q - 2a) by occupation_kernel_row_paper and spatial_physical_pair_paper. P:masked-auxiliary-norm is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses (H:homog, Gamma != 0) by masked_auxiliary_norm_paper, and E:masked-hilbert-fourier is proved for any complex Banach space; its clause for a real H after complexification is stated in wave L13 (MaskedAuxiliaryReal, below). L:variational-heat-envelope and the display of L:variational-global-mean are stated with the section's hypotheses (H:homog, Gamma != 0, a = alpha0) by variational_heat_envelope_paper and variational_global_mean_paper; the latter's first sentence (all mixed derivatives bounded) is proved in wave L13 (VariationalMeanDerivatives, below). L:phase-bessel is proved for any measure space and any complete complex inner product space and stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by phase_bessel_paper (separability carried and not used). P:masked-quotient-obstruction is stated with the proposition's hypotheses by masked_quotient_obstruction_paper, which also proves that Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2 satisfies H:homog (with alpha = 1) and Gamma != 0; E W(F)^2 is read as the covariance functional of E:cov (the noise is not constructed, so this is a narrower result: the identification with noise variances is not formalized). The Rayleigh-form part of P:variational-unmasked-rate (a uniform positive floor, the Lipschitz bounds and 0 < I_Psi < infinity, for the rate defined by E:variational-real-rayleigh) is stated with the section's hypotheses by variational_unmasked_rate_paper; its operator half (H_s self-adjoint, lambda = sqrt(-E_s)) is not formalized. L:spatial-static-controls and P:spatial-smooth-ratio are stated with the section's hypotheses (H:homog, Gamma != 0, a = alpha0) by spatial_static_controls_completed_paper and spatial_smooth_ratio_completed_paper (SpatialOccupationCompleted), with the score displays E:spatial-static-score and E:spatial-smooth-score in an existential form; their supremum forms take the named input S1Bdd there and are stated with nothing supplied in L8Completed (wave L8); R_0 is positive and finite with nothing supplied, by the deterministic bound A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_Gamma(1) b(g)^(alpha/2) of SpatialFourierBound (L:spatial-fourier-bound, which the manuscript uses for the same purpose since a284420), so R_0 < infinity does not depend on T:full-upper. L:positive-series-type is stated with the lemma's hypotheses by positive_series_type_paper. C:white-relative-width and L:white-clock-laplace are stated with the section's hypotheses by white_relative_width_paper and white_clock_laplace_paper, the latter with the damping parameters eta_1, eta_2 > 0 of E:white-self-clock-transform made explicit (the TeX gives them no sign). L:inventory-product is stated with the section's hypothesis H:homog by inventory_product_paper, with the explicit constant inventoryConst alpha alpha0 fixed before M and k. P:spatial-four-linear and P:spatial-energy-map are stated with the section's hypotheses (H:homog, Gamma != 0, a = alpha0) by the _completed wrappers of SpatialOccupationL7Completed (for example spatial_four_linear_paper_completed and spatial_energy_value_paper_completed), which discharge the density of test functions in H^1 (the input hdense of SpatialFourLinear) with H1Density.h1TestDense; the joint continuity of C_4 is proved there in sequential form (in the topology of (H^1)^4 in wave L14, ClassOH1, below), and E:spatial-static-energy-score in the existential form, its supremum form with nothing supplied in L8Completed. P:occupation-physical-class is stated with the section's hypotheses and the TeX's constants R_sp and E_sp by occupation_physical_class_Esp_paper (SquarePairingBounds discharged by squarePairingBounds_holds), over the class O modelled by joint measurable representatives of g and grad g; the construction of such representatives from strong H^1-measurability is proved in wave L14 (ClassOBridge, below). In wave L8: L:spatial-fourier-bound is stated with the manuscript's constant R_alpha of E:intro-spectral-mass by SpectralMassIdentity.spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper, through the identity R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha proved by SpectralMassIdentity.resolvent_eq_ralpha_paper. L:damped-homogeneous-norms is stated with H:homog alone and a narrower closing smoothing remark by DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_full_wave: both bounds of E:damped-multiplier-comparison, the membership of the Gaussian multipliers e^(-eta|xi|^2) in the multiplier class, the N_0 mass identity of the Gaussian-smoothed Green measures, and Green smoothing as that multiplier on the spectral measure for the transforms of G_s, identified with N_{2,m,S} in d = 1 (DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one) and in every d = 1, 2, 3 by WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave (wave L9). One part of the smoothing remark was not a Lean conclusion in waves L8-L11: the spectral identification of the smoothed covariance p_eps * Gamma (spatial smoothing was represented only by the membership of its multiplier); it is proved in wave L12 (DampedSmoothing, below). The boundedness claim S1Bdd of P:variational-positive-scores is proved deterministically from the occupation ceiling (OccupationCeilingFinite, over the space-time positivity of SpaceTimePositivity, completed in L8Completed), so P:variational-positive-scores is stated with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied (L8Completed.variational_positive_scores_sSup_st_paper_completed), Q_2 >= S_2^pos not formalized, and the supremum forms of E:spatial-static-score, E:spatial-smooth-score and E:spatial-static-energy-score hold with nothing supplied. In wave L8 T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling was stated with the section's hypotheses, with the constant K_0 R_sp, an upper bound of C_occ, in place of C_occ and in its first form only (L8Completed.occupation_ceiling_K0_paper_completed, occupation_ceiling_sSup_K0_paper_completed), and C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket with the section's hypotheses for S_2^pos in place of C_2 and with energyValue alpha (K_0 R_sp) in place of E_(1/2)^O (L8Completed.intrinsic_spatial_bracket_paper_completed); these forms remain, and wave L9 adds the exact constant (below). L:positive-raw-embedding is stated with the section's hypotheses in narrower forms (the variance identity in integral form, the row bound and the scalar Schur bound) by SpaceTimePositivity.positive_raw_variance_form_paper and OccupationCeilingFinite. The integral identities of L:occupation-raw-square are proved for continuous compactly supported fields (SpaceTimePositivity.occupation_raw_square_cc_paper), a class different from the lemma's O, and are not counted as a formalization of that lemma; its final display is also proved for the finite-cell fields of OccupationCeilingExact (step_mean_le_sqrt, wave L9), likewise not counted. In wave L14 both lemmas are stated with Q, rho_g, H_sp, H_t, H_I and J_G built (OccupationCompletion, below); the integral forms above remain separate rows. In wave L9: L:low-alpha-convolution is stated with H:homog and alpha < 1 alone in d = 1, 2, 3 by L9Completed.low_alpha_convolution_paper_completed (for the wave Green measures smoothed by N(0, eta I), with integrability; the Fourier display of its proof is proved, not imported). L:phase-contractions is stated with the standing assumptions of S:static-phase alone by L9Completed.phase_contractions_paper_completed (and under H:homog in d = 3 by phase_contractions_homog_completed): E:phase-resolvent, E:phase-trace and the Fourier form of T_eps. The Fourier identities of the wave Green measures in d = 2, 3, the Fourier transform of Mathlib's sphere measure and Archimedes' law for it are proved in WaveGreenFourier, which also identifies the smoothed Green norm of L:damped-homogeneous-norms with N_{2,m,S} in every d = 1, 2, 3 (WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave); in waves L9-L11 that lemma stayed formalized with a narrower conclusion, because the spectral identification of the smoothed covariance was not formalized (proved in wave L12, DampedSmoothing). P:raw-occupation-energy is stated with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied by RawOccupationEnergy.raw_occupation_energy_paper (A(g), C_occ and E_zeta^O defined, 0 < C_occ <= K_0 R_sp, the dilation identities, E:raw-occupation-energy and E:raw-occupation-ratio), over the class O modelled by joint measurable representatives of g and grad g (re-issued over O itself in wave L14, ClassOBridge), and L:occupation-rayleigh-selection likewise by OccupationCeilingExact.occupation_rayleigh_selection_paper (the witness is a finite-cell field of real unit tests). T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling is stated with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied with the exact C_occ, in both forms, by OccupationCeilingExact.intrinsic_occupation_ceiling_paper (O modelled by joint representatives, re-issued over O itself in wave L14; C_2 <= U_2 not formalized), and C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket with the exact E_(1/2)^O in the comparison (OccupationCeilingExact.intrinsic_spatial_comparison_paper), still for S_2^pos in place of C_2. The special case of L:finite-word-cutoff with one Gaussian coordinate per color is stated with nothing supplied, for a single finite word in normalized Hermite coefficients, by the audit theorem HermiteWordFock.cut_eq_raw_fock on the Fock model of FockForm; the lemma allows m_i modes in color i and the insertions J_i = sum_j M_(g_ij) (x) K_ij; that multi-mode case is formalized in wave L11 (below). In wave L10: L:higher-riesz is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses and nothing supplied by HigherRieszThree.higher_riesz_paper (H:homog for Gamma = c norm(x)^(-alpha) dx, d = 2, 3; both clauses and the optimality of M_3; a whole result, with the d = 3 Green measure of the registered model choice M1); H:spatial-maximum is HigherRieszTwo.SpatialMaximum, for a covariance with a density and the wave Green measures, which is no narrowing for this lemma, whose covariance is a density. L:alpha-one-convolution is stated with H:homog and alpha = 1 alone in d = 1, 2, 3 by L10Completed.alpha_one_convolution_paper_completed, with integrability (the Fourier Fubini step and the Fourier transform of G_s are proved, not imported; a whole result, with M1 in d = 3). The spatial white-noise model of S:intrinsic-white-evaluation (Gamma = c delta_0, mu = (c/(2 pi)) Leb) satisfies H:homog with alpha = d = 1 (WhiteModel.white_homogCovariance, nothing supplied; the TeX asserts it without proof), with V = c/pi and A_sp(f) = c int f^4. Five further results are proved, with analytic inputs supplied as named hypotheses, for abstract objects whose identification with the manuscript's is not formalized, so they count among the narrower results: P:radius-mean-anchor (for abstract random paths, the operator paths M_R(Y_m) and the residual noises not constructed; the moment bound of C:radius-covariance-residuals, and measurability of the Holder norm of the stopped paths, supplied), P:moment-growth-logconvex and C:static-moment-constant-continuity (for an abstract moment function, the solution moments not constructed; one hypothesis structure TypeContinuityInputs: the coefficient series and Holder interpolation of L:full-moment-coefficient-holder, the static law E:static-ratio-input, the minorant of P:static-minorant-lower, T:full-upper at each temporal exponent and Cauchy-Schwarz), L:raw-block-indexed-cone (every conclusion for an abstract ground family of S:compact-mean-family, one hypothesis structure) and L:uniform-series-tail (the two facts of L:terminal-wick that its proof cites, absolute L^2 convergence of the scaled series and nonnegative mixed moments, one hypothesis structure TerminalWickInput; eps, delta -> 0+ is read as the joint limit along nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) in both parameters, in the hypothesis and in the conclusion; in wave L8 TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg proves that structure for the chain integrals of a centered Gaussian field with nonnegative covariance, and L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper composes the two, with the chain measures fixed only by their total masses; in wave L11 TerminalWickInputs states the lemma for the constructed chain measures, a whole result, see below); their abstractions are explained in their sections. Parts of further results are formalized in wave L6, with named inputs where stated: P:variational-positive-scores (everything except Q_2 >= S_2^pos, the boundedness of the value sets and the supremum statements on the named input S1Bdd; completed in wave L8, see above), P:wave-two-variances (the spectral core in full; the statement for E|l_R|^2 with E:variance-normalized-covariance, the isometry J and the norm identity of line 529 as named inputs), the finite Gaussian comparison of P:masked-noise-completion, the facts about the wave Green measures quoted in the proof of L:higher-riesz (a whole result since wave L10), and the scalar series bound in the proof of P:static-phase-all-orders. Parts of two further results are formalized in wave L7, with the operator and stochastic inputs named in their sections: the scalar and Hilbert-space steps of C:static-interaction (E:static-block-series in full with nothing supplied; the order, parity and first-variance bounds and the per-block bound supplied) and the assembly steps of P:interval-coefficients (E:interval-coefficient-bound from the energy-split identity and L:fixed-split as supplied inputs, with L:inventory-product proved in InventoryProduct and discharged in IntervalScalarCompleted, and the summation to E:interval-phase-bound). Parts of three further results, and further steps of a fourth, are formalized in wave L8, with the inputs named in their sections: P:variational-remove-mask (RemoveMask: the masks and every rate statement with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, for the Rayleigh-form rates; the point display E:variational-unmasked-point-lower from E:raw-block-original-lower of P:raw-block-original-lower as a supplied input, for a real function in place of the point moment), L:terminal-wick (TerminalWick, on the finite Wick formula of FiniteWick: every conclusion for real r, with the L^2 strong measurability of the field products supplied and the chain measures entering only through their total masses T^(2n)/(2n)!, the measures g_n^{T,x} not being constructed; the comparison is stated for each mixed moment E[Y_m Y_n], not for second moments of finite partial sums; and the Wick formula takes the joint measurability of the covariance on pairs of points, a restriction the manuscript does not make; in wave L11 the lemma is stated for the constructed measures with its hypotheses only, see below), L:symplectic-free (SymplecticFree: both compact-baseline displays on an abstract nonzero Hilbert space, with the free group, reversal and translations (FreeWaveData) and the convergence of the left Young sums supplied; the per-frequency symplectic identity and the force skewness for the L^2 pairing), and the Cauchy and scalar steps of P:static-phase-all-orders (StaticPhaseCauchy: both displays for abstract Banach-space quantities, with the circle bound, entireness in the coupling, the coefficient identification, the norm comparisons, the cutoff removals and the free bound supplied). Parts of six further results are formalized in wave L9, with the inputs named in their sections: L:fock-form and L:interval-contractions (FockForm, on GaussianHermite and HermiteFock: E:fock-sandwich with the symmetry of the sandwiched operator, the band compression, the vacuum phase insertion and E:interval-fock, for finitely many multiplied Gaussian coordinates, from the spatial column bound and E:interval-column supplied as FockColumn; proved in wave L11 on a Fourier-side model, see below), the multiplication bound E:occupied-multiplication of the proof of P:mild-construction (nothing supplied, for polynomials in finitely many standard Gaussians), and L:complex-phase and L:interval-complex (ComplexPhaseScalar: the numerical-range, scalar and Banach-algebra steps with nothing supplied; the operator bounds from Crouzeix-Palencia E:cp-input and the inverse-root integral representation as supplied inputs; the phase propagator itself is not constructed), and L:finite-word-cutoff (HermiteWordFock, nothing supplied, but only for one Gaussian mode per color and a single finite word; the multi-mode case and the sentence on finite sums and Bochner integrals of words are in FiniteWordCutoff, wave L11). Parts of two further results are formalized in wave L10, with the inputs named in their sections: L:fixed-split (FixedSplitCore, the model-free steps, and FixedSplit, the assembly on a finite Fock model of the cutoff Gaussian space: E:fixed-split-bound with C_split = 100^8 e^8 max{1, 12 delta^(-2)} for any delta > 0, from E:interval-column, the segment bound of L:interval-complex, E:interval-cross-cube, the invariance of the cross subspaces and the entire coefficients supplied, the cutoff evolution and its coefficients not being constructed; FixedSplit.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_fixed then discharges the input L:fixed-split of P:interval-coefficients, with an added hypothesis hQ bounding Q_(r,q) by the cutoff inner product, which in the TeX is Q_(r,q) itself by L:finite-word-cutoff; removed in wave L11, see below), and T:white-moment-bounds (WhiteMomentBounds, on WhiteModel: E:white-moment-bounds for the variational value S_2^pos in place of C_2(c,a), for c > 0, with the value E_sp = c^2/6 of P:white-spatial-energy supplied as WhiteSpatialEnergy; C_2 = S_2^pos, the time exponent and c = 0 are not formalized). In wave L11: L:finite-word-cutoff is stated with the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, in its multi-mode form (several Gaussian modes per color, the cutoff on the total Hermite degree of each color, any finite word, and finite sums and integrals of words taken coordinatewise), by FiniteWordCutoff.finite_word_cutoff_paper and finite_word_cutoff_integral, a whole result over the registered model choice M2. The same module removes the added hypothesis hQ of the P:interval-coefficients step row: FiniteWordCutoff.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_words takes Q_(r,q) as the real part of the inner product of the uncut coefficients and proves the bound that hQ assumed from the named input DuhamelWords (the Duhamel word expansion of the ordinary coefficients, lines 4092-4097 and 4166-4170; the evolutions are not constructed), so P:interval-coefficients and L:fixed-split stay results formalized in part. L:fock-form and L:interval-contractions are stated with nothing supplied on a Fourier-side model with finitely many real modes (FockColumnBound.fock_form_paper_completed, interval_contractions_paper_completed, with E:interval-column proved there), whose identification with the physical-space operators and the Gaussian coordinates of W_eps is not formalized (narrower results). In wave L12: L:terminal-wick is stated for the constructed chain measures g_n^{T,x} with the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, every conclusion (TerminalWickComplete.terminal_wick_full_constructed_paper): the comparison sentence for the second moments of the partial sums of every finite order, for real r (partial_sum_mono_constructed_paper; the full-series comparison is a Lean-side corollary; the TeX states the comparison for no complex r, and for complex r it is false), and absolute convergence in the complex L^2 for complex r (terminal_wick_complex_constructed_paper, with a second-moment formula that is a Lean-side addition); a whole result over M1. L:damped-homogeneous-norms is stated with H:homog alone and nothing supplied, every conclusion (DampedSmoothing.damped_homogeneous_norms_whole_paper): the spectral measure of p_eps * Gamma is e^(-eps|xi|^2/2) mu, the unique tempered one (smoothedCov_spectral, spectralMeasure_unique), so spatial smoothing gives a multiplier in the class; a whole result over M1 and M3. L:source-finite-comparison and L:tube-half-action are stated with their hypotheses and nothing supplied (SourceTube.source_finite_comparison_paper, tube_half_action_paper), and P:tube-rayleigh-transfer with its hypotheses and two named inputs from L:tube-closed-geometry, TubeAttained and TubeTail (the Borell input; both true for the manuscript's tubes), in the nonzero-law case, and with nothing supplied in the zero-law case (tube_rayleigh_transfer_paper, tube_rayleigh_transfer_zero_paper): whole results. E:fock-sandwich is proved in operator form on the Fourier-side model of FockColumnBound with the cutoff Hilbert space packaged as a finite l^2 sum (FockSandwichModel.fockSandwich_model, fock_sandwich_paper; A_0 is -Delta on the band, B_(N,m,b) bounded self-adjoint, and the inverse root of the continuous functional calculus is identified on the band range), so L:fock-form stays narrower (the identification of the model with the physical-space operators is not formalized); C:static-interaction and P:static-phase-all-orders are re-issued with FockSandwich, the positivity of A_0 and the self-adjointness of B proved on that model (static_interaction_model_paper, static_phase_all_orders_model), still inputs supplied and narrower (CPInputs, PropagatorBlock and the other inputs). P:mixed itself is the named input MixedMoment and stays not formalized; every wave-L13 statement about E u^2, E u or E[X_m X_n] rests on it. P:d1-upper (D1Upper.d1_upper_paper_riesz, d1_upper_paper_white): both inequalities of E:d1-coefficient on the model at every noise width with nothing supplied, and for the limit coefficients given DiagramLimits (proved for white noise, d1_upper_paper_white'); the TeX's form sum_m E[X_m X_(2k-m)] and E:d1-upper for random variables satisfying MixedMoment, a narrower result. P:low-alpha-upper (LowAlphaUpper.low_alpha_upper_paper, on the model with nothing supplied, M1 in d = 3; low_alpha_upper_moment_paper with MixedMoment) and C:d1-first-calibration (first_calibration_paper and its Riesz and white versions: the constants with nothing supplied, E u <= exp(C_(1,*) t^kappa) with MixedMoment and FirstMomentSeries, the rate clause for an abstract first-moment function) are narrower; their temporal steps are TwoSimplexTime (proof steps). L:white-test and the order-two part of P:riesz-small are proved for the diagram integrals of M4 with nothing supplied (OrderTwoDiagrams), and stated about the chaos terms through MixedMoment (white_test_paper, RieszFourDiagrams.riesz_small_paper'); E:riesz-four with its finiteness for every split and pairing is RieszFourDiagrams.riesz_four_paper (nothing supplied); the multiplicity sentence of P:riesz-small is not formalized; both are narrower results. L:variational-global-mean is stated with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, every conclusion (VariationalMeanDerivatives.variational_global_mean_whole_paper: every iterated derivative of (s,x) -> h_s(x) bounded on K x R^d for each compact K, with the display of VariationalMean), a whole result. P:masked-auxiliary-norm is a whole result: the clause for a real H is MaskedAuxiliaryReal.masked_auxiliary_norm_real_paper, in the complexification Cx H built in the companion, and the complex case remains MaskedAuxiliaryNorm.masked_auxiliary_norm_paper (no single Lean theorem states both). PhaseShiftControl (no labelled result) proves that, for every covariance of S:static-phase with mu != 0 and every s > 0, the inequality of PhaseContractions.gauss_shift_le is strict at some nonzero shift q. H1Mathlib (foundation) identifies the weak-gradient H^1 of WeakSobolev with Mathlib's Bessel-potential space H^(1,2) in both directions, with Mathlib's squared norm \|f\|_2^2 + (2 pi)^(-2) \|grad f\|_2^2 and the manuscript's squared norm \|f\|_2^2 + \|grad f\|_2^2 (used for manuscript constants, decision 5) equivalent, and proves the density of real test and Schwartz functions. ResolventForm (narrower result) ports complex Lax-Milgram over RCLike and builds, for an abstract bounded self-adjoint operator standing for the pairing v_V with E:signed-multiplier-form supplied as the named input SignedMultiplierForm, E:signed-form-bounds and the bounded resolvent R_V = (H_V + c)^(-1) of the form (self-adjoint, positive, injective, \|R_V\| <= 1; signed_closed_form_resolvent_paper). P:signed-closed-form is therefore a narrower result with inputs supplied (coverage inputs-supplied, weaker): H_V itself is not constructed (no LinearPMap), and D(A^(1/2)) = H^1, E:signed-quarter-phase, the negative dual completion H^(-1/2), the commutation with real conjugation and L:signed-limiting-multiplier are not formalized. In wave L14: P:spatial-four-linear is stated with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, every conclusion, by ClassOH1.spatial_four_linear_whole_paper (joint continuity of C_4 on (H^1)^4 in the product topology, H^1 = H1R d, M6), a whole result. The zero-covariance cases are ClassOBridge.zero_covariance_paper, except C_2 = 0, the vanishing of S_c^pos and of the original means, Q = 0 and the free moment model. L:source-spatial-heat is stated with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, every conclusion (SourceHeatGram.source_spatial_heat_paper), a whole result over M5; L:positive-physical-gram (positive_physical_gram_paper) is narrower: the label row E:positive-label-row and the entrywise order (left out by wave L14 decision 5) are not formalized. L:product-endpoints, L:plane-endpoints and L:endpoint-closure are whole results with nothing supplied (RieszPositiveDefinite.product_endpoints_paper_proved, plane_endpoints_paper_proved, EndpointLemmas.endpoint_closure_paper; the EndpointLemmas wrappers take positive definiteness as the named inputs RieszProductPD and PlaneRieszPD, which RieszPositiveDefinite proves by Gaussian subordination, together with RieszIsoPD). C:three-product-riesz and C:three-finite-images are stated with the endpoint hypotheses discharged and the moment and asymptotic bounds from the named input ThreeTransfer (the statement of P:three-transfer) for an abstract ThreeMomentModel, the asymptotic clause only for a supplied spectral measure of the low endpoint (none is constructed for product and Riesz low endpoints) (RieszPositiveDefinite.three_product_riesz_paper_proved, three_finite_images_paper_proved), narrower results. Side conditions the TeX leaves implicit (a probability measure, integrability, measurability) are explicit hypotheses (besides the added hypothesis hQ above, one hypothesis is not implied by the TeX: the joint measurability of the covariance in the general form TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper of L:terminal-wick, recorded there as an added restriction; the wave-L11 wrappers for the constructed chain measures do not take it). Integrability is proved where a statement says so (as a conjunct or in a companion theorem); totalized integral identities (such as the continuous-F Gaussian bridge of FiniteWick and the SymplecticFree cancellation for arbitrary functions) and auxiliary bounds do not by themselves guarantee integrability, and extended nonnegative integrals (such as the physical pairing of L:spatial-physical-pair) need not be finite.

Where a Lean statement needs an analytic fact about the model, that fact enters as an explicit hypothesis of the theorem (a "supplied hypothesis" below). Lean checks the deduction from those hypotheses, not the hypotheses themselves.
  • A successful lake build is not a verification receipt for the manuscript. It shows that the stated Lean theorems are proved from their hypotheses; whether a statement matches the manuscript step it is listed against is a separate, human judgment recorded in this ledger.
  • Three further modules developed alongside these (normalized Gaussian coordinates, vector Gaussian projection, and colored vector words) are withheld from this package because they depend on a library that is not yet public.
  • "no direct label" means the declaration checks a computation from the development of the manuscript that does not appear as, or inside, a labeled statement of the revision cited above, or is a Lean-only auxiliary or example (such as a non-vacuity instance) with no counterpart in the manuscript. Such rows make no claim about the manuscript.

Declarations of the step modules live in StratonovichHAMAudit.<Module> (file StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean); those of the library modules in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.<Module> (file StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean). Status is assigned per claims.yaml entry and need not coincide with this ledger's category "auxiliary to the Lean proof route": helper lemmas have status internal in claims.yaml (the four PositiveGram declarations and the helpers of TemporalEquilibrium, RadiusMeanAnchor, MaskedTrigProducts, WeakSobolev, VariationalDilation, IndexedCone, GaussianIBP, FiniteGaussianMatrix, TimeFractional, Totals: 4502 declarations (3653 theorems, 849 definitions); 2263 are listed against a manuscript label and 2239 have no direct label.

Comparator accounting (since v0.10.0). The comparator checks all 3653 theorems in two configurations. comparator.json holds the 1553 theorems that are the declarations of claims a coverage.yaml row names. 1134 of them were named by the rows at the wave-L13/L14 gate, as reviewed with their waves (243 of these have a "no direct label" cell or only labels without a coverage row: the row names them as steps of the result it covers). The other 419 were credited in v0.10.0 by one rule: to the row of every direct manuscript label in the label cell of the theorem's section-table row that has a coverage row (an outside row names no claims); this appended 433 claim ids to 52 rows. comparator-helpers.json holds the other 2100 theorems, to which neither applies: 1967 whose label cell is "no direct label", 106 whose label cell names only equation, hypothesis or section labels without a coverage row of their own, and 27 whose claims lean-pkg 0.29.0 cannot match to a declaration of their file, because its scanner does not list structure fields or @[ext] lemmas (the fields of VariationalMeanDerivatives.Good, OccupationCompletion.TParams and SpData, EndpointLemmas.IsCov, EndpointPair and ProductParams, ClassOBridge.IsClassO, and MaskedAuxiliaryReal.Cx.ext). lean-pkg-signoff.json declares the helper configuration a smoke check: its theorems are checked against their restatements in Challenge.lean like the others, but they are credited to no manuscript result. Status in claims.yaml follows: every theorem of the helper configuration is internal.

DimensionalMatrix (proof steps)

Defines the backward, coupling and forward 2x2 phase matrices of a single interaction and computes their product with all four entries retained, in unweighted coordinates. At fixed frequencies r, rho the matrices are the factors of S(-t) B(b) S(t) in E:variance-physical-adjoint of P:actual-wave-form (backward = S(-t), coupling = the force B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u), forward = S(t), with cp = cos(rt), sp/p = sin(rt)/r and the coefficient H in place of b), and full_interaction is that unweighted product. It is not yet the normalized kernel E:variance-normalized-kernel: there b_r = <r> sin(rt)/r (L:masked-continuous-wave; defined in Lean as MaskedContinuousWave.bFn), and passing to it needs the Bessel-weighted change of coordinates on the phase space E together with the weight 1/sqrt(<xi><eta>). That conversion, the Fourier interpretation and the zero-frequency case (where the manuscript uses the continuous sine quotient) are outside Lean. The free matrix also appears in the proof of L:complex-phase and, in balanced coordinates, as W_t in L:symplectic-free, which also defines the force B(b).

Paper label Lean declaration What it states Inputs left outside Lean
P:actual-wave-form StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.backward Definition: [[cp, -sp/p], [p sp, cp]], the backward free matrix S(-t) at one frequency. The interpretation of cp, sp as cosine and sine of a phase, and the continuous extension at zero frequency.
P:actual-wave-form StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.coupling Definition: [[0, 0], [H, 0]], the force B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u) with H for b. The meaning of H as a covariance coefficient.
P:actual-wave-form StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.forward Definition: [[cq, sq/q], [-q sq, cq]], the free matrix S(t) at one frequency. As for backward.
P:actual-wave-form StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.full_interaction For all real parameters (field division), backward * coupling * forward = [[-(sp/p) H cq, -(sp/p) H (sq/q)], [cp H cq, cp H (sq/q)]], the unweighted product S(-t) B(b) S(t) at fixed frequencies. The Bessel-weighted coordinate change and the weight 1/sqrt(<xi><eta>) that turn it into E:variance-normalized-kernel; Fourier multiplication and covariance integrals; the zero-frequency case.

HermiteWord (proof steps)

Checks the combinatorial core of L:finite-word-cutoff (exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words), which is applied in P:static-phase-all-orders and L:fixed-split: if the initial vector has degree zero in every color, each step raises a degree bound by one in its color and the projection fixes every vector within the cutoff, inserting the projection around each step does not change the word. The statements are abstract (arbitrary types and maps). The companion file HermiteWordConsumer.lean instantiates them with the scalar Hermite recurrence x He_n = He_(n+1) + n He_(n-1) as private worked examples; it adds no public declarations. The Hermite/Fock realization is proved in FockForm (goodDeg_vac, goodDeg_insert, goodDeg_frame, truncC_eq, one Gaussian coordinate per color) and applied in HermiteWordFock.cut_eq_raw_fock (next section).

Paper label Lean declaration What it states Inputs left outside Lean
L:finite-word-cutoff StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord.raw_support If the initial vector v0 is Good at the zero count, each J i raises the degree bound by one in color i and each F b preserves it, then the uncut word output is Good at the color counts of the word. None for the Fock model with one coordinate per color (FockForm.goodDeg_insert, applied in HermiteWordFock); colors with several coordinates are not formalized.
L:finite-word-cutoff StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw Under the same hypotheses (including the zero-count condition on v0), if P fixes every vector Good at a count at most N and the color counts of the word are at most N, then the cut and uncut words agree. None for one coordinate per color (FockForm.truncC_eq); Bochner integrals of words are not formalized.

HermiteWordFock (narrower result: L:finite-word-cutoff for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)

Applies StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw (the finite-word induction of L:finite-word-cutoff, notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 3036-3058, display E:finite-word-cutoff lines 3048-3055, proof lines 3060-3076) to the concrete Gaussian Fock model of FockForm. HermiteWord predates the module system and is not a module, so a module file cannot import it; this audit file is not a module and imports both StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord and StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FockForm. In this one-mode special case nothing is supplied: the four hypotheses of cut_eq_raw are FockForm.goodDeg_vac, goodDeg_insert, goodDeg_frame and truncC_eq. The lemma itself is not formalized in full: with m_i modes in color i the insertion is J_i = sum_(j=1)^(m_i) M_(g_ij) (x) K_ij (lines 3037-3043), whereas Lean has J_i = M_(g_i) (x) K_i; this is a restriction of the admissible operator data, not an omitted side condition. The multi-mode lemma, with the cutoff on the total degree of each color and the sentence on finite sums and integrals of words, is FiniteWordCutoff (wave L11, a whole result over the model choice M2); this section is unchanged.

Model (that of FockForm and HermiteFock). Coefficient vectors (Fin m -> N) -> X over m colors with one standard Gaussian mode per color (the TeX allows m_i modes in color i); the insertion of color i is J_i v = gmul i (K_i v), multiplication by g_i tensored with a continuous linear operator K_i on X; the frames F_b act on X only; the cutoff P = truncC Nc projects each color onto Hermite degree at most N_c; the start vector is vac u = 1 (x) u (the TeX's (I (x) F_0)(1 (x) v) with u = F_0 v). A word is a list of (color, frame) pairs, read as in HermiteWord (raw, cut). The statement is in normalized Hermite coefficients, where multiplication by g_i is a_i^* + a_i (HermiteFock.coord_smul_iota identifies this with multiplication of the Hermite expansion by the coordinate).

Narrower than the TeX: one mode per color; a single finite word (the sentence on finite sums and Bochner integrals of words, lines 3056-3057, is not formalized); X is a complex inner product space in Type (the universe of HermiteWord), with no completeness used, which is more general than the TeX's Hilbert space.

InteractionDriver (proof steps)

Checks parameter ranges, exponent bookkeeping and margins used in building the operator-valued driver (Section S:actual-operator-driver). The ranges and the Holder margin correspond to E:driver-parameters, L:driver-interval-limit and L:driver-holder-limit; the Lean statements make one explicit choice (the midpoint between theta and H) of the exponent the manuscript only requires to lie in an interval. The manuscript's L:driver-holder-limit lets that exponent be any point of the interval; holder_parameters and dyadic_ratio check the midpoint instance only. The Gaussian mixture and box statements belong to a preliminary derivation; the Gaussian mixture rows are not stated in the revision cited above. The box rows are the dimension-two case of a step of P:radius-mean-anchor: its proof divides Q(1-a) > 2d by 2Q to get e_anchor = (1-a)/2 - d/Q > 0 and combines g_delta with the radius power. With d = 2 and the Lean parameter p taken as the manuscript's even moment exponent Q (not its averaging exponent p), box_margin is that margin and box_scale that power bookkeeping. The general margin and the proposition for abstract random paths are formalized in the section RadiusMeanAnchor (a narrower result) below; these two rows remain as dimension-two instances.

JointTilt (proof steps)

Checks an auxiliary exponent-consistency identity for the Gaussian change of law in P:raw-block-gaussian-law: with v = Var(Z), w = Var(Y), c = Cov(Y, Z), generating-function parameter r and tilt s, the exponent of the tilted Gaussian moment generating function cancels to r^2 w/2. This identity is not displayed in the manuscript, whose proof works with the tilted Gaussian G + s z directly; it is a consistency check, not a kernel verification of the proposition, so the row carries no label. Two further identities (wrong_sign_error, wrong_cost_error) are diagnostics showing what a sign error or a doubled cost would leave behind; the manuscript does not use them. The module also checks the amplitude identity g_delta delta^(a/2) = sqrt delta from the proof of L:raw-block-inputs.

PhaseResponse (proof steps)

Checks the choice of a phase index and its strict margins, two trigonometric identities, and a two-sided frequency window, for a first Gaussian response computed in a physical phase norm in the development of the manuscript. These are not stated in the revision cited above, with one exception: two_frequency_average is the real form of the cosine-cosine case of the expansion in the proof of L:masked-trig-products, which writes the product of two trigonometric factors as four complex exponential modes with frequencies +-r +- rho and coefficients of absolute value 1/4; pairing conjugate modes gives the Lean identity with x = r t, y = rho t. The complex form, the sine cases and the Hilbert-space bound are formalized in the section MaskedTrigProducts (whole result) below.

AlphaOneConvolution (whole result)

Registered model choice: M1 (the d = 3 wave Green measure via volume.toSphere; its identification with surface measure is not proved; see Scope).

L:alpha-one-convolution (Degree-one convolution bound) of notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/AlphaOneConvolution.lean: statement lines 5635-5643 (display E:alpha-one-convolution, lines 5638-5641), proof lines 5645-5708 (display E:alpha-one-polar, lines 5674-5681), with the standing assumptions of the subsection (lines 5552-5563: H:homog, d in {1,2,3}, mu the spectral measure in the convention gamma(x) = int e^(i xi . x) mu(dxi), V = mu{norm(xi) <= 1}, G_h the wave Green measure, G_{h,eta} = p_eta * G_h, G_{h,0} = G_h).

Objects. gamma_eps = Gamma * p_eps is VariationalDilation.conv Gamma (VariationalMean.heatK eps) (a Bochner integral; p_eps has covariance eps I and multiplier e^(-eps norm(xi)^2/2), the TeX's Brownian convention, line 5671), definitionally LowAlphaConvolution.gammaEps Gamma eps (conv_heatK_eq_gammaEps). G_h = WaveGreen.waveGreen d h; G_{h,eta} = LowAlphaConvolution.smoothedGreen (waveGreen d) h eta = DampedMultiplier.gaussKernel eta * G_h (N(0, eta I)); this module defines no Gaussian law or smoothed Green measure of its own (wave L10-A1i removed the local duplicates gaussLaw and smoothedGreen). G_h hat = WaveKernel.waveHat h (the function sin(h norm(xi))/norm(xi), value h at 0). I_a(h,v) is Ia a h v; g_h, p_(2a)^(1) and g_h * p_(2a)^(1) are gBox h, gauss1 a and boxConv a h. The angular measure sigma (line 5657) is sphereMeasure mu, realized as a measure on R^d concentrated on the unit sphere, not on the sphere subtype (a representation choice; the integral over S^(d-1) in E:alpha-one-polar is the integral against this measure).

Formalized (nothing supplied). (i) polar_decomposition (lines 5653-5665): for locally finite mu with mu(cA) = c mu(A) (SpectralHomogeneous mu 1): mu{0} = 0, V < infinity, sigma has mass V and is concentrated on the sphere, and mu = (theta, r) -> r theta of sigma (x) dr|_(0,infinity) (uniqueness on rectangles, as in the TeX); sphereMeasure_apply (the defining formula), sphereMeasure_even, and alpha_one_polar_decomposition_paper (under H:homog with alpha = 1, including the evenness of sigma). (ii) alpha_one_radial (lines 5682-5683, 5691-5703): absolute convergence of the radial integral, I_a(h,v) = pi (g_h * p_(2a)^(1))(v) and 0 <= I_a(h,v) <= pi/2 for a > 0, h >= 0. (iii) alpha_one_polar: the spectral side of E:alpha-one-polar, int waveHat h xi e^(-a norm(xi)^2) cos(xi . z) mu(dxi) = int I_a(h, theta . z) sigma(dtheta), with both integrability statements and the bound pi V/2.

On named inputs. (iv) alpha_one_convolution (general form), alpha_one_convolution_paper (H:homog with alpha = 1; no Gamma != 0, as in the TeX) and alpha_one_convolution_one (d = 1, the Fourier identity discharged by waveGreenFourier_one): V < infinity, and for h > 0, eps > 0, eta >= 0, z, with a = (eps+eta)/2: integrability of y -> gamma_eps(y + z) against G_{h,eta}, absolute convergence of the radial integrals, sigma-integrability of theta -> I_a(h, theta . z), E:alpha-one-polar and E:alpha-one-convolution. The two named inputs are SpectralPairing Gamma mu (the Fourier Fubini representation of the pairing with the integrability of its integrand, lines 5610-5612, used at line 5673; it contains no Fourier transform of G_h and no homogeneity) and WaveGreenFourier d (G_s hat = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi), lines 5614-5618). Both are discharged in L10Completed (spectralPairing_holds from LowAlphaConvolution.smoothed_pairing_spectral, waveGreenFourier_holds from WaveGreenFourier.waveGreen_fourier); they stay hypotheses here so that this module does not depend on WaveGreenFourier.

Hypotheses made explicit. The general form assumes mu locally finite and tempered and mu(cA) = c mu(A); in the wrapper the homogeneity comes from H:homog by MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog (the TeX: "Fourier uniqueness, applied to the distributional homogeneity", line 5653). In the lemma's statements (the general form and the wrappers) and in alpha_one_radial, integrability of the integrals is part of the conclusion; the route identities such as conv_heatK_eq are definitional identities of Bochner integrals and assert no integrability. V < infinity is proved before V.toReal is used.

Differences from the TeX (route; statements unchanged). (ii) uses sin(hr)/r = (1/2) int_(-h)^h cos(ru) du, Fubini and the Gaussian cosine integral (from Mathlib's fourierIntegral_gaussian) instead of Fourier inversion of g_h hat p_(2a) hat; in (iv) the passage from e^(i xi . z) to cos(xi . z) takes the real part of an identity with real left side instead of using the evenness of sigma (lines 5683-5685; the evenness is proved separately and not used); the Gaussian factor of G_{h,eta} comes from Mathlib's charFun_conv and charFun_stdGaussian (charFun_smoothedGreen). The sector-mass step (lines 5659-5660) is the route lemma cone_measure. Ia_neg_h and boxConv_zero_ge are not TeX steps (used by the refutations).

Narrower than the TeX: nothing. Not stated: the commentary sentences "No isotropy or angular density is required" (line 5642) and lines 5704-5706 on the oscillation (they are reflected in the absence of such hypotheses). The route definition nrm (xi -> xi/norm(xi)) has no row. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Refutations (refutations/alpha-one-convolution/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbations: FactorTwoSphereMass (sigma(S^(d-1)) = 2V is false; witness: Lebesgue measure on R, the spectral measure of the white model, alpha = d = 1) and WrongRadialConstant (the radial bound with pi/8 in place of pi/2 fails at a = 1/4, h = 1, v = 0). Control outside the manuscript domain: DroppedPositiveH (I_a(h,v) >= 0 fails at h = -1; the lemma assumes h > 0).

ClassOBridge (narrower results: P:occupation-physical-class and P:raw-occupation-energy whole over the class O itself; L:occupation-rayleigh-selection with the rate in Rayleigh form and the cost in integral form, their identification not formalized; T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling without the C_2 sentence and C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket, its energy comparison only, for S_2^pos in place of C_2, the rate in Rayleigh form and the cost in integral form; in the zero-covariance case C_2 = 0, the vanishing of S_c^pos and of the original means, Q = 0 and the reduction to the free moment model not formalized)

Wave L14 item O (part 2), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/ClassOBridge.lean: the class O of strongly H^1-measurable fields, its bridge to the joint representatives used since wave L7 (debt D3), the results that range over O re-issued on the class itself, and their zero-covariance cases (debt B9). Anchors at 39f2597a: notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex (the class O, lines 497-500; P:occupation-physical-class, statement lines 503-521, proof lines 523-575, the joint representatives constructed in lines 534-540; the zero-covariance remark, lines 577-582) and notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex (E:raw-occupation-definitions, lines 4-21; P:raw-occupation-energy, statement lines 111-131, proof lines 133-177; L:occupation-rayleigh-selection, statement lines 180-188, proof lines 190-236; T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling, statement lines 249-264, proof lines 266-316; C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket, statement lines 319-333, proof lines 335-371; the direct zero case, lines 379-385).

The class and the bridge (nothing supplied). IsClassO u: u : R -> H^1 with H^1 = ClassOH1.H1R d (registered model choice M6, accepted by the author on 2026-11-13), a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure on (0,1), \|g_s\|_2 = 1 at a.e. time and T(g) < infinity. "Strongly H^1-measurable" is read as a.e.-strongly measurable (Bochner), the reading of the TeX's own proof ("use a separably valued strong representative", line 534); the topology of H1R d is Mathlib's H^1 topology (ClassOH1.isEmbedding_toMH1). exists_joint constructs a strongly measurable joint representative of an a.e.-strongly measurable L^2-valued field (lines 534-540), exists_aesm_of_joint gives the converse, and so O corresponds to the earlier model OccupationPhysicalClass.IsOccField up to versions at a.e. time in both directions (isOccField_of_classO, classO_of_isOccField). Every functional unchanged by such changes takes the same values on both (values_eq), so the value sets and suprema over O (energySetO, EstarClassO; ratioSetO, CoccO; rawEnergySetO, EOO) equal the joint-representative ones of the earlier modules (*_eq).

  1. P:occupation-physical-class (occupation_physical_class_whole_paper): with the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: H:homog with a = alpha0, Gamma != 0, D = q - 2a), every conclusion on O itself, nothing supplied: measurability and representative independence of the pairings B_Gamma(g_s^2, g_t^2) (the physical integrals), E:occupation-physical-bound with J(g) < infinity, and E:occupation-own-energy with 0 < E_sp and the energy set nonempty and bounded above. A whole result.
  2. P:raw-occupation-energy (raw_occupation_energy_whole_paper): with the section's standing assumptions (H:homog with a = alpha0, Gamma != 0), every conclusion on O itself, nothing supplied: 0 < C_occ <= K_0 R_sp (R_sp = R_0 finite by ClassOH1.spatial_four_linear_whole_paper), E:raw-occupation-energy, E:raw-occupation-ratio, E_zeta^O > 0 (a finite real supremum of a set bounded above) and E_zeta^O = zeta^(-alpha/(2-alpha)) E_1^O, together with the proof's facts 0 < T(g), E:raw-occupation-bound and the dilation U_l on O (stated up to versions: some u' in O with g'_s = U_l g_s a.e.) with A(U_l g) = l^alpha A(g), T(U_l g) = l^2 T(g). A whole result.
  3. L:occupation-rayleigh-selection (occupation_rayleigh_selection_whole_paper): g_eps in O itself, nothing supplied, with I_Psi built from lambda the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum E:variational-real-rayleigh and v_Psi the integral-form cost; their identification with sqrt(-E_s) and E W(Psi)^2 (the operator half of P:variational-unmasked-rate and the stochastic variance) is not formalized, so the result stays narrower (the class-O clause is gone).
  4. T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling (intrinsic_occupation_ceiling_classO_paper): both forms of E:occupation-score-ceiling with C_occ and E_zeta^O over O itself, nothing supplied; narrower: the moment sentence C_2(Gamma,a) <= U_2 (line 261) needs T:intrinsic-second-moment, and I_Psi, v_Psi are as in 3.
  5. C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket (intrinsic_spatial_comparison_classO_paper): the comparison S_2^pos <= 2^m F_0(E_(1/2)^O) < 2^m F_a(E_(1/2)^O) with E_(1/2)^O over O itself; narrower: S_2^pos in place of C_2(Gamma,a) (T:intrinsic-second-moment); the bracket E:intrinsic-spatial-bracket itself is SpatialBracket.intrinsic_spatial_bracket_paper and the L8Completed wrappers.
  6. The zero-covariance cases (no label: the remark after P:occupation-physical-class, lines 577-582, and the direct zero case, lines 379-385), zero_covariance_paper: under H:homog with Gamma = 0, every physical pairing vanishes, R_sp = 0, E_sp = 0, J = A = 0 on O, E_star^O = C_occ = E_zeta^O = 0 with nonempty value sets (small dilations of one fixed unit compact profile, constant in time; no zero-gradient unit state is used), F_b(0) = 0 (computed), and the ceiling U_c and its E_zeta^O form are both 0. Not formalized: C_2 = 0, the vanishing of the original means and of the variational values S_c^pos (line 379; C_2 needs T:intrinsic-second-moment), Q = 0 (line 380) and the reduction of the moment model to the free case (lines 581-582).

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. Nothing is supplied. Carried and unused: in zero_covariance_paper only alpha < 2 of H:homog is used; the other wrappers use all their hypotheses. T(g) and the energies are extended integrals; the finiteness of T(g) is part of membership in O (IsClassO.energy_lt_top), and its integral representation and the finiteness of J and A are concluded; every sSup is used with nonemptiness and boundedness proved. The time measure is Lebesgue measure on (0,1) (finite, isFiniteMeasure_volI). The pairings and the dilation are stated on the spatial versions gO u (representatives of the L^2 classes), which the TeX's representative independence makes harmless. Proof route: the wrappers transfer the joint-representative results of SpatialOccupationL7Completed, RawOccupationEnergy and OccupationCeilingExact through the bridge and representative independence (sqPair_Jlin_congr, Tlin_congr, Araw_congr). Measurability of the pairings is by Tonelli on the joint representative, not by the continuity of the pairing map on H^1 x H^1; the field is first normalized to F/max(1, \|F\|) and its bounded simple approximations are shown Cauchy in L^2((0,1) x R^d), instead of the TeX's summable L^2(0,1; H^1) errors. The witness of item 3 is the finite-cell field of OccupationCeilingExact moved into O (classO_of_isOccField), not the TeX's countable first-index selection. Registered model choice: M6 (accepted by the author on 2026-11-13; see Scope). Junk values: sSup of a set not bounded above is 0 in Lean; no statement relies on it for zeta > 0 (refutation ZetaZeroJunk).

Refutations (refutations/class-o-bridge/, wave L14 item O), classified. Manuscript-domain perturbation: ZeroCovarianceEnergy (0 < E_star^O without Gamma != 0; fails for the white model with amplitude c = 0, a model of H:homog with d = alpha = 1, a = 1/2, whose covariance is zero). Control outside the manuscript's parameter class (the penalty zeta = 0, outside zeta > 0 of integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex line 16), a counterexample to extending the boundedness to zero penalty: ZetaZeroUnbounded (the value set of E_zeta^O is bounded above at zeta = 0 instead of zeta > 0; fails for the white model with c = 1, a = 1/2, by dilation). Control of Lean's totalized arithmetic outside the manuscript domain: ZetaZeroJunk (0 < E_0^O; Lean's sSup of the unbounded set at zeta = 0 is 0). Lean-route control: EmbeddingTwoPi (for ClassOH1, see that section).

ClassOH1 (whole result)

Wave L14 item O (part 1), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/ClassOH1.lean: the real Sobolev space H^1(R^d; R) as a topological space, and P:spatial-four-linear with every conclusion. Anchors at 39f2597a: notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex (P:spatial-four-linear, statement lines 297-315, proof lines 317-398; the joint-continuity sentence lines 307-308, proof lines 374-376; the graph description of H^1, lines 356-358) and notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex (L:occupation-raw-square, lines 24-43, continuity of Q in lines 26 and 64-66).

The space (registered model choice M6, accepted by the author on 2026-11-13). H1R d is the graph {(f, grad f)} of the weak gradient (WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient) inside L^2(R^d; R) x L^2(R^d; R^d) (Mathlib's Lp classes), with the subspace topology and metric of the product: the TeX's own description of H^1 in the proof of P:spatial-four-linear ("its closed isometric image f -> (f, grad f) in L^2(R^d)^(d+1)", lines 356-358). Its topology is proved to be that of Mathlib's Bessel-potential space H^1(R^d) of wave L13 item K5a (H1Mathlib): toMH1 p = H1Mathlib.toH1 satisfies \|toMH1 p - toMH1 q\|^2 = \|f_p - f_q\|_2^2 + (2 pi)^(-2) \|g_p - g_q\|_2^2 (norm_toMH1_sub_sq), is 2-Lipschitz and 7-antilipschitz, hence a uniform embedding (isEmbedding_toMH1, topology_eq_induced). Not proved: that every real-valued element of Mathlib's H^1(R^d) comes from H1R d (surjectivity of toMH1 onto real elements), which no statement here needs. Every H^1 pair (f, g) of the earlier modules has a class ofPair in H1R d with a.e.-equal representatives.

  1. P:spatial-four-linear (spatial_four_linear_whole_paper): with the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: H:homog with a = alpha0, Gamma != 0), every conclusion, nothing supplied: the conclusions of SpatialOccupationL7Completed.spatial_four_linear_paper_completed for H^1 pairs (E:spatial-homogeneous-bound; finiteness and E:spatial-square-CS; E:spatial-four-linear with absolute convergence; the sequential form of joint continuity, kept as a conjunct; R_sp = R_0; A_sp(f) > 0 for nonzero f), together with the topological joint continuity of C_4 on (H^1)^4 with the product topology (continuous_C4) and the continuity of the square pairings, hence of A_sp, on (H^1)^2 (continuous_sqPair_toReal), for H^1 = H1R d. The density of test functions in H^1 is proved (H1Density), so SquareBound Gamma alpha R_0 holds with nothing supplied (SpatialFourLinear.squareBound_R0).
  2. A step row of L:occupation-raw-square (a narrower result of OccupationCompletion, wave L14 item K1a): Q : H^1 -> H_sp is continuous on H1R d for its topology (continuous_Q, occupation_raw_square_continuous_paper, under H:homog and Gamma != 0); K1a proved only the sequential form.

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. Nothing is supplied and no hypothesis is carried unused. The topology on (H^1)^4 is the product topology. Continuity is deduced from the sequential continuity of SpatialFourLinear.C4_tendsto (telescoping, as in the TeX) because H1R d is a metric space; the TeX's step N(f) <= \|f\|_(H^1) is replaced by the continuity of N along H^1 convergence. The multilinearity of C_4 (proof line 373) is not restated (the statement does not list it). Registered model choices: M6 (accepted by the author on 2026-11-13; see Scope) and, for the two Q rows (continuous_Q, occupation_raw_square_continuous_paper), M5 (the codomain H_sp is OccupationCompletion.Hsp). Junk values: none relied on.

Refutations: one file for this module, in refutations/class-o-bridge/ (wave L14 item O): EmbeddingTwoPi (toMH1 is an isometry for the manuscript norm \|f\|_2^2 + \|grad f\|_2^2; fails for the d = 1 test function cutoff 0, where Mathlib's norm weights the gradient by (2 pi)^(-2)), a Lean-route control (b): it concerns Mathlib's 2 pi convention of the embedding used for the topology, about which the TeX makes no claim.
