ClockCopy (whole result)

Formalizes P:clock-copy-obstruction (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, lines 9033-9207) in full, with its displays E:cross-clock-lambda-weight, E:clock-copy-obstruction and E:degree-one-clock-loss, together with the finiteness part of L:damped-homogeneous-norms (lines 1010-1154) and N_2(theta)^2 >= 0. The module ClockCopy rests on four foundation modules of the D4 layer (Fourier and Laplace analysis of the wave kernel and the time kernel), whose rows are marked "[D4 foundation: ]": WaveKernel (G_s hat as waveHat s xi = s sinc(s|xi|), which is sin(s|xi|)/|xi| with value s at 0; its bounds, scaling and Laplace transform), TimeFractional (subordination r^(-a) = Gamma(a)^(-1) int l^(a-1) e^(-r l) dl, the kernel Psi_a of E:averaged-clock-kernel and its properties, and the two-time Laplace lemma int int e^(-as-bt-lam|s-t|) = (a+b+2lam)/((a+b)(a+lam)(b+lam)) for complex a, b with positive real part), SpectralHomog (consequences of the spectral homogeneity, R_Gamma, h_Gamma, and Gamma != 0 => mu != 0) and DampedNorms (N_1, N_2^2 of E:damped-norm-definitions and their finiteness). H:homog is HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance with temporal exponent a = alpha0; the wrappers clock_copy_obstruction_paper, damped_norms_finite_paper and damped_N2_nonneg_paper state the results with the manuscript's hypotheses (Gamma != 0, theta > 0, -1 <= rho <= 1 for the proposition; Gamma != 0 is not assumed for the lemma). These wrappers take ONE further input as an argument: SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha, mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A) for Borel A and c > 0, which the TeX derives from the scaling of Gamma and Fourier uniqueness in the proof of L:damped-homogeneous-norms (lines 1067-1068; the same derivation is in the proof of L:low-alpha-convolution, lines 5582-5593). This input is now derived under H:homog by MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog, and ClockCopyHomog.clock_copy_obstruction_paper, ClockCopyHomog.damped_norms_finite_paper and ClockCopyHomog.damped_N2_nonneg_paper state the three results with nothing supplied (see "MaskedSpectralGrowth (whole result)"); the statements of this section are unchanged. Its consequences mu{0} = 0, mu(B_r) = r^alpha mu(B_1), int (1+|xi|^2)^(-1) dmu < inf (by the layer-cake formula), and the homogeneity of R_Gamma and h_Gamma are proved; Lebesgue measure on R^1 satisfies the input (see refutations/clock-copy/WrongDegreeOneConstant.lean). Implicit hypotheses made explicit: integrals over (0,inf) and (0,inf)^2 are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure (TimeFractional.L0, TimeFractional.P2). Since the Lean integral of a non-integrable function is 0, every integral the paper asserts to be finite (w_theta, the N_1 and N_2 integrands, the outer integrand of N_2^2, the J integrands and 2 theta/(2 theta + l) w_theta) comes with a proved integrability conclusion; the auxiliary scaling identities SpectralHomog.integral_comp_smul (measurable f only) and ClockCopy.integral_rpow_div_add_scaling (c > 0 only, any a) are identities of Lean's totalized integrals with no integrability conclusion, and are used only where integrability is proved separately (ClockCopy.integrable_rpow_div_add needs 0 < a < 1). G_s hat is real, so the complex conjugate in N_2 is dropped. Psi_a(theta|u-v|, .) and |s-t|^(-a) take Lean's junk values on the diagonal, a null set (the TeX notes the diagonal is irrelevant). Hypotheses carried but unused: in clock_copy_obstruction_paper, rho >= -1 and the fields dim, Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef, mu_even, mu_tempered and the Gamma scaling of HomogCovariance (the latter replaced by the supplied input); in damped_norms_finite_paper, the fields dim, Gamma_radon, Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef, mu_even, mu_tempered, spectral, the Gamma scaling and alpha_range; in damped_N2_nonneg_paper, the fields dim, Gamma_radon, Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef, mu_even, mu_tempered, spectral and the Gamma scaling. The ClockCopyHomog wrappers use mu_tempered, spectral and the Gamma scaling to derive the input. The proof route differs from the TeX, though the statements do not. On the K side Lean does not smooth the covariance and pass to a monotone limit: it expands |s-t|^(-a) by subordination and applies Fubini on (0,inf) x R^d x (0,inf)^2, justified by an absolute majorant built from |G_s hat G_t hat| <= 2(1+s)(1+t)/(1+|xi|^2). This is a different route, not the one after "Alternatively" in the TeX (lines 9116-9118), which bounds the density w_theta by homogeneity; Lean's proof that w_theta is integrable (weight_integrable) does use bounds of that shape, C l^(a-1) near zero (from resolvent_sub_le) and C l^(a-2) at infinity, but derives them without homogeneity. The time integral of the first display of the proof is the complex two-time lemma at theta -+ i|xi|, and needs mu{0} = 0. On the J side the (w,q) substitution and the resolvent identity are replaced by the real two-time lemma at c = (theta^2+|xi|^2)/2 and rate theta l + l^2/2, and J_rho is dominated by J_1 (the TeX's majorant through Psi_a <= r^(-a) and the homogeneity of h_Gamma is not needed). For alpha = 1 only the scaling int l^(a-1)/(c+l) dl = c^(a-1) int l^(a-1)/(1+l) dl is used, not the Beta value. Partial fractions and the strict inequality reuse StratonovichHAMAudit.ClockFilter. Not formalized in this section: N_0, the scaling identities of L:damped-homogeneous-norms, the tails E:damped-tail-norms and E:damped-multiplier-comparison (all in the section DampedNormsHomog, N_0 with the mass identity G_s(R^d) = s supplied), the identity Psi_a(r,v) = E (r+iZ)^(-a), the probabilistic interpretation of the clocks and of h_Gamma as a heat average, and the remark R:clock-copy-scope. The full wrapper hypotheses with Gamma != 0 are not instantiated in Lean (the audit examples use the zero witness of HomogCovariance); the general theorems are instantiated at Lebesgue measure on R^1. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)"; the definitions L0, P2, subKernel, psiKernel, twoTimeC, twoTimeR, FK, MK and FJ only name integrands and measures and have no rows.

ComplexPhaseScalar (narrower result: scalar steps of L:complex-phase and L:interval-complex; the weighted block map not identified with the propagator, the interval-norm telescoping with the propagators not formalized (scalar factors in FixedSplitCore); functional-calculus inputs supplied)

Wave L9 in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/ComplexPhaseScalar.lean. It formalizes the scalar, numerical-range and Banach-algebra steps of L:complex-phase (A complex phase bound; main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 2751-2773, proof 2775-2952) and of L:interval-complex (Complex sums and changing phase weights; statement lines 3473-3491, proof 3493-3572), and states both lemmas with their hypotheses in two layers. Class: inputs supplied, conclusion weaker. Both lemmas are statements about the phase propagator M_z(h) of u'' + Lu = 0 on X_lambda; the propagator, its identification with the weighted block matrix of functional-calculus operators, and the operator functional calculus are not formalized. Proved with nothing supplied: the constants (1 - delta_a >= 3/4, delta_a I_a <= pi/8, 4 delta^2/(1-delta) <= 1/3, 1 + (1-delta)^(-1) <= 7/3, the prefactor bound <= 1/6; lines 2827-2831, 2865-2869, 2907-2909; I_a, delta_a are StaticPhaseCauchy.phaseI, deltaA); the scalar resolvent integral int_0^inf t^(-1/2) (lambda^2+t)^((a-3)/2) dt = lambda^(a-2) I_a with integrability and the operator-norm bound for any integrand dominated as at lines 2821-2826 (kappa_integral, resolvent_integral_le, q_sub_one_le); the Neumann bounds in any normed ring with summable geometric series (for example a complete one) and ||1|| <= 1 (neumann_inverse_le, neumann_root_comparison: ||Q - 1|| <= 1/6 gives ||Q|| <= 7/6, Q invertible, ||Q^(-1)|| <= 6/5); the resolvent difference as a ring identity (resolvent_difference) and the four-factor norm product (integrand_factor_le); the form consequence of E:abstract-sandwich for bounded operators on a complex Hilbert space, with A_rho^(-1/2) the inverse of the continuous-functional-calculus square root of A_rho = rho^2 + A_0 (form_of_sandwich; invertibility proved for rho > 0, so the sandwich hypothesis is not vacuous), and the adjoint sandwich identity (sandwich_adjoint_norm); the numerical-range parabola (lines 2849-2875, 3534-3544), with s = 0 by rho -> 0 (form_opt_le) and |Im r| <= lambda for EVERY square root r of w; the scalar bounds of lines 2881-2912 for C_h, F_h, H_h on the numerical range, with the removable values at w = 0 (phaseG is an if branch that supplies the removable sine-quotient value, and phaseH, a product involving phaseG, consequently has the correct value 0 there; divisions by sqrt(w + lambda^2) occur only where Re(w + lambda^2) > 0 is proved); the assembly constants and the bound of a 2x2 block operator on H + H by the sum of its block norms (lines 2913-2947); and the L:interval-complex instance of E:interval-metric (lines 3556-3571): the multiplier form of the phase-weight change, the jump ratio, and the product over jumps whose ending sets are pairwise disjoint. The wrappers complex_phase_range_paper and interval_complex_range_paper take exactly the lemmas' hypotheses (bounded A_0 >= 0 self-adjoint (IsPositive), B self-adjoint resp. V bounded, 0 < a < 1, d > 0, the sandwich bound, lambda > 0, the coupling condition, h >= 0) and conclude PhaseRangeBounds at every point of W(L) (and, for L:interval-complex, the adjoint sandwich bound), with nothing supplied. The propagator wrappers complex_phase_paper and interval_complex_paper add SUPPLIED inputs (named hypotheses, not formalized): Crouzeix-Palencia E:cp-input (lines 2739-2748, imported in the TeX) for each of C_h, F_h, H_h at L (operators Cop, Fop, Hop with ||Op|| <= (1+sqrt 2) M whenever the scalar function is bounded by M on W(L); the holomorphy precondition of lines 2888-2890 is discharged by the supplier), and the inverse-root integral representation of lines 2801-2826 (resp. 3511-3526) for L^* (an operator Q' with Q' - 1 = pi^(-1) int_0^inf J(t) dt, J strongly measurable, ||J(t)|| <= (c/(1-delta_a)) t^(-1/2) kappa^(a-3), c = |z| d resp. D; the bounded holomorphic calculus). They conclude the three operator bounds 3, 6(1+lambda h), 6 (times e^(lambda h)), ||Q' - 1|| <= 1/6, ||Q'^*|| <= 7/6, ||(Q'^(-1))^*|| <= 6/5, and the bound 100 e^(2 lambda h) for the weighted block map built from these operators. Narrower than the TeX: E:complex-phase-bound is concluded for that block map, not for M_z(h) (the identification of lines 2920-2931, 2948-2951 and 3545-3548 is not formalized); the comparisons with L itself (Q, Q^(-1)) are bounded by the same neumann_root_comparison but not named in the wrappers; s is sqrt(Re <A_0 u,u>) (which equals ||A_0^(1/2) u||, not restated); E:interval-metric is the instance for given finite jump data (interval_metric_paper; the weights' positivity is used only as nonnegativity). The general telescoping lemma for the scalar conversion factors along a time partition is proved in FixedSplitCore (wave L10); its composition with the segment propagators is proved only inside L:fixed-split (FixedSplit.word_chain), with the segment bound supplied. The self-adjointness of B is carried but unused in complex_phase_range_paper and complex_phase_paper (the hypothesis is named _hB; the scalar route allows complex <Bu,u>). Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first slot, so the TeX's <Tu,u> is inner u (T u).

Controls (refutations/complex-phase-scalar/): (a) manuscript-claim perturbations, each refuted at a witness satisfying the manuscript's other hypotheses: BlockExponent (the scalar block-sum majorant (39+12x) e^x <= 100 e^x in place of 100 e^(2x), x = lambda h; x = 6; not an identified propagator bound), NeumannInverse (norm(Q^(-1)) <= 1 in place of 6/5; Q = 5/6, a scalar multiple of the identity), PhaseWeight (the loss factor unsquared in the multiplier, i.e. squared-norm, inequality, where the TeX's unsquared factor is for norms; rho_old = 2, rho_new = 1, x = 0) and ParabolaQuarter (the manuscript's delta <= 1/4 dropped; delta = 1/2); (c) a control of a broader Lean generalization outside the manuscript's domain: ImaginaryRoot refutes abs(Im r) <= lambda/2 for the reduced-premise implication of im_root_le (r^2 = w, abs(w) <= Re w + 2 lambda^2) at lambda = 1, w = -1, which violates the numerical-range condition x >= -lambda^2/4 of main TeX line 2869; whether lambda/2 fails under the manuscript's full hypotheses is not decided. No control is of type (b), and none relies on a junk value.

D1Spatial (whole result)

Wave L13 item D1, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/D1Spatial.lean: one labelled result at 39f2597a, a whole result over the registered model choice M4 (DiagramModel, Scope), with nothing supplied.

  1. L:d1-spatial (main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, statement lines 5359-5379, proof lines 5381-5442; the covariances E:d1-covariances, lines 5317-5322, the constant K_sp of E:d1-constants, lines 5324-5332, the standing 0 < alpha0 < 1, line 5315, and the increment variables and S_(D,eps)(h), lines 5338-5356): same assumptions, every conclusion, nothing supplied (d1_spatial_paper_riesz, d1_spatial_paper_white). Both displays (E:d1-spatial-product, E:d1-spatial-max), both covariance cases, every split m + n = 2k and every pairing D of the two chains (self-pairings included), with a separate width eps_e > 0 for every pair and a bound that does not depend on the widths ("uniformly in eps"). Carried and unused: 0 < alpha0 < 1; c > 0 and h_l > 0 are used only as >= 0; k >= 1 is used only for E:d1-spatial-max.

How the TeX's objects are represented (M4). Labels are 0-based; the positions x_l (sums of the increments of the own chain up to l, each chain from its own root) are DiagramModel.pos m; G(h, y) = (1/2) 1_(|y| < h) (line 5354) is waveGreen 1 h as a measure of the increment, identified with this density by DiagramModel.waveGreen_one_eq, and the TeX's dy-integral over the increments is the product measure Measure.pi. S_(D,eps)(h) with a width for every pair is spatialPair (waveGreen 1) (fun i => covEps Gamma (eps_i)) m D h, the pair named by its opening label, with covEps Gamma eps = p_eps * Gamma the TeX's gamma_eps (line 5348); with one width for all pairs it is the model's DiagramModel.spatial (spatialPair_const), and the positions form of E:mixed-diagram gets the same bounds through DiagramBridge (spatialPos_riesz_le, spatialPos_white_le). The Riesz case of E:d1-covariances is Gamma = c|y|^(-alpha) dy (volume.withDensity (HigherRieszTwo.riesz c alpha), whose smoothing is p_eps * (c|.|^(-alpha)) by covEps_withDensity); the white case is Gamma = c delta_0 (WhiteModel.whiteCov c), so gamma_eps = c p_eps (covEps_whiteCov). The TeX evaluates the pair (i, j), i < j, as gamma_eps(x_j - x_i), the model as gamma_eps(x_i - x_j); both smoothed covariances are even (covEps_riesz_neg, covEps_white_neg), so the integrands agree. O_D is DiagramModel.openers D and C_D is closers D.

Route as in the TeX: the convolution bounds (rearrangement by the layer-cake formula in lintegral_shift_le, the centered value lintegral_centered_le, riesz_conv_le, the Gaussian average smoothCov_conv_le, then riesz_eps_conv_le and white_eps_conv_le, uniform in eps > 0), the integration in descending label order (spatialPair_le, for any dimension, any sigma-finite Green family and one covariance per pair, with pos_update_of_lt, pos_update_self and card_closers), and the weighted arithmetic-geometric mean (amgm_riesz, riesz_constant_eq, amgm_white). Differences from the TeX's route, statements unchanged: the TeX states the Riesz supremum as an equality (line 5394); only the upper bound is proved and used. The common-width forms spatial_riesz_le and spatial_white_le are the ones D1Upper (P:d1-upper) consumes.

Refutations (refutations/d1-spatial/), all manuscript-domain perturbations, class (a), at c_delta = 2, eps = 1, k = 1 and the self-pairing of one chain (m = 2, n = 0), using p_1 >= 1/6 on the unit ball: ConstantQuarter ((c/8)^k in place of (c/2)^k fails at h = (1, 1)), DroppedSumHypothesis (E:d1-spatial-max without sum_l h_l <= 2t fails at h = (12, 1), t = 1) and OpenClosedSwap (prod_(C_D) h_j in place of prod_(O_D) h_i fails at h = (6, 1)). None relies on a junk value.

D1Upper (narrower result: P:d1-upper with E:d1-coefficient proved on the diagram model at every noise width, for the limit coefficients given the diagram limits (DiagramLimits, proved for white noise), and in the TeX's form sum_m E[X_m X_(2k-m)] and E:d1-upper only for random variables satisfying MixedMoment: the solution and its chaos terms are not constructed)

Wave L13 item D2, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/D1Upper.lean (its dimension-free time facts were moved to TwoSimplexTime at the L13 integration). P:d1-upper (main TeX notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, statement lines 5454-5466 with E:d1-coefficient at 5456-5460 and E:d1-upper at 5462-5465, proof lines 5468-5550), under E:d1-covariances (lines 5317-5322: gamma = c|y|^(-alpha), 0 < alpha < 1, c > 0, or gamma = c delta_0, alpha = 1, c > 0), the standing 0 < alpha_0 < 1 (line 5315), the constants b, q, beta, Z, K_sp of E:d1-constants (lines 5323-5332) and A_k(t) = sum_(m=0)^(2k) E[X_m X_(2k-m)] (lines 5446-5451).

Model (registered model choice M4, DiagramModel): the TeX's smoothed mixed expectation at width eps is the model's diagram sum, so the TeX's regularized A_k is coeffA (waveGreen 1) (covEps Gamma eps) alpha_0 k t; one common noise width eps for every pair and the exact time kernel \|s_i - s_j\|^(-alpha_0) replace the TeX's smoothing and temporal truncation delta (not needed: [0, infinity] integrals of the exact kernel are used directly); the TeX's limit A_k(t) is coeffALim 1 Gamma alpha_0 k t, the sum of the limits diagramLim as eps -> 0+, and equals sum_m E[X_m X_(2k-m)] under MixedMoment (DiagramModel.MixedMoment.coeffA_eq). The Riesz case is Gamma = c\|y\|^(-alpha) dy (volume.withDensity (riesz c alpha)), the white case Gamma = c delta_0 (WhiteModel.whiteCov c). L:d1-spatial is D1Spatial; the time integrals are TwoSimplexTime.

What is proved, by conclusion. (1) E:d1-coefficient on the model at every noise width eps > 0, uniformly in eps, both inequalities, both covariance cases, nothing supplied (coeffA_riesz_le, coeffA_white_le, coeffA_riesz_le_factorial, coeffA_white_le_factorial; generic core coeffA_le_of_spatial); this is the TeX's bound for the regularized moments (lines 5520-5528) and the factorial step k! k^(bk) >= (k!)^q (lines 5537-5538, factorial_rpow_le). (2) E:d1-coefficient for the limit coefficients coeffALim: in the Riesz case under the named input DiagramLimits (coeffALim_riesz_le); in the white case with nothing supplied (coeffALim_white_le', d1_upper_paper_white'), since DiagramLimits is proved there (diagramLimits_white, from WhiteCollapse.tendsto_diagram_white). (3) E:d1-coefficient in the TeX's form A_k(t) = sum_m E[X_m X_(2k-m)] and E:d1-upper (E u^2 <= exp(C_dir t^kappa), via the series step of lines 5540-5549, secondMoment_le_of_coeff, SeriesType.seriesNu_summable_le) for real random variables X_n, u on any measure space satisfying the named input MixedMoment (secondMoment_riesz_le, secondMoment_white_le and the wrappers d1_upper_paper_riesz, d1_upper_paper_white, the proposition's hypotheses with MixedMoment supplied). The solution u and its chaos terms are not constructed (blocker D5), so (3) is narrower by the split modelled-object rule; (1) and (2) are statements about the diagram integrals of M4.

Named inputs. DiagramModel.MixedMoment d alpha_0 Gamma P X u t (the statement of P:mixed, main TeX lines 834-849; see DiagramModel): every diagram limit exists and is finite, E[X_m X_n] = sum_(D in Pi) J_(m,n,D)(t) with the product integrable, u^2 integrable and E u^2 = sum_k A_k(t); TRUE for the solution under H:homog (P:mixed), not proved. DiagramLimits d Gamma alpha_0 t (defined here): every model diagram converges as eps -> 0+ to diagramLim; part of L:joint-fixed-order (main TeX lines 1853-1966, invoked at line 5534) and the first clause of MixedMoment without finiteness (diagramLimits_of_mixedMoment); TRUE under H:homog by L:joint-fixed-order (the TeX notes at line 5333 that E:d1-covariances satisfies H:homog); proved for white noise (diagramLimits_white), supplied in the Riesz case. Registered model choice used: M4 (DiagramModel); the Green measure is waveGreen 1 (no M1 here, d = 1).

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. The wrappers take 0 < alpha_0 < 1; only alpha_0 < 1 is used. c > 0 is used only as c >= 0. The TeX's t > 0 is used. E:d1-time-symmetry is an equality in the TeX; only <= is proved and used (card_mul_lintegral_twoSimplex_le, whose measurability hypothesis on F is carried and unused since the L13 integration), which needs no ties argument. The TeX's limit step (lines 5534-5537: L^2 convergence of each smoothed factor by L:joint-fixed-order, L^1 convergence of products by Cauchy-Schwarz) is replaced on the model by the convergence of each diagram (DiagramLimits) and the uniform bound (coeffALim_le_of_forall); the passage from the diagram limits to E[X_m X_n] is the second clause of MixedMoment. riesz c alpha has the junk value 0 at the origin (a null set; no statement depends on it). Status internal marks the Lean-route helpers.

Refutations (refutations/d1-upper/), classified: BinomialPower (TwoSimplexTime.sum_inv_factorial_gen with 2^k in place of 2^(2k), false at k = 1), TelescopeHalf (TwoSimplexTime.sum_incr_le with t in place of 2t, false at m = n = 1, t = 1, s = (4/5, 4/5)) and TimeConstantHalf (TwoSimplexTime.lintegral_timeCov_square with Z/2, false at alpha_0 = 1/2, t = 1): (a) manuscript-claim perturbations in the manuscript domain; SymmetrizeUnsymmetric (card_mul_lintegral_twoSimplex_le without the permutation invariance of F, false for F the indicator of the simplex at m = 2, n = 0, t = 1): (b) a Lean-route-only control of the hypothesis of the Lean formulation of the TeX's step. None relies on a junk value.

DampedMultiplier (narrower result: L:damped-homogeneous-norms, covariance-smoothing identification not formalized here, proved in DampedSmoothing)

Formalizes the parts of L:damped-homogeneous-norms (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, lemma lines 1010-1055, proof lines 1057-1154) that DampedNormsHomog left out: the lower bounds of E:damped-multiplier-comparison (display at lines 1043-1048; the multiplier class and the Laplace domains at lines 1033-1041), and the smoothing assertions at the end of the lemma (lines 1052-1054) and of its proof (lines 1150-1152). Read with E:damped-norm-definitions (lines 988-999) and G_s hat(xi) = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi) (lines 983-984). DampedNormsHomog and WaveGreen are unchanged; the extended wrappers are new declarations. With this module and DampedNormsHomog, WaveGreen, every assertion of the lemma except part of its closing smoothing sentence is a Lean conclusion under H:homog with nothing supplied (damped_homogeneous_norms_full_wave). The smoothing sentence is formalized in the narrower reading fixed by Le's decision 2 for wave L8 (below): spatial smoothing of the covariance only as the membership of e^(-eta norm(xi)^2) in the multiplier class (the spectral identification of p_eps * Gamma is not stated), and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel as the multiplier on the transforms of G_s in every d, identified with N_{2,m,S} in d = 1 by damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one and, since wave L9, in d = 1, 2, 3 by WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave (full_wave itself does not contain that identification). The spectral identification of the smoothed covariance is not formalized in this module; it is proved in wave L12 (DampedSmoothing, whose damped_homogeneous_norms_whole_paper states the whole lemma, over M1 and M3).

Formalized. - The lower bounds: 0 <= N_{1,m,S}(theta) (N1on_nonneg, for any measure and a > 0) and 0 <= N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 (N2onSq_nonneg, for an s-finite measure with int (1+norm(xi)^2)^(-1) dmu < infinity, mu{0} = 0, 0 < a < 1, theta > 0, measurable S); damped_multiplier_comparison states the whole display, both bounds with the integrability of the integrands, for a general measure (the upper bounds are DampedNormsHomog.N1on_smoothed_mono and N2onSq_smoothed_mono). - The multiplier class IsMultiplier (measurable, values in [0,1]; the TeX's m : R^d -> [0,1] measurable, lines 1033-1034), closed under products (IsMultiplier.mul), containing the Gaussian multipliers e^(-eta norm(xi)^2), eta >= 0 (gaussMult, isMultiplier_gaussMult). - The N_0 mass sentence (lines 1053-1054, proof lines 1151-1152): convolution with a probability measure preserves GreenMass (greenMass_conv), so N_0 is unchanged and equals theta^(-2) (N0_conv); instantiated with the Gaussian gaussKernel v and the wave Green measures, d = 1, 2, 3 (gauss_waveGreen_mass). - Green smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (lines 1052-1053, proof lines 1150-1151): for a finite G, the characteristic function of p * G (p = gaussKernel v, v >= 0) is e^(-v norm(xi)^2/2) G hat (charFun_gaussKernel_conv), so the product of the transforms is multiplied by e^(-v norm(xi)^2) (charFun_pair_gaussKernel_conv). Hence the second norm of p * G (N2GreenSq: E:damped-norm-definitions with kernel K_S and G_s hat the characteristic function of G_s) equals the second norm of G with spectral measure e^(-v norm(xi)^2) mu(dxi) (N2GreenSq_gauss, every d, G_s finite for s > 0). Under the Fourier identity GreenFourier G (G_s hat = waveHat s, lines 983-984) the second norm of G is N2onSq (N2GreenSq_eq) and that of p * G is N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 with m = e^(-v norm(xi)^2) (N2GreenSq_gauss_eq); the Fourier identity is proved in d = 1 (greenFourier_one, from WaveGreen.waveGreen_fourier_one) and, in wave L9, in d = 1, 2, 3 (WaveGreenFourier.greenFourier).

Wrappers. damped_homogeneous_norms_full_paper: under H:homog (HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu, temporal exponent a = alpha0, no Gamma != 0, as in the TeX) and GreenMass G (the input of DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper, line 1104), the conclusions of that wrapper with its item on E:damped-multiplier-comparison extended to both bounds, plus the Gaussian multipliers and products, and, for every v >= 0, GreenMass and N_0 of p * G and N2GreenSq_gauss. damped_homogeneous_norms_full_wave: the same with G := waveGreen d and H:homog only (GreenMass by WaveGreen.waveGreen_greenMass with the field dim). damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_paper: under H:homog and GreenFourier G, for v >= 0, theta > 0, measurable S subset S': the outer integrands of the second norms of G and of p * G and of N2onSq(m mu, S), N2onSq(mu, S') are integrable; the second norm of G is N2onSq alpha0 theta S mu; that of p * G is N2onSq alpha0 theta S (m mu) with m = e^(-v norm(xi)^2); and 0 <= N2onSq(m mu, S) <= N2onSq(mu, S'). damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one: the same in d = 1 with G := waveGreen 1 and nothing supplied.

Inputs. GreenMass G (line 1104) as in DampedNormsHomog, a hypothesis on the parameter G, discharged for the wave Green measures. GreenFourier G is used only for the identification of the second norm of G (and of p * G) with N2onSq: G_s finite and its characteristic function equal to waveHat s for s > 0, i.e. that the G_s hat of lines 983-984 is the Fourier transform of G_s, which the TeX uses when it pairs G_theta(s,x) with G_theta(t,y) (lines 1000-1003). It is no stronger than that identity. Proved for d = 1 (greenFourier_one) and, in wave L9, for d = 1, 2, 3 (WaveGreenFourier.greenFourier), where fourier_paper is instantiated as WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave. The lemma's own N_1, N_2 are defined through waveHat (DampedNorms), so no conclusion of full_wave depends on it.

Readings and narrower forms (Le's decision 2 for wave L8). - "Spatial Gaussian smoothing ... give[s] multipliers in this class" (line 1052) is formalized as the membership of e^(-eta norm(xi)^2) in the class; the spectral identity that the spectral measure of p_eps * Gamma is e^(-c eps norm(xi)^2) mu is not stated in this module; it is proved in DampedSmoothing (wave L12) by Fubini against Lebesgue measure times mu, not against Gamma. - "Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel give[s] multipliers in this class" is formalized as N2GreenSq_gauss in every d (transforms of measures), and as an identity of N2onSq norms in every d = 1, 2, 3 (damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one and, wave L9, WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave). - The source's Gaussian p_eta (pp. 13-14 of the source; main lines 2023 and 5561) is represented by the centered Gaussian gaussKernel v = N(0, v I), the image of Mathlib's stdGaussian under x -> sqrt(v) x; every normalization p_eta = N(0, c eta I) is gaussKernel (c eta). The TeX does not fix c in this lemma. - Commentary only, not formalized: "the scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only" (lines 1050-1051) and "It is used after time integration, not pointwise" (lines 1146-1147).

Conventions and junk values. N2GreenSq is a complex Bochner integral (the TeX's int G_s hat conj(G_t hat) dmu is complex before time integration); a non-integrable integrand would give the value 0. N2GreenSq_gauss and N2GreenSq_eq are equalities of integrals whose integrands agree almost everywhere on (0,inf)^2 (N2GreenOuter_gauss_ae, N2GreenOuter_ae_eq), so they hold whether or not the integrands are integrable; fourier_paper and fourier_one conclude the integrability of all four outer integrands. gaussKernel v with v < 0 is the Dirac mass at 0 (sqrt v = 0); every statement where that matters carries v >= 0 (gauss_waveGreen_mass holds for every v). N_0 uses (G s univ).toReal, which is s under GreenMass.

Hypotheses of H:homog used. Directly: alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one, mu_radon (s-finiteness of mu) and, in full_wave, dim; the other fields used are those used by the called lemmas (DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper, DampedNormsHomog.homog_spectral_facts, ClockCopyHomog.damped_norms_finite_paper). No field is claimed unused here.

Proof route. The lower bounds follow the TeX: the nonnegative integrand for N_1 (line 1148); for N_2, the representation N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 = int_S w_theta^(m mu) of DampedNormsHomog.N2onSq_eq with w_theta >= 0, where the TeX uses B_theta(lambda,xi) >= 0 by positive definiteness (lines 1135-1146). The smoothing assertions have no TeX proof beyond lines 1150-1152; the Lean route is Mathlib's convolution and characteristic-function calculus (Measure.conv, charFun_conv, charFun_map_smul, charFun_stdGaussian). Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Refutations (refutations/damped-multiplier/), all without junk-value reliance: GaussianSign (e^(-eta norm(xi)^2) in the class for every real eta; false at eta = -1, norm(xi) = 1), SumNotClosed (the class closed under sums; 1 + 1 = 2 > 1), MassNonProbability (mass preserved by convolution with any finite measure; rho = 2 delta_0, G_s = s delta_0), FourierExponent (e^(-v norm(xi)^2) instead of e^(-v norm(xi)^2/2) for one smoothed transform; G = delta_0, v = 1).

DampedNormsHomog (narrower result: L:damped-homogeneous-norms without the general multiplier lower bounds, which are in DampedMultiplier; covariance-smoothing identification not formalized here, proved in DampedSmoothing)

Formalizes the rest of L:damped-homogeneous-norms (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a: definitions E:damped-norm-definitions, lines 988-998; lemma, lines 1010-1055, with the tails E:damped-tail-norms at lines 1029-1032 and the multiplier comparison E:damped-multiplier-comparison with its definitions at lines 1033-1054, display at lines 1043-1048; proof, lines 1056-1154, the comparison at lines 1129-1152). The finiteness part and N_2(theta)^2 >= 0 were already formalized (DampedNorms, ClockCopy, re-issued with nothing supplied in ClockCopyHomog). This module adds N_0(theta) = theta^(-2), the scaling identities N_1(theta) = theta^(alpha+alpha0-2) N_1(1) and N_2(theta)^2 = theta^(-beta) N_2(1)^2 with beta = 4-alpha-alpha0, both tails N_1^(M)(1) -> 0 and N_2^(M)(1) -> 0 of E:damped-tail-norms (also N_2^(M)(1)^2 -> 0 and the tail form N_2^(M)(1)^2 >= 0), and the upper bounds of E:damped-multiplier-comparison. The wrapper damped_homogeneous_norms_paper bundles all of these with the finiteness part and N_2(theta)^2 >= 0. It assumes H:homog (HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu, temporal exponent a = alpha0) and NOT Gamma != 0, as in the TeX, plus one input, GreenMass G, used only by the N_0 conclusions (discharged by WaveGreen).

Input of this module: GreenMass G, the mass identity G_s(R^d) = s for s > 0 that the proof uses at line 1104 (the TeX imports it from the source, Chen (2.5)). This module defines no wave Green measure, so N0 G theta is defined for an arbitrary family G of measures on R^d and GreenMass G is exactly the identity the TeX uses, no stronger. All other conclusions of the wrapper hold under H:homog alone (they do not use GreenMass). The input is discharged in wave L6 by the module WaveGreen (section below): WaveGreen.waveGreen_greenMass proves GreenMass (waveGreen d) for d = 1, 2, 3, and WaveGreen.damped_homogeneous_norms_wave states the lemma with nothing supplied, except the general multiplier lower bounds 0 <= N_{1,m,S}, 0 <= N_{2,m,S}^2 and the closing smoothing remark (both are in DampedMultiplier, the remark in its narrower reading).

The multiplier comparison E:damped-multiplier-comparison (lines 1033-1054, display 1043-1048; at 975feb3 this was a one-sentence smoothing and truncation claim, which wave L5 read, by Le's decision, as a multiplier and a Laplace-domain restriction; the manuscript at 39f2597a states that reading itself). The lemma takes a measurable m : R^d -> [0,1] and measurable S subset S' subset (0,inf), defines N_{1,m,S}(theta) (replace mu by m mu and restrict the lambda integral of N_1 to S) and N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 (replace mu by m mu and the temporal kernel by K_S(r) = Gamma_E(alpha0)^(-1) int_S e^(-lambda abs(r)) lambda^(alpha0-1) dlambda), and asserts, for every theta > 0, 0 <= N_{1,m,S}(theta) <= N_{1,1,S'}(theta) and 0 <= N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 <= N_{2,1,S'}(theta)^2, for full and tail domains, with the scaling identities asserted only for the original covariance. In Lean: m is g : R^d -> [0,inf), measurable with g <= 1, and m mu is smoothed mu g; N_{1,m,S} is N1on a theta S (smoothed mu g), K_S is KS a S, and N_{2,m,S}^2 is N2onSq a theta S (smoothed mu g), with all lambda-integrals over S cap (0,inf) for any measurable S subset S' in R (this contains the TeX's S subset S' subset (0,inf)). Proved (N1on_smoothed_mono, N2onSq_smoothed_mono, item 4 of the wrapper): both upper bounds, with the integrands integrable; S' = (0,inf) gives the full norms (N1on_univ, N2onSq_univ) and S' = (M,inf), theta = 1 the tails, the TeX's choices at line 1149. The lower bounds 0 <= N_{1,m,S}(theta) and 0 <= N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 for a general m and S and the whole display with both bounds are proved in DampedMultiplier (wave L8: N1on_nonneg, N2onSq_nonneg, damped_multiplier_comparison), and the closing remarks on Gaussian spatial and Green smoothing in a narrower form (isMultiplier_gaussMult: membership of the Gaussian multiplier only, without the spectral identification of the smoothed covariance (proved in DampedSmoothing); greenMass_conv, N0_conv: the N_0 mass identity; N2GreenSq_gauss: Green smoothing on the transforms of G_s, identified with N_{2,m,S} in d = 1 by damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one and in d = 1, 2, 3 by WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave); this module proves the upper bounds. The TeX applies the comparison at lines 1401-1411 (the Laplace domains A_e, Green smoothing) and 2013-2022 (the Gaussian multipliers "can be removed in the upper bounds").

Abstractions: N1tail a M mu and K_M (KM) integrate lambda over (M,inf) cap (0,inf), which is the TeX's int_M^inf for M >= 0; only M -> inf is asserted. N2tail is sqrt(N2tailSq), the printed form of E:damped-tail-norms.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit, and junk values: - Every integral the lemma asserts finite comes with an integrability conclusion (the N_0 integrand, the tail integrands, the integrands of the smoothed and restricted norms), since a Lean Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0. N1_scaling alone is an identity of Lean integrals; integrability is DampedNorms.N1_integrable. - K_S(0) is a divergent integral for S = (M,inf), and its Lean value is 0. This happens only on the diagonal s = t, a P2-null set, so no statement depends on it; integral_FKS_eq holds at every (s,t) because both sides use the same totalized integral. - N2tail = sqrt(N2tailSq) is not a junk square root under H:homog: N2tailSq >= 0 is proved (N2tail_props). N0 uses (G s univ).toReal, which equals s under GreenMass (no infinite-mass junk). - The general lemmas state their side conditions: s-finiteness of mu, mu-integrability of (1+norm(xi)^2)^(-1), mu{0} = 0, measurability of g and of S, S', and 0 < a < 1, theta > 0.

Hypotheses of H:homog used by the wrapper: alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one, threshold, alpha_range (for alpha > 0), mu_radon, and, through MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog, mu_tempered, spectral and scaling. The fields dim, Gamma_radon, Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef and mu_even are carried but unused.

Proof route (differs from the TeX in the first two items, same statements): - N_2 scaling: instead of changing (s,t,xi) in the spectral formula, both sides are written as int_0^inf w_theta (ClockCopy.K_eq_integral_weight) and the one-dimensional substitution lambda = theta u is combined with w_theta(theta u) = theta^(a+alpha-5) w_1(u) (weight_scaling). N_1 scaling uses the same substitution and R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_Gamma(1). - Tails and truncation: instead of dominated convergence in (s,t,xi), the subordinated integrand DampedNorms.FK is restricted to lambda in S (FKS) and Fubini gives N_S(theta)^2 = int_(S cap (0,inf)) w_theta (N2onSq_eq). The tail limit is the tail of the integrable w_1, and nonnegativity is w_theta >= 0 (the TeX uses positive definiteness of the tail kernel). The facts 0 <= K_M <= |r|^(-alpha0) and K_M(r) -> 0 for r != 0 used by the TeX are proved (KS_nonneg, KS_le, KM_tendsto) but are not needed by this route. - Multiplier comparison: the same order as the TeX (lines 1129-1148). For each lambda the time integral comes first and is nonnegative for every xi; then N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 = int_S w_theta^(m mu) (N2onSq_eq) and the weights are compared at each lambda (weight_smoothed_le). The TeX gets B_theta(lambda,xi) >= 0 from positive definiteness of e^(-lambda abs(s-t)); here the time integral is evaluated in closed form, so w_theta(lambda) is a mu-integral of an explicit nonnegative function of xi. For N_1, R_(g mu) <= R_mu (resolvent_smoothed_le), as at lines 1147-1148.

Narrower conclusions: of E:damped-multiplier-comparison, this module proves the upper bounds; the lower bounds and the narrower forms of the smoothing remarks (see the DampedMultiplier section) are in DampedMultiplier; N_0 is proved here for any family G satisfying GreenMass G; for the wave Green measures it is WaveGreen.N0_waveGreen, with nothing supplied. The tails are stated at theta = 1, as in the TeX; the restricted norms are stated for every theta > 0. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)"; the definition FKS only names the restricted subordinated integrand and has no row.

DampedSmoothing (whole result)

Wave L12 item C1, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/DampedSmoothing.lean (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, line numbers at 39f2597a): the covariance-smoothing assertion of L:damped-homogeneous-norms (statement lines 1010-1055, proof lines 1057-1154), "Spatial Gaussian smoothing and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel give multipliers in this class" (lines 1052-1053; proof: "Gaussian spatial and Green smoothing contribute products of multipliers in [0,1] depending only on xi", lines 1150-1151). Before wave L12 the package proved only that the Gaussian factor e^(-eta\|xi\|^2) is a multiplier (DampedMultiplier.isMultiplier_gaussMult); the spectral identification of the smoothed covariance p_eps * Gamma is proved here, and with it L:damped-homogeneous-norms is a whole result. Class: same assumptions, every conclusion, under H:homog alone and nothing supplied (damped_homogeneous_norms_whole_paper), over the registered model choices M1 (the wave Green measure in d = 3) and M3 (the smoothed covariance as a density measure); see Scope.

Objects. p_eps is the centered Gaussian density with covariance eps I (LowAlphaConvolution.heatDens eps, (2 pi eps)^(-d/2) e^(-\|w\|^2/(2 eps))); the lemma leaves the normalization open (the TeX fixes it at lines 5346-5348 and 5915-5916), and N(0, c eps I) is the case eps -> c eps of the statements, which hold for every eps > 0. Its Fourier multiplier is e^(-eps\|xi\|^2/2) = DampedMultiplier.gaussMult (eps/2). The smoothed covariance p_eps * Gamma is smoothedCov Gamma eps, the measure with Lebesgue density gamma_eps(x) = int p_eps(x - y) Gamma(dy) (LowAlphaConvolution.gammaEps), as the TeX defines the convolution of a density with a measure. Registered model choice M3 (accepted by the author on 2026-11-13): this density measure is not identified with Mathlib's Measure.conv of N(0, eps I) and Gamma. "Multipliers in this class" are DampedMultiplier.IsMultiplier (measurable, values in [0,1], lines 1033-1036), and the smoothed spectral measure m mu is DampedNormsHomog.smoothed mu m = mu.withDensity m.

Formalized (proved, nothing supplied): the spectral identification smoothedCov_spectral (route: the pointwise identity LowAlphaConvolution.gammaEps_spectral, then Fubini of phi(x) e^(i xi.x) e^(-eps\|xi\|^2/2) against Lebesgue measure times mu, absolutely integrable since phi is Lebesgue integrable and e^(-eps\|xi\|^2/2) is mu-integrable; no Fubini against the infinite Gamma, Le's decision 2 of wave L8); the properties of gamma_eps (smoothedCov_props); the TeX's sentence in existential form (spatial_smoothing_multiplier); uniqueness of the tempered spectral measure (spectralMeasure_unique, Fourier uniqueness by Measure.ext_of_charFun), so that e^(-eps\|xi\|^2/2) mu is the tempered spectral measure of p_eps * Gamma (smoothedCov_spectral_unique_paper); and the wrapper damped_homogeneous_norms_whole_paper, which combines DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_full_wave, WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave (Green smoothing, d = 1, 2, 3) and the covariance smoothing with the comparison E:damped-multiplier-comparison applied to its multiplier.

Hypotheses: damped_homogeneous_norms_whole_paper takes H:homog (HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance) alone and passes it to the two wrappers it combines, whose field use is recorded in DampedMultiplier and WaveGreenFourier; the covariance smoothing uses the fields mu_radon (s-finiteness), mu_tempered and spectral. The general theorems use each of their hypotheses (SFinite mu, IsTempered mu, IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu, 0 < eps). Not a Lean statement (commentary, as in DampedMultiplier): lines 1050-1051 ("the scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only") and lines 1146-1147. Junk values: eps > 0 throughout (at eps = 0 Lean's density p_0 is 0; refutation EpsZeroJunk).

Refutations (refutations/damped-smoothing/), classified. Manuscript-domain perturbations (white model Gamma = delta_0, mu = (2 pi)^(-1) Leb on R^1, which satisfies H:homog by WhiteModel.white_homogCovariance, eps = 1): WrongGaussConstant (the multiplier e^(-eps\|xi\|^2), the factor 1/2 dropped, is not a spectral measure of p_eps * Gamma) and NoSmoothingChange (mu itself is not). Lean-route-only control: MultiplierNotUnique (uniqueness holds for the measure m mu, not for the function m: Gamma = mu = 0). Controls outside the manuscript domain: EpsZeroJunk (Lean's totalized arithmetic at eps = 0) and NegativeEpsMultiplier (for eps < 0 the formula exceeds 1).

DiagramBridge (foundation: the d = 1 positions/increments change of variables for the diagram model M4, nothing supplied)

Wave L13 item DM0b, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/DiagramBridge.lean. The model M4 (DiagramModel, Scope) reads the Green kernels of E:mixed-diagram as measures of the increments (DiagramModel.spatial, Measure.pi of G_(h_l) at the positions pos m w), while the TeX writes the diagram in the position variables y_l with the factors G(s_l - s_{p(l)}, y_l - y_{p(l)}) and a separate root for each chain (main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, lines 808-824), and switches to increments before L:d1-spatial: "x_l is the sum of increments in its own chain up to label l. The spatial change of variables has determinant one" (lines 5338-5341, an unlabelled claim in the set-up of L:d1-spatial). This module proves that claim in d = 1, nothing supplied, as the identities the TeX uses it for: spatial_waveGreen_one_eq_spatialPos (the increments form of the spatial part equals the literal positions integral with G(h, y) = (1/2) 1_(|y| < h)) and diagram_waveGreen_one_eq_diagramPos (the same for J_{m,n,D}(t)), for every covariance gamma : R^1 -> [0, infinity] (no measurability needed) and every real h (for h_l <= 0 both sides vanish). The wrapper spatial_bridge_paper carries the hypotheses of the set-up of L:d1-spatial (D a pairing, h_l > 0), unused; diagram_bridge_paper carries only D a pairing, unused. Route: incrOfPos and pos are mutually inverse (posEquiv, any d); in d = 1 the increment map is a unipotent lower-triangular matrix (det_incrMatrix) and so preserves Lebesgue measure (measurePreserving_incrOfPos, via Real.map_matrix_volume_pi_eq_smul_volume_pi); the product of the d = 1 Green measures is 2^(-N) Lebesgue on the box prod_l (-h_l, h_l) (pi_waveGreen_one). With it the model's positions form and increment form of E:mixed-diagram agree in d = 1, which is the only identification M4 leaves open in d = 1. The covariance enters only through DiagramModel.covWeight at the positions, with the pair orientation fixed in M4; it covers the smoothed gamma_eps = DiagramModel.covEps Gamma eps at a common width. Not formalized: the d = 2, 3 analogue (line 5748, vectors in R^d); the separate widths eps_e of S_{D,eps} (line 5349) are not part of M4 (they are handled in D1Spatial, and the change of variables does not involve the covariance factor).

Refutations (refutations/diagram-bridge/), classified. Manuscript-domain perturbation, class (a): GlobalPredecessor (increments taken with the global predecessor of the concatenated chains do not invert pos: m = n = 1, w = (e_0, e_0)). Controls of the broader Lean generalization (the bridge for every covariance gamma : R^1 -> [0, infinity]), outside the manuscript's covariance class: GreenHalf (with the kernel 1_(|y| < h) the positions form is 4, not the increments form 1, at m = n = 1, D = (0 1), gamma = 1, a covariance of degree alpha = 0, h = (1, 1)) and SpatialOwnRoot (the positions integral of the concatenated chain is 0, the two-root one positive, for gamma = 1_(|x| >= 1), which is not positive definite, h = (1, 1)). Lean-route-only control, class (b): UnitDiagonal (the triangular matrix with diagonal 2 is not measure preserving at N = 2; the matrix form is the Lean route, the TeX states only the determinant).

DiagramModel (foundation: the deterministic two-chain diagram integrals of E:mixed-diagram, registered model choice M4; P:mixed is the named input MixedMoment, not proved)

Wave L13 item DM0, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/DiagramModel.lean: the deterministic diagram model behind P:mixed (main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, statement lines 834-849, proof lines 851-927; E:mixed-diagram lines 808-832). It is the registered model choice M4 (Scope), on which the wave-L13 sections DiagramBridge, D1Spatial, TwoSimplexTime, D1Upper, LowAlphaUpper, OrderTwoDiagrams, RieszFourDiagrams, WhiteCollapse and WhiteFour state their results. Its interfaces were frozen before those items started and passed a cross-family fidelity review (Codex GPT-6.1-Sol) against E:mixed-moment and the source's Wick formula as quoted in E:Sn2 (lines 542-573; self-pairings, chain orientation): PASS_WITH_NOTES at 52c2697, re-confirmed PASS_WITH_NOTES (high) after the refutation repair ca12a2e.

Objects. Labels are 0-based (i : Fin (m+n) is the TeX label i+1; I_1 is i < m, I_2 is i >= m). pred and predVal give p(l) with a separate root (0,0) for each chain (lines 810-813); twoSimplex m n t is [0,t]^m_< x [0,t]^n_< (open simplices); Pi2 m n is Pi_k as the fixed-point-free involutions of FiniteWick, self-pairings and cross-pairings included (lines 809-810), each pair taken once at its opener (openers); timeWeight and covWeight are the temporal and spatial pairing weights in [0, infinity] (|0|^(-alpha0) = infinity); spatial and diagram are the spatial part and J_{m,n,D}(t) with the Green kernels read as measures of the increments y_l - y_{p(l)} (Measure.pi of G_(h_l), positions pos m w), which is the TeX's generalized-kernel reading (lines 825-829) and the increment form of lines 5338-5356, and covers the d = 3 sphere measure of M1; spatialPos and diagramPos are the literal positions form, identified with the increment form in d = 1 in DiagramBridge; covEps Gamma eps is p_eps * Gamma (lower integral), and for a covariance measure Gamma the TeX's J_{m,n,D}(t) is diagramLim, the limit as the common noise width eps -> 0+ of the diagrams with covEps Gamma eps and the unsmoothed waveGreen d; coeffA and coeffALim are A_k(t) (E:full-second, lines 5446-5451); rev and revPairing are the vertex involution rho and D -> rho(D) of the proof (lines 897-903).

Named input. MixedMoment d alpha0 Gamma P X u t (a Prop, reusable) is the statement of P:mixed for real random variables X n (standing for the chaos terms X_n(t,x), line 796) and u (standing for u(t,x)): every diagram limit exists and is finite (a conclusion of L:joint-fixed-order, lines 1853-1862, which the TeX's J_{m,n,D}(t) presupposes), E[X_m X_n] = sum_{D in Pi_k} J_{m,n,D}(t) with the product integrable (E:mixed-moment; the odd case is the empty sum, and m = n = 0 gives one), and u^2 is integrable with E u^2 = sum_k A_k(t) as a convergent series of nonnegative terms (E:full-second). It is TRUE for the solution and its chaos terms under H:homog (P:mixed), and not proved here: the solution and its chaos terms are not constructed (blocker D5). It is the supplied input of this module's moment consequences; D1Upper also takes DiagramLimits and LowAlphaUpper FirstMomentSeries (the order-two Riesz wrapper of OrderTwoDiagrams also took RieszDiagramLimit, proved in RieszFourDiagrams); results stated on diagram, diagramLim, coeffA and coeffALim are about the model, while results about u and X_n rest on MixedMoment and are narrower by the split modelled-object rule. mixed_moment_paper reads the conclusions of P:mixed off the input (with H:homog carried, unused); it is not a formalization of P:mixed, which stays not formalized (coverage). SpectralSpatial (the spectral form spatialSpec of the smoothed spatial part) is a TRUE Prop recorded for later use; no theorem assumes it.

Proved, nothing supplied: the chain and simplex facts (mem_twoSimplex_iff, pred_second_root), the pairing counts (card_Pi2 (2k-1)!!, card_Pi2_mul P_k 2^k k! = (2k)!, line 799; Pi2_odd), the self-pairing convention (card_Pi2_two_zero, crossPairs_two_zero), the chain reversal (rev_rev, revPairing_mem, sum_revPairing: the combinatorial re-indexing of lines 900-903), the empty diagram (diagram_zero_zero, diagramLim_zero_zero, coeffALim_zero: J_{0,0} = 1, A_0 = 1), the d = 1 Green density (waveGreen_one_eq), and finiteness of the spatial part for a bounded covariance (spatial_le, spatial_waveGreen_le). Not formalized: the proof of P:mixed (the Wick formula at positive widths, the joint limits, the L^2 convergence of the chaos series); the analytic identity of the terminal-chain diagram with J_{m,n,rho(D)} (only the combinatorial bijection is proved); finiteness of J_{m,n,D}(t) (part of MixedMoment); the spectral identity SpectralSpatial; the chain-swap symmetry J_{m,n,D} = J_{n,m,D'}.

Readings (model choices of M4, recorded for the fidelity review). Each pair {j, h} is evaluated once, as gamma(y_j - y_h) and |s_j - s_h|^(-alpha0) with j < h; for the even covariances of H:homog the orientation is immaterial. A covariance measure enters only through covEps Gamma eps at one common noise width, with the Green smoothing removed first; L:joint-fixed-order gives the limit at arbitrary vertexwise widths, so this common-width family has the same limit. The simplices are open and |0|^(-alpha0) = infinity; both choices change only null sets. Junk values: diagramLim is limUnder, unspecified unless the limit exists, which every statement about it obtains from MixedMoment or proves (diagramLim_zero_zero).

Refutations (refutations/diagram-model/), classified. Manuscript-domain perturbations, class (a): EmptyDiagram (J_{0,0}(1) = 0 is false at d = 1, Gamma = delta_0, alpha0 = 1/2: the package value is 1), GreenNormalization (the kernel 1_(|y| < s) without 1/2 has mass 2, not 1, at s = 1), Orientation (rho(D) = D fails for m = 3, n = 1, D = {{1,2},{3,4}}, whose openers also change), OwnRoot (the single concatenated simplex differs from the two simplices at m = n = 1, t = 3, times (2, 1)), SelfPairings (Pi_1 is not the set of cross-pairings at m = 2, n = 0, the E X_2 diagram of L:white-test) and TimeKernelExponent (the exponent +alpha0 in place of -alpha0 gives 1/2 instead of 2 at alpha0 = 1/2, m = 2, n = 0, times (1/4, 1/2)). Control of Lean's totalized arithmetic outside the manuscript domain, class (c), not counted as a refutation: TimeCovJunk (the real power 0^(-1/2) = 0 versus the package value infinity at equal times, a null set in every diagram).

DriverParameters (whole result)

Formalizes the claim after E:driver-parameters that its strict intervals are nonempty, under the parameter part of H:homog with a = alpha_0 (notes/integrated_actual_operator_driver.tex, which retains H:homog). These theorems assume only the numerical part of H:homog (a generalization); HomogHypothesis.parameters_nonempty_paper restates the result under the full hypothesis. Only 0 < a < 1 and a + alpha < 2 are used.

EndpointCorollaries (narrower results: C:three-product-riesz and C:three-finite-images for an abstract ThreeMomentModel (the solution u, its coefficients A_k(t), E u^2(t,x) and the variational constant M_st not constructed), with P:three-transfer supplied as the named input ThreeTransfer; the asymptotic clause only for a supplied spectral measure of the low endpoint (none is constructed for product and Riesz low endpoints); positive definiteness supplied here and proved in RieszPositiveDefinite)

Wave L14 item 3D, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/EndpointCorollaries.lean: the two dimension-three corollaries of S:three-endpoints (main TeX file, revision 39f2597a), assembled from the endpoint lemmas (section EndpointLemmas) and the conditional transfer P:three-transfer (statement lines 7536-7556, proof 7558-7940), which this package does not formalize and which enters as a named input. Both are narrower results.

  1. C:three-product-riesz (statement lines 7944-7959, proof lines 7961-7988): three_product_riesz_paper, with the corollary's hypotheses 0 < alpha0 < 1, 1 < alpha < 2 - alpha0, c > 0. With the fixed midpoint theta = (alpha0 + 2 - alpha)/2, every endpoint hypothesis is discharged in Lean: for the product covariance the endpoints gamma_b, gamma_v of L:product-endpoints (product_target), for the Riesz covariance c|x|^(-1) and c|x|^(-chi) (riesz_endpoints: covariance properties, scalings and the comparison by c|x|^(-alpha) = (c|x|^(-1))^theta (c|x|^(-chi))^(1-theta) and Hoelder); the target is a nonzero covariance measure with scaling 3 - alpha. Then ThreeTransfer yields TransferConclusion: the coefficient bound and the all-time moment bound of E:three-transfer and the asymptotic bound E:three-variational-upper. The constant is chosen after the data and before k, t, x, which is the corollary's dependence statement. Missing: the moment statements concern the abstract ThreeMomentModel, and the asymptotic clause is stated for every spectral measure of the low endpoint, of which none is constructed for gamma_b or c|x|^(-1) (Bochner-Schwartz is absent from Mathlib), so there it can be vacuous.
  2. C:three-finite-images (statement lines 7991-8010, proof lines 8012-8035): three_finite_images_paper, with the corollary's hypotheses (0 < alpha0 < 1, 1 < alpha < 2 - alpha0, admissible components of the three classes (Component, Component.Valid), invertible linear T_i, w_i >= 0, sum_i w_i > 0). Every component gets an endpoint pair with the common theta, chi (component_endpoints, the plane case from L:plane-endpoints); L:endpoint-closure (endpoint_closure_map, endpoint_closure_sum) gives the endpoint pair of the target Gamma = sum_i w_i (T_i)_# Gamma_i, which is a nonzero covariance measure with scaling 3 - alpha (wsum_ne_zero); ThreeTransfer then yields TransferConclusion for these actual target and endpoint measures. Missing: as in item 1 (abstract model, ThreeTransfer supplied, the asymptotic clause only for supplied spectral measures of the low endpoint).

Named inputs. ThreeTransfer Mdl alpha0 theta is the exact statement of P:three-transfer for the model Mdl: for every alpha in (1, 2 - alpha0), alpha0 < theta < 2 - alpha, every nonzero covariance target Gamma with scaling 3 - alpha and every endpoint pair (L, S) of H:three-endpoints, TransferConclusion holds. It is true for the model whose fields are the manuscript's A_k(t), E u^2(t,x) and M_st (it is then P:three-transfer, proved in the manuscript); for an arbitrary Mdl it is an assumption about Mdl. The wrappers also take the three positive-definiteness inputs EndpointLemmas.RieszProductPD, EndpointLemmas.PlaneRieszPD and RieszIsoPD (c|x|^(-e) dx on R^3, c >= 0, 0 < e < 3, the Gaussian mixture of lines 7975-7980); all three are true and are proved in RieszPositiveDefinite, whose wrappers three_product_riesz_paper_proved and three_finite_images_paper_proved take only ThreeTransfer. Discharging them does not change the class.

Abstract objects (missing constructions, not registered model choices). ThreeMomentModel has three fields, A Gamma k t for A_k(t), M2 Gamma t x for E u^2(t,x) (the d = 3 model with the fixed temporal exponent and data (1,0)) and Mst S for M_st of E:three-static-variational (lines 7510-7528); none is constructed in the package. lowConst is C_low = 2 Z_(b_0) pi V_low and staticConst is Lambda_st (lines 7503-7528), with V_low = mu_low({|xi| <= 1}). TransferConclusion states E:three-variational-upper as "for every eta > 0, eventually t^(-kappa) log E u^2(t,x) <= q (C_low^theta Lambda_st^(1-theta))^(1/q) + eta", which is the limsup bound.

Hypotheses. No hypothesis is carried unused beyond those passed to ThreeTransfer (alpha0 < 1 is used only there). Junk values: the Riesz density is 0 at x = 0 (Lean's real power), a Lebesgue-null point; weights enter as ENNReal.ofReal, and the manuscript-facing weighted-sum wrappers assume w_i >= 0.

Refutations (refutations/endpoint-corollaries/); none relies on a junk value. Class (a), a perturbation of a manuscript claim with an instance in the manuscript's domain except for the perturbed condition: MidpointRange (theta < 2 - alpha at the midpoint fails when alpha < 2 - alpha0 is weakened to alpha < 2: alpha0 = 1/2, alpha = 7/4). Controls of the broader Lean generalization, outside the manuscript's covariance/parameter class: RieszWrongExponent (the Riesz factorization with a static exponent that violates alpha = theta + (1-theta) chi fails at |x| = 4: c|x|^(-3/2) against (c|x|^(-1))^(1/2) (c|x|^(-1))^(1/2); the fixture alpha = 3/2, theta = 1/2 has theta = 2 - alpha and its contrast chi = 2, outside theta < 2 - alpha, chi < 2 of lines 7289-7293) and ZeroWeights (the target can vanish when sum_i w_i > 0 is dropped: one component with weight 0, on the exponent-1 Riesz measure, outside 1 < alpha of line 7992). Each has a _contrast theorem stating the package lemma at the same instance.

EndpointLemmas (whole result)

Wave L14 item 3D, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/EndpointLemmas.lean: the three endpoint lemmas of S:three-endpoints (main TeX file, revision 39f2597a), each a whole result. Here two of them take a named input for positive definiteness; wave L14 item 3Dpd proves both inputs and restates those two lemmas with nothing supplied (section RieszPositiveDefinite), so all three are formalized with the manuscript's hypotheses alone.

  1. L:product-endpoints (statement lines 7170-7204, proof lines 7206-7280): every conclusion (product_endpoints_paper). The hypotheses 0 <= a_j < 1, alpha = sum_j a_j in (1,2), 0 < theta < 2 - alpha, c > 0 are those of the lemma; every hypothesis is used. Conclusions: 0 < Lambda < 1, sum_j b_j = 1, sum_j v_j = chi, the reconstruction a_j = theta b_j + (1-theta) v_j, the sign and zero pattern, alpha < chi < 2; the three densities gamma_a, gamma_b, gamma_v are nonnegative (automatic for measures), even, positive definite, locally integrable and tempered (with locally finite density measures), with measure scalings 3 - alpha, 2, 3 - chi, that is covariance homogeneity exponents alpha, 1, chi; and E:product-gaussian-comparison. Positive definiteness is the named input RieszProductPD: c prod_j |x_j|^(-e_j) dx on R^3 is positive definite for c >= 0, 0 <= e_j < 1 (the Gaussian-mixture step of the proof, lines 7253-7266; true; proved in RieszPositiveDefinite.rieszProductPD_proved, and the lemma is restated without it as RieszPositiveDefinite.product_endpoints_paper_proved). The pointwise factorization gamma_a = gamma_b^theta gamma_v^(1-theta) holds at every point with Lean's values (the TeX: almost everywhere).
  2. L:plane-endpoints (statement lines 7316-7332, proof lines 7334-7415): every conclusion (plane_endpoints_paper). Hypotheses: E:three-parameters (0 < alpha0 < 1, 1 < alpha < 2 - alpha0, alpha0 < theta < 2 - alpha), c > 0, a_1, a_2 >= 0, a_1 + a_2 = alpha - 1; carried and unused: alpha0 < 1 and alpha < 2 - alpha0. Conclusions: the exponent facts of the proof; (c m, c prod_j |y_j|^(-v_j) m) with v_j = a_j/(1 - theta) satisfies H:three-endpoints for Gamma_pl (covariance properties, scalings 2 and 3 - chi, the comparison); Gamma_low = c m; mu_low = (c/2pi) delta_0 delta_0 dxi_3 is a spectral measure of c m in the convention of H:homog (planeLow_isSpectral, proved by projection-slice, Fubini and one-dimensional Fourier inversion, not imported); its mass on the closed unit ball (the convention V = mu({|xi| <= 1}) of the alpha-one section, line 1069) and on the open unit ball is c/pi, so V_low = c/pi and the closing bound of L:alpha-one-convolution is pi V_low/2 = c/2. The wrapper also proves that Gamma_pl itself is a covariance measure with scaling 3 - alpha (the section's standing assumption on a target). V_low is computed for this spectral measure; the uniqueness of the spectral measure (Fourier uniqueness of tempered spectral measures, DampedSmoothing.spectralMeasure_unique) is not invoked here, and the temperedness of mu_low is not stated as a Lean lemma. Positive definiteness of the three plane measures is the named input PlaneRieszPD (c prod_j |y_j|^(-e_j) dy delta_0(dz), c >= 0, 0 <= e_j < 1, zero exponents included; proof lines 7359-7384; true; proved in RieszPositiveDefinite.planeRieszPD_proved, and the lemma is restated without it as RieszPositiveDefinite.plane_endpoints_paper_proved).
  3. L:endpoint-closure (statement lines 7418-7424, proof lines 7426-7495): every conclusion, nothing supplied (endpoint_closure_paper, with the general forms endpoint_closure_map and endpoint_closure_sum for any 0 <= theta <= 1). The comparison of H:three-endpoints, with the endpoints' covariance properties and scalings, is preserved by pushing the target and both endpoints forward under any invertible linear T of R^3, and by finite sums with nonnegative weights and common theta, chi; the target keeps its covariance properties and its scaling 3 - alpha; zero weights and the all-zero target are included. The linear-image half takes the target to be a covariance measure (IsCov), the section's standing assumption (lines 7282-7285) made explicit, used for s-finiteness in Tonelli. Carried and unused in the wrapper: alpha0 < 1 and alpha < 2 - alpha0.

Objects. hconv Gamma eps z is the Gaussian convolution (p_eps * Gamma)(z) as a lower Lebesgue integral in [0, infinity] (finite for tempered Gamma, hconv_lt_top; for a density measure it is wave L10's HigherRieszTwo.smoothCov); IsCov (locally finite, even, tempered, positive definite, with the predicates of HomogHypothesis), Scaling, GaussComparison, EndpointPair and ThreeEndpoints model H:three-endpoints (lines 7296-7309) and its comparison E:three-gaussian-comparison, stated in [0, infinity], which is the TeX's real inequality for tempered measures. A covariance function is identified with its density measure (line 7286). No model-choice register entry is used (the measures are Lebesgue density measures and their images under linear maps).

Differences from the TeX's proof route (statements unchanged). For L:endpoint-closure, instead of extending the comparison to every Gaussian q_Sigma through q_Sigma = p_a * q_(Sigma - aI) (lines 7434-7451), the kernel y -> p_eps(x - Ty) is written as an isotropic heat mixture int p_a(w - y) rho(dw) (exists_heat_mixture, by the spectral theorem for T^*T); Tonelli, the comparison at width a and Hoelder on rho then give the pushed-forward comparison with no |det T| bookkeeping. Hoelder is used on the measure p_eps(z - y) nu(dy) itself (no normalization), and the discrete Hoelder of the sums is Hoelder on counting measure.

Junk values. |0|^(-e) = 0 for e > 0 (the TeX density is infinite there) only on Lebesgue-null coordinate planes, against which nothing is integrated except through the density measure; |t|^0 = 1 is the TeX's "zero exponent means one" (line 7203). ENNReal.ofReal clamps negative amplitudes and weights to 0; every manuscript statement carries c > 0 or w_i >= 0.

Refutations (refutations/endpoint-lemmas/); none relies on a junk value. Control of the broader Lean generalization (the geometric-mean comparison for any exponents), outside the manuscript's endpoint class: AmplitudeMismatch (the comparison with endpoints of a different amplitude fails: Gamma = L = dx, S = dx/2, theta = 1/2; all exponents are zero, whereas the manuscript requires alpha = sum_j a_j in (1,2) and sum_j b_j = 1, lines 7171 and 7183). Class (a), perturbations of a manuscript claim with an instance in the manuscript's domain except for the perturbed condition: DroppedThetaBound (sum_j L_j < 1 fails when theta < 2 - alpha is weakened to theta < 1: a = (9/10, 9/10, 0), theta = 1/2) and PlaneExponentBound (v_j < 1 fails when theta < 2 - alpha is weakened to theta < 1: alpha = 3/2, a = (1/2, 0), theta = 3/5). Each has a _contrast theorem stating the package lemma at an admissible instance. The refutations of the positive-definiteness proofs are in refutations/riesz-positive-definite/ (section RieszPositiveDefinite).

FiniteGaussianMatrix (whole result)

Formalizes the finite-dimensional part of Section S:compact-gaussian (notes/integrated_compact_gaussian.tex at 39f2597a): Lemma L:gaussian-trace-bounds (lines 68-129), Proposition P:finite-gaussian-matrix (lines 138-249, including the Hermitian core E:finite-hermitian-gaussian, line 215, and the Hermitian dilation, lines 224-241) and Remark R:gaussian-one-variance-test (lines 257-271). It uses two modules: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/GaussianIBP.lean, a reusable foundation for finite Gaussian integration by parts, and StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FiniteGaussianMatrix.lean, which contains the three results. L:gaussian-scalar-powers is reused from GaussianScalarPowers (finite Hoelder, the integer-power bound, and E Z^r <= (E Z)^r in the bootstrap). The three results are stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by the wrappers gaussian_trace_bounds_paper, finite_hermitian_gaussian_paper, finite_gaussian_matrix_paper and gaussian_one_variance_test_paper. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The integration by parts E[g_k P(g)] = E[d_k P(g)] and the integrability of polynomial moments (TeX lines 168-172) are proved, not assumed.

Abstractions and why they are faithful. - Gaussians. "Independent real standard Gaussians" are g : Fin N -> Omega -> R on an arbitrary probability space with iIndepFun g P and HasLaw (g k) (gaussianReal 0 1) P for every k. GaussianIBP.map_eq_stdPi shows that their joint law is stdPi N = Measure.pi (fun _ => gaussianReal 0 1). The general theorems are stated on stdPi N and transferred to the probability space through integral_comp_eq_stdPi. - One-dimensional integration by parts comes from Mathlib's whole-line integration by parts and the density identity phi' = -x phi. - N-dimensional integration by parts uses Fubini along Fin.insertNth k. The partial derivative is a hypothesis on every coordinate slice. - Matrices are complex matrices indexed by finite types. - ||A||_{S_p}^p = Tr((A^*A)^m) for p = 2m is schattenPow A m, the real part of that trace. schattenPow_trace proves that the trace is real and nonnegative, so taking the real part loses nothing. ||A||_{S_p} = schattenNorm A m = (schattenPow A m)^(1/(2m)). - |Y| and V^(1/2) are CFC.abs Y and CFC.sqrt V, the continuous functional calculus under MatrixOrder. abs_pow_even and schattenNorm_sqrt give the identities the TeX uses: |Y|^(2j) = Y^(2j) and ||V^(1/2)||_{S_p}^p = Tr V^m. - Real traces. The TeX compares several traces as real numbers. Lean compares their real parts. gaussian_trace_bounds_paper also records that the imaginary parts of its right-hand traces vanish; the other wrappers state real-part bounds only, and the reality of those traces follows from the proved matrix lemmas (trace_psd, trace_mul_pow_im).

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: - the measurability of the Gaussians (inside HasLaw); - the integrability of ||X||_{S_p}^p and of Tr Y^(2m), which is part of each conclusion because the Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0 in Lean; - the evenness of p, stated as p = 2m with m >= 1 a natural number.

Every real power has a nonnegative base, so no statement holds through a junk value.

Hypotheses carried but unused: o, n, N >= 1 in finite_gaussian_matrix_paper ([Nonempty o] [Nonempty n] (_hN : 1 <= N)). The general theorem finite_gaussian_matrix_zero also covers the empty family N = 0.

Proof route. The statements are the manuscript's; four steps differ from the TeX route: - The doubly stochastic step diagonalizes D' = U^* D U and applies Jensen's inequality to t^m (convexOn_pow) instead of the tangent-line inequality. - The derivative of t -> Re Tr(B (Y + t B_k)^j) is computed in the type synonym NMat n, matrices with the L-infinity operator norm. This avoids the product-topology diamond on Matrix. Polynomial growth is bounded with the same norm. - The integration by parts is applied to real parts of traces, which are real-valued functions. - The m = 1 case of E:finite-hermitian-gaussian follows from the same integration-by-parts identity with an empty word, where the TeX invokes independence directly.

Not formalized: the infinite-dimensional part of S:compact-gaussian, namely L:cutoff-factorization, P:cutoff-singular-values, P:compact-two-envelopes, L:compact-positive-order, P:localized-finite-variance, C:finite-gaussian-operators and P:cutoff-boundary-tests. These need Schatten classes and singular values of compact operators on Hilbert space, Courant-Fischer, and Sobolev spaces on the torus.

FiniteWick (foundation: the finite Wick formula, used by L:terminal-wick)

A reusable foundation with no manuscript label of its own, proved in full with nothing supplied. It formalizes the Wick (Isserlis) step in the proof of L:terminal-wick (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a): the formula E:terminal-wick-formula (lines 4310-4313) with "each pairing has coefficient one" and "if m+n is odd, the expectation is zero" (line 4329), the Gaussian moment computation of the proof (lines 4365-4378), the moment bound of lines 4351-4356, and the pointwise positivity and comparison of covariance products (lines 4404-4406). The chain integrals themselves are in TerminalWick. Abstractions: a pairing (pair partition) of a finite set S of a linearly ordered finite type is a fixed-point-free involution of S, normalized to the identity off S so that each pair partition is exactly one function (pairings); its weight takes one factor c(a, p a) per pair, at the smaller element a < p a, so every unordered pair contributes once with coefficient one (pairWeight); wickSum c S is the sum of the weights. For S all of Fin (2k) these are the pair partitions Pi_k of the TeX. The double factorial is Nat.doubleFactorial with natural subtraction, so (2*0-1)!! = 0!! = 1, the empty-product convention of line 4330. Gaussian side: stdPi N (from GaussianIBP) is the law of N independent standard Gaussians, and Mathlib defines multivariateGaussian 0 K as the image of the standard Gaussian under x -> sqrt(K) x (CFC.sqrt). CenteredGaussianField W K P states the TeX's hypothesis "centered real Gaussian field with covariance K" (lines 4292-4293) as: for every finite family of points p : Fin n -> X, the matrix (K(p_a, p_b)) is positive semidefinite and (W(p_a))_a has law multivariateGaussian 0 (K(p_a, p_b)). Implicit hypotheses made explicit: K positive semidefinite (otherwise Mathlib's multivariateGaussian 0 K is the Dirac mass at 0), and every integral identity for Gaussian monomials (products of finitely many coordinates or field values) comes with the integrability of its integrand, either as a conjunct or in a separate theorem. The exception is the bridge integral_multivariateGaussian_eq for an arbitrary continuous F: it is an equality of Lean's totalized integrals and assumes no integrability, so for a non-integrable F (for instance exp(x_0^4) under a nondegenerate Gaussian) both sides are the junk value 0; integrability transfers only through the separate equivalence integrable_multivariateGaussian_iff. No hypothesis is carried unused. Proof-route differences: the Gaussian identity is proved by Stein's recursion E[g_e F(g)] = E[partial_e F(g)] (GaussianIBP.integral_coord_mul_eq_of_growth) for x = A g, expanded along the partner of the least index (wickSum_eq_sum_erase), instead of differentiating the moment generating function (lines 4367-4376); the conclusion is the same. The moment bound E(prod_{a<n} W(p_a))^2 <= (2n-1)!! V^n (CenteredGaussianField.sq_moment_le) is the Wick formula for the 2n values together with the count of (2k-1)!! pairings (card_pairings_even, wickSum_abs_le) and |K(x,y)| <= V (CenteredGaussianField.abs_le), instead of Hoelder's inequality and L^(2n) Gaussian moments; the bound is the same. No conclusion is narrower than the TeX step it formalizes. Junk values: wickSum is a finite sum, and every Bochner integral of a Gaussian monomial appears with a proof of integrability; only the continuous-F bridge above can equate two junk values, and the monomial results apply it to integrable monomials. Refutations (refutations/finite-wick/), all combinatorial or one-dimensional controls without junk-value reliance: PairingCount ((2k)!/k! pairings of a 2k-set; k = 2 gives 12, not 3), AbsBound (the pairing-sum bound without (2k-1)!!; c = 1 on Fin 4), NonnegDropped (pairing sums nonnegative for arbitrary real weights, not a covariance; c = -1 on Fin 2) and FourthMoment (E x^4 = 1 for a standard Gaussian x, an actual Gaussian law; the Wick formula gives 3). Not formalized here: everything about the chain measures, the L^2-valued integrals and the series (see TerminalWick). The four route definitions unpair, pairUp, matBound and monoDeriv are public but are not listed as claims; they appear only inside the statements of the auxiliary rows below.
