FiniteWordCutoff (whole result)

Wave L11 (item K10) in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FiniteWordCutoff.lean: L:finite-word-cutoff (Exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words; main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 3036-3058 with E:finite-word-cutoff at lines 3048-3055, proof lines 3060-3076) in its multi-mode form, and its use in P:interval-coefficients (lines 4054-4228): the coefficient Q_(r,q) = <U_r v, U_q v>_(H_(1/T)) (lines 4142-4144) and the exact preservation of the selected coefficients by the cutoff N_i = 2k_i (lines 4163-4170). Class of L:finite-word-cutoff: same assumptions, every conclusion, over the registered model choice M2 (Scope); nothing is supplied.

The model. The coordinates are Fin m, mode j of color col j, so the TeX's g_ij (1 <= j <= m_i) are the modes j with col j = i. A Gaussian polynomial with coefficients in X is its vector of normalized Hermite coefficients (Fin m -> N) -> X (model choice M2, as in HermiteFock, FockForm and FixedSplit); X is a complex inner product space, and the wrapper finite_word_cutoff_paper takes it complete, as the lemma does (completeness carried and unused). Multiplication by g_j acts by creation plus annihilation (HermiteFock.gmul), so J_i = sum_(col j = i) M_(g_j) (x) K_j is field col K i; P is truncN col N, the projection onto the multi-indices of FixedSplit.cutIdx col N (the total Hermite degree of every color i, summed over its modes, at most N_i); frames I (x) F_l act on X only, and the start (I (x) F_0)(1 (x) v) is 1 (x) F_0 v.

Formalized (proved): the abstract finite-word induction (bump, counts, raw, cut, raw_support, cut_eq_raw: the definitions and proof of StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw, re-proved in this module, which cannot import the non-module HermiteWord); the degree bookkeeping for color total degrees (colorGood_vac, colorGood_field: an insertion of color i raises the total degree of color i by at most one and keeps the other colors, lowering terms retained; colorGood_frame, truncN_eq); E:finite-word-cutoff for every finite word with r_i <= N_i (finite_word_cutoff, finite_word_cutoff_paper); and the last sentence of the lemma, for finite sums of integrals of words, coordinatewise in the Hermite basis (finite_word_cutoff_integral; each word carries its own first frame F_0, and the integrands agree everywhere, so no integrability is needed). The use in P:interval-coefficients: the phase form of the display (phase_word_cutoff, insertions (u, w) -> (0, sigma_i B_i u), line 3861), the bridge to FixedSplit's cutoff model (extP_cutWordC, cutWordC_eq_raw: the cutoff word of FixedSplit.fockJ, extended by zero, is the word with P before and after every insertion), the exact preservation of the selected coefficient (coef_cutoff_eq, lines 4166-4170), the identification of Q_(r,q) with the cutoff inner product of FixedSplit (fullInner_extP, Q_identification), and the step row interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_words, which is FixedSplit.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_fixed without its added hypothesis hQ.

The added hypothesis hQ of FixedSplit (Le's temporary acceptance of 2026-11-12) is removed in this step row, exactly as follows. In interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_fixed the coefficient Q p was a free real function with hQ: \|Q_(r,q)\| <= \|<U_r v, U_q v>_(1/T)\| for the cutoff coefficients. In interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_words Q_(r,q) is the real part of <U_r v, U_q v>_(H_(1/T)) (fullInner) for uncut coefficients U, and hsplits (E:interval-energy-splits with the reflection parity, lines 4145-4157) is stated for it; the bound that hQ assumed is proved from the named input DuhamelWords (the Duhamel expansion of the ordinary coefficients, lines 4092-4097 and 4166-4170: U_r v and the cutoff coefficient c_r are the same finite sum of integrals of words with exactly r_i insertions of color i, uncut for U_r and cut for c_r), required for every degree split and split, with the insertions S_b M_(e_j) S_b of SplitInputs. The evolutions are not constructed in the package (FixedSplit already takes the cutoff coefficients as parameters), so this expansion is supplied; unlike hQ, it does not assume the conclusion. Q_(r,q) is the real part of the TeX's complex inner product: E:interval-energy-splits is a real identity, and \|Re z\| <= \|z\|. Every other hypothesis is that of interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_fixed (hsplits, SplitInputs, FockColumn and the operator hypotheses of L:fixed-split remain supplied). hQ remains a hypothesis of FixedSplit.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_fixed itself, which is unchanged.

Differences from the TeX (registered as M2): the Gaussian space L^2(Omega; X) over the finitely many coordinates is represented by its Hermite coefficients, the uncut space by all functions (Fin m -> N) -> X, and its inner product fullInner is a tsum, evaluated in the theorems only on extensions of cutoff vectors, which are finitely supported; integrals of words are taken coordinatewise in the Hermite basis (the Hermite coefficients of a Bochner integral in L^2(Omega; X) are the integrals of the coefficients; this identification is not proved). Junk values: none; Bochner integrals are compared only for everywhere-equal integrands, so they agree whether or not they are integrable. Mathlib's complex inner product is linear in the second slot, the TeX's in the first (line 3374); the two differ by conjugation, which leaves the real part and the modulus used here unchanged. Hypotheses carried and unused: the completeness of X in finite_word_cutoff_paper; hRdef in interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_words (as in fixed_split_paper).

Refutations (refutations/finite-word-cutoff/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbations (wrong statements inside the lemma's hypotheses): SelfContraction (the compressed word at an admissible cutoff is not a pure creation chaos: the word g g at N = 2 has vacuum coefficient E[g^2] = 1) and PerModeCutoff (the color total-degree cutoff is not the per-mode cutoff k_j <= N_(col j): two modes of one color, N = 1, multi-index (1, 1)). Controls outside the manuscript domain (they show that the count hypothesis r_i <= N_i is needed, with a witness that violates it): CutoffBelowCounts (the word g g at N = 1: degree-2 coefficient sqrt 2 against 0) and CoefficientBeyondCutoff (a genuine instance of DuhamelWords with r = 2 at cutoff N = 1, so the input is not vacuous; the cutoff coefficient vanishes at degree 2, the uncut one is sqrt 2).

Wave L10 (item L10-FS1) in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FixedSplit.lean: the assembly of L:fixed-split (A fixed degree-split estimate; main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 3675-3716 with E:fixed-split-bound at lines 3702-3713, proof lines 3718-4051), on the model-free core FixedSplitCore (its own section) and the Fock layer of HermiteFock and FockForm. The lemma is concluded on a finite Fock model, with the operator facts about the cutoff evolution that the package does not construct as named inputs. Class: inputs supplied, narrower conclusion.

The Fock model. The Gaussian modes are Fin m, mode j of color (interval) col j, so the TeX's m_i modes of color i are the j with col j = i. A cutoff vector of the Gaussian L^2 space with values in the spatial band space X (any complete complex inner product space) is a coefficient vector f : cutIdx col N -> X in the normalized Hermite basis, cutIdx col N the multi-indices of color degree <= N_i in every color (N_i = 2k_i). Phase vectors are pairs (f, g), and \|(f,g)\|_rho is the norm of fockEmb S rho (f, g), with S_rho standing for A_rho^(-1/2) (lines 3370-3372; the coefficient norm is the Gaussian L^2 norm by HermiteFock.integral_norm_sq_iota). Z_S (lines 3845-3855) is fockZ: both components supported on multi-indices of color degree one on S, zero off A and S, and at most N_i on A. The insertion J_i(u, w) = (0, sigma_i B_i u) (line 3861) is fockJ, with the color-i field sum_(col j = i) g_j S_b M_(e_j) S_b acting by HermiteFock.gmul, followed by the cutoff.

Formalized (proved): the common partition E:split-partition (lines 3779-3790: cutSet, cutPt, nCut, cutPt_spec, nCut_le); the chronological word and E:split-word-product for it (word_chain, lines 3895-3930, feeding the norms of the partial words to FixedSplitCore.split_word_bound, split_segment_product_paper and interval_copy_metric_paper); E:split-fresh-insertion on the Fock model (coef_insertion, fock_insertion, fock_insertion_bound: J_i maps Z_S into Z_(S + i) for a color in its vacuum, with \|J_i x\|_rho <= c_i \|x\|_rho for every rho >= lambda, from E:interval-column through FockForm.interval_contractions); the vacuum start and the identity between phase norms (vacPhase_mem, fockEmb_vacPhase, fockEmb_cmp, lines 3811-3817); E:interval-cross-vector from E:interval-cross-cube (the simplices are measurable and disjoint, sum_pi \|D_pi\| <= prod_C h_i, and Minkowski's bound, lines 3947-3967; no factor m! enters); the per-copy bound of E:split-vector-cauchy (copy_coefficient_bound, through FixedSplitCore.torus_coefficient_norm_le); and E:split-before-absorption with the absorption into E:fixed-split-bound (Cauchy-Schwarz with \|w\|_(1/T) <= k \|w\|_lambda and \|v\|_lambda <= \|v\|_(1/T), lines 3997-4050: fixed_split_abstract, fixed_split, fixed_split_paper). interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_fixed is the step row of P:interval-coefficients with its input hfixed discharged by fixed_split_paper.

Supplied inputs (named propositions): FockForm.FockColumn (E:interval-column, lines 3388-3391) for the modes of each color at every rho > 0; SegmentBound (the segment bound of L:interval-complex as applied in E:split-segment-product, lines 3791-3801: the background propagator has norm at most 100 e^(2 Lambda (t-s)) on every interval free of background endpoints); DysonCrossCube (E:interval-cross-cube, lines 3937-3960, on the torus of the background radii, with the integrability of the word on each simplex); BackgroundPreserves (lines 3855-3859: the background propagator preserves every Z_S); EntireCoefficients (lines 3729-3733: the ordinary coefficients converge absolutely on every polydisc). SplitInputs bundles them for one split. The background propagator P_z, the cutoff evolution M^cut_z(T) and its coefficients U_r v are not constructed: they are parameters (P, c), constrained only by these inputs.

Hypotheses on the abstract operators, all properties of the TeX's operators: S_rho symmetric with \|S_rho\| <= rho^(-1) and the spectral comparison \|S_rho' g\| <= max{1, rho/rho'} \|S_rho g\| (from A_rho'^(-1) <= q^2 A_rho^(-1), line 3817); M_(e_j) symmetric; S_b a symmetric idempotent commuting with S_rho; V >= \|(u, w)\|_(1/T)^2; I_i^T = (a_i, b_i) with b_i - a_i <= h_i, and [a_i, b_i] subset [0, T] for the cross colors. In the step row interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_fixed the coefficient Q_(r,q) of P:interval-coefficients stays a real number, and the hypothesis hQ (\|Q_(r,q)\| is at most the modulus of the cutoff inner product <U_r v, U_q v>_(1/T)) is ADDED: it is not a hypothesis of the proposition. In the TeX Q_(r,q) is that inner product (line 4142) and the cutoff keeps the selected coefficients exactly (lines 4163-4170, by L:finite-word-cutoff); the author accepted hQ for now on 2026-11-12. Wave L11 removes it: FiniteWordCutoff.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_words is this step row without hQ, with Q_(r,q) the real part of <U_r v, U_q v>_(H_(1/T)) for uncut coefficients and the named input DuhamelWords (the Duhamel word expansion of the coefficients) in its place (section FiniteWordCutoff). This row keeps hQ; it is not changed.

Differences from the TeX. delta > 0 is a free parameter. FixedSplit does not specialize it to StaticPhaseCauchy.deltaA (alpha/2) (the TeX's delta_a = delta_(alpha/2) of L:complex-phase, defined there); the inputs are taken at the given delta. The reductions of lines 3736-3741 (k_i = 0, zero-length intervals) are not needed. The identity norms are bounded by the general telescoping lemma at every cut (no use of q_j = 1 at insertion cuts). The insertion bound holds in every norm rho >= lambda (the TeX uses rho = Lambda(t_i)). DysonCrossCube is required only on the torus \|z_i\| = rho_i. The comparison of the projected initial phase with the original data (line 4049) is the free bound V. fixed_split_paper carries the definition of R_alpha (_hRdef) unused and uses H:homog only for alpha < 2. Junk values: none (positive bases of the real powers; the Dyson integrals are integrable by the input, and dysonSum_norm_le holds in either case; cutPt returns T beyond its last index, never used; extTime and the choice in cutOp are used only on C and at distinct insertion times). Refutations (refutations/fixed-split/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbations: CubeFactorial (charging every ordering the full cube overcounts by m!; two cross colors) and OccupiedInsertion (the coefficient insertion bound fails for a color that is not in its vacuum; one mode, cutoff 2). Lean-route-only control outside the manuscript domain: InsertionBelowLambda (the monotonicity rho^((alpha-2)/2) <= lambda^((alpha-2)/2) used for rho >= lambda fails for rho < lambda; witness alpha = 0).

Not formalized: the construction of the phase evolution with the bounded potential V_z(t), of P_z and of the coefficients U_r v; the proofs of the supplied inputs (the operator theory of L:interval-complex, variation of constants for E:interval-cross-cube); the spatial half of E:interval-column; and, in this module, the identification of Q_(r,q) with the cutoff inner product (the added hQ; proved in FiniteWordCutoff from the named input DuhamelWords). The route definitions extTime and extC have no rows; route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

FixedSplitCore (proof steps of L:fixed-split (model-free), with the telescoping of the scalar conversion factors of E:interval-metric; analytic bounds as premises)

Wave L10 (item L10-FS0) in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FixedSplitCore.lean. It formalizes the model-free core of L:fixed-split (A fixed degree-split estimate; main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 3675-3716, proof 3718-4051): the steps of the proof that involve neither the Gaussian fields, the Fock spaces nor the phase evolution. The lemma itself is assembled from these steps in FixedSplit (wave item L10-FS1, its own section), on a finite Fock model with named inputs. Each analytic bound that a step uses enters here as a premise of an implication about real numbers (no named input is introduced in this module).

Proved, with nothing supplied (the TeX's displays as stated, with the variants listed below):

  • E:interval-copy-metric (lines 3809-3837): the one-cut ratio max{1, Lambda_X/Lambda_Y} <= prod_(X \ Y) (1 + omega_i/lambda) (cut_ratio_le, lines 3818-3827), and a GENERAL telescoping lemma (metric_telescoping) for any finite family of weights whose activity pattern is order-convex (ActivityConvex: each color is active on one block of consecutive segments; ending_card_le_one: each color ends once, line 3830). interval_copy_metric instantiates it for intervals (a_i, b_i) and a monotone partition (intervalAct, intervalAct_convex; outer heights Lambda_0 = Lambda_(M+1) = lambda); interval_copy_metric_paper is the TeX form with omega_i = k_i/h_i, lambda = k/T, a strict partition and right side D_A. intervalLambda_eq_height identifies Lambda_j with the value of Lambda(t) (lines 3765-3766) on (tau_(j-1), tau_j) when every endpoint in (tau_0, tau_M) is a cut. The same lemma is the telescoping of E:interval-metric along a time partition (L:interval-complex, lines 3556-3571) for the scalar conversion factors, which wave L9 left open; its composition with the segment propagators is done inside L:fixed-split (FixedSplit.word_chain, segment bound supplied).
  • E:split-segment-product (lines 3787-3804): the exponent identity (segSum_eq) and the bound sum_j Lambda_j (tau_j - tau_(j-1)) <= 2k (segSum_le), M <= 3k + 1 (partition_count_le, from the count of interior points as premise), and prod p_j <= 100^M exp(2 sum) <= M_k = 100^(3k+1) e^(4k) (split_segment_product, split_segment_product_paper) with the segment bound p_j <= 100 e^(2 Lambda_j (tau_j - tau_(j-1))) of L:interval-complex as premise; M_k^2 <= (100^8 e^8)^k (Mk_sq_le, line 4038).
  • The radius step after E:split-radii (lines 3743-3777): D(t) <= delta Lambda(t)^(2-a), a = alpha/2 (split_radius_sum), through sum x_i^q <= (sum x_i)^q for q >= 1 (sum_rpow_le_rpow_sum).
  • E:split-word-product (lines 3907-3930): for the sequence of norms of the partial words, w_M <= (prod p)(prod q)(prod b) |v| (split_word_product), insertion cuts carry prod_(i in C) c_i and other cuts at most one (insertion_product_le), so w_M <= M_k D_A (prod c_i) |v| (split_word_bound) given prod p <= M_k, prod q <= D_A.
  • E:split-vector-cauchy (lines 3973-3991): torus_coefficient, the normalized torus extraction of the coefficient of an absolutely convergent multivariate power series with values in a complex Banach space (with integrability), and the Cauchy bound |c_r| <= prod rho_i^(-r_i) sup |Phi| (torus_coefficient_norm_le). Proof by orthogonality of the exponentials on [0, 2 pi]^n and dominated convergence; no multivariable Cauchy integral formula.
  • E:split-before-absorption (lines 3997-4020): the scalar product of the two per-copy bounds (split_before_absorption) from Cauchy-Schwarz and the per-copy bounds as premises, with the metric product D_(A_r) D_(A_q) = prod_B (1 + k_i/(lambda h_i))^(l_i) (metric_product_eq) and the radius product prod_B rho_i^(-2k_i) (inside two_copy_product).
  • E:split-radius-factorial (lines 4022-4036): the three lines as two bounds from the left-hand side (split_radius_factorial; the comparison of the last two right-hand sides is used inside the proof, not exported) and the form under the lemma's hypotheses (split_radius_factorial_paper).
  • E:split-explicit-constant (lines 4037-4050): split_absorption and split_explicit_constant_paper: the before-absorption bound implies E:fixed-split-bound with C_split = 100^8 e^8 max{1, 12 delta^(-2)}, in exactly the form of the input hfixed of IntervalScalarCompleted.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_completed; interval_coefficient_of_before_absorption_paper is that step row of P:interval-coefficients with hfixed replaced by the before-absorption bound.

Not in this module (they are in FixedSplit, on a finite Fock model): the subspaces Z_S, the insertion bound E:split-fresh-insertion (only the constant c_i is defined here), E:interval-cross-vector, the per-copy bound, the norm comparisons |w|_(1/T) <= k |w|_lambda, |v|_lambda <= |v|_(1/T), Cauchy-Schwarz and E:fixed-split-bound itself. Not formalized anywhere: the evolution M^cut_z(T), its propagators and the coefficients U_r v (parameters of FixedSplit), the Dyson cube identity E:interval-cross-cube (a named input of FixedSplit), and the reductions of lines 3736-3741 (zero-length intervals), which FixedSplit does not need.

Abstractions and differences from the TeX: delta > 0 is arbitrary (the TeX uses delta_a = delta_(alpha/2) of L:complex-phase, which the package does not define as a function of alpha here); the copy-metric lemma needs only a monotone partition (the TeX's is strict); the exponent identity is replaced by the inequality "total length of the segments where i is active is at most max{0, b_i - a_i}" (occupation_le; the TeX states equality with omega_i (b_i - a_i)); the word product is stated for the norms of the partial words. split_radius_factorial_paper and split_explicit_constant_paper take H:homog (used for alpha < 2, hence alpha <= 3) and the definition R = R_alpha as _hRdef, carried and unused. one_add_sum_le_prod and one_le_prod_one_add duplicate ComplexPhaseScalar lemmas with the same statements (found at integration); they are listed as route lemmas.

Refutations (refutations/fixed-split-core/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbation: MkSquareConstant (the base 100^7 e^8 fails at k = 1). Control of a broader generalization: TorusNormalization (the torus theorem for any multi-index, refuted at r = 0, n = 1, Phi = 1: the unnormalized angular measure gives 2 pi, not 1; the TeX selects only positive degrees, A_r = {r_i > 0}, lines 3750-3751, so r = 0 is not a manuscript instance). Controls outside the manuscript domain: AbsorptionMaxOne (the constant 12 delta^(-2) without max{1, .} fails at alpha = 2, delta = 4; H:homog has alpha < 2) and NonConvexActivity (the telescoping fails for a color active on two separate blocks; the TeX's intervals are connected).

FockColumnBound (narrower result: L:fock-form and L:interval-contractions, with E:interval-column, on a Fourier-side model with finitely many real modes; the identification of the model with the physical-space operators and of the modes with the Gaussian coordinates of W_eps not formalized; for L:fock-form, coordinates i > m not modelled, and symmetry of the sandwiched coefficient action without the bounded self-adjoint operator packaging of A_rho and B_(N,m,b); for L:interval-contractions, the tensor extension by another Hilbert factor not formalized for the Fourier-side model)

Wave L11 item K2, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FockColumnBound.lean (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, line numbers at 39f2597a). It proves the named input FockForm.FockColumn of FockForm.fock_form_paper (L:fock-form, statement lines 2960-2977, proof lines 2979-3028, spatial half lines 2987-3008) and of FockForm.interval_contractions_paper (L:interval-contractions, statement lines 3384-3404 with E:interval-column at lines 3388-3391, proof lines 3406-3470) for concrete operators, and re-issues both wrappers at those operators with every operator input discharged (fock_form_paper_completed, interval_contractions_paper_completed). The abstract wrappers of FockForm are unchanged.

The concrete model is on the Fourier side. The Hilbert space is X = L^2(R^d, d eta) (Mathlib's Lp C 2 volume), read as the normalized Fourier image of spatial L^2(R^d). On it, A_rho^(-1/2) (A_rho = rho^2 - Delta) is multiplication by w_rho(eta) = (rho^2 + |eta|^2)^(-1/2) (sqrtResolvent, wt); S_b is multiplication by 1_(|eta| <= b) (bandProj); the smoothed field has spectral measure mu_eps(dxi) = e^(-eps|xi|^2) mu(dxi) (nuEps, lines 2505-2506); the modes are a finite orthonormal family psi_1, ..., psi_m in the complex L^2(mu_eps), and multiplication by the mode e_i is represented by (M_(psi_i) f)(eta) = int conj(psi_i(xi)) f(eta - xi) mu_eps(dxi) (conv, modeOp, modes). The reality of a mode is the hypothesis psi_i(-xi) = conj(psi_i(xi)) mu_eps-a.e. (hreal), which models the TeX's real isonormal space (line 2987). Why this is the TeX's object: conjugation by the unitary Fourier transform carries multiplication by e_i to this convolution, -Delta to multiplication by |eta|^2 and S_b to the band indicator, and every conclusion of the wrappers (norm bounds, self-adjointness, column bounds) is invariant under a unitary conjugation. That correspondence is classical and is stated in the module comments only; it is NOT formalized. Neither is the link between the psi_i and the Gaussian coordinates of W_eps (the TeX's e_i(x) = E[W_eps(x) g_i] and W_eps = sum_i g_i e_i, lines 2963-2964 and 2987-2988). The completed theorems are therefore statements about the Fourier-side operators.

Proof-route differences: the TeX's Gaussian isometry and spatial Plancherel identity (an equality for the full mode family, lines 2991-3001 and 3437-3443) is replaced by Bessel's inequality in L^2(mu_eps) at each frequency (sum_conv_le), followed by Tonelli and translation invariance of Lebesgue measure (lintegral_weight_shift); for a finite family this is the TeX's sub-sum step (line 3444). The resolvent bound int mu_eps(dxi)/(rho^2 + |q+xi|^2) <= R_alpha rho^(alpha-2) (nuEps_resolvent, lines 2998-3004 and 3427-3430) comes from PhaseContractions.phase_resolvent and e^(-eps|xi|^2) <= 1. The substitution of lines 3455-3459 is column_sandwich.

Hypotheses of the completed wrappers: fock_form_paper_completed takes the class of S:static-phase as PhaseContractions.PhaseCovariance (lines 2490-2493, on R^3), R = R_alpha, eps, rho > 0, the modes, the band radius b, N and a coefficient vector of degree <= N; interval_contractions_paper_completed takes H:homog (as the other S:interval-upper wrappers), R = R_alpha, eps, rho > 0, the modes and b. Compared with FockForm.fock_form_paper, eps > 0 and the evenness and temperedness of mu are now used (for mu_eps finite and the self-adjointness of M_(psi_i)). The finite orthonormal family with the reality condition is an added form of the TeX's "orthonormal basis of the real isonormal space": it restricts to finitely many modes and states reality on the spectral side. Recorded as carried and unused in the module header (not re-checked here): Gamma_radon, Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef in both wrappers, and dim, alpha0_lt_one of H:homog.

Narrower than the TeX: finitely many modes (the TeX's E:interval-column sums over the full family; the statement's uniformity in the mode cutoff is covered, since the constant does not depend on m); operators on the Fourier side, not identified with the TeX's physical-space operators; for L:fock-form, the Hermite coefficient model of FockForm (coordinates g_i, i > m, are not modelled) and symmetry of the sandwiched coefficient action without the bounded self-adjoint operator packaging of A_rho and B_(N,m,b) ("These are bounded selfadjoint operators", line 2971); for L:interval-contractions, the tensor extension by another Hilbert factor (line 3403) is not formalized for the Fourier-side model (the abstract FockForm wrappers allow any X, with the column bound supplied). Junk values: every wrapper takes rho > 0 and eps > 0, so w_rho has a positive denominator; conv is a Bochner integral (0 where not integrable), but for f in L^2 and finite nu its integrand is integrable for almost every eta (ae_lintegral_shift_lt_top), and modeOp is defined through the bound convMap_bound; the resolvent integrals are lower integrals bounded by a finite value. Class of both rows: same assumptions, narrower conclusion (the completed wrappers take the lemmas' hypotheses and nothing supplied, for the Fourier-side operators, whose identification is not formalized; this is a missing identification, not a registered model choice).

Refutations (refutations/fock-column-bound/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Controls outside the manuscript domain (they show that a hypothesis is needed, with a witness that violates it): BesselNeedsOrthogonality (unit vectors without orthogonality violate Bessel's inequality: two copies of 1 in C), ComplexMultiplier (multiplication by the non-real constant i is not self-adjoint; the modes of the TeX are real) and WeightNeedsShift (without the shift rho > 0 the multiplier \|eta\|^(-1) is unbounded; evaluated at eta != 0).

Not discharged by this module: the operator form of E:fock-sandwich (StaticInteractionCompleted.FockSandwich, ||A_rho^(-1/2) B A_rho^(-1/2)|| <= d rho^(a-2) for one operator B on a complete Hilbert space with A_rho^(-1/2) the continuous-functional-calculus inverse root of a bounded positive A_0 shifted by rho^2). fock_form_paper_completed is a different statement: coefficient vectors of degree <= N with no packaged Hilbert space, sandwiches H_i that depend on rho, and sums of squared coefficient norms instead of an operator norm. Discharging FockSandwich would need a packaged l^2 Hilbert space of degree-<= N coefficient vectors, a bounded A_0 (for example -Delta on the band) whose inverse root agrees with multiplication by w_rho, a rho-independent B, the conversion of the coefficient bound into an operator norm, and the physical-side identification above. Wave L12 (FockSandwichModel) provides all of these except the physical-side identification, with the inverse root agreeing with multiplication by w_rho on the band range (the sandwiched operator is the TeX's operator extended by zero), and discharges FockSandwich on this Fourier-side model.

Route definitions without claim rows (they appear in the statements of the rows below): L2Map (the data of a bounded map on L^2 representatives), L2Map.toLinear, L2Map.op, mulMap, mulOp (multiplication by a bounded measurable real function), convMap, band (the indicator of |eta| <= b).

Consumers of the Hermite/Fock foundation (GaussianHermite, HermiteFock) in notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a (main TeX; all line numbers in this section refer to that file). Three labelled results and the hypotheses of one audit lemma.

L:fock-form (statement lines 2960-2977, display E:fock-sandwich lines 2972-2976, proof lines 2979-3028). The proof has a spatial half (lines 2987-3008: the representation W_eps = sum_i g_i e_i, Gaussian isometry, spatial Plancherel and E:phase-resolvent of L:phase-contractions, giving sum_i H_i^2 <= R_alpha rho^(alpha-4) for H_i = A_rho^(-1/2) M_(e_i) A_rho^(-1/2), then compression to S_b) and a Fock half (lines 3016-3027). The Fock half and the compression are proved; the bound sum_i H_i^2 <= R_alpha rho^(alpha-4) is the named input FockColumn H (R_alpha rho^(alpha-4)) (column form sum_i ||H_i u||^2 <= c ||u||^2, which is the TeX's quadratic-form inequality). The wrapper fock_form_paper states the lemma with the standing class of S:static-phase (lines 2490-2502) and R = R_alpha (line 2497). Class here: inputs supplied. Wave L11 proves the spatial column bound on a concrete Fourier-side model with finitely many real modes (FockColumnBound.fock_column_completed) and re-issues the lemma there with nothing supplied (FockColumnBound.fock_form_paper_completed); the identification of that model with the physical-space operators is not formalized (section FockColumnBound). The abstract FockForm wrappers are unchanged.

L:interval-contractions (statement lines 3384-3404, proof lines 3406-3470). E:interval-column (lines 3388-3391), the first display of the lemma, is the named input (FockColumn for the operators A_rho^(-1/2) M_(e_m) with constant R_alpha rho^(alpha-2)). Proved from it: the same column bound for band-compressed multiplications (lines 3444-3447), the phase insertion on a color in its vacuum with norm at most sqrt(R_alpha) rho^((alpha-2)/2) in ||(f,g)||_rho (lines 3394-3397, 3447-3449), the substitution sum (A_rho^(-1/2) M A_rho^(-1/2))^2 <= R_alpha rho^(alpha-4) (lines 3455-3459) and E:interval-fock (lines 3400-3402, 3460-3464). The wrapper interval_contractions_paper assumes H:homog, as the other S:interval-upper wrappers do, and R = R_alpha (line 3370). Class here: inputs supplied. E:interval-column is proved on the Fourier-side model of wave L11 (FockColumnBound.interval_column_completed), and FockColumnBound.interval_contractions_paper_completed re-issues the wrapper there with nothing supplied.

E:occupied-multiplication (lines 2189-2191, inside the proof of P:mild-construction; statement lines 2151-2165, proof from line 2171), for finitely many coordinates: ||HF||_2 <= 2 sqrt(n+1) ||H||_2 ||F||_2 for H = sum_i a_i g_i and F a real polynomial of total degree at most n in independent standard Gaussians g_1, ..., g_m, on stdPi m (occupied_multiplication, squared form) and on a probability space (occupied_multiplication_paper). Nothing is supplied. Narrower than the TeX: F ranges over polynomials in finitely many coordinates and H over their span, not over the closed space P_(<=n) and all centered linear Gaussians; the closure step and the almost-sure identification (lines 2197-2201) are not formalized.

The degree-raising hypotheses of StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw for the concrete Fock model (goodDeg_vac, goodDeg_insert, goodDeg_frame, truncC_eq): coefficient vectors over colors Fin m with one Gaussian mode per color, insertion J_i v = gmul i (K_i v) (multiplication by g_i tensored with an operator K_i on X), frames acting on X, and per-color degree truncation P = truncC Nc. They have exactly the shapes of the hypotheses hv0, hJ, hF, hP of cut_eq_raw (with bump i d = fun c => d c + if c = i then 1 else 0). The application is the audit file StratonovichHAMAudit/HermiteWordFock.lean (section HermiteWordFock (narrower result:L:finite-word-cutofffor one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)), since HermiteWord is not a module.

Model. Spatial L^2 is an abstract complex inner product space X; the operators of the TeX enter as continuous linear maps on X: H_i for A_rho^(-1/2) M_(e_i) A_rho^(-1/2), P for the band projection S_b, S for A_rho^(-1/2), M_i for M_(e_m). The Gaussian factor is HermiteFock's coefficient model (degrees <= N; the truncation P_N is restriction of coefficients) or its expansion iota on stdPi m. Self-adjointness is used in the symmetric form <T u, w> = <u, T w>, derived from IsSelfAdjoint (on a complete X) in the wrappers. The quantifier "uniformly in eps, m, b" is the independence of the constant d_N rho^(alpha/2-2) from eps, m and P, given the supplied column bound.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit. rho > 0 (the TeX writes A_rho = rho^2 - Delta); S_b symmetric and idempotent and commuting with A_rho^(-1/2); ||A_rho^(-1/2) f|| <= rho^(-1) ||f|| (from A_rho >= rho^2).

Hypotheses carried but unused (underscore hypotheses, confirmed by the proofs). fock_form_paper: local finiteness of Gamma and mu, evenness, temperedness, positive definiteness, the spectral relation and the scaling of Gamma, and eps > 0; used are 0 < alpha < 2, the formula for R_alpha (to get R_alpha >= 0 by IntervalScalar.ralpha_nonneg) and rho > 0. interval_contractions_paper: of H:homog only the fields alpha_range, threshold and alpha0_pos are used (for 0 < alpha < 2), and eps > 0 is carried and unused.

Route differences. General coefficient operators H_i replace the TeX's rotated basis (line 2192), and the annihilation part is bounded through the finite adjoint identity (see HermiteFock); for E:occupied-multiplication the case H = 0 needs no separate treatment.

Narrower conclusions and not formalized. In L:fock-form, the Gaussian factor consists of the m multiplied coordinates (coordinates g_i with i > m, on which P_N also acts in the TeX, are not modelled), and symmetry is proved for the sandwiched truncated operator on the coefficient model (the finite coefficient pairing identity; no operator-space packaging as a self-adjoint operator is stated), not for B_(N,m,b) itself. Not formalized: the spatial half of L:fock-form and E:interval-column (supplied), the construction of W_eps, e_i, M_(e_i), A_rho and S_b on spatial L^2, the closure step of E:occupied-multiplication and the rest of P:mild-construction.

Junk values. rho > 0 throughout, so rho^(alpha-4), rho^(alpha-2) and rho^(alpha/2-2) are genuine powers; square roots are of nonnegative reals (R_alpha >= 0 is proved in the wrappers); every integral conclusion includes integrability. fockD N R uses Lean's real square root, 0 for R < 0, which no wrapper reaches.

Refutations (refutations/fock-form/): CompressNonProjection (compression by a symmetric P that is not idempotent can increase the column bound), OccupiedConstant (the constant n+1 in place of 4(n+1) in occupied_multiplication fails for H = F = g, n = 1) and TruncWithoutCutoff (truncC_eq without d <= N fails).

FockSandwichModel (narrower result: L:fock-form in operator form on a Fourier-side model with finitely many real modes, the identification of the model with the physical-space operators and of the modes with the Gaussian coordinates of W_eps not formalized, coordinates i > m not modelled; C:static-interaction and P:static-phase-all-orders with FockSandwich proved on that model; for C:static-interaction and P:static-phase-all-orders, FockSandwich, the positivity of A_0 and the self-adjointness of B proved on that model for mode families of every size m (an orthonormal family of every size m is assumed, which excludes mu = 0), the order display and the interaction estimate only (as in StaticInteractionCompleted), phases not constructed, CPInputs, PropagatorBlock and the other inputs of StaticInteractionCompleted supplied)

Wave L12 item F1, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FockSandwichModel.lean (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, line numbers at 39f2597a): the named input StaticInteractionCompleted.FockSandwich (E:fock-sandwich of L:fock-form in operator form, statement lines 2960-2977, proof lines 2979-3028) is proved on a concrete model of the cutoff Hilbert space, and the wrappers of C:static-interaction and P:static-phase-all-orders are re-issued without it. FockSandwich A_0 B d a states \|A_rho^(-1/2) B A_rho^(-1/2)\| <= d rho^(a-2) for every rho > 0, with A_rho^(-1/2) read as ComplexPhaseScalar.invSqrtShift A_0 rho, the Ring.inverse of the continuous-functional-calculus square root of A_0 + rho^2 for a bounded positive A_0.

The model. Spatial L^2(R^3) is the Fourier side L^2(R^3, d eta) of FockColumnBound (L2), on which S_b is multiplication by 1_(\|eta\| <= b) (bandProj), A_rho^(-1/2) is multiplication by (rho^2 + \|eta\|^2)^(-1/2) (sqrtResolvent) and M_(e_i) is the convolution modes ... i of a finite orthonormal family of real modes in L^2(mu_eps). As in FockColumnBound, the identification with the physical-space operators (conjugation by the unitary Fourier transform) and of the modes with the Gaussian coordinates of W_eps (lines 2963-2964, 2987-2988) is not formalized; every conclusion here (operator norms, self-adjointness, positivity) is invariant under that unitary conjugation, but the identification is a missing construction, not a registered model choice, so the row stays narrower. The Gaussian factor truncated to degrees <= N is the Hermite coefficient model of HermiteFock (registered model choice M2, Scope) over the multi-indices of degree <= N in m modes; coordinates g_i, i > m, are not modelled (as in FockForm). The cutoff Hilbert space is the finite l^2 sum FockSp X m N = PiLp 2 (degLE m N -> X) (P_N is built in), and FockH is the same space as a type that carries only its complex Hilbert structure. The band cutoff is not built into the space: on all of FockH, A_0 = diag M_(\|eta\|^2 1_(\|eta\| <= b)) (opA0), which is -Delta on the band range and 0 off it and is bounded by b^2 (line 3025, "Boundedness of -Delta on S_b is explicit"), and B = B_(N,m,b) (fieldB) is the truncated field of the compressed S_b M_(e_i) S_b, which maps into the joint range and vanishes off it (fieldB_band). On the joint range, invSqrtShift A_0 rho is A_rho^(-1/2) = (rho^2 - Delta)^(-1/2) (invSqrtShift_band), so the operator bounded by FockSandwich is the TeX's operator extended by zero.

Formalized (proved, nothing supplied): the diagonal extension diagOp with products, unit, sums, scalars, adjoints, self-adjointness and positivity; the truncated field fockOp as a continuous linear map on FockSp X m N, equal componentwise to HermiteFock.fieldOp in degrees <= N (fockOp_apply), self-adjoint for symmetric H_i (fockOp_isSelfAdjoint), with the norm bound fockOp_norm_le from a column bound; M_a >= 0 for a >= 0 and M_1 = 1; the functional calculus on the model (shiftOp_eq, sqrt_shiftOp_eq by CFC.sqrt_eq_iff, invSqrtShift_eq by an explicit two-sided inverse, so Ring.inverse is the genuine inverse); the sandwich identity sandwich_eq (the truncated field of S_b H_i S_b with the H_i = A_rho^(-1/2) M_(e_i) A_rho^(-1/2) of FockColumnBound), hence, with FockForm.fock_form and FockColumnBound.fock_column_completed, FockSandwich A_0 B d_N (alpha/2) with A_0 >= 0 and B self-adjoint (fockSandwich_model) and the operator form of L:fock-form (fock_sandwich_paper: A_0 >= 0, B_(N,m,b) self-adjoint, B on the joint range, invSqrtShift A_0 rho = A_rho^(-1/2) there, and E:fock-sandwich, with d_N = 2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(R_alpha) independent of eps, m, b and the modes). Class of L:fock-form: same assumptions, narrower conclusion (unchanged): this module adds the operator form and the bounded self-adjoint packaging of A_0 and B_(N,m,b) on the model; the narrowings above (the Fourier-side identification, finitely many modes, coordinates i > m) remain.

The re-issued wrappers. static_phase_all_orders_model (E:all-static-phase-orders of P:static-phase-all-orders, lines 3098-3105, proof 3127-3192) and static_interaction_model_paper (C:static-interaction, lines 3216-3240, proof 3264-3311) are StaticInteractionCompleted.static_phase_all_orders_cp and static_interaction_completed_paper with the cutoff Hilbert spaces FockH (L^2(d eta)) m n, A_0 = opA0 b and B = fieldB b ... (psi m) for every Gaussian cutoff m and band b in N; FockSandwich, A_0 >= 0 and B = B^* are proved (in the wave-L11 wrappers they were supplied: FockSandwich as a named input, the positivity of A_0 and the self-adjointness of B as hypotheses at every cutoff). Still supplied, so both rows stay inputs-supplied with a narrower conclusion: CPInputs and PropagatorBlock (now at these concrete A_0, B), entireness, the coefficient identification and the cutoff removals of StaticPhaseCauchy.static_phase_all_orders_step (hentire, hz, hv, hband, hgauss), and for C:static-interaction also the free estimate, group law and norm comparisons (hT, hS, hTS, hZ0, hcmp, hN1), the Gaussian parity (hodd) and the first-variance bounds (hborn, hmean); the phases are not constructed.

Hypotheses beyond the manuscript's class (as in FockColumnBound): finitely many modes psi_1, ..., psi_m orthonormal in L^2(mu_eps) and real (psi_i(-xi) = conj(psi_i(xi))), the band radius b, the Fourier-side model. The class of S:static-phase is PhaseContractions.PhaseCovariance (lines 2490-2502); used: 0 < alpha < 2 and the local finiteness, evenness, temperedness, spectral relation and scaling of mu (through fock_column_completed); carried, unused in all three wrappers: the fields Gamma_radon, Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef. fock_sandwich_paper uses hRdef (R = R_alpha). Added restriction of the two re-issued wrappers static_phase_all_orders_model and static_interaction_model_paper (the binder hpsi : forall m, Orthonormal C (psi m), with hreal): an orthonormal real family psi_m of size m in L^2(mu_eps) for every Gaussian cutoff m. This forces mu != 0; the case mu = 0, which the TeX keeps (line 3089, "Retain the full covariance class"; proof lines 3126-3127: then every positive-order term is zero), is not covered by these wrappers. It is not part of the registered model choice M2. Junk values: rho > 0 throughout, so (rho^2 + \|eta\|^2 1_b)^(-1/2) has a positive base and rho^(alpha/2-2) is a genuine power; Ring.inverse is applied only to an operator with an explicit two-sided inverse; R_alpha >= 0 is proved.

Refutations (refutations/fock-sandwich-model/), classified; none relies on a junk value except InverseNeedsShift, which exhibits one. Lean-route-only control: ShiftedSymbolOffBand (invSqrtShift A_0 rho is not (rho^2 - Delta)^(-1/2) off the band: the model's symbol and wt differ at rho = 1, b = 0, \|eta\| = 1; the identification holds after S_b). Control of Lean's totalized arithmetic outside the manuscript domain: InverseNeedsShift (without rho > 0 the symbols symI and symR are not inverse: both are 0 at rho = 0, eta = 0). Control of a broader generalization: SymbolNeedsBand (without the band the symbol \|eta\|^2 of -Delta is unbounded; the witness is in d = 1, while the TeX's space is R^3, where the same unboundedness holds).

FrequencyRow (whole result)

Formalizes Proposition P:frequency-row (lines 48-165) and Corollary C:frequency-time (lines 172-199) of notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex at a284420 (the file is byte-identical at ba01d98, so the line numbers hold for both revisions). It also formalizes the definitions E:variance-scale-profile (lines 12-20), E:frequency-row-kernel (lines 33-37) and E:frequency-row-integral (lines 38-42), and the closed-ball remark after E:frequency-translated-growth (lines 29-31). bracket and frequencyPair (Q_h of E:masked-frequency-pair) are reused from MaskedTrigProducts. J_h(xi) is a lower Lebesgue integral in [0, inf], the "nonnegative extended integral" of line 43, so no Bochner junk value enters its definition. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.

The quantifier order is exactly exists K, forall d nu C h xi. frequency_row proves exists K >= 0, forall d (nu a measure on R^d) C, C >= 0 -> growth -> forall h, 0 < h -> h <= 1 -> sup_xi J_h(xi) <= K C B_alpha(h). It also proves, for each xi, nu-integrability of lambda -> Phi_h(xi, xi-lambda) and the real-integral bound <xi>^(2 gamma) int Phi_h(xi,xi-lambda) nu(dlambda) <= K C B_alpha(h) (the finiteness at lines 162-163). Its hypotheses are a < 1, alpha + a < 2, 2 gamma <= 1 and alpha + 2 gamma < 2. The section's range 0 < gamma < min(1/2, (2-alpha)/2) (E:variance-gamma-range, lines 7-9) implies the last two. frequency_time has the same form, exists K_beta >= 0, forall d nu C h, with the extra hypotheses 2 beta < 2 - a and 2 beta < 3 - a - alpha. The _paper wrappers take the section's hypotheses: H:homog with a = alpha0 as HomogCovariance d alpha a Gamma mu (lines 5-6), the range of gamma, a locally finite (Radon) nu, C >= 0 and the growth bound. The corollary also takes 1/2 < beta < min(1 - a/2, (3-a-alpha)/2) (E:variance-beta-range, lines 174-176). In the wrappers the constant is chosen before d, Gamma, mu, nu, C, h (and xi).

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: B(y,r) in E:frequency-translated-growth is read as the open ball, the weaker hypothesis, and closedBall_le derives the closed-ball bound. nu is a measure on the Borel sigma-algebra. Measurability of the kernel is proved, not assumed. Integrability is part of the conclusion.

Hypotheses carried but unused (wrappers): gamma > 0, beta > 1/2, local finiteness of nu, and all of H:homog except alpha0 < 1 and alpha0 + alpha < 2. The general theorems hold for every d, including d = 0, and every real alpha meeting their numerical hypotheses.

Proof route. The integrand is bounded pointwise by two dyadic shell majorants of closed balls of radius 2^j: one around xi on the near region |lambda| <= 4|xi|, one around 0 on the far region. The TeX splits at 4q, q = max(1,|xi|). On the near region <xi> >= 2^n/5 gives the single ratio 2^(alpha+2gamma-2) < 1 for all three cases of alpha. This replaces the three-case bound on A_xi(q) (lines 68-109). The far region and the bound on S(h) follow lines 113-161, split at the first M with h 2^M > 1, which is L + 1 of line 147. The corollary follows lines 186-197. Rows labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve only this route.

Not formalized: the instance nu = mu with C = C_Gamma. It needs P:masked-spectral-growth (integrated_covariance_foundation.tex), which is not in this module. The rest of S:wave-variance (the forms on the full phase, lines 224 onward) is also not formalized, except L:phase-bessel (lines 426-449, module PhaseBessel) and P:wave-two-variances (module WaveTwoVariances, with named inputs; there P:frequency-row is applied at nu = nu_R, C = C_nu).

GaussianComparison (narrower result: only the finite Gaussian comparison of P:masked-noise-completion)

Formalizes the finite Gaussian comparison used in P:masked-noise-completion (Completion on the same noise) of S:masked-covariance (notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 249-267, the comparison sentence lines 262-266; proof lines 269-328, the comparison argument lines 320-327). This is a standalone finite result supporting the label, not the label. For a finite index type iota, real matrices A, B with A and B - A positive semidefinite (A <= B in positive semidefinite order, lines 321-322: b^T A b <= b^T B b for every real b), every seminorm N on R^iota (EuclideanSpace R iota) and every real p >= 1, the moments x -> N(x)^p are integrable against the centered Gaussian laws N(0,A) and N(0,B) (Mathlib's multivariateGaussian) and int N(x)^p dN(0,A) <= int N(x)^p dN(0,B) (line 325, E norm(X)^p <= E norm(X+Z)^p, with the finiteness of lines 326-327). Every norm is a seminorm, so the TeX's "every norm" is covered; the integrability statements are conclusions because a Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0.

Outside Lean (D1): the identification of A with the covariance matrix of the masked noise evaluations W(zeta_R F_i) and of B with the auxiliary Gram matrix of N_R (lines 262-264 and 320-321), the inequality E W(zeta_R F)^2 <= N_R(F)^2 behind A <= B (lines 304-305), the noise identity E:masked-actual-noise-norm (lines 251-254), membership of mathcal D in the test-noise completion, the contraction extension and its joint Gaussianity (lines 260-262, 304-311). No hypothesis of the Lean theorems stands for them; they are what a statement about the noise would add.

Proof-route differences. The coupling of lines 323-325 ("diagonalizing B - A constructs a centered Gaussian vector Z ... independent of X, on a product space") is the identity of laws N(0,B) = N(0,A) * N(0,B-A) (multivariateGaussian_conv, by characteristic functions, Measure.ext_of_charFun), and the integral against the convolution is the iterated integral over the product. The conditional Jensen step is Jensen's inequality (ConvexOn.map_integral_le) for the convex function y -> N(x+y)^p and the centered law N(0,B-A), for almost every x. Finite moments come from IsGaussian.memLp_id and N(x) <= C norm(x).

The calibration lemmas coordSeminorm, coordSeminorm_apply and integral_coord_sq (int |x_i|^2 dN(0,S) = S_ii) have no manuscript label and are used by the refutations (refutations/gaussian-comparison/).

GaussianHermite (foundation: normalized Hermite polynomials)

A foundation with no manuscript label of its own; everything is proved and nothing is supplied. The manuscript (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, main TeX) uses "normalized Hermite polynomials" in three proofs: L:fock-form (lines 3016-3018), the multiplication bound E:occupied-multiplication inside the proof of P:mild-construction (lines 2192-2197) and L:finite-word-cutoff (lines 3061-3063). It uses two facts about them: multiplication by the coordinate g_i acts by g_i h_k = sqrt(k_i+1) h_(k+e_i) + sqrt(k_i) h_(k-e_i), and the h_k are orthonormal under independent standard Gaussians. The TeX takes the creation and annihilation algebra from Janson (cited at lines 2954-2955). This module proves both facts, and the spanning step of E:occupied-multiplication.

Formalized. The probabilists' Hermite polynomials He_n are Mathlib's Polynomial.hermite mapped to real coefficients (hermR, values He). The module proves the Appell property He_(n+1)' = (n+1) He_n (absent from Mathlib), the recurrences, Gaussian integration by parts on polynomials (gE_X_mul, from GaussianIBP.integral_mul_eq_integral_deriv), the shift E[He_(n+1) q] = E[He_n q'], and orthogonality E[He_n He_m] = n! delta_(nm). The normalized h_n = He_n/sqrt(n!) are orthonormal (integral_hn_mul_hn) and satisfy x h_n = sqrt(n+1) h_(n+1) + sqrt(n) h_(n-1) (mul_hn). The products h_k(x) = prod_i h_(k_i)(x_i) on R^m are orthonormal under GaussianIBP.stdPi m, the product of m standard Gaussian laws (integral_hk_mul_hk), and satisfy the coordinate recurrence of the TeX (coord_mul_hk). The spanning step: every real polynomial in x_1, ..., x_m of total degree at most n is a real combination of the h_l with |l| <= n (mvPolynomial_mem_hermiteSpan, via monomial_mem_hermiteSpan and the triangularity pow_mem_span1).

Abstractions. Gaussian coordinates are the coordinate functions on Fin m -> R under stdPi m; the transfer to independent standard Gaussians on a probability space is GaussianIBP.integral_comp_eq_stdPi, used in FockForm.occupied_multiplication_paper. Multi-indices are functions Fin m -> N; k - e_i is pointwise truncated subtraction.

Junk values. None of the statements depends on one: sqrt(n!) > 0, every integral statement comes with its integrability, and k - e_i (or n - 1) only appears multiplied by a coefficient that vanishes exactly when the subtraction truncates: sqrt(k_i) (or sqrt(n)) in the normalized formulas, k_i (or n, as in n * hermR (n - 1)) in the unnormalized ones.

Not formalized here: the closed Gaussian polynomial spaces, infinitely many coordinates, and the Wiener chaos decomposition. Labelling: a row is labelled with a manuscript step only where the TeX states it (the recurrence and the orthonormality of the normalized polynomials, and the spanning step of E:occupied-multiplication, which the TeX uses when it passes to "finite-coordinate polynomials"); the remaining public facts are foundation rows ("no direct label") or route helpers.

Refutations (refutations/gaussian-hermite/, each a Lean proof that a wrong variant is false, with the package statement at the same point): OrthogonalityNoDelta (dropping the Kronecker delta in E[He_n He_m] = n! delta_(nm)), UnnormalizedOrthonormal (E[He_2^2] = 2, so the normalization is needed) and RecurrenceNoLowering (dropping the lowering term of mul_hn).

GaussianScalarPowers (whole result)

Formalizes all four parts of L:gaussian-scalar-powers (notes/integrated_compact_gaussian.tex). In the last part, "E" is the integral against a probability measure, "finite expectation" is integrability, Z >= 0 holds almost everywhere, and the integrability of Z^r is proved as part of the conclusion. Finite Hoelder is proved through Mathlib's inequality rather than the manuscript's normalization; the statement is the manuscript's.

GramScalarAlgebra (whole result)

Formalizes all three parts of L:gram-scalar-algebra (notes/integrated_positive_gram.tex), with C_ij = <k_i, k_j> as in the section's setup. The Hilbert-space statements hold in any real inner product space (completeness is not needed), and the section's other standing assumptions (C_ij >= 0, ell_i > 0, b_i >= 0) are not used by this lemma. gram_scalar_algebra_paper restates all three parts with exactly the manuscript's hypotheses (a real Hilbert space and C_ij >= 0). These overlap the step facts PositiveGram.scalar_sqrt_dual and PositiveGram.gram_norm_square.

H1Density (foundation: density of test functions in H^1)

A deterministic foundation of wave L7 (item L7-c), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/H1Density.lean: smooth compactly supported functions are dense in the weak-gradient H^1(R^d; R) of WeakSobolev. It carries no manuscript label of its own. The manuscript states the fact in one sentence in the proof of P:spatial-four-linear (notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex at revision 39f2597a, proposition lines 297-315, proof lines 317-398; the density sentence and its sketch are lines 352-356) and uses it to extend smooth-profile statements to H^1 profiles: in the same proof at lines 360-361 ("take smooth approximants converging in H^1") and line 390, and in the proof of P:spatial-energy-map (lines 432-461) at lines 437-439 and 452. Every hypothesis is stated; nothing is supplied. In the completion module SpatialOccupationL7Completed it discharges the density hypothesis hdense of SpatialFourLinear (P:spatial-four-linear and P:spatial-energy-map).

  • The space is the package's own weak-gradient H^1 (identified with Mathlib's Bessel-potential H^{1,2} in H1Mathlib, wave L13): WeakSobolev.IsTestFunction (C_c^infinity(R^d; R)), WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient f g (int f d_v phi = -int <g, v> phi for every test function phi and direction v) and WeakSobolev.MemH1 (f in L^2 with a weak gradient in L^2); the gradient of a smooth function is the classical field VariationalFloor.grad. The approximation is in the graph norm: norm(phi_n - f)_2 -> 0 and norm(grad phi_n - g)_2 -> 0, which is convergence in the TeX's H^1 norm.
  • H1TestDense d is the predicate (its body is fixed for the consumers of wave L7); h1TestDense d proves it for every d, including d = 0, which is more than the manuscript's d = 1, 2, 3. exists_test_approx is the eps form and h1TestDense_of_memH1 the MemH1 form.
  • hasWeakGradient_of_tendsto is the converse (an L^2 graph limit of test functions has the limit gradient as weak gradient), so the weak-gradient H^1 is the closure of C_c^infinity in the graph norm. The manuscript does not state it; it is used by the refutation DropWeakGradient.
  • Lean proof route (different from the TeX in order and in the mollification step). (1) Mollify first: mollify phi u = rho_phi * u with the normalized bump rho_phi = phi.normed volume; the L^2 contraction eLpNorm_mollify_le (Cauchy-Schwarz against the probability weight, then Tonelli and translation invariance) and the density of continuous compactly supported functions in L^2 give rho_n * u -> u in L^2 when the bump radii tend to 0 (tendsto_mollify), where the TeX invokes L^2 translation continuity; the weak-gradient identity tested against y -> rho_phi(x - y) gives grad(rho_phi * f) = rho_phi * g (grad_mollify). (2) Then cut off the smooth function h = rho * f with chi_n(x) = chi(x/(n+1)), chi = 1 on the closed unit ball and 0 outside the ball of radius 2; the classical product rule (grad_cutoff_mul), dominated convergence (tendsto_cutoff_smul) and norm(h grad chi_n)_2 <= C norm(h)_2/(n+1) (norm_grad_cutoff_le) give tendsto_cutoff_test. This is the cutoff estimate of TeX lines 352-355 with R = n + 1, applied after mollification to a smooth function, so no weak product rule is needed. (3) An eps/2 argument and eps = 1/(k+1) give the sequence. The mollifiers are VariationalFloor.bumpN (so mollify (VariationalFloor.bumpN d n) f is VariationalFloor.moll f n by definition, for real f).
  • Not formalized: the separability remark of the same proof (lines 356-358), and the "common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e." of lines 360-361 (the density gives L^2 convergence only; an a.e.-convergent subsequence is a separate step for the consumer).
  • Junk values: none relied on. In the density statements f and g are in L^2, so the integrals in HasWeakGradient against test functions are genuine; all norms are eLpNorm values in [0, infinity].

Refutations (refutations/h1-density/): DropMemLpF (drop f in L^2: the constant 1 in d = 1, weak gradient 0, is not an L^2 limit of test functions), DropWeakGradient (drop the weak-gradient hypothesis: f = 0, g = prof e_0 in d = 1, via hasWeakGradient_of_tendsto and WeakSobolev.weakGradient_ae_unique), NotTestFunction (every H^1 function a test function: the indicator of the origin in d = 1), and ContractionConstant (the contraction with constant 1/2, refuted at u = VariationalFloor.prof in d = 1 by tendsto_mollify). No junk-value reliance. Lemmas labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve only the Lean proofs and are not TeX steps.

H1Mathlib (foundation: the weak-gradient H^1 identified with Mathlib's Bessel-potential space H^{1,2}, the norm conventions and density)

Wave L13 item K5a (the D8-lite foundation), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/H1Mathlib.lean. It carries no manuscript label of its own; it identifies the package's weak-gradient space WeakSobolev.MemH1 (the manuscript's H^1(R^d; R), "the real Sobolev space of square-integrable functions with square-integrable first weak derivatives", main TeX notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, lines 748-750) with Mathlib's Bessel-potential space H^{1,2}(R^d; C) (MemSobolev 1 2, BesselPotentialSpace), and is used by ResolventForm and the class-O bridge of wave L14. Every hypothesis is stated; nothing is supplied and no hypothesis is added.

  • toL2C, toDistr: a real f in L^2 as an element of L^2(R^d; C) and as the tempered distribution T_f(chi) = int chi f; testSchwartz: a real test function as a Schwartz function.
  • lineDeriv_toDistr: an L^2 weak gradient g of f is its distributional gradient, d_v T_f = T_<g, v>.
  • memH1_iff_memSobolev: for real f in L^2, MemH1 f iff MemSobolev 1 2 (toDistr hf); both directions are proved, so the plan's fallback input H1Converse is not needed.
  • Norm conventions. Mathlib's Fourier transform uses e^(-2 pi i <x, xi>), so its H^1 norm is \|f\|_2^2 + (2 pi)^(-2) \|grad f\|_2^2 (norm_sq_of_besselPotential_eq, norm_toH1_sq for the bundled element toH1 h). The manuscript's norm is \|f\|_2^2 + \|grad f\|_2^2 (no 2 pi; notes/integrated_signed_static.tex, proof of P:signed-closed-form, line 85: q_V = z^2 - b^2 - v_V(u,u) with z = \|u\|_(H^1), b = \|u\|_2), defined here as manuscriptH1NormSq; by wave-L13 decision 5 manuscript constants use it, never the Bessel-potential norm. The two are equivalent with constants 1 and (2 pi)^2 (norm_toH1_sq_le_manuscript).
  • Density: real test functions converge to every real H^1 profile in Mathlib's H^1 norm (exists_test_tendsto_toH1; the density sentence of the proof of P:spatial-four-linear, notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex lines 352-356, in Mathlib's space), and Schwartz functions are dense in H^s(R^d) for every real s and complex-valued elements (exists_schwartz_tendsto; the "Fourier cutoffs give its density in H^1" of notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex line 177, in Schwartz form).
  • h1_identification_paper collects the identification, the two norm statements and the density for a real square-integrable f, the only hypothesis (needed to form toDistr hf).

Lean route: the weak-gradient identity is extended from test functions to smooth functions with h, grad h in L^2 by the cutoffs of H1Density (weak_smooth), then to complex Schwartz functions through real and imaginary parts (weak_schwartz); the forward direction writes J^1 T_f = J^(-1) T_f + sum_j R_j(xi_j T_f) with bounded multipliers (besSym_one_eq, besselPotential_one_eq); the converse reads off L^2 components of d_(e_j) T_f from MemSobolev.lineDerivOp (weak_coord_of_eq); the norm identity is Plancherel after F W = <xi> F f and F(d_j f) = 2 pi i xi_j F f almost everywhere (ae_eq_of_smulLeft). Not formalized: density of complex-valued C_c^infinity in the complex H^1(R^d) (only real profiles; for complex elements only Schwartz density), the separability remark of P:spatial-four-linear (lines 356-358), a gradient map on the bundled complex space (not constructed in this module; see ResolventForm.gradOp); the restatement of P:spatial-four-linear on Mathlib's H^1 is not part of this item.

Refutations (refutations/h1-mathlib/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Manuscript-claim perturbations in the manuscript domain (a): NonSquareIntegrable (dropping f in L^2 from the definition of H^1: f = 1 on R has the weak gradient 0 in L^2 but is not square integrable) and WrongTwoPi (Mathlib's H^1 norm is not the manuscript's \|f\|_2^2 + \|grad f\|_2^2: d = 1, the test function cutoff 0, whose gradient energy is positive, integral_norm_grad_sq_pos). Lean-route-only control (b): DroppedWeakGradient (the norm identity of norm_toH1_sq for an L^2 field g that is not a weak gradient fails: g = grad f and g = 0 give different right sides).

HermiteFock (foundation: the finite Gaussian Fock layer)

A foundation with no manuscript label of its own; everything is proved and nothing is supplied. It is the finite Gaussian Fock layer used in notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a (main TeX): the Fock half of the proof of L:fock-form (lines 3016-3027), the Fock sentences of the proof of L:interval-contractions (lines 3460-3464), the phase insertion on a color in its vacuum (lines 3394-3397 and 3447-3449), and the Hermite step of E:occupied-multiplication (lines 2192-2197). The TeX cites Janson (lines 2954-2955) for the creation and annihilation algebra; this module proves what is used.

Model (decision 5 of wave L9). The Gaussian L^2 space with values in a complex inner product space X is represented by coefficient vectors (Fin m -> N) -> X, indexed by multi-indices, restricted to total degree at most N (degLE m N; Supp N v says v vanishes above degree N). The expansion iota N v (x) = sum_(|k| <= N) h_k(x) v_k in the normalized Hermite functions of GaussianHermite links the two pictures: it is an isometry into L^2(stdPi m; X) (integral_norm_sq_iota; stdPi m is the law of m independent standard Gaussians), multiplication by x_i is a_i^* + a_i on coefficients (coord_smul_iota), and sum_i x_i H_i is the field operator fieldOp H (sum_coord_smul_iota). No tensor-product inner product is used: the "other Hilbert factor" of the TeX is X itself, and the spatial operators H_i are continuous linear maps of X. The TeX rotates H/||H|| to a first coordinate (line 2192); the general column form with operators H_i makes that step unnecessary. Convention: Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first slot, whereas the TeX's is linear in the first slot (line 3374); every adjoint identity stated here survives the conjugation, and the norm-square and real-part identities are unchanged.

Formalized. The annihilation and creation operators (a_i v)_k = sqrt(k_i+1) v_(k+e_i), (a_i^* v)_k = sqrt(k_i) v_(k-e_i), the number identity sum_i a_i^* a_i = |k|, and the finite adjoint identity between a_i and a_i^*. The creation row from degrees <= N to degrees <= N+1 has norm at most sqrt(N+1) (creRow_bound), attained on u_i = a_i w for w of exact degree N+1 (creRow_attained). For symmetric H_1, ..., H_m with the column bound sum_i ||H_i u||^2 <= c ||u||^2, c >= 0 (hypotheses of these lemmas, not manuscript inputs here), the field operator sum_i (a_i^* + a_i) (x) H_i maps degrees <= N to degrees <= N+1 with norm at most 2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(c) (fieldOp_bound), the same after truncation to degrees <= N (fieldOp_bound_trunc), the truncated operator is symmetric (fieldOp_symm_trunc), and both bounds hold in Gaussian L^2 with integrability (gaussian_field_bound, gaussian_field_bound_trunc). Vacuum insertion: E||sum_i g_i w_i||^2 = sum_i ||w_i||^2 (vacuum_insertion_isometry).

Route difference. The TeX bounds the annihilation part as the adjoint of the creation part (line 3023); Lean uses the same adjoint relation through the finite identity sum_inner_ann and Cauchy-Schwarz. Its annihilation theorem maps input degrees <= N+1 to output degrees <= N with squared norm at most (N+1) c; the TeX's sqrt(n) (lines 2193-2196) concerns input degrees <= n, so the two operator domains are indexed differently, and the Fock proof says "the same bound after truncation" (lines 3023-3024). Applied to an input already supported through N, the N+1-to-N theorem leaves an unused degree of slack. The constant 4(N+1)c of the sum does not need the sharper value.

Junk values. The truncated subtraction k - e_i occurs only multiplied by sqrt(k_i), which vanishes exactly when it truncates; c >= 0 is a hypothesis where it is used; every integral conclusion includes integrability. Coefficient vectors are arbitrary functions; only their values in degrees <= N (or <= N+1) enter the stated sums.

Not formalized here: the full Gaussian L^2 space, infinitely many coordinates, the closed polynomial spaces and unbounded number operators.

Refutations (refutations/hermite-fock/): CreRowConstant (the constant N in place of N+1 in creRow_bound fails at the vacuum), NumberOrder (|k| + 1 in place of |k| in number_identity) and VacuumSquareOfSum ((sum_i ||w_i||)^2 in place of sum_i ||w_i||^2 in vacuum_insertion_isometry).

Formalized, nothing supplied. F3w_eq (spherical coordinates, lines 6134-6138: F_3(w) = ((1+rho)^v - abs(1-rho)^v)/(2 v rho) for alpha < 2, w != 0, by PhaseContractions.sphere_convolution with Archimedes' law from L9Completed.archimedesLaw_holds); F3w_zero (F_3(0) = 1); F3w_le (F_3(w) <= 2^(1-alpha)/(2-alpha) for 1 < alpha < 2 and every w) and F3w_unit (equality for norm(w) = 1); riesz_three_unsmoothed, M3_pos; higher_riesz_three (H:spatial-maximum in d = 3 with delta = alpha - 1 and M = M_3 for c > 0, 1 < alpha < 2); higher_riesz_three_optimal (M_3 <= M for every M with H:spatial-maximum, lines 6186-6189: Fatou at a shift norm(z) = 1, h = 1, eta = 0, eps_n = 1/(n+1), with HigherRieszTwo.approx_identity; the point y = -z is G_1^(3)-null); higher_riesz_three_full (both, for the lemma's own range 1 < alpha < 2, without H:homog); the wrappers higher_riesz_three_paper and higher_riesz_paper with the manuscript's hypotheses: H:homog for Gamma = gamma dx (HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 (volume.withDensity (riesz c alpha)) mu), d in {2,3}, c > 0, 1 < alpha, and alpha < 3/2 when d = 2; conclusion H:spatial-maximum with delta = alpha - 1 and M = M_d, and in d = 3 the optimality of M_3.

Hypotheses. In d = 3, H:homog is used only for alpha < 2 (from alpha0 > 0 and alpha0 + alpha < 2, the section's alpha < 2 - alpha0); in d = 2 it is carried, unused, and of 1 < alpha only 0 < alpha is used. The d = 3 clause uses 1 < alpha (in HigherRieszTwo.F3_max).

Differences from the TeX (route; statements unchanged). The maximum of the closed form is HigherRieszTwo.F3_max (a chord bound), not the TeX's monotonicity on each side of rho = 1; the value at w = 0 is computed directly (F_3(0) = 1) and compared through 2^(1-alpha) >= 2 - alpha (two_sub_le_rpow) instead of by continuity of the closed form; the Gaussian averaging is HigherRieszTwo.smoothed_average_le.

Narrowings inherited and unchanged. H:spatial-maximum is stated for a covariance with a density (HigherRieszTwo.SpatialMaximum; for this lemma the covariance is the density c norm(x)^(-alpha) itself, so the lemma's statement is not narrowed). The d = 3 Green measure is the recorded definitional choice of WaveGreen ((s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere, Le's decision 4 of wave L6), not identified with Hausdorff surface measure. All integrals in the statements are lower integrals; the real-valued display is HigherRieszTwo.SpatialMaximum.real_form.

Not formalized: C:higher-riesz (it needs P:higher-transfer, not formalized). Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Refutations (refutations/higher-riesz-three/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Controls outside the manuscript domain: DroppedAlphaGtOne (the bound fails at alpha = 1/2) and DroppedAlphaLtTwo (M_3 > 0 fails at alpha = 3).

Registered model choice: M1 (the d = 3 wave Green measure via volume.toSphere; its identification with surface measure is not proved; see Scope), used only in the steps shared with d = 3.

L:higher-riesz (Riesz spatial maxima) of notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/HigherRieszTwo.lean: the dimension-two clause in full and the proof steps shared with dimension three (statement lines 6103-6112, proof lines 6114-6190), and Hypothesis H:spatial-maximum (lines 5919-5929, display E:higher-convolution at lines 5922-5925) with the section's notation (lines 5912-5917). The dimension-three clause and the whole lemma are in HigherRieszThree (its own section), which reuses these steps unchanged.

Objects. gamma(x) = c norm(x)^(-alpha) is riesz c alpha, an [0, infinity]-valued function (value 0 at x = 0 for alpha > 0, Lean's 0^(-alpha) = 0; the point is null for every measure gamma is integrated against: Lebesgue measure, the absolutely continuous G_h^(1) and G_h^(2), and the atomless sphere measure G_h^(3) (M1; the scaling G_h(hA) = h G_1(A) carries the null singleton)). gamma_eps = p_eps * gamma is smoothCov g eps and G_{h,eta} = p_eta * G_h (G_{h,0} = G_h) is smoothGreen nu eta, both through lower Lebesgue integrals, with p_eps = VariationalMean.heatK eps (covariance eps I, line 5915); pairing is int G_{h,eta}(dy) gamma_eps(y + z). G_h is WaveGreen.waveGreen d h. M_2 is M2 c alpha; F3 v rho is the closed form ((1+rho)^v - abs(1-rho)^v)/(2 v rho) of lines 6136-6138 as a function of v = 2 - alpha and rho = norm(w) (value 0 at rho = 0, never used).

H:spatial-maximum is SpatialMaximum d g delta M: M > 0 and int G_{h,eta}(dy) gamma_eps(y + z) <= M h^(-delta) for every h > 0, z, eps > 0, eta >= 0, for G_h = waveGreen d h and a covariance with density g. NARROWER than the TeX's hypothesis in one respect: the TeX's gamma is the covariance of H:homog (in general a measure, lines 5554-5557); here it must have a density. This is no narrowing of L:higher-riesz, whose covariance c norm(x)^(-alpha) dx has a density. The lower bound 0 <= of E:higher-convolution is automatic for the lower integral, and the upper bound forces finiteness; SpatialMaximum.real_form gives the display as written (real-valued, with integrability) for a measurable density. smoothGreen and smoothCov are defined independently of LowAlphaConvolution.smoothedGreen, LowAlphaConvolution.gammaEps and VariationalDilation.conv (same objects mathematically; no bridge lemma is stated).

Formalized, nothing supplied. Step (a) ball_mass_two (G_1^(2)(B(w,R)) <= 2R^(3/2) for every w, 0 < R <= 1/4); step (b) layer_cake_le (for any measure of mass at most one with that ball bound) and F2_le (F_2(w) <= M_2/c, uniform in w); step (c) unsmoothed_scaling (int G_h(dy) gamma(y + z) = c h^(1-alpha) F_d(z/h), d = 1, 2, 3); step (d) average_le and smoothed_average_le (a bound uniform in the shift passes to both Gaussian widths, any d, any s-finite measure); riesz_two_unsmoothed, M2_pos, higher_riesz_two (the dimension-two clause for 0 < alpha < 3/2) and its wrapper higher_riesz_two_paper (H:homog for Gamma = volume.withDensity (riesz c alpha) in d = 2, c > 0, 1 < alpha < 3/2); step (e) F3_max (for 1 < alpha < 2 the closed form is maximal at rho = 1 with value 2^(1-alpha)/(2-alpha)); step (f) approx_identity (for norm(y)^(-lambda) on R^j, 0 < lambda < j, x != 0: each p_eps * f(x) is a genuine integral and tends to f(x)).

Hypotheses. higher_riesz_two_paper carries H:homog unused, and of 1 < alpha it uses only 0 < alpha (higher_riesz_two states the clause for 0 < alpha < 3/2). H:homog contains alpha0 + alpha < 2, the section's alpha < 2 - alpha0 (lines 5912-5913).

Differences from the TeX (route; statements unchanged). (a) A reflection instead of a rotation; for centers norm(w) < 1/2 the density bound 1/pi (mass <= R^2) instead of 2/(pi sqrt 7) (mass <= 2R^2/sqrt 7), both <= 2R^(3/2) (ball_mass_small, a route lemma); the slice integral by its closed form. (b) The layer cake in the level t instead of the radius R = t^(-1/alpha). (d) Two successive Tonelli averages instead of p_eps * p_eta = p_{eps+eta} (the display of lines 6173-6176 is not stated). (e) A chord bound (convexity of (1+rho)^v - (1-rho)^v on [0,1], subadditivity of t^v for rho >= 1); the TeX's monotonicity of F_3 on each side of rho = 1 is not stated, only the maximum. (f) A split at norm(y) = 2 norm(x) and Mathlib's peak-function theorem instead of the TeX's three regions.

Not in this module: the identity F_3(w) = F3 (2-alpha) norm(w), the dimension-three clause and the optimality of M_3 (all in HigherRieszThree); P:higher-transfer and C:higher-riesz, which use H:spatial-maximum, are not formalized. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)"; the route definitions dens2, e0 and coordSwap have no rows.

Refutations (refutations/higher-riesz-two/), classified; none relies on a junk value of Lean's totalized arithmetic. Manuscript-domain perturbations (wrong statements inside the lemma's hypotheses): MaxAtZero (the maximum of the closed form is not its limiting value 1 at rho -> 0; alpha = 3/2) and WrongMaxValue (the value 2^(1-alpha)/(2-alpha) without its factor 1/2 is wrong at alpha = 3/2). Controls outside the manuscript domain (they show that a hypothesis is needed, with a witness that violates it): DroppedAlphaRange (M_2 > 0 fails at alpha = 2) and DroppedCPositive (M_2 > 0 fails at c = 0). Lean-route-only control: DroppedVLessOne (the chord bound of the route lemma F3_num_le needs v < 1).

HomogHypothesis (whole result)

States Hypothesis H:homog (main TeX file, Section S:model) in full as the predicate HomogCovariance, and restates E:kappa and E:driver-parameters under it. The manuscript's Fourier convention Gamma = int e^(i xi.x) mu(d xi) is written out explicitly rather than through Mathlib's Fourier transform. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on R^d a locally finite Borel measure is a Radon measure. The proofs of the two restated results use only the numerical part of the hypothesis.
