OccupationKernelRow (whole result)

Formalizes two lemmas of the section S:spatial-occupation-foundation (notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex at 39f2597a): L:occupation-kernel-row (lines 477-495) with the kernel E:occupation-damped-kernel (lines 465-472) and the display E:occupation-kernel-row (lines 481-484), and L:spatial-physical-pair (lines 13-34) with E:spatial-physical-pair (lines 16-18). Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. Kstar is the manuscript's formula word for word, with K_star(0) = 0 (line 472) and Gamma_E read as Mathlib's Real.Gamma. Kstar_eq_Psi identifies it, for u != 0, with the averaged clock kernel TimeFractional.Psi a |u| (|u|/D) (main file, E:averaged-clock-kernel, line 8982), and positivity and the bound K_star(u) <= |u|^(-a) are reused from TimeFractional. kstarIntegrand_integrable proves that the defining integral converges for a > 0, D > 0, u != 0. It is a separate theorem, not a conjunct of the headline. The headline occupation_kernel_row (for 0 < a < 1, D > 0) proves exactly nine conjuncts: evenness; positivity off zero; local integrability; strict decrease on (0,inf) (the TeX says "decreasing", which this implies); K_star(u) <= |u|^(-a) off zero; interval integrability of each row t -> K_star(s-t), s in [0,1], on [0,1]; that R_star = 2 int_0^(1/2) K_star is the greatest element of the set of row values over s in [0,1] (so the maximum exists, equals R_star and is attained at s = 1/2); interval integrability of K_star on [0,1/2]; and 0 < R_star (a real number, hence finite). occupation_kernel_row_paper states this under the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: H:homog as HomogCovariance d alpha a Gamma mu with a = alpha0, Gamma != 0, D = (4 - alpha) - 2a). D > 0 and a < 1 are derived from H:homog (a + alpha < 2, a < 1); Gamma != 0 and the other clauses of H:homog are carried and not used. The TeX proof shows the row bound Phi(s) + Phi(1-s) <= 2 Phi(1/2) by concavity of Phi. Lean proves it instead by a shift comparison that uses the same monotonicity of K_star (Phi_sum_le_of_le_half, auxiliary). For L:spatial-physical-pair, pairMeasure Gamma = volume.prod Gamma on R^d x R^d (EuclideanSpace), and pairing is the lower Lebesgue integral of f(x) h(x-y) for [0,inf]-valued f, h. This allows arbitrary [0,inf]-valued functions, a class that contains the TeX's finite Borel representatives. spatial_physical_pair assumes only that Gamma is locally finite, for any d, and proves four conjuncts: sigma-finiteness of nu; representative independence under Lebesgue-a.e. changes of f and h; nu-a.e. measurability of f(x) h(x-y) for Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable f, h (the TeX's "measurable in the nu completion"); and the transfer of Lebesgue-a.e. convergence of real sequences F n -> G (indexed by N) to nu-a.e. convergence at x and at x - y. ae_pair_of_ae is the null-set transfer of the proof (lines 27-30), for an arbitrary a.e. property. spatial_physical_pair_paper states it under HomogCovariance and Gamma != 0; only local finiteness of Gamma is used. The sentence "Signed pairings will be used only after absolute convergence" (lines 32-33) is a usage convention, not a claim, and is not formalized. The real-valued kernel-integral conclusions include integrability; the physical pairing remains an extended nonnegative integral and need not be finite.

OccupationPhysicalClass (narrower result: P:occupation-physical-class over the modelled class O; the bridge and the whole result over O itself are in ClassOBridge, wave L14)

Formalizes P:occupation-physical-class (The full physical occupation class, notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex at 39f2597a): the class O and T(g) defined just before it (lines 497-500), the statement (lines 503-521) with J(g) (lines 507-510) and the displays E:occupation-physical-bound (lines 512-514) and E:occupation-own-energy (lines 516-520), and the proof (lines 523-575), under the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: a nonzero covariance satisfying H:homog, a = alpha0, q = 4 - alpha, D = q - 2a). The wrapper occupation_physical_class_paper takes HomogCovariance d alpha a Gamma mu, Gamma != 0, D = (4 - alpha) - 2a and the named input SquarePairingBounds Gamma alpha R_0 (R_0 is SpatialSmoothRatio.R0), discharged in SpatialOccupationL7Completed. The H:homog clauses it uses directly are Gamma_radon (local finiteness), alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one, threshold, scaling, and through SpatialSmoothRatio.homog_consequences (0 < alpha < 2) also dim and alpha_range; R_0 >= 0 is taken from SpatialSmoothRatio.spatial_smooth_ratio_R0_paper, which uses H:homog and Gamma != 0 (through it, also spectral, mu_radon and mu_tempered). Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef and mu_even are carried but unused (the completed form in SpatialOccupationL7Completed also uses Gamma_even, through SquarePairingBounds). Gamma != 0 is also used for positivity. mu enters only through H:homog.

Objects. B_Gamma(f^2, h^2) is sqPair, i.e. OccupationKernelRow.pairing (the extended nonnegative integral of E:spatial-physical-pair) at the squares, so the pairings in Lean are the physical integrals by definition, and A_sp(f) = sqPair Gamma f f. b(f) (line 36) is gradSqE gf, the extended integral of the squared norm of a weak gradient gf of f; for gf in L^2 it is the real integral (gradSqE_eq), and by Tlin_unique T(g) does not depend on which L^2 weak gradient is chosen. T(g) and J(g) are defined as extended integrals (Tlin, Jlin, "positive Tonelli is valid before finiteness is known", line 558) with real values T, J; Jlin integrates first in t, then in s, and occupation_physical_bound identifies its value with the Bochner integral over (0,1)^2. E_star^O is EstarO, the sSup of energySet; the set is proved nonempty and bounded above, so EstarO is not Lean's junk value. spEnergyVal alpha R is the right side of E:spatial-energy-map (lines 414-419) with R_sp replaced by a real R.

Modelling of O (narrower than the TeX, recorded). The TeX's fields are strongly H^1(R^d;R)-measurable maps on (0,1); this module has no H^1-valued type (wave L14 adds one, ClassOH1.H1R). IsOccField G DG asks instead for a.e.-strongly measurable joint representatives (s,x) -> g_s(x) and (s,x) -> grad g_s(x) on (0,1) x R^d (Lebesgue), a unit H^1 pair IsUnitH1 (G s) (DG s) at a.e. time, and T(g) < infinity. The TeX proof (lines 535-540) builds such joint representatives from strong measurability; that construction and the converse (joint representatives give a strongly H^1-measurable field) are not formalized in this module. So O, energySet and E_star^O here are over fields given by joint representatives; the two classes are identified in wave L14 (ClassOBridge.exists_joint, exists_aesm_of_joint, isOccField_of_classO, classO_of_isOccField), which restates the proposition over O itself.

Named input (no stronger than its source), discharged in SpatialOccupationL7Completed: SquarePairingBounds Gamma alpha R, two conclusions of P:spatial-four-linear (lines 297-315) for real f, h in L^2 with L^2 weak gradients: E:spatial-homogeneous-bound A_sp(f) <= R N(f)^4, read in [0,inf], and E:spatial-square-CS in the equivalent squared form B_Gamma(f^2,h^2)^2 <= A_sp(f) A_sp(h) in [0,inf] (squareCS_of_sqrt converts the real square-root form). The wrapper takes R = R_0, the constant of E:spatial-homogeneous-bound. This input is discharged in SpatialOccupationL7Completed by squarePairingBounds_holds (from SpatialFourLinear.squarePairingBounds_paper with the density of H1Density), and occupation_physical_class_completed_paper there states the result without it. The TeX writes R_sp in E:occupation-physical-bound; R_sp = R_0 is the last claim of P:spatial-four-linear, and the TeX proof uses E:spatial-homogeneous-bound, which carries R_0. This module states the bound with R_0 and does not use R_sp; SpatialOccupationL7Completed.occupation_physical_class_Esp_paper states both displays with R_sp and E_sp. The upper bound of E:occupation-own-energy is stated with spEnergyVal alpha R_0; its identification with E_sp is E:spatial-energy-map at R_sp = R_0 (P:spatial-energy-map, formalized in SpatialFourLinear), which this module does not use or assume.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: the measurability above; T(g) and J(g) as extended integrals (their finiteness and the Bochner forms are conclusions); 0 < a < 1, D > 0, 0 < alpha < 2 in the general forms (derived from H:homog in the wrapper); the general forms also assume a locally finite Gamma (not needed for Jlin_le), and the energy forms the scaling VariationalDilation.SetScaling alpha Gamma and Gamma != 0, used only for positivity. R >= 0 is arbitrary in the general forms.

Proof route. As in the TeX for the bound (lines 551-559): B_Gamma(g_s^2, g_t^2) <= R_0 F(s) F(t) with F(s) = b(g_s)^(alpha/4), then 2 F(s) F(t) <= F(s)^2 + F(t)^2, the row bound E:occupation-kernel-row and its column form by evenness, and Tonelli. Differences: measurability (lines 533-545) is proved by Tonelli on the joint representative and representative independence, without the continuity of the pairing map on H^1 x H^1; the concavity step int_0^1 b^(alpha/2) <= T^(alpha/2) is proved by Holder (lintegral_rpow_le); positivity (lines 567-572) uses the lower bound J >= K_star(1) l^alpha A_sp(g) (K_star decreasing, Kstar_one_le) with an explicit l instead of the exact value J_0 l^alpha A_sp(g), so J_0 and its finiteness are not formalized. The scalar maximum (lines 564-566) is scalar_max, proved by weighted AM-GM rather than differentiation.

Not formalized in this module: the remark on zero covariance (lines 577-582, outside the proposition) and the construction of joint representatives (lines 535-540), both in ClassOBridge (wave L14; the remark except the reduction to the free moment model); the commentary of lines 572-574 (no attaining profile asserted; no point trace used), which makes no claim.

Refutations (refutations/occupation-physical-class/): ScalarConstant (the constant of scalar_max halved, at alpha = c = T = 1), ScalarExponent (the exponent 2/(2-alpha) of c dropped, at alpha = 1, c = 4, T = 16), AlphaTwo (scalar_max at alpha = 2, where (2-alpha)/2 = 0; Lean reads 2/(2-alpha) as 0 there, but the vanishing factor decides the outcome), JensenExponent (lintegral_rpow_le with p < 1 dropped, at p = 2) and KstarDiagonal (Kstar_one_le with t != s dropped; uses the manuscript's K_star(0) = 0, not a junk value). Junk values: J and T are toReal of extended integrals, finite on IsOccField fields (proved); EstarO is an sSup of a set proved nonempty and bounded above; Nnorm uses Bochner integrals but enters only through SquarePairingBounds, whose clauses assume L^2 membership. The headline statements do not rely on a junk value.

OrderTwoDiagrams (narrower results: L:white-test and the order-two part E:riesz-two of P:riesz-small, every value proved for the diagram integrals of the registered model M4 (DiagramModel); the identification of the diagrams with the chaos moments E X_1^2, E X_2 of the solution, which is not constructed, rests on the named input MixedMoment (P:mixed), and the Riesz wrapper of this section also on RieszDiagramLimit (proved in RieszFourDiagrams); the order-four part of P:riesz-small is in RieszFourDiagrams)

Wave L13 item D4, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/OrderTwoDiagrams.lean: the order-two closed forms of the two-chain diagram integrals in d = 1, main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a. The objects are those of DiagramModel (registered model choice M4, see Scope): diagram G gamma alpha0 m n D t is J_(m,n,D)(t) of E:mixed-diagram for a covariance density, diagramLim d Gamma alpha0 m n D t the TeX's J for a covariance measure (the limit as eps -> 0+ of the diagrams with p_eps * Gamma), coeffA, coeffALim the total-order coefficients A_k(t).

  1. L:white-test (statement lines 940-949, display E:white-test, proof lines 951-964). On the model, with nothing supplied: for spatial white noise in d = 1 (Gamma = delta_0, diagramLim), alpha0 < 1 and t >= 0, every pairing gives J_(1,1,D)(t) = c_0 t^(3-alpha0) (white_cross) and J_(2,0,D)(t) = J_(0,2,D)(t) = c_0 t^(3-alpha0)/2 (white_self_two_zero, white_self_zero_two), and A_1(t) = 2 c_0 t^(3-alpha0) (white_coeffALim_one). The eps -> 0+ limits are WhiteCollapse.tendsto_diagram_white (wave L13 item D6), specialized here by tendsto_white_self and tendsto_white_cross; the collapsed spatial parts follow the TeX's proof (whiteSpatial_cross: int G_s G_r = min(s,r)/2; whiteSpatial_self: G_r has mass r, G_(s-r)(0) = 1/2), and the time integrals are Beta integrals (time_white_cross, time_white_self). About the chaos terms: white_test_paper states E X_1^2 = c_0 t^(3-alpha0), E X_2 = c_0 t^(3-alpha0)/2 and sum_(m=0)^2 E[X_m X_(2-m)] = 2 c_0 t^(3-alpha0) (the total-order-two contribution to E:full-second) with the named input MixedMoment and X_0 = 1.
  2. P:riesz-small, order two (statement lines 5125-5142, display E:riesz-two, proof lines 5174-5193). On the model, with nothing supplied: for gamma(y) = c\|y\|^(-alpha) in d = 1, c >= 0, alpha < 1, alpha0 < 1, t >= 0, the density diagrams satisfy both displays of E:riesz-two (riesz_self_two_zero, riesz_self_zero_two, riesz_cross) and A_1(t) = J_(1,1) + 2 J_(2,0) (riesz_coeffA_one, "their total is E X_1^2 + 2 E X_2", line 5142). The route is the TeX's: the spatial parts c h_0 h_1^(1-alpha)/(1-alpha) (spatial_riesz_self) and K(h_0, h_1) (spatial_riesz_cross, rK), then "integrate on s > r and double, set v = s - r, and integrate r over (0, t-v)" (time_riesz_cross, the bracket rbr) and two elementary integrations (time_riesz_self). About the chaos terms: riesz_small_paper states the two displays for E X_2, E X_1^2 and the total with the named inputs MixedMoment and RieszDiagramLimit; its successor RieszFourDiagrams.riesz_small_paper' needs MixedMoment only.

Named inputs. DiagramModel.MixedMoment d alpha0 Gamma P X u t (both wrappers): the statement of P:mixed (main lines 834-849): every diagram limit exists and is finite, E[X_m X_n] = sum_D J_(m,n,D)(t) with the products integrable, u^2 integrable and E u^2 = sum_k A_k(t); true for the solution under H:homog, not proved (the solution and its chaos terms are not constructed). RieszDiagramLimit c alpha alpha0 t (riesz_small_paper only; defined here): at total order two, the model's diagramLim for the measure Gamma(dy) = c\|y\|^(-alpha) dy equals the density diagram (the regularization convention of lines 825-832 and L:joint-fixed-order, lines 1853-1966); true, and proved in RieszFourDiagrams.rieszDiagramLimit for c >= 0, 0 <= alpha < 1, 0 <= alpha0 < 1, t >= 0.

Class and what is missing. Both results are narrower by the split modelled-object rule: every value is a theorem about the diagram integrals of M4 (whole on the model), and the identification of those integrals with E X_1(t,x)^2, E X_2(t,x) and the contribution to E:full-second of the solution is the named input MixedMoment about arbitrary random variables X, u. The order-four part of P:riesz-small (E:riesz-four, its finiteness, and the sentence on the multiplicities of E:total-four) is not in this module; see RieszFourDiagrams. P:nogo-04 (the a -> 1 limit 2^(2-alpha)(1-alpha)) does not exist at a284420 and is not formalized.

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. The diagram values need only alpha0 < 1, alpha < 1, c >= 0, t >= 0, which is broader than the TeX's 0 < alpha0, 0 < alpha, c > 0 (alpha0 = 0 is the static case the TeX uses at line 5119). white_test_paper takes H:homog for d = alpha = 1, Gamma = delta_0 and uses only alpha0 < 1 from it; riesz_small_paper carries H:homog, 0 < alpha and 0 < alpha0 unused and uses c > 0 only as c >= 0. X_0 = 1 is the TeX's convention (line 796), a hypothesis here because X is arbitrary. Each pair is evaluated once at its opener (gamma(y_j - y_h), j < h; gamma is even here); the time domain is the model's open simplices; the Riesz density at 0 is Lean's 0^(-alpha) = 0 for alpha > 0 (one for alpha = 0), and the time weight \|0\|^(-alpha0) is infinity for alpha0 > 0 (one for alpha0 = 0, zero for alpha0 < 0) (null sets). Junk values: c0 alpha0 is Lean's 0 at alpha0 = 1; every statement assumes alpha0 < 1.

Refutations (refutations/order-two-diagrams/), classified. Manuscript-claim perturbations in the manuscript domain: WhiteCrossDoubled (the (1,1) white diagram is not 2 c_0 t^(3-alpha0), at alpha0 = 1/2, t = 1) and RieszStaticDenominator (the static denominators (1-alpha)(2-alpha) (3-alpha)(4-alpha) kept at alpha0 > 0 fail for J_(2,0,D) at c = 1, alpha = alpha0 = 1/2, t = 1: 1/3 against 16/105). Lean-route-only control: WhiteSelfZeroIncrement (the hypothesis h_1 > 0 of the auxiliary whiteSpatial_self is needed: at h = (1, 0) the collapsed part is 0, not 1/2; domain: increments with h_1 = 0, a null set the TeX never uses). Control of Lean's totalized arithmetic outside the manuscript domain: ZeroDenominatorJunk (c0 1 = 0 in Lean; domain alpha0 = 1, excluded by H:homog).

PhaseBessel (whole result)

Formalizes L:phase-bessel (Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality) of S:wave-variance (notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex at 39f2597a: statement lines 426-435 with the display E:phase-bessel at lines 430-433, proof lines 437-449). The lemma cites no labels, and the section's standing assumptions (lines 5-8: H:homog, a = alpha0, the range of gamma) are not used by it and are not carried. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The general theorem phase_bessel holds for any measure space (X, mu) (no sigma-finiteness), any complete complex inner product space H (no separability) and any finite index types iota (the family index k) and J (the vector index j; the TeX has J = {1,2}); phase_bessel_paper states the TeX's hypotheses exactly: X = R^d (EuclideanSpace R (Fin d)) with Lebesgue measure volume, J = Fin 2, a family indexed by Fin K, and H separable. The spaces L^2(R^d; C^2) and L^2(R^d; H^2) are encoded componentwise: each u k j and each g j is MemLp 2 (this includes the measurability the TeX leaves implicit), and orthonormality is the integral identity int sum_j u k j(eta) conj(u l j(eta)) d eta = delta_kl (IsOrthonormalL2), which is the TeX's L^2(C^2) inner product. Convention remark: Mathlib's inner product inner C x y is conjugate-linear in the FIRST slot, while the TeX's <u_k, u_l> = int sum_j u_kj conj(u_lj) is linear in the first slot. Orthonormality is stated as the explicit integral above, so no Mathlib inner product on L^2 enters the hypothesis, and the inequality (a statement about norms) does not depend on the convention. The integral in IsOrthonormalL2 cannot be a junk 0, since its integrand is integrable for L^2 components (integrable_mul_of_memLp). The TeX's "The Bochner integrals exist" is part of the conclusion: integrability of every coefficient integrand eta -> sum_j u k j(eta) g j(eta) and of eta -> sum_j ||g j(eta)||^2. Carried but unused: separability of H (_hsep in phase_bessel_paper). Proof route (differs from the TeX): the TeX expands g in a countable orthonormal basis of H (this is where it uses separability), applies scalar Bessel coefficientwise and sums with Parseval and Tonelli. Lean runs the projection argument that the TeX uses for scalar Bessel directly in H: with x_k = coeff mu u g k and phi_j(eta) = sum_k conj(u k j(eta)) x_k, 0 <= int sum_j ||g_j - phi_j||^2 = int sum_j ||g_j||^2 - 2S + S, S = sum_k ||x_k||^2 (residual_expand), so no basis, Parseval or separability is needed. The conjugated version follows because the componentwise conjugate family is orthonormal (isOrthonormalL2_conj). No conclusion is narrower than the TeX's. L:phase-bessel is applied to P:wave-two-variances in WaveTwoVariances (input_fixed, output_fixed). Not formalized: the rest of S:wave-variance (see "Not in Lean"). Rows labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve only this route.

PhaseContractions (whole result)

Registered model choice: M1 (the d = 3 wave Green measure via volume.toSphere; its identification with surface measure is not proved; see Scope).

L:phase-contractions (Two static contraction bounds) of notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/PhaseContractions.lean: statement at lines 2509-2523 (displays E:phase-resolvent, E:phase-trace and the definition of T_eps), proof at lines 2525-2586, the standing assumptions of Section S:static-phase at lines 2490-2493 and the constants of E:phase-constants at lines 2494-2506.

Objects. PhaseCovariance alpha Gamma mu is the section's class (0 < alpha < 2; Gamma nonnegative, even, positive definite, tempered, locally finite on R^3 with Gamma(cA) = c^(3-alpha) Gamma(A); mu its spectral measure in the convention Gamma = int e^(i xi.x) mu(dxi), locally finite, even, tempered as in H:homog); PhaseCovariance.of_homog shows that H:homog in d = 3 implies it (the TeX: "any member of the original three-dimensional class", lines 2481-2482). R_alpha is SpectralMassIdentity.ralpha (V = mu(B_1), open ball, line 2503); M, c_Gamma, b_alpha, D_Gamma are massM, cGam, bAlpha, dGam (dGam_eq: the expression of the hDdef hypotheses of IntervalScalar). p_v is pdens v (covariance v I, a probability density by integral_pdens), Gamma_eps = p_(2eps) * Gamma is gammaEps (not LowAlphaConvolution.gammaEps, which is p_eps * Gamma, the gamma_eps of L:low-alpha-convolution; each module follows its section's notation), G_a is WaveGreen.waveGreen 3 a (the recorded toSphere definitional choice, Le's decision 4), G_a hat is WaveKernel.waveHat a, and T_eps(a,q) = int e^(i <q,x>) Gamma_eps(x) G_a(dx) is traceT.

Formalized. phase_contractions_paper: the lemma under PhaseCovariance and the two named inputs below: E:phase-resolvent with integrability; for every x, the integrability of y -> p_(2eps)(x - y) against Gamma and Gamma_eps(x) >= 0; the integrability of both integrands of T_eps; the identity T_eps(a,q) = int G_a hat(q+xi) e^(-eps norm(xi)^2) mu(dxi); and abs(T_eps(a,q)) <= D_Gamma a^(1-alpha). General forms with fewer hypotheses: phase_resolvent (every d; also R_Gamma(lambda) = lambda^(alpha-2) R_alpha at q = 0), phase_trace (no spectral measure, no Fourier input; also T_eps(a,0) = int Gamma_eps dG_a and abs(T_eps(a,q)) <= T_eps(a,0)) and traceT_fourier; and the proof steps gauss_shift_le, lintegral_norm_radial, measure_singleton_zero, lintegral_waveGreen_three, integral_normal_coordinate, sphere_convolution, middle_region_le, three_regions, kernel_le_bAlpha, lintegral_gammaEps_le and gammaEps_fourier. After wave L9 both named inputs are discharged: L9Completed.phase_contractions_paper_completed states the lemma under PhaseCovariance alone and L9Completed.phase_contractions_homog_completed under H:homog in d = 3 (section L9Completed).

Named inputs (definitions of type Prop, both proved in wave L9 and discharged in L9Completed). - WaveFourierThree: int e^(i <xi,x>) G_s(dx) = waveHat s xi for s > 0, xi in R^3: the d = 3 case of G_s hat(xi) = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi) (lines 983-984), which the TeX uses as G_a hat at lines 2520 and 2555-2556; no stronger. Used only for the Fourier form of T_eps. Proved by WaveGreenFourier.waveGreen_fourier_three. - ArchimedesLaw: for every unit e in R^3, the image of volume.toSphere under omega -> <e,omega> is 2 pi Lebesgue measure on [-1,1]: the classical fact behind "direct integration over its normal coordinate" (lines 2573-2574) and the radiality of G_a * p_(2eps) (line 2566); it concerns only the sphere measure. Used only for the bound E:phase-trace. Proved by WaveGreenFourier.archimedes.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: in the principal statements under the tempered, locally finite class (phase_resolvent, phase_trace, traceT_fourier, phase_contractions_paper and the L9Completed wrappers) the integrability of every integrand is a conclusion, so none of them holds through the junk value of a non-integrable Bochner integral. Three auxiliary statements are statements about Lean integrals without an integrability conclusion: gauss_shift_le (the Gaussian pairing inequality under the bare predicate IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu, which is an equality of totalized integrals and does not by itself force temperedness or local finiteness), gammaEps_fourier (the Fourier identity for Gamma_eps, same predicate) and gammaEps_nonneg (nonnegativity for any Gamma); they are used only inside the principal statements, where the integrability is proved; mu(B_1), Gamma(B_1) finite (local finiteness), so R_alpha and D_Gamma use no junk toReal; 2 - alpha > 0 and sin(pi alpha/2) > 0; Borel sets in the scaling. No Gamma != 0 is assumed (for Gamma = 0 both bounds hold with value 0). Hypotheses carried but unused (checked through every called lemma, as recorded in the module): Gamma_even, Gamma_posdef, mu_even.

Differences from the TeX (route; the statements are the TeX's). - Gaussian pairing (lines 2534-2542): both sides are written by MaskedSpectralGrowth.masked_gaussian_transform and the shifted one is bounded by its absolute value (abs(e^(i q.x)) = 1, Gamma >= 0), so evenness is not needed for the realness used by the TeX. - The value at q = 0 is SpectralMassIdentity.resolvent_eq_ralpha (layer cake and a Beta integral) instead of the polar formula; mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A) is MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_scaling. - The radial law (lines 2558-2565) is proved for nonnegative measurable radial functions, not only Schwartz ones; the same lemma for Lebesgue measure (beta = 3) gives c_Gamma. All Fubini steps are nonnegative (lower integrals); the radial form of G_a * p_(2eps) comes from Archimedes' law. Instead of evaluating [p_(2eps) * (G_a * norm(.)^(-alpha))](0) the proof bounds int p_(2eps)(z) (G_a * norm(.)^(-alpha))(-z) dz by the supremum. - The three regions (lines 2580-2584) are closed (r <= a/2, r >= 2a, a/2 <= r <= 2a), so no continuity argument is needed; the outer bounds use the TeX's distance bounds a/2 and a (kernel_le_of_dist).

Narrower conclusions: none relative to the TeX statement. Not formalized: the operator A_lambda and the phase-pair norms that follow the lemma (line 2587 on). The definition pprof (the Gaussian profile u -> (2 pi v)^(-d/2) e^(-u/(2v))) only names a route object and has no row. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Controls (refutations/phase-contractions/): (a) manuscript-claim perturbations in the manuscript's domain: MiddleRegionExponent (the power a^(2-alpha) in place of a^(1-alpha) in the middle region; a = r = 1/4, alpha = 1) and NormalCoordinateConstant (an extra factor 1/2 in the normal-coordinate integral; a = r = alpha = 1); (c) a control of a broader Lean generalization outside the manuscript's domain: ShiftInvariance refutes equality in gauss_shift_le, which Lean states for any pair with IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu, at d = 1, Gamma Lebesgue measure, mu = delta_0. Lebesgue measure has homogeneity exponent alpha = 0, outside the class of S:static-phase (d = 3, 0 < alpha < 2, lines 2490-2493), so it is not a counterexample under the manuscript's standing class. The in-domain control is refutations/phase-contractions/ShiftInvarianceInDomain (wave L13, item C5, section PhaseShiftControl), a class (a) refutation for every PhaseCovariance with mu != 0. No control is of type (b), and none relies on a junk value.

PhaseShiftControl (foundation: an in-domain control for the Gaussian pairing step of L:phase-contractions)

Wave L13 item C5, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/PhaseShiftControl.lean. It formalizes no labelled result and changes no coverage row. It upgrades the control of the proof step PhaseContractions.gauss_shift_le (the Gaussian Fourier pairing int e^(-s\|q+xi\|^2) mu(dxi) <= int e^(-s\|xi\|^2) mu(dxi) in the proof of L:phase-contractions, main TeX notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, lemma lines 2509-2523, pairing display lines 2534-2542; standing assumptions of S:static-phase lines 2490-2493) from a control outside the manuscript domain (class (c), refutations/phase-contractions/ShiftInvariance.lean) to one inside it (class (a), ShiftInvarianceInDomain.lean): for every covariance of the class of S:static-phase with mu != 0, the comparison is not an equality for every shift q.

  • not_gauss_shift_invariant (general form): for a nonzero, locally finite, tempered mu on R^d with mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A) (SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha), alpha < d, and s > 0, the map q -> int e^(-s\|q+xi\|^2) mu(dxi) is not constant. Route (no manuscript counterpart; the TeX has no such statement): if it were constant, its average against e^(-t\|q\|^2) dq would grow like t^(-d/2) as t -> 0, while Tonelli and the weight comparison weight_le bound it by (2 pi/s)^(d/2) (t/2)^(-alpha/2) int e^(-\|xi\|^2) mu(dxi) (homogeneity of the Gaussian mu-masses, integral_gauss_homog); since alpha < d this forces the value at 0 to vanish, contradicting mu != 0.
  • not_gauss_shift_invariant_phase and exists_gauss_shift_lt_phase: the same for every PhaseContractions.PhaseCovariance alpha Gamma mu (d = 3, 0 < alpha < 2, the scaling of Gamma, mu its tempered spectral measure) with mu != 0 and s > 0, and the comparison of gauss_shift_le is strict at some nonzero q. Fields of PhaseCovariance used: alpha_lt_two, the local finiteness and temperedness of mu, the spectral convention and the scaling; carried, unused: alpha > 0, the local finiteness, evenness, temperedness and positive-definiteness of Gamma and the evenness of mu. The hypothesis mu != 0 is added and necessary: phaseCovariance_zero shows that the zero pair lies in the class, and for it the shifted Gaussian masses all vanish.

The refutations quantify over the in-domain covariances; the existence of a nonzero member of the class (for example a Riesz pair) is not formalized in this module. Nothing is supplied. All declarations are controls or auxiliary to the Lean proof route and carry no manuscript label.

Refutations (refutations/phase-contractions/ShiftInvarianceInDomain.lean), class (a), manuscript-claim perturbations in the manuscript domain (every PhaseCovariance with mu != 0, every s > 0): shift invariance F(q) = F(0) for all q, shift invariance at every nonzero q, and the reversed comparison F(0) <= F(q) for all q, where F(q) = int e^(-s\|q+xi\|^2) mu(dxi); each with a _contrast partner (the package inequality, its strictness at a nonzero shift, and the zero pair satisfying all three variants). No junk value is involved (mu tempered makes the Gaussian integrals integrable and F(0) > 0).

QuotientObstruction (narrower result: covariance-functional obstruction; noise W not constructed, identification with noise variances not formalized)

Formalizes P:masked-quotient-obstruction (A physical mask need not preserve noise-null tests) of S:masked-covariance (notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 339-345, proof lines 347-382) in full, with nothing supplied. The wrapper masked_quotient_obstruction_paper takes exactly the manuscript's hypotheses: d = 2, alpha = 1, 0 < a < 1 (the section's a = alpha0), Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2 (Gamma0) and the section's T > 0. It concludes that Gamma0 with mu0 = (2 pi)^(-1) dxi_1 delta_0(dxi_2) satisfies H:homog (HomogCovariance 2 1 a Gamma0 mu0, lines 353-357), that Gamma0 != 0 (the section's standing assumption, lines 7-8, holds for this Gamma), and that some real C^infinity compactly supported mask zeta on R^2 admits no real C with covW a Gamma0 (zeta F) <= C covW a Gamma0 F for every test F with IsTest T F. masked_quotient_obstruction states the proof's computation with the explicit witnesses zeta = chi(x_1) chi(x_2), g = chi(x_1) chi''(x_2) (gtest) and a bump tau supported in (0,T) (the proof chooses tau nonnegative and nonzero; the exported existential records IsTest (tau g), temporal integrability and positive timeQ, not these properties of tau separately): the test F = tau g, the integrability of every integrand it evaluates, V(g) = 0, V(zeta g) = J_chi I_chi^2, covW(F) = 0 and covW(zeta F) = norm(tau)_a^2 J_chi I_chi^2 > 0.

Definitional boundary (D1). The noise W is not constructed. E W(F)^2 is read as the covariance functional of E:cov (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, lines 378-381): covW a Gamma F = int_t int_s |t-s|^(-a) int Gamma(dz) int F(t,x) F(s,x-z) dx, iterated Lean Bochner integrals with time over R (equal to [0,T]^2 for the tests used). Because a Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0, the values 0 and > 0 of the witnesses come with integrability conclusions (time integrand on R x R, spatial integrands for every z and against Gamma0), so they are genuine.

Abstractions. "Compact smooth test F" (line 344) is IsTest T F: (t,x) -> F t x is C^infinity with compact support and vanishes unless t in (0,T). This restricts the tests, so the nonexistence of C is stronger than over all compact smooth tests. C ranges over all reals. Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2 is lineMeasure e2, the pushforward of Lebesgue measure under t -> t e_2; the plane R^2 is EuclideanSpace R (Fin 2) with coordinates through the volume-preserving plane : R x R -> R^2. chi is Mathlib's ContDiffBump with radii 1 and 2 (equal to 1 on [-1,1], 0 outside (-2,2)); the TeX's explicit formula (lines 366-369) is introduced "for example", and evenness of chi and J_chi >= 2 are not used.

Proof-route differences. V(g) (lines 359-361) is identified with the spatial covariance (lines 357-358, "by ordinary Fubini") for every real continuous compactly supported g through the substitution x = y + t e_2 and Fubini on R x R^2 (autocorr_e2, auxiliary, under a product decay bound PlaneDecay). Positive definiteness of Gamma (line 355) is proved directly, int Gamma(dz) (phi * phi~)(z) = int |int phi(u,v) dv|^2 du, not through the spectral measure. The spectral identity (lines 353-354, "Fourier inversion on Schwartz tests") is proved by one-dimensional Fourier inversion (Integrable.fourierInv_fourier_eq) for the marginal Phi(u) = int phi(u,v) dv, whose Fourier transform is the restriction of the two-dimensional Fourier transform of phi to the first axis; the Schwartz decay of that restriction gives the integrability inversion needs. The remaining fields of H:homog (Radon, even, tempered with k = 2, scaling Gamma(cA) = c Gamma(A) for every set A) come from the line-measure lemmas. Positivity of norm(tau)_a^2 (lines 377-379) uses TimeSchur.time_schur_paper for integrability and a product of two intervals on which the integrand is positive.

Hypotheses carried but unused: none of the wrapper's (0 < a is used by TimeSchur.time_schur_paper and by HomogCovariance). The general lemmas state their own hypotheses: isEven_lineMeasure holds for every v, the other line-measure lemmas need norm(v) = 1; covW_tensor needs no integrability.

Not formalized: the noise W and its test-noise completion (D1); the claim "This is not spatial white noise in dimension two" (line 357) is not a theorem of the module (the refutation refutations/quotient-obstruction/WhiteNoise.lean shows Gamma0 != volume).

The definitions plane, e1, e2, wt and chiBump only name objects of the proof route and have no rows of their own.

RadiusMeanAnchor (narrower result: P:radius-mean-anchor for abstract random paths; the operator paths M_R(Y_m) and the residual noises not constructed, their identification not formalized; moment inputs supplied)

Formalizes P:radius-mean-anchor (notes/integrated_radius_anchor.tex at ba01d98): the mean bound E:radius-mean-anchor with integrability of Z_delta, the margin e_anchor = (1-a)/2 - d/Q > 0 for every dimension d, the decay bound E:radius-mean-anchor-decay for R_delta = delta^(-1) + 2, and the limit of that bound as delta -> 0+. The proof steps are checked separately: stopping a path and extending it constantly does not increase its supremum or Holder seminorm, the scaling by g_delta, Lyapunov's inequality for a probability measure, linearity of the finite block sum, N >= 1 and N + 1 <= 2/(delta B), R_delta <= 3/delta and the radius substitution. C^theta([0,B];E) is represented explicitly, following the manuscript's definition (notes/integrated_actual_operator_driver.tex, "the supremum norm plus the theta-Holder seminorm"). supNorm is the real supremum of ||f t|| over [0,B], holderSemi is the real supremum of ||f t - f s|| / |t - s|^theta over s != t in [0,B], holderNorm is their sum, and IsCHolder (membership in C^theta) says both sets are bounded above. Mathlib's HolderWith is a predicate about a constant on the whole domain, not a norm on [0,B], so it was not used. A real sSup of an unbounded set is 0 in Lean, so holderNorm is meaningful only for paths with IsCHolder. The supplied input requires this almost surely for M_m, and stopped_isCHolder gives it for the stopped paths. Paths are functions R -> E into a real normed space; only their values on [0,B] enter. The stochastic objects W, Y_m, M_R and the deterministic projection are abstracted to an arbitrary family of random paths M m : Omega -> R -> E, so the bounds are uniform in the projection, as the proposition states. The only manuscript input is the moment bound of C:radius-covariance-residuals (with C = 1, v = p; it rests on P:radius-actual-moments). It is a hypothesis on the unstopped paths M_m = M_R(Y_m): almost surely IsCHolder, the pth power of the C^theta norm is integrable, and (E ||M_m||_{C^theta}^p)^(1/p) <= C sqrt(p) R^(d/Q). Taking the input on M_m rather than on X_m means the stopping and the factor g_delta are proved in Lean. Implicit hypotheses made explicit: mu is a probability measure, and hXmeas says omega -> ||X_m(omega)||_{C^theta} is AE-strongly measurable. The full Holder space is not separable, so this is not automatic; for the manuscript's paths it follows from the construction (the transferred paths are strongly measurable in a separable closed span, integrated_source_convergence.tex, and stopping, scaling and the norm are continuous), so hXmeas is a consequence of the manuscript's construction supplied as a hypothesis, not a gap in the argument. The constant C >= 0 is derived from the input, not assumed. radius_mean_anchor_paper states the proposition with exactly the manuscript's hypotheses: H:homog in its parameter part, E:radius-anchor-parameters, E:radius-anchor-Q with Q even and Q >= 2, integer B >= 1, 0 < delta < min(1, 1/B), N and ell_m from S:actual-cameron-mean, p >= 1 and R >= 1. The hypotheses carried but unused are d in {1,2,3}, 0 < a, the conditions on alpha, gamma, eta_t, beta_t, evenness of Q, Q gamma > d and beta_t - eta_t - 1/Q > 0. The general theorems need only a < 1, 0 < Q, 0 <= theta, 0 <= delta, p >= 1 and 0 <= ell_m. Not formalized: the moment bound itself (C:radius-covariance-residuals, P:radius-actual-moments) and the construction of the operator path M_R and of the residual noises Y_m.

RawOccupationEnergy (narrower result: P:raw-occupation-energy over the modelled class O; the bridge and the whole result over O itself are in ClassOBridge, wave L14)

Wave L9, item A1, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/RawOccupationEnergy.lean. It formalizes P:raw-occupation-energy (Original occupation energy and dilation; notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 111-131, proof lines 133-177) with the objects of E:raw-occupation-definitions (lines 10-18), and nothing is supplied. Standing assumptions of the section (lines 4-21): the original covariance under H:homog (HomogCovariance d alpha a Gamma mu, written with a for alpha0), the ORIGINAL kernel K(s,t) = |s-t|^(-a) on I = (0,1) (TimeSchur.kern a (s - t); its diagonal value is Lean's 0^(-a), on a null set, as the TeX allows), and Gamma != 0 (line 20). Objects reused, not redefined: the class O is OccupationPhysicalClass.IsOccField (joint representatives, wave L7), B_Gamma(f^2,h^2) is OccupationPhysicalClass.sqPair, T(g) is OccupationPhysicalClass.T (the real value of the extended Tlin), K_0 = 2^a/(1-a) is OccupationCeilingFinite.K0, D_zeta is SpatialBracket.Dzeta, R_sp is SpatialFourLinear.Rsp. New: Araw/A (A(g), extended and real values), ratioSet and Cocc (C_occ), energySet and EO (E_zeta^O), and the dilation dilField/dilGrad (U_l, line 157). raw_occupation_energy_paper has exactly the section's hypotheses and proves every claim of the proposition: 0 < C_occ <= K_0 R_sp with the ratio set nonempty and bounded above (hence finite); for every field of O: 0 < T(g), A(g) < inf and 0 <= A(g) <= K_0 R_sp T(g)^(alpha/2) (E:raw-occupation-bound), U_l g in O, A(U_l g) = l^alpha A(g), T(U_l g) = l^2 T(g) and U_(1/l) U_l = id; for every zeta > 0: the energy value set is nonempty and bounded above, E:raw-occupation-energy, E:raw-occupation-ratio, E_zeta^O > 0 and E_zeta^O = zeta^(-alpha/(2-alpha)) E_1^O. No input is supplied: SquarePairingBounds Gamma alpha R_0 (two conclusions of P:spatial-four-linear) is SpatialOccupationL7Completed.squarePairingBounds_holds, R_sp = R_0 is spatial_ratio_H1_paper_completed, and SetScaling alpha Gamma is the field scaling of H:homog; the general forms (raw_occupation_energy, raw_occupation_bound, Araw_le, exists_pos_member) take SquarePairingBounds Gamma alpha R with R >= 0 and give R in place of R_sp. Implicit hypotheses made explicit: A(g) and T(g) are extended integrals; the finiteness of A(g) is a conclusion, while T(g) < infinity is part of the membership in O (the field energy_lt_top of IsOccField, as T(g) < infinity in the TeX's definition of O) and its real integral representation is a conclusion; C_occ and E_zeta^O are sSups whose sets are proved nonempty and bounded above, so neither is Lean's junk value; T(g) > 0 on O (needs d >= 1, from H:homog), so no ratio is a division by zero; the dilation lemmas take an s-finite Gamma (automatic for the locally finite Gamma of H:homog). Proof route: as in the TeX (lines 141-175), except that the spatial bound B_Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) <= R b_s^(alpha/4) b_t^(alpha/4) enters as <= (R/2)(b_s^(alpha/2) + b_t^(alpha/2)) (OccupationPhysicalClass.sqPair_le_half) followed by the sharp row bound int_0^1 |s-t|^(-a) dt <= K_0 in both variables (same constant K_0 R); positivity uses |s-t|^(-a) >= 1 on (0,1)^2, so A(g) >= A_sp(g) > 0 for a constant-in-time unit test; the dilation identity is an identity of extended integrals for ALL real functions (sqPair_dil), so the TeX's approximation step to full H^1 (line 166) is not needed; the scalar maximum is weighted AM-GM (scalar_max_zeta) with the attained value scalar_attain_zeta; the lower bound in E:raw-occupation-energy dilates members whose ratios approach C_occ to the scalar optimizer. Recorded representation: the class O is modelled by joint representatives (IsOccField: a.e.-strongly measurable (s,x) -> g_s(x) and (s,x) -> grad g_s(x), a unit H^1 pair at a.e. time, T(g) < inf), as for P:occupation-physical-class (wave L7). These describe the same a.e. data as the TeX's strongly H^1-measurable occupations (notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex lines 497-499; the TeX constructs such representatives at lines 533-540), so this is not a smaller mathematical class; the bridge between the two descriptions is not formalized in this module, so here C_occ and E_zeta^O are the suprema over the modelled class; wave L14 proves the bridge and the equality of the suprema over O itself (ClassOBridge.CoccO_eq, EOO_eq). The direct zero case Gamma = 0 (lines 379-385) is not formalized here (in part in ClassOBridge.zero_covariance_paper). Both hypotheses of raw_occupation_energy_paper are used (Gamma != 0 through squarePairingBounds_holds and the positivity witness).

Controls (refutations/raw-occupation-energy/): (a) manuscript-claim perturbations of the scalar maximum, in the manuscript's domain: EnergyExponent (the exponent 1/(2-alpha) in place of 2/(2-alpha); alpha = 1, zeta = 1/2) and ScalarConstantHalved (D_zeta halved; alpha = 1, zeta = 1/2); (c) a control of Lean's totalized arithmetic: PenaltyPositive (zeta >= 0 in place of zeta > 0) is false in Lean only through the value D_0 = 0 produced by 1/0 = 0; the TeX does not define D_0, so this witness is outside the manuscript's domain. No control is of type (b).

RayleighTail (narrower result: L:tube-rayleigh-tail, application to the operator moment not formalized)

Formalizes L:tube-rayleigh-tail (notes/integrated_gaussian_tubes.tex): the bound, with integrability of the tail integrand, and the remark that the integral over [0, M] is finite. "Borel" is measurability, G is defined on the reals with the growth bound assumed for r >= 0 (the domain used in the section). The general theorems assume only delta > 0; the section fixes 0 < delta < 1, and rayleigh_tail_paper states the lemma with exactly the manuscript's hypotheses, including delta < 1. The lemma's "In particular" application to the coarse-envelope bound of another proposition is not formalized.

RemoveMask (narrower result: P:variational-remove-mask for Rayleigh-form rates and integral-form costs, their identification not formalized; the point display for a real function in place of the canonical solution's moment, over a supplied input)

Formalizes P:variational-remove-mask (Monotone rates and the original point moment) of notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex at 39f2597a (statement lines 227-238, display E:variational-unmasked-point-lower lines 234-237, proof lines 240-302). The section's standing assumption (line 4) is a nonzero covariance satisfying H:homog with a = alpha0; the wrappers carry HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu, Gamma != 0 and Psi in C_pos (VariationalDilation.CPos), with I = [0,1]. Reused: the mean h_(Psi,s) (VariationalDilation.mean), v_Psi in the integral form of E:compact-raw-cost (rawCost), the rate lambda_(Psi,s) (VariationalDilation.rate, the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum E:variational-real-rayleigh) and I_Psi (integratedRate), the Rayleigh sets of WeakSobolev, the dilation floor of VariationalFloor, VariationalMean.global_mean and VariationalRate.unmasked_rate. New: the profile chi(r) = smoothTransition(2 - r), equal to the TeX's F(2-r)/(F(2-r) + F(r-1)) with F = expNegInvGlue (chi_eq, expNegInvGlue_eq, lines 248-251); the masks m_R(x) = chi(|x|/R); the masked mean m_R h_s; the masked rate lambda_(R,s), DEFINED as the square root of the supremum of the real Rayleigh values of m_R h_s (the convention of rate); int_I lambda_(R,s) ds; and the named input RawBlockOriginalLower.

The rate part is proved with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied (variational_remove_mask_rates_paper): the masks form an increasing family of admissible radial masks tending to one (mask_family, lines 250-257), a common margin eps <= lambda_(R,s)^2 <= M for R >= R_0 (lines 270-271), lambda_(R,s) <= lambda_(R',s) <= lambda_(Psi,s) for 0 < R <= R', a Lipschitz bound in s, the exchange of suprema (lines 277-283), pointwise and uniform convergence on I (lines 284-288), and int_I lambda_(R,s) ds nondecreasing, at most I_Psi and tending to I_Psi (line 289). The display E:variational-unmasked-point-lower is proved over one supplied input (variational_remove_mask_paper): RawBlockOriginalLower alpha0 Gamma Psi (rawCost alpha0 Gamma Psi) L, for all sufficiently large R, 2 int_I lambda_(R,s) ds - v_Psi/2 <= liminf_(T -> infinity) L(T) in EReal, where L(T) stands for T^(-kappa) log E|u(T,x)|^2 at a fixed x. It is E:raw-block-original-lower of P:raw-block-original-lower (notes/integrated_raw_block_lower.tex lines 739-747) applied with the mask m_R (eligible there: even, [0,1]-valued, one on B_R, supported in the closed ball of radius 2R, lines 7-8, once R exceeds the radius of P:compact-original-common-trial), as the proof does (integrated_unmasked_variational.tex lines 295-298). It is asserted only for large R and one fixed x, so it is no stronger than its source, but it is read through two identifications the TeX makes and Lean does not formalize: the compact ground rate of m_R h_s is the Rayleigh rate maskedRate (lines 272-273), and v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2 is rawCost (L:compact-raw-profile). The canonical solution u and its moment are not defined in Lean, so the display relates the same function L that the input bounds.

Narrower than the TeX: the rates are the Rayleigh rates; the compact ground statements (P:compact-ground-family applied to m_R h_s) and their identification with the Rayleigh form are not formalized (foundation D8), as for lambda_(Psi,s) in VariationalRate. Implicit hypotheses made explicit: I = [0,1], "uniformly on I" is TendstoUniformlyOn on [0,1], finiteness of the suprema is stated as nonempty bounded-above value sets, integrability of lambda_(R,.) on (0,1) is a conclusion. The general forms remove_mask and unmasked_point_lower do not take HomogCovariance; the wrappers give them Gamma_tempered, mu_tempered, spectral, Gamma_radon, scaling, alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one and alpha < 2 (from threshold and alpha0_pos), so the other fields of HomogCovariance (dim, Gamma_even, Gamma_posdef, mu_radon, mu_even, alpha_range) are carried and not used. Proof routes that differ from the TeX: the common margin uses the test function of VariationalFloor.dilation_floor (the route of VariationalRate.unmasked_rate), supported in a ball of radius R_1, with R_0 = R_1 + 1, instead of the trial of P:compact-original-common-trial; the exchange of suprema is proved as convergence of the suprema as R -> infinity (dominated convergence for each fixed trial, tendsto_sSup_rayleighSet); uniform convergence is Mathlib's Dini theorem applied to R -> lambda_(max(R,R_0),s) instead of the finite subcover along R_n = R_0 + n; and int_I lambda_(R,s) ds -> I_Psi is dominated convergence with the bound sqrt M, not a consequence of the uniform convergence. Junk values: for R <= 0, m_R is identically one (Lean's division and sign); maskedRate is a square root of an sSup, used only where the value set is proved nonempty and bounded above (R >= R_0 or 0 < R, s in [0,1]); maskedIntegratedRate is a Bochner integral, used only for R >= R_0 or eventually; the liminf is taken in EReal, so it is never a junk value. Rows marked "auxiliary to the Lean proof route" have no manuscript label.

ResolventForm (narrower result: P:signed-closed-form, the form bounds E:signed-form-bounds and the bounded resolvent of the form for an abstract bounded pairing P on Mathlib's H^1, with E:signed-multiplier-form supplied as SignedMultiplierForm and the Hermitian pairing supplied; not formalized: the self-adjoint operator H_V itself, D(A^(1/2)) = H^1 (E:signed-form-domain), E:signed-quarter-phase, the dual completion H^(-1/2), the commutation with real conjugation and L:signed-limiting-multiplier)

Wave L13 item K5b, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/ResolventForm.lean, on Mathlib's Bessel-potential space H^1(R^d) as consumed from H1Mathlib (wave L13 item K5a). A narrower result: P:signed-closed-form is formalized in part (item 3), with inputs supplied (coverage row P:signed-closed-form, inputs-supplied, weaker, added after the wave-L13/L14 reviews); no labelled result is formalized whole here. Anchors at 39f2597a, all in notes/integrated_signed_static.tex: L:signed-limiting-multiplier (lines 11-19, display E:signed-multiplier-form lines 16-18), P:signed-closed-form (statement lines 49-67, proof lines 69-130) and the sentence of the proof of L:signed-spectral-wave on real and complex diagonals (line 164).

  1. Complex Lax-Milgram over any RCLike field (IsCoerciveSesq.equiv, a port of Mathlib's real IsCoercive.continuousLinearEquivOfBilin to sesquilinear forms, conjugate-linear in the first slot as Mathlib's inner product), and the resolvent R = iota S of a coercive Hermitian form relative to a bounded iota : V -> L (solOp, formResolvent): the weak equation and its uniqueness, self-adjointness, positivity, \|R\| <= 1 when \|iota u\|^2 <= re B(u,u), injectivity when (range iota)^perp = 0. Nothing supplied.
  2. On H^1(R^d): the embedding iota = embL2 and the gradient components d_j = gradOp j as Fourier multipliers, their identification with f and its weak gradient on real profiles (embL2_toH1, gradOp_toH1), the dense range of iota (embL2_sep), the manuscript norm z^2 = \|u\|_2^2 + sum_j \|d_j u\|_2^2 (msNormSq, no 2 pi; wave L13 decision 5: manuscript constants are never stated in Mathlib's norm) with \|u\|^2 <= z^2 <= (2 pi)^2 \|u\|^2, the manuscript H^(1/2) norm (h12NormSq, the convention of integrated_compact_gaussian.tex line 277) and the Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz step \|u\|_(H^(1/2))^2 <= b z of the proof (line 80). Nothing supplied.
  3. P:signed-closed-form, the form and resolvent part (signed_closed_form_resolvent_paper). The pairing v_V(u,w) is <P u, w> for an abstract bounded operator P on H^1; the limiting multiplier V of L:signed-limiting-multiplier is not constructed. Two inputs are supplied: SignedMultiplierForm P k (named; the bound E:signed-multiplier-form, TRUE for the manuscript's V by L:signed-limiting-multiplier, which is not formalized) and the self-adjointness of P (the Hermitian pairing of that lemma's proof, lines 36-39). Conclusions: E:signed-form-bounds with c = 2 + K^2, L_K = 3(1 + K^2) (signed_form_bounds also gives the proof's sharper lower bound z^2/2 + (1 + K^2/2) b^2), the form version b^2 <= q_V(u) + c b^2 of A >= 1, and the bounded resolvent R_V = (H_V + c)^(-1) of the form: self-adjoint, positive, injective, \|R_V\| <= 1, given by the unique weak solution. Not formalized: the self-adjoint operator H_V itself (it is defined only by its resolvent; no LinearPMap), the uniqueness of the represented operator, A >= 1 and D(A^(1/2)) = H^1 as operator statements (E:signed-form-domain), E:signed-quarter-phase, the negative dual completion H^(-1/2), the commutation with real conjugation (proof, line 128), and L:signed-limiting-multiplier. A bounded measurable real potential V satisfies E:signed-multiplier-form with k = sup \|V\| (potOp_signedMultiplierForm), a special case, not the manuscript's distributional V.
  4. The real/complex reduction of L:signed-spectral-wave (line 164): for a Hermitian form with a real cross term the diagonal at x + i y is the sum of the two real diagonals (re_diag_split), and for the shifted form on real profiles (re_formOp_split, the real cross term proved for bounded real potentials by im_potOp_toH1). The decomposition of a general complex H^1 element into real profiles is not formalized, so the equality of the real and complex form infima is not concluded.

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. No hypothesis of a wrapper is carried unused: signed_closed_form_resolvent_paper uses the self-adjointness of P for the Hermitian form, E:signed-multiplier-form for the bounds, and K >= max(1, k). The constant k is any constant of the bound (the TeX's k = \|L\|). Mathlib's complex inner product is conjugate-linear in the first slot; the forms here follow it. No registered model choice is used: H^1 is Mathlib's space (its relation to the weak-gradient H^1 of WeakSobolev is H1Mathlib). Junk values: none relied on.

Refutations (refutations/resolvent-form/), classified. Manuscript-domain perturbation: WrongFormNorm (the manuscript norm z^2 of a real H^1 profile equals Mathlib's \|toH1 f\|^2; fails for the d = 1 test function cutoff 0, whose gradient term Mathlib weights by (2 pi)^(-2)). Lean-route controls: NoCoercivity (a Hermitian form with nonnegative diagonal has a surjective Riesz map; fails for B = 0 on C), DroppedLowerBound (\|R\| <= 1 without \|iota u\|^2 <= re B(u,u); R = 4 for B = <.,.>, iota = 2 on C) and NoDenseRange (injectivity of R without dense range; iota = 0). Broader Lean generalization outside the manuscript domain: ComplexCrossTerm (the diagonal splits for arbitrary x, y; fails for x = 1, y = i in C, where B(x,y) is not real).

RieszFourDiagrams (narrower result: P:riesz-small: E:riesz-four with its finiteness, the five splits and the three pairings proved for the density diagrams of the registered model M4 (DiagramModel) with nothing supplied; the order-two displays about E X_1^2, E X_2 through the named input MixedMoment (P:mixed), the solution not being constructed; the sentence that the total coefficient uses the multiplicities of E:total-four not formalized)

Wave L13 item D4 (follow-up), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/RieszFourDiagrams.lean: the Riesz diagrams in d = 1, the order-two diagram limit and the order-four unit-domain representation. Main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, P:riesz-small (statement lines 5125-5172, proof lines 5174-5220); the objects are those of DiagramModel (registered model choice M4) and of OrderTwoDiagrams (RieszDiagramLimit, rbr, riesz_small_paper).

  1. The order-two diagram limit. rieszDiagramLimit proves the former named input OrderTwoDiagrams.RieszDiagramLimit for c >= 0, 0 <= alpha < 1, 0 <= alpha0 < 1, t >= 0 (tendsto_riesz_two: the diagrams with gamma_eps = p_eps * Gamma, Gamma(dy) = c\|y\|^(-alpha) dy, converge to the density diagram at total order two), so that the model's measure-form diagramLim is the density diagram there (the regularization convention, main lines 825-832). Lean route, not the TeX's pointwise one: gamma_eps(x) = int p_eps(z) gamma(x - z) dz, so the smoothed spatial part is a Gaussian average over shifts of the spatial part with gamma(. - z), which is continuous in z and bounded by sup_u int c\|u - y\|^(-alpha) G_h(dy) <= c(2h)^(1-alpha)/(1-alpha) (rq_le); the time integrals converge by dominated convergence with the integrable time weight (tendsto_diagram_of_spatial, lintegral_twoSimplex_timeWeight_ne_top). riesz_small_paper' is OrderTwoDiagrams.riesz_small_paper with that input discharged: with the proposition's hypotheses and the named input MixedMoment alone, E X_2 and E X_1^2 are the two displays of E:riesz-two and sum_(m=0)^2 E[X_m X_(2-m)] = E X_1^2 + 2 E X_2.
  2. The order-four representation E:riesz-four (lines 5144-5171, proof 5199-5219), on the model's density diagrams diagram (waveGreen 1) (riesz c alpha) (the TeX's J for the density gamma(y) = c\|y\|^(-alpha)), with nothing supplied. diagram_riesz_eq proves, for every order m + n = 2k, c >= 0 and t > 0, J_(m,n,D)(t) = c^k t^(k beta) I_(m,D) with the unit-domain integral I_(m,D) (rieszUnit, written as in the TeX: hm is H_m, timePos is S, yPos is Y, unifLaw the uniform law), beta = 4 - alpha - alpha0, following the TeX's proof (time increments with determinant one, measurePreserving_incr; spatial increments h_l U_l, pi_waveGreen_eq_smul_map; scaling by t). diagram_riesz_ne_top and rieszUnit_ne_top prove finiteness for every order (0 <= alpha < 1, 0 <= alpha0 < 1), as in the TeX (enlarge to a cube and a box, bound the Green indicators, integrate the disjoint pair factors one at a time, lintegral_pi_matching_le). riesz_four gives the order-four case (three pairings for every split, the representation with c^2 t^(2 beta), finiteness), riesz_coeffA_two the coefficient A_2(t) = c^2 t^(2 beta) sum_m sum_D I_(m,D) < infinity, and riesz_four_paper both with the proposition's hypotheses.

What is missing for P:riesz-small (narrower): the order-two identification with the chaos moments of the solution is the named input MixedMoment (split modelled-object rule; X, u are arbitrary random variables); the sentence "The total coefficient uses the multiplicities in E:total-four" (line 5170-5171) is not formalized: riesz_coeffA_two is the plain sum over the five splits, and the multiplicity form 2 sum_D J_(0,4,D) + 2 sum_D J_(1,3,D) + sum_D J_(2,2,D) needs the chain-swap symmetry J_(m,n,D) = J_(n,m,D'), which is not proved. At order four the identification of the measure-form diagramLim (the object of MixedMoment) with the density diagram is not proved (only at order two, rieszDiagramLimit); E:riesz-four itself is a statement about the TeX's J for the density, so this is not a narrowing of E:riesz-four, but no order-four moment statement about X follows from this module.

Named input: DiagramModel.MixedMoment (the statement of P:mixed, main lines 834-849; true for the solution under H:homog, not proved), in riesz_small_paper' only. Nothing else is supplied.

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. The diagram results need c >= 0, 0 <= alpha < 1, 0 <= alpha0 < 1 (broader than the TeX's strict inequalities); diagram_riesz_eq needs only c >= 0 and t > 0. The wrappers riesz_small_paper' and riesz_four_paper carry H:homog unused and use 0 < alpha, 0 < alpha0, c > 0 only as >= 0. U_l uniform on [-1,1] is unifLaw = G_1 = (1/2) 1_(\|y\|<1) dy on R^1 (map_e1_unifLaw); \|Y_j - Y_q\| is the norm of R^1; the time factor is the model's timeWeight (\|0\|^(-alpha0) = infinity for alpha0 > 0, one for alpha0 = 0) and \|0\|^(-alpha) = 0 for alpha > 0 (one for alpha = 0) in the spatial factor (null sets, volume_pos_eq_null). diagram_riesz_pos (positivity for c > 0, alpha0 >= 0, t > 0) is a Lean-only auxiliary for the refutations; the TeX states nonnegativity.

Refutations (refutations/riesz-four-diagrams/), classified; all are manuscript-claim perturbations in the manuscript domain (c = 1, alpha = alpha0 = 1/2), none relies on a junk value. SelfPairingDropped (the self-pairing of one chain does not drop out in the limit: the measure-form J_(2,0,D)(1) = 1/3, not 0), TimeExponentHalved (the order-four terms scale like t^(2 beta), not t^beta: split (4,0), t = 2), UniformNormalizationTwice (the Green factors 1/2 are not counted twice: J = I_(4,D), not I_(4,D)/16), DivergentUnitIntegral (every (2,2) unit-domain integral is finite) and SecondChaosOnly (A_2(t) is not the diagonal split sum_D J_(2,2,D) alone: the split (0,4) contributes a positive amount).

RieszPositiveDefinite (narrower results: C:three-product-riesz and C:three-finite-images re-issued without the positive-definiteness inputs, still with ThreeTransfer (P:three-transfer) supplied and the moments of the abstract ThreeMomentModel (the solution, its coefficients and M_st not constructed); L:product-endpoints and L:plane-endpoints whole with nothing supplied; the asymptotic clause only for a supplied spectral measure of the low endpoint)

Wave L14 item 3Dpd, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/RieszPositiveDefinite.lean: the three positive-definiteness facts that wave L14 item 3D took as named inputs are proved, and the four wrappers that consumed them are re-issued without them. Positive definiteness is the package's HomogHypothesis.IsPosDefDistr (for every complex Schwartz phi, int (phi * phi~) dGamma is a nonnegative real; phi * phi~ = acorr phi). Main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a.

  1. RieszProductPD (rieszProductPD_proved): c prod_j abs(x_j)^(-e_j) dx on R^3 is positive definite for c >= 0, 0 <= e_j < 1 (the Gaussian-mixture argument in the proof of L:product-endpoints, lines 7251-7265). With it, L:product-endpoints (statement lines 7170-7204, proof 7206-7280) is stated with the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, every conclusion (product_endpoints_paper_proved): a whole result; its conclusions are those of EndpointLemmas.product_endpoints_paper (see that section).
  2. PlaneRieszPD (planeRieszPD_proved): c prod_j abs(y_j)^(-e_j) dy delta_0(dz) on R^3 is positive definite for c >= 0, 0 <= e_j < 1, including the low endpoint e = 0 (proof of L:plane-endpoints, lines 7353-7384). With it, L:plane-endpoints (statement lines 7316-7332, proof 7334-7415) is stated with E:three-parameters and the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, every conclusion (plane_endpoints_paper_proved): a whole result (alpha0 < 1 and alpha < 2 - alpha0 carried, unused, as in EndpointLemmas.plane_endpoints_paper).
  3. RieszIsoPD (rieszIsoPD_proved): c \|x\|^(-e) dx on R^3 is positive definite for c >= 0, 0 < e < 3 (proof of C:three-product-riesz, lines 7971-7980). With all three, C:three-product-riesz (statement lines 7944-7959, proof 7961-7988) and C:three-finite-images (statement lines 7991-8010, proof 8012-8035) are re-issued (three_product_riesz_paper_proved, three_finite_images_paper_proved) with the hypotheses of EndpointCorollaries.three_product_riesz_paper and three_finite_images_paper minus the three positive-definiteness inputs. They stay narrower for the reasons recorded in EndpointCorollaries: the moment statements concern the abstract ThreeMomentModel (the solution u, its coefficients A_k(t), E u^2(t,x) and the static constant M_st are not constructed) and rest on the supplied named input ThreeTransfer (the statement of P:three-transfer, lines 7536-7556, not formalized; true for the manuscript's quantities by that proposition); the asymptotic clause is stated for every spectral measure of the low endpoint.

No new named input; no register entry is used (the measures are densities against Lebesgue measure and their images under linear maps).

Proof route (the TeX's Gaussian subordination, with two Lean-route changes). Mixture: abs(u)^(-e) = Gamma(e/2)^(-1) int_0^infinity s^(e/2-1) e^(-s u^2) ds for e > 0, u != 0 (mixOne_spec), and a zero exponent uses the Dirac mixing measure at s = 0 (no Gamma factor, line 7265); products use the product mixing measure (prodRiesz_mixture), the isotropic power its diagonal image (riesz_mixture); these identities hold off Lebesgue-null sets. Gaussian positivity without Fourier transforms (change 1): for s_j > 0, g_s is a positive multiple of the autocorrelation of g_(2s) (gauss_autocorr), so its form against acorr phi is a nonnegative multiple C of int abs(int h(a) phi(iota a + w) da)^2 dw >= 0 (gauss_form_eq; the sign is autocorr_form_nnr); with iota the plane embedding this is the TeX's tangential quadratic form integrated in z. Degenerate Gaussians (change 2): instead of a separate argument for zero parameters, the density is damped by e^(-delta\|x\|^2), Fubini is applied over the mixing measure and delta -> 0 by dominated convergence (nnr_of_mixture). Absolute integrability uses the radial decay \|acorr phi(x)\| <= C_k (1+\|x\|)^(-k) (acorr_decay) and the temperedness of the measures, in place of the TeX's coordinatewise bound C_N prod_j (1+abs(x_j))^(-N) (line 7252). Junk values: Lean's real power gives 0^(-e) = 0 for e > 0 on the Lebesgue-null coordinate planes (the TeX density is infinite there), so the mixture identities are stated almost everywhere; mixOne e for e < 0 is a clamped density never used.

Refutations (refutations/riesz-positive-definite/), classified, each with a _contrast partner. Manuscript-domain perturbation: NoGammaNormalization (the mixture formula without Gamma(e/2)^(-1) fails at e = 1, u = 1, where the integral is Gamma(1/2) = sqrt(pi); e = 1 is the exponent of the low Riesz endpoint c \|x\|^(-1) in the proof of C:three-product-riesz, lines 7971-7978, which the file's domain sentence names). Lean-route-only controls: MixtureAtZero (the one-dimensional mixture fails at u = 0, where Lean's abs(0)^(-1/2) = 0; the identities are needed almost everywhere only) and NegativeGaussParameter (g_s with s = -1 is not integrable on R; the route needs positive parameters). Control of Lean's totalized arithmetic: JunkAtOrigin (with e_j = 1/2 the Lean density is 0 at the origin, not positive; positive at (1,1,1)).

SeriesType (foundation: elementary series bounds)

Elementary scalar facts that notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex (main file, at 39f2597a) uses inline inside proofs, plus one standalone Gamma-function tool (gamma_mid_sq_le) for which no manuscript line is claimed. None of them is a labelled result. Everything is proved and nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The module contains:

  • the finite ell^nu inequality sum a_k^nu <= (sum a_k)^nu for nu >= 1 and a_k >= 0;
  • the series bound S_nu(x) = sum_k x^k/(k!)^nu <= exp(nu x^(1/nu)) for nu >= 1 and x >= 0, with summability as part of the conclusion (a Lean tsum of a non-summable family is 0);
  • the beta < 1 Hoelder variant of the proof of P:static-phase-all-orders (lines 3198-3207): sum x^n/(n!)^beta <= 2^(1-beta) exp(2 beta x^(1/beta)) for 1/2 <= beta < 1, proved by the TeX's own Hoelder factorization, and the displayed bound <= 2 e^(3x^(1/beta)) for every 1/2 <= beta <= 3; the TeX needs it only at beta = (3-alpha)/2 in (1/2, 3/2);
  • (k!)^2 <= r! s! when r + s = 2k (lines 3295, 6048);
  • the two-sided bound k log k - k + 1 <= log k! <= k log k - k + 1 + log k for k >= 1, a step of the proof of L:positive-series-type (lines 8448-8451);
  • Gamma((x+y)/2)^2 <= Gamma(x) Gamma(y) (the standalone tool; its row has its own label "no direct label (SeriesType foundation: standalone Gamma tool, no manuscript line claimed)").

The powers (k!)^nu with real nu are Real.rpow of the positive real k!, so no junk value of rpow enters. Proof-route differences:

  • The factorial bounds are proved by induction on k with 1 + x <= e^x (factorial_ge_exp, factorial_le_exp, auxiliary), not by the TeX's integration of log x on [1,k].
  • (k!)^2 <= r! s! is proved through the central binomial coefficient; the TeX gives no proof.

The rows with label "no direct label (SeriesType foundation ...)" give the manuscript lines where the fact is used; this records use and does not claim that any proposition containing those lines is formalized. Nothing is narrower than the TeX statement it mirrors. gamma_mid_sq_le is recorded for later coefficient comparisons; no formalized result uses it.

SourceHeatGram (narrower result: L:positive-physical-gram without the label row E:positive-label-row (the uniform mean T_R and the multiplier form v_L are not constructed) and without the entrywise order 0 <= C^R_ij <= D_ij (out by wave L14 decision 5); L:source-spatial-heat whole)

Wave L14 item K1b, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SourceHeatGram.lean: two labelled results at 39f2597a, one whole and one narrower. Both use the registered model choice M5 (the K1 completions as Lp completions, Scope): H_Gamma is a closure in L^2(mu; C), and H_I is Mathlib's completion of L^2(I; H_Gamma) for the kernel form, not a Hilbert tensor product.

  1. L:source-spatial-heat (notes/integrated_source_convergence.tex, statement lines 169-182 with E:source-heat-definition at lines 176-179, proof lines 184-202): the section's hypotheses (H:homog and Gamma != 0, lines 10-16), every conclusion, nothing supplied (source_spatial_heat_paper). H_Gamma (HGamma mu, M5) is the closure, in L^2(mu; C) viewed as a real Hilbert space, of the real span of the vectors iota f (vec, the class of f^(xi) = int f(x) e^(i xi.x) dx) of the real tests. Since <iota f, iota g> = B_Gamma(f,g) (inner_vec, with Gamma even), iota is an isometry from the tests with the seminorm B_Gamma(f,f)^(1/2), so this closure realizes the TeX's real test-null completion (the null quotient is the kernel of iota). Proved: the display in both forms, <iota f, iota g> = B_Gamma(f,g) = (2 pi)^d int f^ conj(g^) dmu with the TeX's unitary transform (texHat, spatialPair_texHat); H_Gamma closed (complete) and separable; real Schwartz tests in H_Gamma, each the limit of the vectors of the expanding smooth cutoffs f chi_n (rapid_mem_HGamma, the TeX's route of lines 189-192); for eps > 0, C_eps (heatH, the restriction to H_Gamma of the multiplier m_eps(xi) = e^(-eps|xi|^2/2)) positive and self-adjoint, \|C_eps\| <= 1, \|I - C_eps\| <= 1, and C_eps(iota f) = iota(p_eps * f) on tests (E:source-heat-definition); and C_eps -> I strongly as eps -> 0+. C_eps is defined as the multiplier on all of H_Gamma and agrees with p_eps * on the dense test vectors; the TeX defines it on tests and extends.
  2. L:positive-physical-gram (notes/integrated_intrinsic_constant.tex, statement lines 143-161, proof lines 163-196): the section's hypotheses (H:homog, a = alpha0, Gamma != 0, lines 4-21) and the lemma's data, nothing supplied, narrower (positive_physical_gram_paper). Proved: the vectors k_i^R = J(h_i (x) iota(m_R f_i^2)) and k_i^infty = J(h_i (x) iota(f_i^2)) as elements of H_I (gramVec, with h_i = 1_(I_i)/ell_i and m_R = eta(./R)^2), the factorization <k_i, k_j> = <h_i, h_j>_(H_t) B_Gamma(q_i, q_j) of both Grams (proof lines 187-189), and their positive semidefiniteness (line 187). Missing: (i) the label row E:positive-label-row (lines 153-158), which needs the uniform mean operator T_R and the multiplier form v_L of S:uniform-physical-products, not constructed in the package; (ii) the entrywise order 0 <= C^R_ij <= D_ij (lines 159-161, proof 189-195), deliberately left out by wave L14 decision 5 (adjacent to the reserved board item B3). The temporal factor <h_i, h_j>_(H_t) is the double integral tPair; the TeX's statement that h_i lies in H_t (via L:positive-raw-embedding) is represented by the route through L^2(I; G) and J_G.

Objects shared with OccupationCompletion (wave L14 item K1a, integrated in wave L14): KernParams is OccupationCompletion.TParams, kForm a F H is OccupationCompletion.kform on representatives, HI p G is OccupationCompletion.HK p G and JI p G is OccupationCompletion.J p G, so the package has one kernel form and one completion. The spatial factors differ: OccupationCompletion.HI p S = HK p (Hsp S) uses the completion Hsp S of the tests under B_Gamma, this module the Fourier-side closure HGamma mu; both realize M5's spatial space, and no isometry Hsp S = HGamma mu is formalized.

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. The TeX's tests are WeakSobolev.IsTestFunction (smooth, compact support); the cells are measurable sets; eta is smooth (the TeX's fixed cutoff profile). Carried and unused (checked against every lemma the proofs call): Gamma != 0 in both wrappers; in source_spatial_heat_paper, from H:homog, d in {1,2,3}, the local finiteness and positive-definiteness of Gamma, the evenness of mu, the scaling law and the ranges of alpha and alpha0 (only Gamma even and tempered, mu locally finite and tempered and the spectral relation are used); in positive_physical_gram_paper, the same items except 0 < alpha0 < 1 (used), and moreover Gamma tempered, mu locally finite, the cells' inclusion in I, disjointness and nonemptiness, ell_i > 0, sum ell_i = 1, \|f_i\|_2 = 1, 0 <= eta <= 1, eta = 1 on the unit ball, supp eta in B_2 and R >= 1 (they serve the excluded order sentence and the label row). The TeX's cells form a partition of I; Lean asks only for measurable cells. The display is proved with no evenness of mu (the TeX uses it for reality); separability comes from H_Gamma being a subspace of the separable L^2(mu) (the TeX uses the local bound and countable approximation); the heat claims are proved for the multiplier on all of L^2(mu) and pass to the invariant closed subspace H_Gamma (the TeX argues on dense Schwartz tests and extends by uniform boundedness). Junk values (outside the manuscript domain; every wrapper conclusion avoids them): vec mu F = 0 when F^ is not in L^2(mu); heatMult eps = 1 for eps <= 0, and heatH Gamma mu eps = id for eps <= 0 or when the spectral data fail; spatialVec mu q = 0 when iota q is not in H_Gamma. Integrability is claimed only where a conclusion states it (memLp_fourierQ, rapid_mem_HGamma, kint).

Refutations (refutations/source-heat-gram/), classified, each with a _contrast partner. Manuscript-domain perturbation: HeatNotStrictContraction (no uniform strict contraction \|C_eps\| <= c < 1 over eps > 0 for the spatial white noise Gamma = delta_0, mu = (2 pi)^(-1) Leb on R, which satisfies H:homog with d = alpha = 1, alpha0 = 1/2 and Gamma != 0; operator-level, through C_eps -> I). Lean-route-only controls: ConstantNotRapid (the constant 1 is not IsRapid, so the cutoff route does not apply to it), UniformConvergence (1 - m_eps(xi) <= 1/2 uniformly fails at eps = 1, |xi| = 2; the route gives strong, not norm, convergence) and UnnormalizedKernel (without the factor (2 pi eps)^(-d/2) the multiplier exceeds one at xi = 0, d = 1, eps = 1). Control of Lean's totalized arithmetic outside the manuscript domain: TotalizedMultiplier (heatMult eps is not e^(-eps|xi|^2/2) at eps = -1).
