SourceTube (whole result)

Wave L12 item SRC, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SourceTube.lean: three labelled results at 39f2597a, each a whole result.

  1. L:source-finite-comparison (notes/integrated_source_convergence.tex, statement lines 21-29, proof lines 31-45): same assumptions, every conclusion, nothing supplied (source_finite_comparison_paper). "A centered Gaussian vector with covariance bounded by C I" is a vector of R^N with a Gaussian law (HasGaussianLaw), E xi_j = 0 and the Loewner bound C I - Cov xi >= 0 for its covariance matrix cov[xi_i, xi_j]; "independent standard real g_j" is iIndepFun with each law N(0,1), on a probability space that may differ from that of xi. The moments are Bochner integrals, and their finiteness (TeX lines 33-34) is a conclusion. Route: the law of xi is N(0, Cov xi) and that of g is N(0, I) (map_gaussian_eq, map_indep_std_eq); the seminorm moment comparison GaussianComparison.gaussian_seminorm_moment_le_paper at B = C I, with N(0, C I) the image of N(0, I) under x -> sqrt(C) x (multivariateGaussian_smul_one), gives E:source-finite-comparison; the TeX's conditional-Jensen coupling with an auxiliary Z is not used. The Banach space may be any real normed space (completeness is carried, unused, in the wrapper).
  2. L:tube-half-action (notes/integrated_gaussian_tubes.tex, statement lines 581-588, proof lines 590-597): same assumptions, every conclusion, nothing supplied (tube_half_action_paper). g_J(r) is the real supremum sSup (J '' closedBall 0 r) (ballSup), the true supremum under the hypothesis "bounded above on every ball"; the identity is stated in the extended reals (EReal), and every term is real. It holds in every seminormed group (tube_half_action); the wrapper carries the Hilbert structure and completeness of the section's H, unused.
  3. P:tube-rayleigh-transfer (notes/integrated_gaussian_tubes.tex, statement lines 225-237, proof lines 239-271): inputs supplied, every conclusion. The nonzero-law case (tube_rayleigh_transfer_paper) takes two named inputs, both conclusions of L:tube-closed-geometry (lines 150-215), which the manuscript proves from the imported Gaussian isoperimetric theorem of Borell and Sudakov-Tsirelson (Friz-Hairer, Theorem 11.6, lines 134-148) and which this package does not formalize: TubeAttained (every tube T_r is closed and {d_delta <= r} = T_r, lines 158-161, proof lines 167-193) and TubeTail (P(d_delta(X) > r) <= e^(-r^2/(2 delta)), lines 161-162, proof lines 199-214). Both are true statements about the manuscript's tubes T_r = A_delta + M_delta(B_H(r)) (paperTube) when the law of X is nonzero; the plan of the wave named only TubeTail, and TubeAttained was accepted under the true-named-input default. The zero-law case (tube_rayleigh_transfer_zero_paper, lines 235-236 and 267-269) needs no input. Expectations and the Rayleigh integral are lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, infinity], as the TeX allows infinite expectations (lines 263-265); no continuity of G is needed (jumps of G, layer cake in lintegral_monotone_le_rayleigh).

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. tube_rayleigh_transfer_paper takes the section's standing objects (a real separable Banach space with its Borel sets, a real separable Hilbert space H, M_delta compact, 0 < delta < 1, X measurable with E\|X\|^2 < infinity and nonzero law) and the proposition's hypotheses on F and G; carried and unused: the compactness of M_delta, delta < 1, E\|X\|^2 < infinity, the nonzero law and the Borel measurability of F and G. The section's Gaussian hypotheses on X (centered Gaussian, coordinates l(X) = W(k_l), C = E[X W(h)] = sqrt(delta) M_delta h, lines 4-17) are not hypotheses of the wrapper: they enter only through TubeTail, which is true for the manuscript's X under them. F is taken on the whole Banach space, while the TeX's F is defined on E_0; only the values of F on the tubes and at X enter, and a Borel F on the closed E_0 extends by zero. E_0 is closure(range M_delta), which equals the TeX's closure C(H) since C = sqrt(delta) M_delta with delta > 0. The zero-law wrapper holds for any normed additive group in place of the Banach space; delta < 1 and the measurability of F and G are carried, unused. Junk values: ballSup is 0 on a set not bounded above, and every statement assumes boundedness (refutation HalfActionUnbounded); the tube radius is extended-valued (inf of the empty set = infinity), and its real value is used only on the almost sure event d(X) < infinity (ae_tubeRadius_lt_top).

Refutations (refutations/source-tube/), classified; none relies on a junk value except where stated. Manuscript-domain perturbations: SourceReversed (the reversed inequality fails: N = 1, v_1 = 1, p = 2, xi = 0, C = 1), SourceScaleC (C in place of sqrt(C) fails at C = 1/4), HalfActionFullSquare (r^2 in place of r^2/2 fails for J(h) = h on R), TransferNonMonotone (the zero-law case without "G nondecreasing" fails at delta = 1/2) and TransferWeight (the weight r in place of r/delta fails at delta = 1/2). Control of Lean's totalized arithmetic outside the manuscript domain: HalfActionUnbounded (without "bounded above on every ball", Lean's ballSup is 0 and the identity fails for J(h) = 1/h).

SpaceTimePositivity (foundation: integral-form identities of the space-time occupation form)

Wave L8, item c1, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SpaceTimePositivity.lean. It proves, with nothing supplied, the space-time facts that the deterministic proof of the boundedness claim of P:variational-positive-scores needs, and states narrower forms of two lemmas. TeX at 39f2597a: notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex (standing assumptions lines 4-21, E:raw-occupation-definitions lines 10-18, L:occupation-raw-square statement lines 24-43 with E:occupation-raw-identities lines 34-38 and the bound of line 41, proof lines 45-108) and notes/integrated_intrinsic_constant.tex (L:positive-raw-embedding statement lines 23-40 with E:positive-bochner-inclusion lines 27-31 and E:positive-raw-mean lines 34-37; E:positive-local-spatial-bound lines 88-91). The cost v_Psi, the mean h_(Psi,s) and the class C_pos are reused from VariationalDilation (rawCost, mean, CPos: integral forms of E:compact-raw-cost and E:compact-raw-mean). The physical pairing B_Gamma(F,G) = int (int F(x) G(x-y) dx) Gamma(dy) is SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair. New objects: stPair (the pairing of the time slices Phi1(s,.), Phi2(t,.)) and the space-time form stForm a Gamma Phi1 Phi2 = int_(0,1)^2 |s-t|^(-a) B_Gamma(Phi1(s,.), Phi2(t,.)), a Bochner integral for the product Lebesgue measure on (0,1)^2. It is the integral of E:positive-bochner-inclusion with G = H_sp written through the physical pairing, and A(g) of E:raw-occupation-definitions at Phi1 = Phi2 = g^2. stFormIter is the same form as an iterated integral, verbatim OccupationCeilingFinite.stForm, and stFormIter_eq identifies the two for continuous compactly supported fields. Every field in the principal statements (positivity, Cauchy-Schwarz, and the mean and variance identities) is a continuous compactly supported real function on R x R^d; the TeX's fields live in L^2(I; H_sp). Some auxiliary bounds take more general fields (for instance abs_cross_le only support and pointwise bounds, conv_stronglyMeasurable only continuity); their rows state them, and some of them are totalized (they also hold for Lean's value 0). Implicit hypotheses made explicit: a < 1 for integrability, 0 < a for positivity (the mixture representation of the kernel needs it), local finiteness of Gamma in place of the physical covariance bound E:positive-local-spatial-bound, evenness of Gamma for symmetry. Integrability of every integrand of the principal statements is a conclusion (stIntegrand_integrable and the first two conjuncts of the mean identities), so none of them holds through Lean's value 0 of a non-integrable Bochner integral; the exceptions are the explicitly totalized auxiliary bounds noted in their rows. Proof route (the TeX works in the completed Hilbert spaces H_sp and H_t (x) H_sp): spatial positivity B_Gamma(Q,Q) >= 0 for continuous compactly supported Q by uniform approximation with mollified test functions; positivity of stForm by writing |s-t|^(-a) as a positive mixture of rank-one kernels (TimeCompletion.kern_eq_mixture) and Fubini (weighted_stPair); Cauchy-Schwarz by the discriminant; the identities by Fubini (spatialPair_eq_conv, integral_mean_mul_eq_stForm_swap). Wrappers: space_time_positivity_homog (all facts under H:homog with a = alpha0, Gamma != 0 not assumed); spaceTimeCS_holds (the proposition SpaceTimeCS alpha0 Gamma, whose fields are definitionally those of OccupationCeilingFinite.SpaceTimeCS; its nonnegativity hypothesis on the field is not needed); occupation_raw_square_cc_paper and positive_raw_variance_form_paper with the sections' standing assumptions (H:homog, a = alpha0, Gamma != 0; Gamma != 0 is carried and not used, the parameter is named _hΓ). Narrower conclusions: for L:occupation-raw-square, the profile class is continuous compactly supported fields g in place of the class O (no unit-norm condition is needed), and only the integral forms are proved (A(g) >= 0 as a genuine integral, the pairing int_I int h_(Psi,t) g_t^2 = F(Psi, g^2), and the bound by sqrt(v_Psi A(g))); for L:positive-raw-embedding, only the variance identity F(Psi,Psi) = v_Psi with integrability and v_Psi >= 0. Not formalized in this module: H_sp, the map Q, rho_g in H_I and ||rho_g||^2 = A(g); H_t, H_I, J_G and its bound by K_0 (the scalar Schur bound is OccupationCeilingFinite.schur_sharp), all built in OccupationCompletion (wave L14); the mean identity T_R Psi(s) = B_E(m_R h_(Psi,s)) and the canonical versions of L:positive-raw-embedding (not formalized anywhere). Supplied inputs: none.

Refutations (refutations/space-time-positivity/), all without junk-value reliance: CSConstant (the constant 1/2 in the Cauchy-Schwarz bound stForm_sq_le), VarianceFactor (F(Psi,Psi) = 2 v_Psi) and DropAlphaLtOne (the kernel |s-t|^(-a) integrable at a = 1). CSConstant and VarianceFactor take Gamma Lebesgue on R^1 (spectral measure delta_0), which is not a covariance of H:homog (positive homogeneity exponent): they are controls for the general statements over locally finite even Gamma, not witnesses inside the manuscript's model.

Formalizes C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket (A common spatial-energy bracket) of notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex at 39f2597a (statement lines 319-333, display E:intrinsic-spatial-bracket lines 323-327, proof lines 335-371) for the variational value S_2^pos in place of C_2(Gamma,a), together with the scalar map E:occupation-scalar-map (lines 238-246), the ceiling value U_c of E:occupation-score-ceiling (lines 252-260) as a function of its constant, the factor D_zeta of E:raw-occupation-energy (lines 118-123), K_0 (line 113), the number Delta of the proof (lines 346-354) and the numerical counterexample at zeta = 1 (lines 361-369). Standing assumptions (section setup, lines 4-21): H:homog as HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu, a = alpha0, q = 4 - alpha, k = 3 - alpha, m = q/k, and Gamma != 0 (lines 20-21). Reused, not redefined: S_c^pos = sSup (VariationalRate.scoreSet alpha0 Gamma c) (P:variational-positive-scores, notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex lines 370-384), VariationalRate.S1Bdd, C_pos = VariationalDilation.CPos, I_Psi = VariationalDilation.integratedRate (rate = square root of the real Rayleigh supremum), v_Psi = VariationalDilation.rawCost (integral form), R_sp = SpatialFourLinear.Rsp, E_sp = SpatialFourLinear.Esp, F_0 = SpatialFourLinear.F0, M_a = TemporalEquilibrium.mass and SpatialFourLinear.energyValue (the right side of E:spatial-energy-map).

Supplied input (named, one): OccupationCeilingK0 alpha alpha0 Gamma, for every c > 0 and Psi in C_pos, c I_Psi - v_Psi/2 <= U_c with C_occ replaced by K_0 R_sp. It stands for T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling (E:occupation-score-ceiling, lines 249-264) combined with C_occ <= K_0 R_sp of P:raw-occupation-energy (lines 111-116), exactly as the proof uses them (lines 340-342), and is no stronger: U_c increases with its constant, and the pointwise form is equivalent to "the value set is bounded above and S_c^pos <= U_c" because the value sets are nonempty. It is discharged in L8Completed by occupationCeilingK0_holds (from OccupationCeilingFinite.occupation_ceiling_K0_paper) (wave item L8-c2, whose K0 and ceilingValue have the same bodies as here), whose own input SpaceTimeCS is SpaceTimePositivity.spaceTimeCS_holds (L8-c1); after integration the corollary for S_2^pos holds with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied. S1Bdd is never an input of the headline: intrinsic_spatial_bracket_paper derives it from the named input (S1Bdd_of_ceiling, case c = 1); only spatial_bracket_lower_sSup_paper takes it as a hypothesis, and the existential form spatial_bracket_lower_paper needs neither.

Narrower than the TeX: (1) the corollary is stated for S_2^pos, not for C_2(Gamma,a); the identification C_2 = S_2^pos is T:intrinsic-second-moment (stochastic, outside Lean), used in lines 340-344. (2) The comparison C_2 <= 2^m F_0(E_(1/2)^O) < 2^m F_a(E_(1/2)^O) (lines 328-332) is stated as S_2^pos <= 2^m F_0(E) < 2^m F_a(E) with E = energyValue alpha (K_0 R_sp) = D_(1/2) (K_0 R_sp)^(2/(2-alpha)), which is at least E_(1/2)^O = D_(1/2) C_occ^(2/(2-alpha)); the class O with the original kernel, A(g), C_occ and E_zeta^O (E:raw-occupation-definitions) are not defined in this module, and every scalar identity is stated for a real constant C >= 0 (C > 0 in the ratio identity) in place of C_occ. They are defined in wave L9 (RawOccupationEnergy: A, Cocc, EO, with the class O modelled by joint representatives; over O itself in ClassOBridge, wave L14), and the comparison with the exact E_(1/2)^O is OccupationCeilingExact.intrinsic_spatial_comparison_paper. (3) The direct zero case Gamma = 0 (lines 379-385, after the corollary) is not formalized in this module (in part in ClassOBridge.zero_covariance_paper, wave L14); every wrapper carries Gamma != 0, the section's standing assumption. (4) I_Psi and v_Psi are the Rayleigh-form rate and the integral-form cost, as everywhere in VariationalRate. HomogCovariance is passed whole to the cited wrappers; no field is claimed unused. Proof route: as in the TeX for S_2^pos. The lower half multiplies E:spatial-static-energy-score by 2^m, the existential form through E:variational-score-set-scaling (dilating one control), the supremum form through E:variational-score-homogeneity; Delta > 0 uses the strict midpoint convexity of x log x (one of the two arguments the TeX names, lines 351-354). Junk values: Fb, ceilingValue and Dzeta are total real functions; Lean's real power gives meaningless values for a negative base, so every statement restricts to z >= 0, C >= 0, zeta > 0. sSup of the coefficient-two set is used only where its boundedness is proved or S1Bdd is assumed. Rows marked "auxiliary to the Lean proof route" have no manuscript label.

SpatialFourierBound (whole result)

Formalizes L:spatial-fourier-bound (Deterministic Fourier bound for the spatial energy, notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 121-131 with the display E:spatial-fourier-bound at lines 126-129, proof lines 133-215; it is new at a284420, introduced at lines 117-118). The quantities are A_sp(g) = B_Gamma(g^2,g^2) and b(g) = norm(grad g)_2^2 of line 36, with B_Gamma of E:spatial-physical-pair (lines 13-18). The module proves, for every real unit g in C_c^inf(R^d) and every covariance allowed by H:homog (including Gamma = 0 and singular covariances; no Gamma != 0 is assumed, as in the lemma), b(g) > 0 and

0 <= A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_Gamma(1) b(g)^(alpha/2),

with R_Gamma(1) = int mu(dxi)/(1+norm(xi)^2) (SpectralHomog.resolvent mu 1; main TeX lines 8992-9001 at 39f2597a). The lemma writes the constant as R_alpha of E:intro-spectral-mass (main TeX line 696, R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))) and uses R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_alpha (lines 200-206, from the resolvent calculation in the proof of L:damped-homogeneous-norms); the identity R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha (and R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_alpha) is proved in SpectralMassIdentity (resolvent_one_eq_ralpha, resolvent_eq_ralpha_paper, wave L8), and SpectralMassIdentity.spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper states the lemma with the constant R_alpha; this module keeps the constant R_Gamma(1). The manuscript now proves "R_0 is finite" of P:spatial-smooth-ratio (lines 223-227) by this lemma (proof lines 250-253), not by the finiteness of S_1^pos; the consequence for R_0 itself is drawn in SpatialSmoothRatio (R0_pos_finite, spatial_smooth_ratio_R0_paper), so R_0 < inf does not depend on T:full-upper, in the manuscript and in Lean.

Labelling. spatial_fourier_bound_paper is L:spatial-fourier-bound with the lemma's hypotheses (constant R_Gamma(1); the lemma as printed, with R_alpha, is SpectralMassIdentity.spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper); spatial_fourier_bound is the general form of the display E:spatial-fourier-bound; the proof steps that have a sentence in the TeX proof are labelled as those steps; gradEnergy_pos is the statement's b > 0 (line 125; proof lines 143-144; the proof of P:spatial-smooth-ratio states it again at lines 245-247).

Definitions: autocorr (c_Q(y) = int Q(x) Q(x-y) dx; the package's one autocorrelation, for which VariationalFloor.autocorr_pos is stated), spatialPair (B_Gamma(F,G) as the iterated Bochner integral of real functions; the TeX's form is the [0,inf]-valued OccupationKernelRow.pairing; the identification of the two is not proved in this module, and is proved for continuous, compactly supported, nonnegative functions and locally finite Gamma by SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair), spatialEnergy (A_sp), gradEnergy (b, through the operator norm of the Frechet derivative, which equals the Euclidean norm of the gradient), fourierQ (Q hat(xi) = int Q(x) e^(i <xi,x>) dx, the convention of HomogHypothesis.IsSpectralMeasure), IsUnitTest (smooth, compact support, int g^2 = 1: the profiles of lines 123-124 and 225). fourierQ uses e^(+i <xi,x>), the exponent of E:masked-spectral-convention; the TeX proof's unnormalized transform F_0 Q(xi) = int e^(-i xi.x) Q(x) dx (lines 145-147) is its complex conjugate for real Q, so norm(fourierQ Q) = abs(F_0 Q) and every statement here, which uses only the modulus, is the TeX's.

Proof route (the TeX proof, lines 133-215, follows the same route; helpers without a TeX sentence are "auxiliary to the Lean proof route"): c_Q = Q * Q(-.) is smooth with compact support, hence a Schwartz function (HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap), so the spectral convention applies to it; a hand Fubini gives int c_Q(x) e^(i <xi,x>) dx = norm(Q hat(xi))^2, so A_sp(g) = int norm(Q hat)^2 dmu with Q = g^2; norm(Q hat) <= norm(Q)_1 = 1 and, by integration by parts with values in C, norm(xi) norm(Q hat(xi)) <= 2 sqrt(b); hence norm(Q hat)^2 <= 8b/(4b + norm(xi)^2), and int mu(dxi)/(4b+norm(xi)^2) = R_Gamma(2 sqrt b) = (2 sqrt b)^(alpha-2) R_Gamma(1) (SpectralHomog.resolvent_homog; the homogeneity of mu from MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog). b(g) > 0 (gradEnergy_pos, d >= 1): b = 0 forces grad g = 0, so g is constant and, having compact support in the noncompact R^d, zero, as in the proof of L:spatial-fourier-bound (lines 143-144); the proof of P:spatial-smooth-ratio (lines 245-247) argues instead by the Fourier support of a function with zero weak gradient (same conclusion). The claim is false for d = 0.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: the integrability of c_Q against Gamma (A_sp < inf), of norm(Q hat)^2 and of 1/(1+norm(xi)^2) against mu are conclusions (a Lean Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0). integral_autocorr_eq_spectral and norm_fourierQ_le alone are statements about Lean's totalized integrals with no integrability conclusion. Hypotheses of H:homog used by spatial_fourier_bound_paper: dim (d >= 1), alpha0_pos and threshold (alpha < 2), Gamma_radon, mu_radon, spectral, and mu_tempered and scaling (through spectralHomogeneous_of_homog). Carried but unused: alpha0_lt_one, Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef, mu_even, alpha_range. Supplied inputs: none. Not proved in this module: the identification of spatialPair with OccupationKernelRow.pairing (proved for continuous, compactly supported, nonnegative profiles and locally finite Gamma by SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair). The bound is for C_c^inf profiles; its extension to H^1 is P:spatial-four-linear, formalized in SpatialFourLinear through R_0 (not through this module's deterministic bound), with the density of H1Density (completed in SpatialOccupationL7Completed).

Refutations (refutations/spatial-fourier-bound/): ScalarExponent (2^alpha instead of 2^(1+alpha) in scalar_identity, at alpha = b = 1), FourierNormHalf (norm(Q hat) <= norm(Q)_1/2, at xi = 0 for Q = g^2), ConstantFactor (the bound with 2^(alpha-1), with Gamma Lebesgue, mu = delta_0, alpha = 0, where A_sp(g) = 1; outside H:homog, inside the general theorem's hypotheses). No junk-value reliance.

SpatialFourLinear (narrower result: P:spatial-four-linear with sequential continuity (topological continuity and the whole result in ClassOH1, wave L14); rate and cost identification not formalized)

Formalizes two propositions of the section S:spatial-occupation-foundation (notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex at 39f2597a): P:spatial-four-linear (statement lines 297-315, proof 317-398) with the displays E:spatial-homogeneous-bound (line 302), E:spatial-square-CS (lines 303-305) and E:spatial-four-linear (lines 309-312), and P:spatial-energy-map (statement lines 405-430, proof 432-461) with E:spatial-energy-map (lines 414-419) and E:spatial-static-energy-score (lines 421-427), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SpatialFourLinear.lean (wave L7-d). The _paper wrappers take the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: H:homog as HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu, so a = alpha0, and Gamma != 0) and one named input, hdense, which is discharged in SpatialOccupationL7Completed (section below).

Objects reused, not redefined: B_Gamma is the extended pairing OccupationKernelRow.pairing of L:spatial-physical-pair (a lower integral in [0,inf]), so A_sp(f) = B_Gamma(f^2, f^2) and B_Gamma(f^2, h^2) are pairing Gamma (zE f^2) (zE h^2); on smooth profiles it agrees with the real SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair (SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair). R_0 is SpatialSmoothRatio.R0, unit profiles are SpatialStaticControls.IsUnitH1, and H^1 is the weak-gradient space of WeakSobolev. A real H^1 profile is an H^1 pair (f, g) (IsH1Pair: f, g in L^2, g a weak gradient of f), so that N(f) (Nnorm alpha f g, line 299) and b(f) = int ||g||^2 are written with the named gradient; the weak gradient is a.e. unique (WeakSobolev.weakGradient_ae_unique), so this is faithful. New definitions: l2, Nnorm, IsH1Pair, H1Tendsto (H^1 convergence of profiles, that is L^2 convergence of each function and its weak gradient), C4 (line 307, a Bochner integral against nu = pairMeasure Gamma), ratioSetH1 and Rsp (R_sp, line 313), energySet and Esp (E_sp, lines 407-411), energyValue (the right side of E:spatial-energy-map), F0 (F_0, lines 424-426), and the route predicate SquareBound (the conclusion of the Fatou step).

Named input, discharged in SpatialOccupationL7Completed: hdense, the density of test functions in H^1 (every f in L^2 with an L^2 weak gradient g is the L^2 limit of test functions phi_n with VariationalFloor.grad (phi_n) -> g in L^2). It stands for the proof sentence at lines 352-358 ("Smooth compact functions are dense in H^1", by cutoff and mollification) and is no stronger; the separability remark there is not used. Its body is verbatim H1Density.H1TestDense d (wave L7-c), which H1Density.h1TestDense d proves, so the input is discharged at integration in the completion module SpatialOccupationL7Completed. Every _paper wrapper uses hdense except spatial_Asp_pos_paper (positivity needs no density). The sSup form spatial_static_energy_score_sSup_paper also takes the named input VariationalRate.S1Bdd alpha0 Gamma (the boundedness claim of P:variational-positive-scores), as in SpatialOccupationCompleted; it is proved in wave L8 and discharged in L8Completed.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: H^1 profiles carry their gradient; finiteness is part of each [0,inf] bound (an ofReal right side); real values of pairings (toReal) are taken only where finiteness is proved; R_sp and E_sp are Real.sSups whose nonemptiness and boundedness are proved in the same wrappers. Clauses of H:homog used (per the module doc comment): dim, alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one, alpha_range, threshold (for d >= 1, 0 < alpha < 2, M_a > 0), Gamma_radon, Gamma_even (symmetry of B_Gamma), spectral (positivity of smooth signed covariance), mu_radon, mu_tempered and scaling (through SpatialSmoothRatio: R_0 in (0,inf), positivity, smooth dilation); positivity of A_sp (spatial_Asp_pos_paper) uses only Gamma_radon and scaling. Gamma_tempered is not used by the extension, continuity, R_sp = R_0 and energy-value statements, but the two energy-score wrappers (spatial_static_energy_score_paper and its sSup form) use it: they apply SpatialOccupationCompleted.spatial_smooth_score_completed_paper (and its sSup form), whose discharge of StaticControls calls SpatialStaticControls.spatial_static_score_paper, which uses hH.Gamma_tempered. Carried but unused by every wrapper: Gamma_posdef, mu_even.

Proof route, as in the TeX unless stated: the smooth homogeneous bound by normalization in R_0 (smooth_homog_bound); positive semidefiniteness of B_Gamma on smooth signed profiles from the spectral identity and the covariance Cauchy-Schwarz (spatialPair_self_nonneg, spatialPair_sq_le); the Fatou step along a.e.-convergent subsequences of the density approximants (squareBound_of_smooth; Lean extracts the subsequences for f and h separately); Cauchy-Schwarz under nu for E:spatial-four-linear; telescoping for continuity. Differences: E:spatial-square-CS on H^1 passes the smooth inequality B(phi^2,psi^2)^2 <= A_sp(phi) A_sp(psi) to the limit by continuity of C_4 (the TeX passes positive semidefiniteness to combinations of H^1 squares); b > 0 on unit profiles (lines 388-389) uses VariationalFloor.ae_eq_zero_of_hasWeakGradient_zero (mollification), not the Fourier support argument; positivity of A_sp (lines 391-396) uses a compact set of positive measure and Mathlib's continuity of the measure of its translates, not L^2 translation continuity of 1_E, and assumes only a.e.-strong measurability and f not a.e. zero (no H^1 membership); for E:spatial-energy-map the upper bound applies E:spatial-homogeneous-bound and weighted AM-GM (young_bound) to every unit H^1 profile and the lower bound dilates smooth unit tests only (energyValue_mem), so the extension of E:spatial-dilation to H^1 (lines 437-439) is not formalized and not needed; the scores follow from E:spatial-smooth-score (SpatialSmoothRatio) by the substitution score_identity and continuity of the scalar maps along smooth ratios increasing to R_0.

Narrower than the TeX: joint continuity of C_4 on (H^1)^4 is stated sequentially (H1Tendsto of each of the four pairs), which is continuity for the H^1 seminorm topology but is not a Continuous statement; continuity of A_sp and of the square pairings (proof, lines 375-376) is not restated (they are C4 f f f f and C4 f f h h as real values, pairing_toReal_eq_C4); E:spatial-static-energy-score is proved in the existential form (every y below M_a^(-1/k) F_0(E_sp) is exceeded by some I_Psi - v_Psi/2, with the package's real-Rayleigh rate and integral-form cost), and in the sSup form only on S1Bdd. spatial_four_linear_paper bundles every claim of the proposition except multilinearity and |C_4| <= R_0 prod N(f_j), which are in spatial_four_linear_multilinear_paper and spatial_four_linear_bound_paper. Not formalized: the separability of H^1 (lines 356-358), the TeX's common a.e. subsequence (Lean uses one per profile), the H^1 dilation. Junk values: l2 f = 0 off L^2; C4 is 0 for a non-integrable integrand (every C4 statement is under SquareBound or for test functions, where it is integrable, except the symmetries C4_comm_* and pairing_toReal_eq_C4, which also holds when the pairing is top, both sides then being 0); Rsp, Esp are 0 for an empty or unbounded set (the wrappers prove nonempty and bounded above); ratioSetH1 divides by (int ||g||^2)^(alpha/2), positive on unit pairs (gradL2_pos); spatialPair_self_nonneg is a Bochner statement that asserts no integrability. squarePairingBounds_paper restates E:spatial-homogeneous-bound and the squared [0,inf] form of E:spatial-square-CS in the spelling of OccupationPhysicalClass.SquarePairingBounds; SpatialOccupationL7Completed.squarePairingBounds_holds uses it to discharge that input.

Refutations (refutations/spatial-four-linear/): EnergyConstant (half the constant in young_bound, at alpha = R = beta = 1), EnergyExponent (exponent 1 on R in young_bound, at alpha = 1, R = 4, beta = 16), Maximizer (the maximizer beta = alpha R in energy_attain, at alpha = 1, R = 4), ZeroCovariance (pairing_sq_pos without Gamma != 0, with Gamma = 0 on R^1 and f = 1). No junk-value reliance.

Integration module of wave L6 for Section S:spatial-occupation-foundation of notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex (at 39f2597a), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SpatialOccupationCompleted.lean. It discharges the two named inputs of the wave's spatial modules under the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: a nonzero covariance satisfying H:homog, a = alpha0) and re-issues the manuscript wrappers without them:

  • rayleighFloor_of_homog: SpatialStaticControls.RayleighFloor Gamma (for every nonnegative nonzero test function z, the Rayleigh set of U_z = Gamma * z contains a positive value), from the dilation floor VariationalFloor.rayleighSet_floor at V = U_z (with alpha < 2 from H:homog, and the integrability and bound of U_z from SpatialStaticControls.convZ_props). This positivity route differs from the TeX's (lines 68-73, through P:variational-unmasked-rate and P:compact-original-common-trial).
  • spatial_static_controls_completed_paper: L:spatial-static-controls, part (i) (lines 42-51), with exactly the manuscript's hypotheses.
  • staticControls_of_homog: SpatialSmoothRatio.StaticControls alpha0 Gamma from SpatialStaticControls.spatial_static_score_paper (part (ii), existential form), with the Rayleigh set of x -> 1 * U_z(x) rewritten as that of U_z, and B_Gamma(z,z).toReal = SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair Gamma z z (SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair).
  • spatial_smooth_score_completed_paper, spatial_smooth_score_sSup_completed_paper, R0_finite_of_S1Bdd_completed_paper, spatial_smooth_ratio_completed_paper: the four P:spatial-smooth-ratio wrappers (lines 223-233) without StaticControls. The supremum forms keep the named input VariationalRate.S1Bdd alpha0 Gamma exactly where the originals had it (proved in wave L8; L8Completed re-issues the sSup forms with nothing supplied).

Nothing else is supplied. The boundaries of the instantiated results (the Rayleigh-form rate and the integral-form cost of VariationalDilation, whose identification with sqrt(-E_s) and E W(Psi)^2 is outside Lean; the existential form of E:spatial-static-score and E:spatial-smooth-score) are those recorded in the SpatialStaticControls, SpatialSmoothRatio and VariationalRate sections. The refutations FloorNeedsNonzero and R0NeedsNonzero show that Gamma != 0 cannot be dropped (the zero covariance satisfies H:homog).

  1. The density input hdense of SpatialFourLinear. It stands for the sentence "Smooth compact functions are dense in H^1" of the proof of P:spatial-four-linear (lines 352-358), and its type is the body of H1Density.H1TestDense d, which H1Density.h1TestDense d (wave L7-c) proves for every d. Re-issued without hdense (name <source>_completed, each proof one line): the general theorems squareBound_of_smooth (the Fatou step, lines 360-365), C4_square_CS and square_pairing_CS (E:spatial-square-CS on H^1), and the _paper wrappers spatial_homogeneous_bound_paper, spatial_square_CS_paper, spatial_four_linear_bound_paper, spatial_four_linear_multilinear_paper, spatial_four_linear_continuous_paper, spatial_ratio_H1_paper, spatial_four_linear_paper (P:spatial-four-linear, lines 297-315), squarePairingBounds_paper, spatial_energy_value_paper (E:spatial-energy-map, lines 414-419), spatial_static_energy_score_paper and spatial_static_energy_score_sSup_paper (E:spatial-static-energy-score, lines 421-427). SpatialFourLinear.spatial_Asp_pos_paper takes no density input and is not re-issued; the auxiliary SpatialFourLinear.squareBound_R0 (no label) is not re-issued either. SpatialSmoothRatio (narrower result: P:spatial-smooth-ratio, rate and cost identification not formalized)

Formalizes P:spatial-smooth-ratio (The finite smooth spatial ratio, notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex at 39f2597a, lines 223-290) with its displays E:spatial-smooth-score (lines 228-233) and E:spatial-dilation (lines 254-260), under the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: a nonzero covariance satisfying H:homog, a = alpha0), written HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu and Gamma != 0.

What is proved: - First claim, input-free (spatial_smooth_ratio_R0_paper): for every real unit g in C_c^inf(R^d), b(g) > 0, A_sp(g) is a genuine integral and positive, 0 < R(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_Gamma(1); the ratio set is nonempty and bounded above, 0 < R_0 <= 2^(1+alpha) R_Gamma(1) and R(g) <= R_0, i.e. R_0 is a positive finite real number. Finiteness is by the route of the TeX (lines 250-253): the deterministic bound L:spatial-fourier-bound (SpatialFourierBound, constant R_Gamma(1)), not the finiteness of S_1^pos. So R_0 < inf does not depend on T:full-upper, for every Gamma in H:homog including singular ones. (Before a284420 the manuscript bounded every ratio by the finite S_1^pos.) Positivity as in the TeX (lines 247-252), from Gamma(B_r) > 0 and positivity of the autocorrelation of g^2 >= 0 near 0 (lines 107-110; imported as VariationalFloor.measure_ball_pos and VariationalFloor.autocorr_pos), plus a normalized bump (exists_unitTest). - E:spatial-dilation on C_c^inf (spatial_dilation_paper). - E:spatial-smooth-score in the EXISTENTIAL form of Le's decision 2 (spatial_smooth_score_paper): for every unit g and every y below k [R(g) alpha^(alpha/2)/(8 M_a q^(q/2))]^(1/k) (k = 3-alpha, q = 4-alpha, M_a = TemporalEquilibrium.mass alpha0) some Psi in C_pos has y < I_Psi - v_Psi/2. This form is implied by the TeX's S_1^pos >= ... and equivalent to it whenever S_1^pos is finite; it needs no S1Bdd. On the named input S1Bdd the TeX's sSup form (spatial_smooth_score_sSup_paper) is also proved, and so is the bound R_0 <= 8 M_a q^(q/2) (S_1^pos/k)^k / alpha^(alpha/2) (R0_finite_of_S1Bdd_paper), E:spatial-smooth-score solved for R(g): the manuscript's route to finiteness before a284420, which now keeps S_1^pos only for the score inequality (lines 286-288). spatial_smooth_ratio_paper states both claims together.

Supplied inputs (named hypotheses): - StaticControls a Gamma = L:spatial-static-controls (lines 42-115; wave item L6-f; discharged from SpatialStaticControls in SpatialOccupationCompleted): for every nonnegative nonzero test z, the Rayleigh set of Gamma * z is bounded above (part of "positive and finite", lines 49-50) and E:spatial-static-score (lines 52-55) holds in the existential form, with lambda_z(1) = rayleighRate (Gamma * z) and B_Gamma(z,z) = spatialPair Gamma z z. It is that lemma's conclusion (the TeX's form with a finite S_1^pos implies it), so no stronger than the manuscript. Used only by the score statements. - VariationalRate.S1Bdd a Gamma (BddAbove score1Set, the first claim of P:variational-positive-scores, unmasked TeX lines 370-374, whose manuscript proof uses T:full-upper; Le's decision 1): only for the sSup form and "S1Bdd implies R_0 finite" (the manuscript at 39f2597a also retains the finite real S_1^pos only for the score inequality, lines 286-288). S1Bdd is proved in wave L8 (L8Completed.s1Bdd_paper_completed), and L8Completed re-issues the sSup wrappers without it. The L6-d foundations are imported, not assumed: Gamma(B_r) > 0 (VariationalFloor.measure_ball_pos), positivity of B_Gamma(Q,Q) for nonnegative nonzero continuous compactly supported Q (VariationalFloor.autocorr_pos, stated for SpatialFourierBound.autocorr, the package's one autocorrelation), and the weak gradient of a test function (VariationalFloor.grad, VariationalFloor.hasWeakGradient_of_test). The coefficient-one score set, S1Bdd and S1pos are VariationalRate.score1Set, VariationalRate.S1Bdd, VariationalRate.S1pos, and M_a > 0 is TemporalEquilibrium.mass_pos. StaticControls is discharged in SpatialOccupationCompleted (outside this section).

Abstractions and why faithful: I_Psi, v_Psi, C_pos are those of VariationalDilation (rate by the real Rayleigh form, cost in integral form; their identification with sqrt(-E_s) and E W(Psi)^2 is outside Lean, P:variational-unmasked-rate, L:compact-raw-profile); B_Gamma is the real iterated integral SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair; U_l g = l^(d/2) g(l .) is WeakSobolev.dilL2; lambda_z(1)^2 is the supremum of WeakSobolev.rayleighSet (Gamma * z). R0 and VariationalRate.S1pos are sSups; every statement about R0 establishes nonemptiness and boundedness of ratioSet (the positivity statements assert both; R0_finite_of_S1Bdd and its _paper wrapper assert boundedness, and their proofs establish nonemptiness by exists_unitTest), and S1pos is used only under S1Bdd, so no statement rests on the sSup junk value; ratio uses Lean division, but b(g) > 0 on unit tests in d >= 1.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: d >= 1, 0 < alpha < 2 and M_alpha0 > 0 are derived from H:homog (homog_consequences; the general forms state them). The pairing identity int (Gamma * G) F = B_Gamma(F,G) used at lines 267-268 is proved with integrability (integral_conv_mul), and Gamma * z is continuous (conv_continuous). Hypotheses of H:homog used: dim, alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one, alpha_range, threshold, Gamma_radon, mu_radon, spectral, mu_tempered, scaling. Carried but unused: Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef, mu_even; in spatial_dilation_paper also Gamma != 0.

Proof-route differences: b(g) > 0 by constancy, as in the proof of L:spatial-fourier-bound (lines 143-144), not by Fourier support as in this proof (lines 245-247); the optimisation (lines 269-286) substitutes the maximiser L = q X^(1/k) directly instead of maximising L - C L^q (score_algebra).

Narrower conclusions: E:spatial-smooth-score is proved in the existential form; its sSup form, and the bound on R_0 by S_1^pos, rest on S1Bdd (proved in wave L8, L8Completed); B_Gamma is the real iterated integral. Not proved inside SpatialSmoothRatio: the identification of spatialPair with OccupationKernelRow.pairing (it is proved, on the continuous, compactly supported, nonnegative profiles used here and locally finite Gamma, by SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair and used in SpatialOccupationCompleted); L:spatial-static-controls itself (it is in SpatialStaticControls, supplied here as StaticControls). Fallback (R0Fin as a named input) not used.

Refutations (refutations/spatial-smooth-ratio/): ScoreConstant (the factor 2 dropped in score_algebra, at alpha = M = R = 1), DilationExponent (A_sp(U_l g) = l^(alpha+1) A_sp(g), with Lebesgue Gamma, alpha = 0, l = 2), GradDilation (b(U_l g) = l b(g), at l = 2), DropGammaNonzero (0 < R_0 without Gamma != 0: for Gamma = mu = 0, R_0 = sup {0} = 0). No junk-value reliance.

SpatialStaticControls (narrower result: L:spatial-static-controls, rate and cost identification not formalized)

Formalizes L:spatial-static-controls (Smooth temporal controls) of the section S:spatial-occupation-foundation (notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex at 39f2597a): statement lines 42-56 (the definition of lambda_z(c)^2, lines 44-48; the display E:spatial-static-score, lines 52-55), proof lines 58-115. The section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10) are a nonzero covariance from H:homog and a = alpha0; U_z = Gamma * z pointwise for smooth compact z (lines 38-39). The wrappers carry HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu and Gamma != 0, and use the exponent alpha0.

Objects. lamSq U c is sSup of the real Rayleigh set (WeakSobolev.rayleighSet) of the potential c U, that is the supremum of c int U g^2 - ||grad g||_2^2 over unit g in H^1(R^d;R) (weak gradients); lam U c = sqrt (lamSq U c) and lamZ Gamma z = lam (Gamma * z) is lambda_z. The definition is the TeX's display with a general potential; for the bounded potentials used here the side condition of WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial is automatic (isRayleighTrial_iff_of_bounded), so the set is the manuscript's set. I_Psi and v_Psi are the package's VariationalDilation.integratedRate (the integral of the real-Rayleigh rate) and VariationalDilation.rawCost (the integral form of the cost); their identification with sqrt(-E_s) and E W(Psi)^2 (P:variational-unmasked-rate, L:compact-raw-profile) stays outside Lean, as for VariationalDilation. B_Gamma(z,z) is OccupationKernelRow.pairing (the extended nonnegative integral of E:spatial-physical-pair) at zE z = ofReal o z; pairing_bridge proves it finite and equal to ofReal (int z U_z), and the statements use its toReal only after that. M_a is TemporalEquilibrium.mass (E:temporal-equilibrium-mass) and f_a is TemporalEquilibrium.density.

Part (i). spatial_static_controls_rate_paper proves, for a nonnegative nonzero test function z: every y -> z(x-y) is Gamma-integrable; for c > 0 the Rayleigh set of c U_z is nonempty and bounded above (so lambda_z(c)^2 is a finite supremum), 0 < lambda_z(c)^2, 0 < lambda_z(c); and lambda_z is Lipschitz on every [c_1, c_2] with c_1 > 0. The general form static_rate also gives |lambda_z(c)^2 - lambda_z(c')^2| <= M |c - c'| for every upper bound M of U_z (the TeX's constant ||U_z||_inf, lines 73-74) without any floor. Positivity rests on the named input RayleighFloor Gamma: for every nonnegative nonzero test function z, the Rayleigh set of U_z contains a positive value. It stands for the dilation floor lemma of wave item L6-d at V = Gamma * z (VariationalFloor.rayleighSet_floor); it is discharged under the section's hypotheses in SpatialOccupationCompleted (rayleighFloor_of_homog, with the completed wrapper spatial_static_controls_completed_paper). Disclosure: since U_z is bounded (proved here), this input is equivalent to lambda_z(1)^2 > 0 for every such z, that is to the positivity claim of part (i) itself; the Lean content of part (i) beyond the input is the finiteness, the transfer of positivity to every c > 0 (through Gamma * (c z) = c U_z) and the Lipschitz bounds. The TeX's positivity route is different: a positive rate of a smooth test with mean c U_z through P:variational-unmasked-rate and P:compact-original-common-trial (lines 68-73). The input is satisfiable (rayleighFloor_volume: Gamma = Lebesgue measure, an unrestricted constant covariance outside H:homog: it scales like c^d, i.e. alpha = 0, and it is not spatial white noise, which is Gamma = delta_0) and fails for Gamma = 0 (refutation FloorZeroCovariance). The boundedness of U_z comes from the Gaussian envelope (VariationalMean.conv_le), not from P:variational-unmasked-rate as in the TeX (lines 71-72).

Part (ii). spatial_static_score_paper states E:spatial-static-score in the existential form (the owner's decision 2 of wave L6): B_Gamma(z,z) is finite, the Rayleigh set defining lambda_z(1) is nonempty and bounded above, and every y < lambda_z(1) - (M_a/2) B_Gamma(z,z) is exceeded by I_Psi - v_Psi/2 for some Psi in C_pos whose rate and time cost integrand are integrable on (0,1). This is equivalent to the TeX display whenever S_1^pos is a finite supremum; spatial_static_score_sSup_paper gives the display itself, lambda_z(1) - (M_a/2) B_Gamma(z,z) <= S_1^pos, on the named input VariationalRate.S1Bdd alpha0 Gamma (boundedness above of VariationalRate.score1Set, that is of {I_Psi - v_Psi/2 : Psi in C_pos}, word for word the boundedness claim of P:variational-positive-scores, integrated_unmasked_variational.tex lines 372-374, whose manuscript proof, lines 430-446, uses T:full-upper; Lean proves it deterministically in wave L8, L8Completed.s1Bdd_paper_completed). Part (ii) uses neither the floor nor Gamma != 0. The proof follows the TeX: Psi_n = f_n (x) z (ctrl, in C_pos by ctrl_mem), mean k_n(s) U_z (mean_ctrl), rate lambda_z(k_n(s)) (rate_ctrl), cost (int_0^1 f_n k_n) int z U_z (rawCost_ctrl), k_n -> 1 with 0 <= k_n <= 1 (E:temporal-equilibrium-potential via TemporalEquilibrium.potential_eq_one), int f_n k_n -> M_a, and the limit of the scores (score_tendsto); ctrl_genuine shows that every Rayleigh set of Psi_n is nonempty and bounded and every integrand is integrable, so no score is a junk value.

Two bridges connect this module to P:spatial-smooth-ratio: pairing_eq_spatialPair proves that the extended pairing OccupationKernelRow.pairing and the real iterated integral SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair agree (and are finite) for continuous, nonnegative, compactly supported functions and locally finite Gamma, and isUnitH1_of_unitTest shows that a real unit test of SpatialFourierBound with its classical gradient is a unit H^1 pair. The weak gradient of a test function (VariationalFloor.hasWeakGradient_of_test), the radius lemma (VariationalFloor.exists_radius_fn) and the score set, S1Bdd, S1pos (VariationalRate) are shared with other modules and documented there.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: local finiteness of Gamma (Gamma_radon, for Tonelli in B_Gamma); integrability of every integrand; nonemptiness and boundedness of every Rayleigh set whose supremum is used; finiteness of B_Gamma(z,z) before toReal. Hypotheses carried but unused: Gamma != 0 in both wrappers (part (i) relies on it only through RayleighFloor), and the fields of H:homog other than Gamma_tempered, mu_tempered, spectral, Gamma_radon, alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one.

Proof-route differences: (1) the cutoff is cut_n(t) = smoothTransition((n+4)t - 1) smoothTransition((n+4)(1-t) - 1) instead of chi(1/(nt)) chi(1/(n(1-t))) (lines 81-87); fn = f_a cut_n has the properties the proof uses (smooth, vanishing near the endpoints, nonzero, 0 <= f_n <= f_a, f_n -> f_a); monotonicity in n is not proved or used; (2) dominated convergence replaces the monotone convergence of lines 90-92 and 106-107; (3) the TeX's floor c_0 <= k_n(s) (line 93) is not needed, because lambda_z^2 is globally Lipschitz and lambda_z therefore continuous on R (lam_continuous); (4) the mean and cost of f_n (x) z are unconditional identities of Bochner integrals. Not formalized: the positivity of B_Gamma(z,z) (lines 107-110), which the stated bound does not need; the identifications of lambda, I_Psi, v_Psi named above; the finiteness of S_1^pos (the named input S1Bdd; proved in wave L8, L8Completed). Constant potentials (rayleighSet_const, lamSq_const) support the satisfiability check and the refutations (refutations/spatial-static-controls/: the floor fails for Gamma = 0, the Lipschitz constant M/2 is false, lambda is not Lipschitz on [0,1], positivity fails for z = 0).

SpectralMassIdentity (whole result)

Proves that the spectral-mass constant R_alpha of E:intro-spectral-mass (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, lines 693-697: B_1 the unit ball of R^d and R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))) is exactly the resolvent at 1, R_Gamma(1) = int mu(dxi)/(1+norm(xi)^2), and hence that R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_alpha for q > 0. The second identity is the display in the proof of L:spatial-fourier-bound (notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex at 39f2597a, lines 200-206). That proof cites "the deterministic resolvent calculation in the proof of L:damped-homogeneous-norms" (main file, lines 1069-1076: int mu(dxi)/(a^2+norm(xi)^2) = alpha V a^(alpha-2) int_0^inf u^(alpha-1)/(1+u^2) du with V = mu(B_1)) together with E:intro-spectral-mass. The value of the radial integral, pi/(2 sin(pi alpha/2)), is not written in the TeX; it is proved here. With the identity, the module states L:spatial-fourier-bound with the manuscript's constant R_alpha (spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper), so that lemma is now formalized as printed (statement lines 121-131 of integrated_spatial_occupation.tex, display E:spatial-fourier-bound at lines 126-129).

Abstractions. ralpha mu alpha is the formula of line 696 verbatim, with B_1 the open unit ball Metric.ball 0 1 (the same expression as the hypothesis hRdef of the IntervalScalar and IntervalScalarCompleted wrappers). The TeX does not say open or closed; for a locally finite alpha-homogeneous mu with alpha > 0 the two balls have the same mass, but that equality is not stated in Lean and is not needed. R_Gamma(q) is SpectralHomog.resolvent mu q, the Bochner integral of 1/(q^2+norm(xi)^2).

Hypotheses. The general theorems (resolvent_one_eq_ralpha, resolvent_eq_ralpha, hRdef_iff_resolvent) assume a locally finite mu with mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A) for measurable A and c > 0 (SpectralHomog.SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha; the sentence of main lines 1067-1068) and 0 < alpha < 2. The _paper wrappers assume H:homog (HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu) and nothing else; Gamma = 0 is allowed (then mu = 0 and both sides are 0), as in the lemma ("allowing Gamma = 0", line 123). The homogeneity is derived by MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog, and 0 < alpha < 2 by alpha_mem_Ioo_of_homog. Fields of H:homog used by resolvent_eq_ralpha_paper and hRdef_iff_resolvent_paper (checked against every lemma they call: alpha_mem_Ioo_of_homog, spectralHomogeneous_of_homog, resolvent_one_eq_ralpha, resolvent_eq_ralpha): alpha_range, alpha0_pos, threshold, mu_radon, and mu_tempered, spectral, scaling (through spectralHomogeneous_of_homog). Carried but unused by these two: dim, alpha0_lt_one, Gamma_radon, Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef, mu_even. spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper uses the fields of SpatialFourierBound.spatial_fourier_bound_paper (listed in that section: dim, alpha0_pos, threshold, Gamma_radon, mu_radon, spectral, mu_tempered, scaling) and alpha_range; carried but unused: alpha0_lt_one, Gamma_even, Gamma_tempered, Gamma_posdef, mu_even. Supplied inputs: none.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit, and junk values. The integrability of 1/(1+norm(xi)^2) (and of 1/(q^2+norm(xi)^2)) against mu is a conjunct of each identity, so no identity holds through the Lean value 0 of a non-integrable Bochner integral; this is the TeX's "< infinity" of line 205. mu(B_1) < infinity by local finiteness, so (mu(B_1)).toReal is not a junk value, and sin(pi alpha/2) > 0 for 0 < alpha < 2, so the division is genuine. ralpha itself is defined for all real alpha; outside (0,2) it is only a formula and no theorem here uses it there.

Proof route (differs from the TeX, same conclusion). The TeX uses polar coordinates. Lean uses the layer-cake formula (as in SpectralHomog.integrable_inv_one_add_sq, which proves finiteness): for 0 < t < 1 the level set {1/(1+norm(xi)^2) > t} is the open ball of radius sqrt((1-t)/t) (levelset_eq_ball; empty for t >= 1), whose mass is ((1-t)/t)^(alpha/2) V (SpectralHomog.measure_ball), and the real Beta integral int_0^1 t^(-a) (1-t)^a dt = a pi/sin(pi a) for 0 < a < 1 (beta_real, from Mathlib's complex Beta function and the reflection formula) at a = alpha/2. R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_Gamma(1) is SpectralHomog.resolvent_homog. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Consequences recorded here. hRdef_iff_resolvent(_paper): the hypothesis R = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2)) carried by the IntervalScalar and IntervalScalarCompleted wrappers is equivalent to R = R_Gamma(1); those wrappers are unchanged. The general form of L:spatial-fourier-bound with constant R_Gamma(1) stays SpatialFourierBound.spatial_fourier_bound and spatial_fourier_bound_paper. Not formalized: nothing of E:intro-spectral-mass or of the display at lines 200-206 is left out.

Refutations (refutations/spectral-mass-identity/): SinFactorTwo (sin(pi alpha/2) instead of 2 sin(pi alpha/2) in R_alpha, with mu Lebesgue on R^1, alpha = 1), ExponentSign (q^(2-alpha) instead of q^(alpha-2), same mu, q = 2), AlphaPositive (the identity without alpha > 0, at mu = delta_0, alpha = 0, where R_Gamma(1) = 1 and Lean's R_0 is 0), FourierBoundAlphaZero (the R_alpha form of the bound under the general theorem's hypotheses without alpha > 0, with Gamma Lebesgue, mu = delta_0, alpha = 0; outside H:homog). AlphaPositive and FourierBoundAlphaZero are controls of Lean's totalized division outside the manuscript's domain, not convention-independent counterexamples: at alpha = 0, which H:homog excludes and where the TeX gives R_alpha no value, R_0 is the quotient 0/0, undefined as an ordinary quotient, and Lean's convention x/0 = 0 makes it 0. The continuous extension of alpha pi/(2 sin(pi alpha/2)) at alpha = 0 is 1; with it R_0 = 1, the identity holds at the witness and the bound holds there (1 <= 2).

StaticInteractionCompleted (narrower result: C:static-interaction with the identification I = sum sigma^n Y_n, the order bounds and the per-block step proved; the operator form of E:fock-sandwich, the inputs of L:complex-phase, the propagator identification, the other inputs of P:static-phase-all-orders, the Gaussian parity, the first-variance bounds and the per-block bound on adapted phases supplied; the free estimates, the group law, the zeroth-phase identity and the norm comparisons supplied; phases not constructed)

Wave L11 item K8, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/StaticInteractionCompleted.lean: C:static-interaction (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a; statement lines 3216-3262, proof lines 3264-3341) re-issued with fewer supplied inputs, using StaticPhaseCauchy (wave L8-h), ComplexPhaseScalar (wave L9-H3) and PhaseContractions. The earlier wrappers IntervalScalar.static_interaction_paper and IntervalScalar.independent_static_blocks_paper supplied five inputs: the identity I_sigma^eps(h)(f,g) = sum sigma^n Y_n, the order bounds of lines 3285-3292, the Gaussian parity (line 3293), the two first-variance bounds (lines 3275-3280) and, for the blocks, the scalar step m_(j+1) <= e^(lambda h_j)(1 + E_j) m_j.

Proved here: 1. The identity. With T standing for S_0(-h) (a continuous linear map), sum_n sigma^n Z_n converges (from the order bounds) and T(sum_n sigma^n Z_n) = sum_n sigma^n T Z_n (static_interaction_orders). Lines 3220-3223 define I_sigma^eps(h)(f,g) as S_0(-h) sum_n sigma^n Z_n, so the conclusion is about that map, not about a supplied series. 2. The order bounds of lines 3285-3292, from E:all-static-phase-orders, |S_0(-h)|_lambda <= sqrt(e) and the norm comparisons for lambda h <= 1 (transported_le), with the TeX's constant A_alpha = 400 sqrt(2) e^2/delta_(alpha/2) (StaticPhaseCauchy.allOrdersA). 3. E:all-static-phase-orders from the inputs of StaticPhaseCauchy.static_phase_all_orders_step, with its circle bound 100 e^(2 lambda h) (lines 3129-3132) no longer supplied: it is proved by ComplexPhaseScalar.complex_phase_paper at a = alpha/2, lambda = n/h (circle_of_complex_phase, static_phase_all_orders_cp) from the more primitive inputs FockSandwich, CPInputs, PropagatorBlock. 4. The per-block step of E:independent-static-blocks: from the factorization M_j = S_0(h_j) I_j, |S_0(h_j)|^2 <= e^(lambda h_j) and the per-block interaction bound on phases adapted to the past (independent_static_blocks_operator, _paper).

Still supplied (named hypotheses): FockSandwich (E:fock-sandwich in operator form, lines 2972-2976, E:abstract-sandwich of L:complex-phase, lines 2755-2759); CPInputs (E:cp-input, imported in the TeX at lines 2739-2748, and the inverse-root integral, lines 2801-2826); PropagatorBlock (the identification of M_z(h) in X_lambda with the weighted block map, lines 2920-2931 and 2948-2951); the other inputs of static_phase_all_orders_step (entireness, lines 3134-3135; the coefficient identification via L:finite-word-cutoff with |z|_(1/h) <= n |z|_(n/h), lines 3143-3154; the lemma itself is proved in FiniteWordCutoff, wave L11, but the identification of the phase coefficients is not formalized; |S_b(f,g)|_(n/h) <= |(f,g)|_(1/h), line 3155; the two cutoff removals, lines 3168-3192, as convergence of norms); the free estimate |S_0(-+h)|_lambda <= sqrt(e), the group law S_0(-h) S_0(h) = 1, Z_0 = S_0(h)(f,g) and the two norm comparisons; the Gaussian parity (line 3293) and the first-variance bounds of P:static-phase-variance (lines 3275-3280); for the blocks, the per-block bound hI on adapted phases (density and tensoring with the independent past, lines 3333-3337).

FockSandwich is not discharged by FockColumnBound (wave L11 K2), whose fock_form_paper_completed is a different statement: a Hermite coefficient model with no packaged Hilbert space, sandwiches that depend on rho, and a bound on sums of squared coefficient norms on the Fourier side. Discharging FockSandwich would need a packaged l^2 Hilbert space of degree-<= N coefficient vectors, a bounded positive A_0 whose functional-calculus inverse root (A_0 + rho^2)^(-1/2) agrees with multiplication by w_rho, a rho-independent B, the conversion to an operator norm, and the identification of the Fourier side with physical space. Wave L12 (FockSandwichModel) provides all of these except the physical-side identification, with the inverse root agreeing with multiplication by w_rho on the band range (the sandwiched operator is the TeX's operator extended by zero), and re-issues the wrappers of this module with FockSandwich, the positivity of A_0 and the self-adjointness of B proved on the Fourier-side model (static_interaction_model_paper, static_phase_all_orders_model; for an orthonormal mode family of every size m, which excludes mu = 0).

Model and hypotheses. E (a complete real inner product space, a real normed space for the blocks) stands for L^2(Omega; X_lambda); the L^2(Omega; X_(1/h)) norms of the Duhamel phases are the real numbers z_n; the cutoff spaces of the order bounds are abstract complex Banach and Hilbert spaces indexed by the order, the Gaussian cutoff and the band. Adaptation to the past is an abstract predicate P j with P 0 x and preservation by each block (hadapt): an explicit modelling of "random initial phases independent of the jth field" (lines 3336-3337), not the probabilistic notion; the refutation BlocksNoAdaptation shows that the bound fails without it. The section's class enters as PhaseContractions.PhaseCovariance (lines 2490-2493) with R_alpha = ralpha mu alpha and D_Gamma = dGam Gamma alpha (E:phase-constants, lines 2494-2501). Recorded in the module header: only 0 < alpha < 2 is used; local finiteness and the other fields are carried, unused. lambda h_j <= 1 is carried, unused, in independent_static_blocks_operator_paper (the TeX needs it for hI). Narrower: the conclusions concern the quantities named by the inputs, and uniformity in eps is that of the inputs. Junk values (module header): real powers have positive bases or are (sqrt R)^n, (n!)^gamma, t^(-1/2) with t > 0; R_alpha, D_Gamma use toReal of finite ball masses; delta_(alpha/2) > 0; summability is proved, never assumed through tsum. Class: inputs supplied, narrower conclusion (C:static-interaction and, through static_phase_all_orders_cp, P:static-phase-all-orders).

Refutations (refutations/static-interaction-completed/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbation: TransportedDropFactor (the transported order bound of lines 3272-3292 without the comparison factor 1/(lambda h) fails at lambda h = 1/2). Lean-route-only perturbation: InteractionDropOne (the bound of E:static-interaction without the free term 1 fails; the witness has R = D = 0, admissible for the general form static_interaction_orders with R, D >= 0, not an instance of the class of S:static-phase with mu != 0). Lean-route-only control: BlocksNoAdaptation (the block bound fails without the abstract adaptation hypothesis hadapt).

StaticPhaseCauchy (proof steps of P:static-phase-all-orders, analytic inputs supplied)

Formalizes the complex-analytic, scalar and Banach-space steps of the proof of P:static-phase-all-orders (All regularized static phase orders) of notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a (main TeX; statement lines 3087-3115, proof lines 3117-3211; all line numbers in this section refer to that file). The proposition is an operator and stochastic statement. Every row below is either a step proved with nothing supplied or a step row of E:all-static-phase-orders (lines 3099-3105) or E:all-static-phase-sum (lines 3109-3114) whose operator and Gaussian inputs are supplied hypotheses (class inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement). It extends the existing proof-step rows of SeriesType for this proposition (the elementary series bound of lines 3198-3207), which all_static_phase_sum_step uses.

Constants (nothing supplied): I_a and delta_a = min{1/4, pi/(8 I_a)} of L:complex-phase (lines 2761-2762), with I_a proved integrable and positive for a < 2 (the TeX uses a = alpha/2 in (0,1)), so delta_a is a genuine positive number; A_alpha = 400 sqrt(2) e^2/delta_(alpha/2) (lines 3095-3097); d_N = 2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(R_alpha) of E:fock-sandwich (lines 2972-2976).

Steps (nothing supplied): Cauchy's estimate for an entire map with values in a complete complex normed space, operator-valued included (lines 3134-3142), and the coefficient bound ||C_n|| <= M (d/c)^n in the TeX's form, quantified over every d' >= d, d' > 0 (this covers the TeX's R_alpha = 0 case of line 3126 without dividing by zero); the arithmetic at lambda = n/h (lines 3149-3163): d_n <= 2 sqrt(2n) sqrt(R), the display of lines 3158-3160, 100 n <= 200^n, n! <= n^n; the pointwise Fourier multiplier form of the norm comparisons of lines 3154-3155 (the integration against the Fourier transform is not formalized); the exponent identity of E:all-static-phase-sum.

Step rows. E:all-static-phase-orders at fixed cutoffs (static_phase_order_cutoff) and after both cutoff removals (static_phase_all_orders_step, wrapper static_phase_all_orders_paper), and E:all-static-phase-sum (all_static_phase_sum_step, wrapper all_static_phase_sum_paper). Abstractions: a complex Banach space stands for the cutoff space L^2(Omega; X_lambda) and a real Banach space for L^2(Omega; X_(1/h)); the phase propagator is an entire map F from the complex coupling to the bounded operators, its argument v is the initial phase S_b(f,g) times the vacuum, and the phase norms are real numbers z1, zc m b, z, N1 named by the inputs. The supplied inputs are: entireness of the phase entries in the coupling (lines 3134-3135); the circle bound 100 e^(2 lambda h) from L:fock-form and L:complex-phase with a = alpha/2 (lines 3129-3132), stated for every d' >= d_n, d' > 0, which L:complex-phase gives from the sandwich bound of L:fock-form (a sandwich bound with constant d_N holds with every larger constant; the coefficient-model sandwich estimate of L:fock-form is FockForm.fock_form_paper, with the spatial column bound supplied, and the scalar steps of L:complex-phase are in ComplexPhaseScalar, with its own supplied inputs; their combination into the propagator bound is not formalized in this module (it is derived from named inputs in StaticInteractionCompleted, wave L11; the propagator is not constructed)); the identification of the coefficient with the cutoff Duhamel phase via L:finite-word-cutoff (lines 3143-3148; the lemma is proved in HermiteWordFock for one Gaussian coordinate per color and, with the m coordinates per color that the phase words use, in FiniteWordCutoff, wave L11; the identification of the phase coefficients is not formalized) together with the norm comparison ||z||_(1/h) <= n ||z||_(n/h) (line 3154); ||S_b(f,g)||_(n/h) <= ||(f,g)||_(1/h) (line 3155; the contraction ||S_b(f,g)||_lambda <= ||(f,g)||_lambda is implicit in the TeX); the cutoff removals b -> infinity and m -> infinity (lines 3168-3192) as convergence of the norms along natural-number cutoffs (the TeX proves strong convergence, which implies it); and the free bound ||Z_0(h)||_(1/h) <= sqrt(e) ||(f,g)||_(1/h) (line 3207). No input assumes a conclusion. In wave L11 the circle bound is derived (StaticInteractionCompleted.circle_of_complex_phase) from L:complex-phase and the named inputs FockSandwich, CPInputs and PropagatorBlock (section StaticInteractionCompleted).

The wrappers state the section's standing class as in IntervalScalar.static_interaction_paper (lines 2490-2502): locally finite mu, Gamma on R^3, 0 < alpha < 2, R = R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2)); evenness, positive definiteness and scaling of Gamma enter only through the supplied inputs. Carried and not used (underscore hypotheses, confirmed by the proofs): in static_phase_all_orders_paper, local finiteness of mu and Gamma, 0 < alpha and the formula for R (the step holds for every real R and alpha < 2); in all_static_phase_sum_paper, local finiteness (0 < alpha and the formula for R are used there, to get 0 <= alpha and R_alpha >= 0).

Junk values: delta_a is not a junk value (I_a is a proved-integrable positive integral); every real power has a positive base or a nonnegative base with a positive exponent; there is no division by d_N; summability is proved, not assumed through tsum. sqrt(R) is the real square root; in the wrappers R = R_alpha >= 0.

Narrower than the TeX, and not formalized: the regularized Duhamel phases Z_n^eps(h) themselves, their being Gaussian polynomials of degree at most n, the uniformity in eps (it is that of the inputs), the convergence of sum sigma^n Z_n^eps(h) as an L^2 phase identified with the Duhamel series (Lean proves absolute convergence of the abstract series), the lemma L:complex-phase (its scalar and weighted-block-map deductions are in ComplexPhaseScalar, with inputs supplied), the propagator bound built from it and L:fock-form (the coefficient-model sandwich estimate of L:fock-form is in FockForm with the spatial column bound supplied), not formalized in this module (in wave L11 StaticInteractionCompleted derives the propagator bound from named inputs; the propagator is not constructed), and the cutoff-removal arguments. The conclusions are the two displays for the quantities named by the inputs.

SymplecticFree (narrower result: J_E, the duality-form identification and symplectic preservation on E not formalized; force skewness only at the L^2 level; free-group data and Young convergence supplied)

Formalizes the abstract core of L:symplectic-free (Free wave form and compact Young baseline) of notes/integrated_symplectic_phase.tex at 39f2597a (statement lines 31-61, proof lines 63-160; all line numbers in this section refer to that file). The lemma is an operator statement on E = H^(1/2) x H^(-1/2); every row below is either a finite or operator-theoretic step proved with nothing supplied, or a statement about the free group that takes the supplied structure FreeWaveData (class inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement).

What is formalized. (1) The per-frequency free matrix W_t(xi) of lines 80-88 (freeMatrix, freeMatrixAt), written with the continuous sine quotient t sinc(tk) so that its value at xi = 0 is the TeX's matrix [[1, t], [0, 1]]; determinant one and W_t^T J_symp W_t = J_symp at every frequency, zero included (lines 89-91), the per-frequency group law and the reversal identity R W_t R = W_(-t) (lines 143-145). At nonzero frequency the matrix is the forward matrix of DimensionalMatrix (freeMatrix_eq_forward). (2) The force skewness of lines 41-42 and 102-105: abstractly for a bilinear pairing that is symmetric through the force (omega_force_skew), and at the L^2 level on R^d with the integrability of the cancellation integrand (omegaL2_force_skew, integrable_mul_force). (3) The operator steps of the two compact baselines: closedness of the compact ideal along a nontrivial filter, each left Young sum compact, telescoping of ordered products, a compact operator maps a bounded weakly null family to a norm-null one, the abstract bound ||S|| <= ||S + K|| for S commuting with weakly null isometries, and 1 <= ||A|| from B A = I, B = R A R. (4) The two displays E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline (lines 46-50) and E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline (lines 54-59) in general form and as exact-hypothesis wrappers, and their conjunction with the per-frequency identity and the L^2 force skewness (symplectic_free_paper).

Abstractions and supplied inputs. E is an abstract nonzero real Hilbert space. FreeWaveData d E (D8) carries the free group S_E (S_E(0) = I, group law), an isometry R with S_E(-h) = R S_E(h) R, and isometries tau_y, y in R^d, commuting with every S_E(h) and weakly null along the cocompact filter of R^d: exactly the properties that lines 121-145 state for the free wave group, the velocity reversal (u,v) -> (u,-v) and the spatial translations (the weak nullity is the Riemann-Lebesgue argument of lines 123-128). LeftYoungSumsConverge X U s t (D7) stands for P:constant-young-linear applied on L(E) (lines 105-112): along some nontrivial filter of finite node lists (n, p) whose nodes p 0, ..., p n lie eventually in [s,t], the left Young sums of X converge in operator norm to U(t,s) - I. The node lists need not be partitions: ordered nodes, the endpoints p 0 = s, p n = t and a vanishing mesh are not required, so the condition does not characterize the Young evolution; convergence as the mesh of genuine partitions tends to zero implies it, so it is no stronger than its source. The Young evolution itself is not constructed: U is any operator family with this property. The wrappers take H:homog as the standing hypothesis; it is used only through d >= 1.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: E != 0 (on the zero space every operator has norm 0, and ||S_E(h)|| >= 1 fails), d >= 1 (from H:homog; it makes the cocompact filter nontrivial), and the nodes lying in [s,t]. Hypotheses carried but unused (stated in the wrappers' doc comments and confirmed by their proofs): theta, the Hoelder bounds and X(0) = 0 (they are the hypotheses of the supplied Young input) in both baseline wrappers, and T > 0 in the single-path wrapper symplectic_compact_young_baseline_paper (the product wrapper has the horizon B and no positivity hypothesis); H:homog and smoothness beyond continuity in symplectic_force_skew_paper.

Proof-route differences: the compact-maps-weakly-null step (lines 128-130) is proved along an arbitrary filter through cluster points in the compact closure of the image of a ball and the adjoint, not by subsequences; the norm bound of lines 132-142 is proved for each z by a limit along the filter; the per-frequency symplecticity goes through M^T J_symp M = (det M) J_symp for every 2 x 2 matrix. Helpers that serve only this route are labelled auxiliary.

Narrower than the TeX, and not formalized: the operator J_E (bounded, isometric, skew-adjoint, J_E^2 = -I), the identity omega = <., J_E .>_E with its duality form (lines 33-40, 73-78), the preservation of omega by S_E on all of E (the Fourier integration of the per-frequency identity, lines 92-96), the identification of the H^(1/2)-H^(-1/2) duality with the L^2 integral and the estimate ||bu||_(H^(-1/2)) <= ||b||_infinity ||u||_(H^(1/2)) (line 102), the construction of S_E, tau_y and the reversal with the properties of FreeWaveData, the Young evolution, and the remark that a zero length gives P_j = I (lines 156-157). The two displays are stated exactly as in the TeX, for the supplied objects.

TemporalEquilibrium (whole result)

Formalizes the section S:temporal-equilibrium (notes/integrated_temporal_equilibrium.tex at 39f2597a): Lemma L:equilibrium-gamma-beta (recurrence, Beta-Gamma identity, duplication) and Lemma L:temporal-equilibrium (positivity, L^1(0,1) ∩ L^2(0,1), the potential identity E:temporal-equilibrium-potential for every s in [0,1], endpoints included, and the mass E:temporal-equilibrium-mass). Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The manuscript's Gamma_E is Mathlib's Real.Gamma; gammaE_integral records that for x > 0 it equals the manuscript's integral, which converges and is positive. Beta is defined as the manuscript's integral over (0,1), and Beta_eq_betaIntegral identifies it with Mathlib's Complex.betaIntegral. density is the manuscript's f_a with r = (1-a)/2 written out; it is a total function on the reals, and only its values on (0,1) are used. L^p(0,1) is MemLp for volume.restrict (Ioo 0 1). Every evaluation of an ordinary integral that the manuscript states includes the integrability of its integrand, since the Lean integral of a non-integrable function is 0; the evaluated auxiliary lintegrals establish finite nonnegative values, while the general reflection and splitting identities do not themselves assert finiteness. The kernel |s-t|^(-a) uses Lean's rpow, whose value at t = s is irrelevant on a null set. Hypotheses that are carried but unused: x > 0 in gamma_beta_duplication (the general version needs none) and a < 1 in density_sq_integrableOn (square integrability needs only a > 0). The proof route differs from the TeX, though the statements do not. The TeX expands hypergeometric series. Lean proves the Euler-type identity int_0^t (t-u)^(-2r) u^(r-1) (1-u)^(r-1) du = Beta(r,1-2r) [t(1-t)]^(-r) by the Möbius substitution u = tv/(1-t+tv) and then applies a Tonelli swap. This gives the TeX's incomplete-Beta formula for the left part; the right part and the endpoints follow by reflection and splitting at s. The remark that the mass "has not been renormalized" is a statement about the manuscript, not a formula, so it is not formalized. The use of L:equilibrium-gamma-beta in notes/integrated_white_evaluation.tex is outside this module. normalizer_eq_pi_div_sin is an extra remark that is not in the TeX.
