TerminalWick (narrower result: L:terminal-wick for real r only, comparison per mixed moment only, chain measures specified by their masses, not constructed; inputs supplied and an added measurability restriction)

Formalizes L:terminal-wick (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a; the chain measure E:terminal-chain-measure, lines 4275-4288; the statement, lines 4291-4336, with the displays E:terminal-term-majorant (4302-4306), E:terminal-wick-formula (4310-4313) and E:terminal-pairing-integral (4315-4328); the proof, lines 4338-4410), built on FiniteWick, with every stated conclusion proved for real r and two inputs left outside Lean, and one added hypothesis (3). (1) Supplied: hmeas, the a.e. strong measurability of z -> prod_j W(z_j) as an L^2(Omega)-valued map for each nu n. In the TeX it follows from the cell-wise mean-square continuity ("the product is strongly measurable in L^2 on the stated pieces", lines 4357-4359); it is assumed here, almost everywhere only, so it is no stronger than the TeX's claim. (2) Not constructed: the chain measures g_n^{T,x}. The general theorems take arbitrary finite measures nu n on n-tuples of points; the wrappers take finite measures on n-tuples of points of [0,T] x R^d (Pt d T) with total mass chainMass d n T. chainMass d n T is the lower integral of chainWeight d n T, the recursion on the last vertex of 1_{[0,T]^n_<}(s) prod_j G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(R^d) with s_{n+1} = T and the wave Green measures WaveGreen.waveGreen d (in d = 3 the module's documented choice of surface measure). Lean proves chainMass d n T = T^(2n)/(2n)! for d in {1,2,3}, T >= 0 (chainMass_eq, from G_h(R^d) = h and the recursion M_{n+1}(T) = int_0^T (T-t) M_n(t) dt, lines 4348-4351), but not that this is the total mass of the measure E:terminal-chain-measure (a Tonelli and pushforward identity), since that measure is not built. Only the total masses of the nu n are used, so every conclusion holds for any finite measures with these masses, in particular for g_n^{T,x} once constructed; the point x enters only through the measures. (3) Added restriction, not in the manuscript: hK, the joint (Borel) measurability of (p, q) -> K p q on pairs of points of [0,T] x R^d, a hypothesis of mixed_moment_eq_sum_pairings, integrable_pairWeight and terminal_wick_paper, used only to split the integral of the pairing sum into the separate pairing integrals and to prove each pairing integrand integrable. The TeX assumes bounded variance and joint mean-square continuity only on the open cells of a finite partition of [0,T]; these leave the covariance at the cut times unrestricted, so hK does not follow from them (a field that vanishes off one cut time c and equals 1_A(y) Z there, with A not Borel and Z standard Gaussian, meets every TeX hypothesis and the supplied hmeas, but its covariance is not measurable). The wrapper is therefore narrower than the lemma by this restriction; terminal_wick_mono_paper, mixed_moment_odd, mixed_moment_nonneg and terminalWickInput_of_nonneg do not take it. Y_n is chainIntegral nu hW n, the Bochner integral in Mathlib's Lp R 2 P of prodL2 hW z, the L^2 class of prod_j W(z_j); E[Y_m Y_n] is the integral of Y_m(omega) Y_n(omega), equal to the L^2 inner product. V = sup_p K(p,p) (the TeX's sup E|W|^2; under CenteredGaussianField the one-point law of W(p) is multivariateGaussian 0 of the 1 x 1 matrix K(p,p)) is the supremum iSup with BddAbove as hypothesis (the TeX's V < infinity), so it is a genuine supremum, and V^(n/2) is a real power. The pairing integral T^K_{m,n,D} is pairingIntegral nu K m n D, the integral against nu m x nu n of prod_{{a,b} in D} K(tau_a, tau_b) with tau the concatenation (Fin.append) of the two tuples, which carry both time and space. Implicit hypotheses made explicit: positive semidefiniteness of the covariance matrices (part of CenteredGaussianField), finiteness of each nu n, BddAbove of the variances, and T > 0 (the measurability hK of the covariance is not implicit in the TeX; see (3)). Hypotheses carried but unused (checked by recompiling both wrapper proofs with them removed): in terminal_wick_paper, IsProbabilityMeasure P and MeanSquareCellContinuous K (which stands behind the supplied hmeas); in terminal_wick_mono_paper, both probability instances, both cell-continuity hypotheses, d in {1,2,3} and the masses. Proof-route differences: the L^2 bound of the product uses the Wick formula and the count of pairings (FiniteWick.CenteredGaussianField.sq_moment_le) instead of Hoelder's inequality (lines 4351-4356), with the same bound; the Wick formula comes from FiniteWick (Gaussian integration by parts, not the moment generating function); Fubini is applied through integral_inner and integral_prod_symm; absolute convergence is by comparison with sum c^n/n! through sqrt((2n-1)!!)/(2n)! <= 1/n! instead of the ratio test (lines 4406-4408). Narrower conclusions: absolute convergence of sum_n r^n Y_n is stated for real r only (the TeX also states complex r; a complexified L^2 is not set up in this module: both narrowings are removed in wave L12, TerminalWickComplete); the comparison sentence ("compares all finite partial-order second moments", lines 4332-4333) is stated for each mixed moment E[Y_m Y_n]; second moments of finite partial sums are not stated as such. The majorant is proved for every n, including n = 0 (the TeX states n >= 1). Junk values: chainIntegral would be 0 for a non-integrable integrand, but the wrapper proves integrability from hmeas; the bound norm_chainIntegral_le and the summability summable_norm_smul_chainIntegral need no measurability because they also hold for the junk value; every pairing integrand is proved integrable, so pairingIntegral is a genuine integral in the wrapper. Cross-item discharge: terminalWickInput_of_nonneg (and the last conjunct of terminal_wick_paper) proves both fields of UniformSeriesTail.TerminalWickInput for the family Y_n and every real r when K >= 0. Not formalized: the construction of g_n^{T,x} and of its density g_n of E:expansion in d = 1, 2; the symmetrization paragraph (lines 4384-4390, identification with the symmetrized convention of E:expansion); the d = 3 Green-regularization paragraph (lines 4392-4398, agreement with the source's fixed-noise convention); and complex r. No conclusion of the module uses the two omitted paragraphs. Wave L11 constructs g_n^{T,x} and proves hmeas from the cell continuity (TerminalWickInputs): terminal_wick_constructed_paper and terminal_wick_mono_constructed_paper state the lemma for the constructed measures with its hypotheses only (no hmass, hmeas or hK), and in TerminalWickRegularization the mass and convergence facts of the Green-regularization paragraph are proved for a common-noise construction whose factors are identified with p_eta * G_h one at a time (the identification of the whole regularized chain measure with the TeX's product, and the paragraph's last clause, are not formalized); the rows below, the general forms, are unchanged, and hK remains an added restriction of terminal_wick_paper only. Wave L12 (TerminalWickComplete) adds complex r and the second moments of partial sums for the constructed measures. The route definitions chainWeightReal and chainMassReal (the same recursion with each Green mass G_h(R^d) replaced by h) are public but not listed as claims; they appear in the statements of the rows below. Refutations (refutations/terminal-wick/), all scalar controls without junk-value reliance and without a Gaussian field: ChainMassSimplex (M_n(T) = T^n/n!, forgetting the Green masses; d = 1, n = 1, T = 1), ChainMassFactorial (M_n(T) = T^(2n)/(n!)^2; d = 2, n = 1, T = 1) and MajorantFactor (sqrt((2n-1)!!)/(2n)! <= 1/(2n)!; n = 2).

L:terminal-wick StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper Wrapper with the TeX's hypotheses plus one added restriction, the measurability of the covariance (TeX lines 4291-4336, proof 4338-4410). Hypotheses: a probability measure P (carried, unused), d in {1,2,3}, T > 0, CenteredGaussianField W K P on Pt d T = [0,T] x R^d, the variances K p p bounded above (V = sup_p K p p finite), MeanSquareCellContinuous K (carried, unused), finite measures nu n on n-tuples of points with nu n (total) = chainMass d n T, the supplied hmeas, and measurability of (p, q) -> K p q. Nine conjuncts: z -> prodL2 hW z is nu n-integrable for every n (the Bochner integrals Y_n exist); Y_0 = 1 a.e.; \|Y_n\|_2 <= sqrt((2n-1)!!) V^(n/2) T^(2n)/(2n)! for every n including n = 0 (E:terminal-term-majorant, V^(n/2) a real power); E[Y_m Y_n] = sum_{D in pairings of Fin (m+n)} pairingIntegral nu K m n D (E:terminal-wick-formula, empty sum when m + n is odd); every pairing integrand is nu m x nu n-integrable; E[Y_m Y_n] = 0 for odd m + n; if K >= 0, every pairingIntegral nu K m n D >= 0 and every E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0; sum_n \|r^n Y_n\|_2 < infinity for every real r (complex r not stated); and, if K >= 0, TerminalWickInput P (n -> Y_n) r for every real r. Verified by recompiling the proof without them: the probability instance and MeanSquareCellContinuous are not used. Supplied hmeas (from the proof of L:terminal-wick, TeX lines 4357-4359): z -> prodL2 hW z is nu n-a.e. strongly measurable for every n. The chain measures are not constructed: nu n is any finite measure with the stated total mass (for g_n^{T,x} of E:terminal-chain-measure). Added restriction not in the manuscript: joint measurability of (p, q) -> K p q (hK); the TeX's cell-wise mean-square continuity leaves the covariance at the cut times unrestricted, so hK does not follow from its hypotheses. Hypothesis names in Lean: hmass.
L:terminal-wick StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.TerminalWick.terminal_wick_mono_paper Exact-hypothesis wrapper of the comparison sentence (TeX lines 4331-4333, proof 4404-4406): for probability measures P1, P2, T > 0 and two CenteredGaussianFields on [0,T] x R^d with variances bounded above and MeanSquareCellContinuous covariances, the same finite measures nu n with nu n (total) = chainMass d n T, hmeas for both, and 0 <= K1 <= K2 entrywise: E1[Y1_m Y1_n] <= E2[Y2_m Y2_n] for all m, n. Carried, unused (checked by recompiling the proof without them): d in {1,2,3}, the masses, the cell continuity and both probability instances. Stated for each mixed moment E[Y_m Y_n]. Supplied hmeas₁, hmeas₂ for the two fields (from the proof of L:terminal-wick, TeX lines 4357-4359); the masses _hmass are carried, unused. The chain measures are not constructed: nu n is any finite measure with the stated total mass (for g_n^{T,x} of E:terminal-chain-measure).

TerminalWickComplete (whole result)

Wave L12 item TW, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TerminalWickComplete.lean (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, line numbers at 39f2597a): the two parts of L:terminal-wick (statement lines 4291-4336, proof lines 4338-4410) that TerminalWickInputs left narrower, for the constructed terminal-chain measures g_n^(T,x) of E:terminal-chain-measure (lines 4275-4288, TerminalWickInputs.chainMeasure). Class of L:terminal-wick: same assumptions, every conclusion, for the constructed g_n^(T,x), nothing supplied; in d = 3 the Green measure is the registered model choice M1 (Scope), so the result is whole over M1.

What the TeX claims. Lines 4331-4333: "If K >= 0, every integral above is nonnegative. Consequently, entrywise comparison 0 <= K_1 <= K_2 compares all finite partial-order second moments in the same direction"; the proof (lines 4404-4406) compares the covariance products pairing by pairing, "including self-pairs and unequal chains". The phrase is read in both senses: the mixed moments E[Y_m Y_n] (TerminalWickInputs.terminal_wick_mono_constructed_paper) and the second moments E(sum_(n<=N) r^n Y_n)^2 of the partial sums of every finite order N, for real r. Lines 4333-4335: "The series sum_(n>=0) r^n Y_n converges absolutely in L^2 for every real or complex r". The TeX states the comparison for no complex r, and the comparison for complex r is false (refutation ComplexComparison below), so the comparison rows are for real r and are no narrowing.

Formalized (proved, nothing supplied): 1. The partial-sum comparison for every real r and every finite order N (norm_sq_partial_le, from the entrywise comparison of the mixed moments and the vanishing of the odd ones, line 4329: every surviving coefficient r^(m+n) has an even exponent); for the constructed measures, partial_sum_mono_constructed_paper. The full-series comparison, by the limit of the partial sums (norm_sq_tsum_le), is a Lean-side corollary, not a sentence of the TeX. 2. Complex r: Y_n enters the complex L^2(P) through the isometric embedding toC (norm_toC, inner_toC); sum_n r^n Y_n converges absolutely and converges there (summable_norm_smul_toC, summable_smul_toC), reduced to the real series at \|r\|. The second-moment formula E\|sum_(n<=N) r^n Y_n\|^2 = sum_(m,n<=N) r^m conj(r)^n E[Y_m Y_n] and its limit for the full series (norm_sq_sum_smul_toC, tendsto_norm_sq_tsum_toC) are a Lean-side addition, not a sentence of the TeX; their rows carry no label. For the constructed measures: terminal_wick_complex_constructed_paper. 3. The wrapper terminal_wick_full_constructed_paper: every conclusion of L:terminal-wick for the constructed g_n^(T,x), with the lemma's hypotheses only (a second field W_2 with the same hypotheses for the comparison sentence).

Hypotheses: those of TerminalWickInputs.terminal_wick_constructed_paper (T > 0, so 0 <= T for chainMeasure); no hypothesis is added. Recorded as carried and unused in the module header: IsProbabilityMeasure of each law (the TeX's setting). The open ordered simplex, the Green measure in d = 3 (M1), the density remark for d = 1, 2 (lines 4285-4287, in the definition before the lemma; not formalized), the symmetrization paragraph (lines 4384-4390; not formalized) and the Green-regularization paragraph (lines 4392-4398, TerminalWickRegularization) are as in TerminalWickInputs: the two proof paragraphs identify conventions, and none of the three is a conclusion of the lemma statement. Junk values: second moments of partial sums are stated as E X^2 of an L^2 element and equal its squared norm (UniformSeriesTail.integral_sq_eq_norm_sq, integral_norm_sq_eq); summability is proved, never assumed through tsum. A wording note for the author (manuscript, not acted on): "all finite partial-order second moments" could say "the mixed moments E[Y_m Y_n], hence the second moments of the partial sums for real r".

Refutations (refutations/terminal-wick-complete/), classified; none relies on a junk value. All three are Lean-route-only controls of the abstract lemma norm_sq_partial_le (witnesses in R, not chain integrals): ComplexComparison (the comparison for complex r fails, since r^m conj(r)^n need not be nonnegative for even m + n: Y = (1,0,0), Y' = (1,0,1), r = i), GeneralWeights (arbitrary real weights in place of the powers r^n fail: weights (1,0,-1)) and NoParity (without the vanishing of the odd mixed moments of the larger family the comparison fails at r = -1; for the chain integrals the parity is proved, line 4329).

TerminalWickInputs (narrower result: L:terminal-wick for the constructed chain measures, real r only, the comparison per mixed moment (complex r and second moments of finite partial sums not stated here; both in TerminalWickComplete); L:uniform-series-tail whole, for the constructed chain measures)

Wave L11 item K4 (parts i and iii), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TerminalWickInputs.lean (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, line numbers at 39f2597a): the chain measure E:terminal-chain-measure (lines 4275-4288), L:terminal-wick (statement lines 4291-4336, proof lines 4338-4410) and L:uniform-series-tail (lines 4419-4464). It discharges the inputs that TerminalWick (wave L8-f) left supplied and removes its added hypothesis hK.

  1. Strong measurability of the chain product (lines 4357-4359: "the product is strongly measurable in L^2 on the stated pieces"). fieldL2 is the field value W(p) in L^2(P); mean-square continuity at p is continuity of p -> W(p) into L^2 (continuousAt_fieldL2), and the chain product is continuous at every tuple of such points (continuousAt_prodL2). Under the cell continuity of the lemma (TerminalWick.MeanSquareCellContinuous, lines 4294-4296) and for chain measures without time atoms, z -> prod_j W(z_j) is a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_prodL2_of_cell): this is the input hmeas of TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper, proved.
  2. The pairing integrands without measurability of K. hK (joint measurability of the covariance) was an added restriction of TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper, not implied by the TeX. Under the cell continuity, K(p,q) = <W(p), W(q)> is continuous at pairs of continuity points, so each pairing integrand is a.e. strongly measurable and integrable (aestronglyMeasurable_pairWeight_of_cell, integrable_pairWeight_of_cell), and E:terminal-wick-formula holds without hK (mixed_moment_eq_sum_pairings_of_cell). terminal_wick_paper_measurable is terminal_wick_paper without hmeas and hK, for abstract chain measures with the masses T^(2n)/(2n)! and no time atoms.
  3. The measures g_n^{T,x}, constructed. chainMeasureRaw d n T x is the image of timeMeasure n T x G_1^(x n) (timeMeasure: Lebesgue measure with density 1_(0<s_1<...<s_n<T) prod_j (s_(j+1) - s_j)) under (s, v) -> (s_j, x - sum_(l>=j) (s_(l+1) - s_l) v_l)_j. This avoids the measurability of h -> G_h as a measure-valued map, through the scaling G_h(hA) = h G_1(A) (WaveGreen.waveGreen_scaling). chainMeasureRaw_apply proves that it is the TeX's measure: for every measurable A, g_n^{T,x}(A) = int_(0<s_1<...<s_n<T) ((x)_j G_(s_(j+1)-s_j))({w : (s_j, x - sum_(l>=j) w_l)_j in A}) ds, s_(n+1) = T (lines 4276-4285). chainMeasure d n T hT x is its image on n-tuples of points of [0,T] x R^d, the point set of the lemma, by projecting each time into [0,T] (the identity on the support). g_0^{T,x} is the unit mass on the empty tuple (chainMeasure_zero, lines 4287-4288). The total mass is T^(2n)/(2n)! (chainMeasureRaw_univ, chainMeasure_univ, chainMeasure_univ_eq_chainMass: the input hmass, lines 4348-4351), and there are no time atoms (timeAtomless_chainMeasure).
  4. Wrappers. terminal_wick_constructed_paper is L:terminal-wick for nu n = g_n^{T,x} with the lemma's hypotheses only: d in {1,2,3}, T > 0, x, a probability P, a centered real Gaussian field with V < infinity and the cell continuity (used). None of hmass, hmeas, hK remains. uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_constructed_paper is L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper with the fixed g_n^{T,x} (the TeX's chain measures) in place of the (eps, delta)-dependent abstract measures, hmass and hmeas replaced by the cell continuity of each regularized covariance, all other hypotheses and all conclusions unchanged. terminal_wick_mono_constructed_paper is the comparison sentence (lines 4331-4333), TerminalWick.terminal_wick_mono_paper with nu n = g_n^{T,x} and its hmass, hmeas1, hmeas2 discharged; and uniform_series_tail_second_moment_constructed_paper is the last sentence of L:uniform-series-tail (the bound B_1, lines 4441-4442), UniformSeriesTail.uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper for the chain integrals over g_n^{T,x} with its TerminalWickInput discharged by terminal_wick_constructed_paper.

Why the construction is faithful: the TeX defines g_n^{T,x} exactly as the pushforward of prod_j G_(s_(j+1)-s_j)(dw_j) under y_j = x - sum_(l=j)^n w_l integrated over the ordered simplex, and chainMeasureRaw_apply is that formula on every measurable set. Differences: the simplex is the open one (OpenSimplex), which is the manuscript's open ordered simplex [0,T]^n_< (lines 550-551); in d = 3 the Green measure is WaveGreen.waveGreen 3, the registered model choice M1 (Scope). Hypotheses: TimeAtomless is an added hypothesis of the general statements for abstract chain measures (the TeX has only g_n^{T,x}), proved for g_n^{T,x}; 0 <= T is a parameter of the definition of chainMeasure (the wrappers take T > 0, as the TeX's [0,T] presumes); d in {1,2,3} is used for the identification and the mass. Recorded as carried and unused in the module header: IsProbabilityMeasure P (as in TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper). Proof-route differences: the L^2 continuity of the product comes from the Wick formula (norm_sub_prodL2_sq), not from continuity in every finite L^p and Hoelder's inequality (lines 4357-4359); the measurability of the pairing integrands comes from continuity of K off the cut times.

Classes. L:terminal-wick: same assumptions, narrower conclusion: every conclusion with the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, for the constructed g_n^{T,x}, with two narrowings unchanged from TerminalWick: real r only (complex r is not stated) and the comparison stated for each mixed moment E[Y_m Y_n] (second moments of finite partial sums are not stated as such); wave L12 (TerminalWickComplete) removes both narrowings, and there the lemma is a whole result. L:uniform-series-tail: same assumptions, every conclusion, for the constructed g_n^{T,x} (in d = 3 over M1; the bounds and the L^2 limit by uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_constructed_paper, the bound B_1 by uniform_series_tail_second_moment_constructed_paper); the regularized fields W^{eps,delta} are hypotheses of the lemma, not constructions. The added restriction hK remains a hypothesis of the general form TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper only. Not formalized: the density remark for d = 1, 2 (lines 4285-4287, the ordered kernel g_n of E:expansion) and the symmetrization paragraph (lines 4384-4390). For the Green-regularization paragraph (lines 4392-4398), TerminalWickRegularization proves the mass and convergence facts for a common-noise construction (the identification of the whole regularized chain measure with the TeX's product, and the paragraph's last clause, are not formalized). Junk values: with g_n^{T,x} every Y_n is a genuine Bochner integral (integrability is conclusion (1)) and every pairing integrand is integrable (conclusion (5)); masses are ofReal of nonnegative reals. Refutations (refutations/terminal-wick-inputs/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbations: ChainMassNoGreenMass (forgetting the Green masses gives the total mass T^n/n! instead of T^(2n)/(2n)!; d = 1, n = 1, T = 1) and ExtraFirstGap (an extra Green factor from time 0 changes the time density; n = 1, T = 1, s_1 = 1/2). Lean-route-only control: TimeAtoms (a finite chain measure can have a time atom, so the hypothesis TimeAtomless of the general statements is not vacuous; it is proved for g_n^{T,x}).

Route definitions without claim rows (they appear in the statements of the rows below): gramWick, gramPairWeight (the pairing sum and a pairing weight of a Gram matrix), chainMap (the map whose image is chainMeasureRaw), toPt (projection of the times into [0,T]).

TerminalWickRegularization (proof steps of L:terminal-wick: the Green-regularization paragraph of its proof, the regularized chain measure identified with the factors p_eta * G one factor at a time)

Registered model choice: M1 (the d = 3 wave Green measure via volume.toSphere; its identification with surface measure is not proved; see Scope).

Wave L11 item K4 (part ii), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TerminalWickRegularization.lean: the Green-regularization paragraph of the proof of L:terminal-wick (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, lines 4392-4398: replace G by p_eta * G; same masses; weak convergence to G; dominated convergence for the mixed second moments with two Green widths; L^2 convergence to the Bochner integral of the lemma).

Construction. Each regularized spatial factor p_eta * G_h (h = s_(j+1) - s_j > 0) is h law(h V + sqrt(eta) Z) with V ~ G_1 and Z ~ N(0, I_d) independent (regFactor_eq_conv, from the scaling G_h(hA) = h G_1(A); the convolution is Mathlib's Measure.conv). So the regularized chain measure g_n^(T,x,eta) (chainMeasureReg) is the image of one fixed noise measure timeMeasure n T x G_1^(x n) x N(0,I_d)^(x n) (noiseMeasure) under (s, v, zeta) -> (s_j, x - sum_(l>=j) ((s_(l+1) - s_l) v_l + sqrt(eta) zeta_l))_j (regMap, regPt, with the times projected into [0,T]). At eta = 0 this is the g_n^(T,x) of TerminalWickInputs (chainMeasure_eq_map_noise). Since Lean's real square root is 0 on negative reals, g_n^(T,x,eta) is g_n^(T,x) for every eta <= 0; the limits are taken along eta -> 0+ (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)), so this convention does not enter them. The construction is stated for every d; the masses use d in {1,2,3}.

Formalized, with nothing supplied: the masses T^(2n)/(2n)! for every eta (chainMeasureReg_univ, chainMeasureReg_univ_eq_chainMass); no time atoms (timeAtomless_chainMeasureReg); weak convergence of the chain measures (tendsto_integral_chainMeasureReg); Y_n^eta -> Y_n in L^2(Omega) (tendsto_chainIntegral_reg); and the two-width mixed moments E[Y_m^(eta_1) Y_n^(eta_2)] -> E[Y_m Y_n] (tendsto_mixed_moment_reg). Wrappers: terminal_wick_regularization_paper (the four facts) and terminal_wick_reg_paper (the conclusions of TerminalWickInputs.terminal_wick_paper_measurable for the regularized measures, any eta). Both take the hypotheses of L:terminal-wick (d in {1,2,3}, T > 0, x, a probability P, a centered real Gaussian field with V < infinity and the cell continuity); IsProbabilityMeasure P is recorded as carried and unused in the module. The Lean docstring of terminal_wick_regularization_paper calls it an "exact-hypothesis wrapper": its hypotheses are exactly those of L:terminal-wick, which is what the phrase means here; it does not claim to formalize the whole paragraph (see below).

Proof-route difference: the TeX's dominated convergence for the finite Wick sums of the mixed moments is replaced by dominated convergence of the L^2-valued Bochner integrals on the common noise space (bound sqrt((2n-1)!!) V^(n/2); the chain product is continuous in L^2 off the cut times, TerminalWickInputs.continuousAt_prodL2); the mixed-moment limit then follows by continuity of the inner product. The TeX states the paragraph in dimension three; Lean proves it for d in {1,2,3}.

Not formalized: the identification of the whole regularized chain measure with the TeX's chain measure built from the factors p_eta * G_(s_(j+1)-s_j) (each factor is identified by regFactor_eq_conv, but the analogue of TerminalWickInputs.chainMeasureRaw_apply for the product is not proved); and the final clause "exactly the fixed-noise Green convention used in the source", which concerns the source's definitions. Junk values: the masses are ofReal of nonnegative reals; every Y_n^eta is a genuine Bochner integral (conclusion (1) of terminal_wick_reg_paper). The paragraph is part of the proof of L:terminal-wick, not a conclusion of the lemma, so this module gives proof steps of that lemma.

Refutations (refutations/terminal-wick-regularization/), all manuscript-domain perturbations (a wrong weight or mass of the regularized measures); none relies on a junk value: FactorWithoutWeight (without the weight h the factor has mass 1, not h; d = 1, h = 2, eta = 1), RegMassGrows (the smoothing does not add mass: T^2/2 + eta is wrong at T = eta = 1) and RegMassNoGreenMass (forgetting the Green weights gives T^n/n!).

Route definitions without claim rows (they appear in the statements of the rows below): Noise (the noise space), noiseMeasure, regMap, regPt.

TimeCompletion (whole result)

Covers two modules, TimeCompletion and MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted, on notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex at 39f2597a. It formalizes L:masked-time-completion (lines 188-204, display E:masked-time-schur at 197-200, proof 206-241) with the completion H_a constructed. It re-issues L:masked-trig-products (lines 459-489) and L:masked-continuous-wave (lines 494-558, display E:masked-continuous-wave at 501-505) in this concrete H_a, with nothing supplied. Standing hypotheses: T > 0 and 0 < a < 1 (the section's a = alpha0, lines 6-9). The section also assumes H:homog and Gamma != 0, but lines 7-9 say the purely temporal estimates hold independently of Gamma. These lemmas are purely temporal, so neither hypothesis is assumed.

What is constructed. L2fun T is complex L^2(0,T) as a space of functions (MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))). On it, TimeSchur.timeForm (<f,g>_a = int int f(t) conj g(s) |t-s|^(-a)) is a Hermitian sesquilinear form (conj_timeForm, timeForm_add_right, timeForm_smul_right) and is positive semidefinite (timeForm_re_nonneg). These are the axioms of a pre-inner product (core; the arguments are swapped because Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first slot). Ha p is Mathlib's UniformSpace.Completion of the resulting pre-Hilbert space Pre p, so it is a complex Hilbert space, and functions at seminorm distance zero are identified (coe_eq_of_ae, the null quotient). emb p is the inclusion of L^2(0,T). Its squared norm is Re timeForm a T f f (emb_norm_sq). This is faithful to the TeX's "null-quotient completion" for the following reason. The TeX completes the real compact smooth tests and then complexifies. dense_span_realTestSet proves that the complex span of the images of the real tests supported in (0,T) is dense in Ha p. So Ha p is the closure of the complexified tests, and its norm on a test is the TeX's form. H_a is built directly over C. The TeX's real space is represented by the real functions of emb_norm_sq_real and the positivity clause, not by a separate real Hilbert space.

The paper wrapper masked_time_completion_paper has exactly the hypotheses 0 < a < 1, T > 0 and states, in eight conjuncts: - positivity on real compact smooth tests, with integrability of the integrand; - separability of Ha p; - E:masked-time-schur for ||emb f||; - the continuous linear extension extL2 p on a.e.-classes of L^2(0,T), agreeing with emb, with the same constant; - the complexification clause: ||emb f||^2 equals the complex double integral with f(t) conj f(s), it is the sum of the squared norms of the real and imaginary parts, and the integrand is integrable; - for real g, ||emb g||^2 equals the real double integral; - interval amplitudes: a bounded a.e.-strongly measurable amplitude on [c,d], extended by zero, lies in L^2(0,T) and hence has an image under emb; - density of the complex span of the real tests' images.

Proof route and differences from the TeX. - Positivity follows the TeX (lines 216-229). Gamma subordination (TimeFractional.rpow_neg_eq_subordination) and the exponential-kernel identity exp_abs_eq give, for t != s, |t-s|^(-a) = int Gamma(a)^(-1) 2 lambda^a 1_(u<=t) e^(-lambda(t-u)) 1_(u<=s) e^(-lambda(s-u)) d lambda du (kern_eq_mixture, an identity in [0, infinity]). The TeX argues for each lambda separately. Lean makes one Fubini exchange over [0,T]^2 x (0,infinity) x R in the general criterion re_form_nonneg_of_mixture (s-finite measures, nonnegative measurable weight and profiles). Absolute integrability comes from the Schur bound, as in the TeX (cross_integrable). Positivity is proved for every complex f in L^2(0,T), which is stronger than the TeX's real tests. - Separability uses the separability of Lp (Mathlib) and the Lipschitz representative map ofLp, not a countable family of tests. - The TeX extends the inclusion from tests to L^2 by density. Here H_a is built over L^2(0,T), so the inclusion is defined on all of L^2. The density of the tests is proved afterwards by exists_test_approx, which uses three ingredients: Mathlib's MemLp.exist_eLpNorm_sub_le; a ContDiffBump equal to one on [eta, T-eta] and supported in [eta/2, T-eta/2]; and uniform integrability (MemLp.eLpNorm_indicator_le) for the boundary layer. - masked_trig_products_completed_paper instantiates MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper with E = Ha p, V = L2fun T and emb p. hmem comes from MaskedModulation.memLp_modeFn, and hnorm from emb_norm_sq. - masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper instantiates MaskedContinuousWave.masked_continuous_wave_paper in the same way. Its hmem quantifies over every A in C^1(I). For each such A, MaskedModulation.envelope_of_contDiffOn (using h > 0) gives continuity and boundedness on I, and memLp_modeFn gives membership.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: - L^2(0,T) is MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T)), and [0,T] versus (0,T) is immaterial. - The kernel's diagonal value 0^(-a) = 0 is irrelevant, because the diagonal is null for the product measure (ae_ne_diag). The mixture identity is used only off the diagonal. - Integrability on [0,T]^2 is a conjunct of the wrapper's double-integral conclusions (items 1 and 5), so no Bochner integral is Lean's junk 0. - mixWeight uses |lambda|^a, equal to lambda^a on the only values that mixMeasure charges, so no rpow of a negative base occurs. - M and D in the trig-products wrapper are suprema of bounded nonempty sets (envelope_of_contDiffOn).

Hypotheses carried but unused: - tsupport f in (0,T) in item 1 of the paper wrapper (positivity holds on all of L^2(0,T)). - h <= 1 in masked_trig_products_completed_paper.

T > 0 is needed to build Ha p (it is a field of TimeParams), although the bounds themselves do not use it.

Not formalized: a separate real Hilbert space H_a and its abstract complexification (both are represented as described above). The H_a-valued Schwartz functions and the noise of P:masked-noise-completion are also not formalized.

The two calibration lemmas timeForm_one and norm_sq_waveFn_cc_zero give the exact value at the constant function and at 1_[0,h]. They have no manuscript label and are used by the refutations (refutations/time-completion/, refutations/masked-continuous-wave-completed/).

TwoSimplexTime (proof steps of P:d1-upper, P:low-alpha-upper and C:d1-first-calibration: the time integrals of the diagram model)

Wave L13 items D2 and D3 (deduplicated at the L13 integration), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TwoSimplexTime.lean: the dimension-free temporal half of the two-chain upper bounds, from the proof of P:d1-upper (main TeX notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, proof lines 5468-5550), which the proofs of P:low-alpha-upper (lines 5774-5779: "the temporal symmetry, cube integral and split count ... do not involve the spatial dimension") and C:d1-first-calibration (lines 5845-5853) cite. Everything is proved; nothing is supplied. All statements are about the deterministic diagram integrals of DiagramModel (registered model choice M4: ordered chains with open time simplices, pairings as fixed-point-free involutions with self-pairings, the exact time kernel \|s_i - s_j\|^(-alpha_0) in [0, infinity]); no statement here is about the solution u or its chaos terms.

Steps formalized: the increments of a time vector in [0,t]^m_< x [0,t]^n_< sum to the two terminal times, hence to at most 2t (lines 5484-5485, sum_incr, sum_incr_le), and to at most t for one chain (line 5845, sum_incr_le_one); the full symmetry of F_k = sum_(D in Pi_k) prod_((i,j) in D) \|s_i - s_j\|^(-alpha_0) (lines 5493-5494, sum_timeWeight_comp_perm); E:d1-time-symmetry (lines 5503-5506) as the inequality m! n! int_(simplices) F_k <= int_(cube) F_k (factorial_mul_twoSimplex_le, from the general symmetrization card_mul_setLIntegral_le and the pairwise disjointness of the m! n! chain-reordered simplices chainPerms_disjoint); the TeX states it as an equality, and only <= is used, in the TeX as here; the pair integral int_([0,t]^2) \|s - r\|^(-alpha_0) = Z t^(2-alpha_0) as an equality (lintegral_timeCov_square on the closed square, pairInt_eq on the open one, lines 5495-5497), Z = 2/((1-alpha_0)(2-alpha_0)) of E:d1-constants (line 5325, Zc); the cube integral of one pairing (Z t^(2-alpha_0))^k (lines 5498-5501, lintegral_cube_timeWeight); P_k = (2k)!/(2^k k!) and the binomial identity sum_m 1/(m!(2k-m)!) = 2^(2k)/(2k)! (lines 5514-5518, card_Pi2_eq, sum_inv_factorial); the product of the counts (lines 5520-5528, time_total_le); the generic bounds diagram_le, coeffA_le (two chains, increments summing to at most 2t) and oneChain_le (one chain, at most t), which take a uniform bound B of the spatial part as a hypothesis (the callers D1Upper and LowAlphaUpper prove it); and the scalar series inequality sum_k z^k/(k!)^q <= exp(q z^(1/q)) for q >= 1, z >= 0 in partial-sum form (lines 5540-5545, sum_div_factorial_rpow_le). The TeX's temporal truncation delta and smoothed temporal factors are not used: the model's diagrams carry the exact kernel. The simplices are open, as in the TeX (line 551); the open cube replaces the TeX's closed cube up to a null boundary. Status internal marks the Lean-route helpers.

Refutations (in refutations/d1-upper/ and refutations/low-alpha-upper/, listed with those sections) that target declarations of this module: BinomialPower (sum_inv_factorial_gen with 2^k in place of 2^(2k), false at k = 1), TelescopeHalf and OneChainBound (sum_incr_le with t in place of 2t, false for m = n = 1, t = 1 at s = (4/5, 4/5), resp. (3/4, 3/4)) and TimeConstantHalf (lintegral_timeCov_square with Z/2, false at alpha_0 = 1/2, t = 1): (a) manuscript-claim perturbations in the manuscript domain; SubunitExponent (sum_div_factorial_rpow_le for q = 1/2, false at z = 1, n = 2): (c) a broader Lean generalization outside the manuscript domain, where q = 3 - alpha >= 2. None relies on a junk value.

TypeContinuity (narrower result: P:moment-growth-logconvex and C:static-moment-constant-continuity for an abstract moment function, the solution moments not constructed and their identification not formalized; L:positive-series-type whole)

Formalizes the section S:temporal-type-continuity of notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex (main file, at 39f2597a) together with the lemma it uses from the preceding section S:near-static-lower. The section's parameters (lines 8239-8246) are nu = 3 - alpha, a_max = min(1, 2 - alpha), beta(a) = 4 - alpha - a, kappa(a) = beta(a)/nu and kappa_st = (4 - alpha)/nu. In Lean they are nuOf, amaxOf, betaOf, kappaOf and kappaSt.

L:positive-series-type (statement lines 8419-8431, proof lines 8433-8470) is formalized in full by positive_series_type_paper, with the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied:

  • The hypotheses are nu >= 1, c_k >= 0 and c_0 = 1. "F(z) < inf for every z >= 0" is stated as summability of k -> c_k z^k.
  • The type tau (seriesType) is an EReal limsup, with no truncation and no boundedness side condition.
  • The coefficient type K (coeffType) is in [0, inf]. Its terms ((k!)^nu c_k)^(1/k) are nonnegative reals, so ENNReal.ofReal does not truncate them. The k = 0 term (1/0 = 0 in Lean) does not affect the limsup.
  • Both directions are proved, and the equality is stated with K.toReal together with K < top.
  • Proof-route difference: the first half uses the eventual bound F(z) <= e^(L z^(1/nu)) instead of the TeX's global C_L e^(L z^(1/nu)). This suffices because the test points (nu k/L)^nu tend to infinity.
  • coeffType_exp_family and seriesType_exp_family check non-vacuity: c_k = A^k/(k!)^nu gives K = A and tau = nu A^(1/nu).

P:moment-growth-logconvex (statement lines 8769-8781, proof lines 8783-8839) and C:static-moment-constant-continuity (statement lines 8842-8861, proof lines 8863-8874) are proved with every conclusion, from named inputs. The moment E[u^(a)(T,x)^p] is an abstract real function mom p a T at a fixed point x. mom p 0 is the static moment, as the TeX defines u^(0) = U (lines 8249-8251). Because x is fixed, the spatial stationarity used at line 8805 is not needed. The rates of E:moment-growth-types (lines 8757-8766) are EReal limsup and liminf (growthUpper, growthLower). Statements about real values use toReal only together with a proved finiteness and positivity, so no junk toReal enters.

The inputs are the fields of TypeContinuityInputs, each no stronger than its source:

  • L0_pos and static_law: E:static-ratio-input (lines 8256-8264), verbatim.
  • series: E:full-moment-positive-series with nonnegative coefficients and c_0 = 1 (the definition E:full-moment-coefficients), for 0 <= a < a_max, from L:full-moment-coefficient-holder (lines 8667-8673). "< inf" is stated as summability.
  • holder: E:full-moment-coefficient-holder (lines 8674-8678), verbatim.
  • minorant: E:static-minorant-rate of P:static-minorant-lower (lines 8478-8482), in the equivalent real form "every y < p^(kappa_st) L_0 is eventually below T^(-kappa(a)) log mom".
  • full_upper: E:full-upper-bound of T:full-upper (lines 4474-4488) applied at temporal exponent a, as the TeX does at line 8794. The finite constant C R_alpha^(1/(3-alpha)) is merged into one finite C.
  • cauchy_schwarz: (E u)^2 <= E u^2, the step at line 8795.

What is proved from these inputs:

  • Positivity and finiteness of the rates are derived exactly as in the TeX proof (lines 8791-8797), by upper_rate_pos_fin; they are not supplied.
  • The identification of the type of F_{p,a} with Lambda-bar_p(a) through z = T^(beta(a)) (lines 8803-8807) is proved by growthUpper_eq_seriesType, not supplied.
  • The corollary's own inputs, P:static-minorant-lower and Lambda-bar_p(0) = C_p, are derived from minorant and static_law.

Further details:

  • Convexity of log Lambda-bar_p is stated on [0, a_max), the range of the inequality.
  • Continuity on (0, a_max) is proved with ConvexOn.continuousOn_interior instead of the TeX's secant slopes (lines 8828-8837).
  • Standing assumptions: the section's "nonzero spatial covariance in H:homog" (lines 8239, 8657) is carried as HomogCovariance and Gamma != 0. Only alpha < 2 is used, which gives nu >= 1, a_max > 0 and beta(a) > 0. Gamma != 0 is carried and not used.
  • The general forms growth_logconvex_core and static_constant_core state the arguments for an arbitrary family, with positivity and finiteness of the rates as hypotheses.
  • Every conclusion formula is proved for the abstract moment function; its identification with the solution moments is not formalized.
  • Not formalized: the inputs above, that is L:full-moment-coefficient-holder (stochastic diagram limits), the Chen-Hu static law, T:full-upper, P:static-minorant-lower and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the solution. Lean also does not show that these inputs are jointly satisfiable.

UniformSeriesTail (narrower result: L:uniform-series-tail for an abstract L^2 family with the two facts of L:terminal-wick supplied; identification with the terminal-chain terms not formalized)

Formalizes L:uniform-series-tail (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a; statement lines 4419-4443 with the display E:uniform-series-tail, lines 4434-4440; proof lines 4445-4464), with every conclusion proved and one supplied input from L:terminal-wick (lines 4291-4336), the structure TerminalWickInput. The TeX proof cites exactly two facts from L:terminal-wick (lines 4446-4447): absolute L^2 convergence of every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. TerminalWickInput mu Y r states these two facts for one family Y : N -> L^2 and the given r: sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity (L:terminal-wick gives it for every real or complex r, lines 4334-4335) and E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0 for all m, n (its Wick formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative, and zero when m + n is odd, lines 4329-4332). Nothing else about the Gaussian field, the chain measures g_n^{T,x} or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean statements hold for an arbitrary family of real L^2(Omega) elements with these two facts. For the chain integrals Y_n of a centered Gaussian field with nonnegative covariance, TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg (wave L8) proves TerminalWickInput from that lemma's own inputs, and L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper composes the two; the identification of the regularized family Y_n^{eps,delta} with such terms is not formalized here. In wave L11, TerminalWickInputs states the lemma for chain integrals over the constructed g_n^{T,x} with its hypotheses only (uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_constructed_paper, uniform_series_tail_second_moment_constructed_paper), a whole result (section TerminalWickInputs). The fixed point (T,x) is implicit in the family. L^2(Omega) is Mathlib's Lp R 2 mu (real-valued), E|f|^2 is written as the Bochner integral of f(omega)^2 (equal to ||f||^2 by integral_sq_eq_norm_sq, a genuine integral), E[fg] as the integral of f(omega) g(omega) (equal to the inner product by integral_mul_eq_inner), B_r^{1/2} as Real.sqrt B, r^{-n} as (r^n)^(-1) and the tail sum_{n>N} Z_n as tsum_n Z (n + (N+1)). uniform_series_tail_paper takes the regularized terms as Y eps delta n for real eps, delta, assumes r > 1, TerminalWickInput and E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B for every eps, delta > 0 (the uniform bound sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r), and Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n in L^2 for each n, where eps, delta down to 0 is read as the joint limit along the product filter nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) (other readings, such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute convergence of sum X_n; u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n in L^2 along that filter; the two term bounds and the two tail bounds of E:uniform-series-tail, the bounds for Y for every eps, delta > 0; and absolute convergence of each sum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n ("including absolute convergence", lines 4451-4452). uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper proves the last sentence (lines 4441-4442): if also E|u^{eps,delta}(1)|^2 <= B_1 for all eps, delta > 0, then E|u|^2 <= B_1. The probability measure (IsProbabilityMeasure mu) is the manuscript's setting and is carried but not used by either wrapper. The general forms uniform_series_tail and uniform_series_tail_second_moment hold in any complete real inner product space, for any index type of regularizations and any nontrivial filter, with the hypotheses required only eventually along the filter. Proof route: the term bound is the TeX's (the double sum E|u(r)|^2 = sum_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n] dominates its diagonal term, norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg), and the tail bounds are the geometric series and the triangle inequality (tail_bound). The limit u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u is proved by Mathlib's dominated convergence for series (tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence) with the summable majorant B^{1/2} r^{-n}, instead of the TeX's explicit head/tail split at level N (lines 4454-4461), which uses the same majorant. No conclusion is narrower than the TeX. Junk values are not reached: the scaled series is absolutely summable by hypothesis and the unscaled ones are proved absolutely summable, so every tsum is a genuine sum; B >= 0 follows from the moment bound, so Real.sqrt B is the true square root; r > 1 makes (r^n)^(-1) and 1 - r^(-1) positive. Not formalized: the regularized family itself (the terms Y_n^{eps,delta} as terms of L:terminal-wick) and the application of the lemma to the regularized solution in later proofs; L:terminal-wick is in TerminalWick, with its own inputs.

VariationalDilation (narrower result: L:variational-control-dilation, rate and variance identification not formalized)

Formalizes Lemma L:variational-control-dilation (Radon and Rayleigh dilation; notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex lines 314-367 at 39f2597a) together with the definitions it uses, in two modules: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WeakSobolev.lean (a hand-built real Sobolev space and the real Rayleigh value set) and StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalDilation.lean (the control class, the dilation, the mean, variance, rate and integrated rate, and the lemma). The wrapper variational_control_dilation_paper states the lemma with the section's standing hypotheses (line 4: a nonzero covariance satisfying H:homog, modelled by HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance, with a = alpha0): for r > 0, D_r is a bijection of the class with inverse D_(1/r), and the four identities of E:variational-dilation-values hold. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.

Abstractions and why they are faithful. The class E:variational-positive-class (lines 5-10) consists of smooth functions on R x R^d with compact support inside (0,1) x R^d, i.e. elements of C_c^infinity((0,1) x R^d) extended by zero. CPos_nonempty proves that the class is nonempty (lines 13-17) using a different bump. The mean h_{Psi,s} and the variance v_Psi are the displays E:compact-raw-mean and E:compact-raw-cost (notes/integrated_compact_mean_family.tex lines 533-543), with (Gamma * phi)(x) = int phi(x-y) Gamma(dy) and int_0^1 taken over Ioo 0 1. WeakSobolev (written before the package used Mathlib's Bessel-potential H^{1,2}, with which H1Mathlib, wave L13, identifies it) defines H^1(R^d; R) by weak gradients (int f d_v phi = -int <g,v> phi for every test function phi and direction v). It proves that an L^2 weak gradient is unique a.e. (weakGradient_ae_unique), so a Rayleigh set built from pairs (f, g) is the manuscript's set of f.

The rate lambda_{Psi,s} is defined in Lean by the real Rayleigh form E:variational-real-rayleigh: rate = sqrt(sSup R_s), where R_s is the set of values int h_s f^2 - ||grad f||_2^2 over unit f in H^1(R^d; R). The manuscript's primary definition is lambda = sqrt(-E_s), with E_s the spectral bottom of the self-adjoint -Delta - h_s on H^2. The manuscript proves that the two agree (P:variational-unmasked-rate), but that equality is not formalized, because it needs unbounded self-adjoint operators and spectral theory. Likewise v_Psi is the integral form of E:compact-raw-cost, and its identification with E W(Psi)^2 (L:compact-raw-profile, which needs the Gaussian noise) is not formalized. The TeX proof itself works with exactly these two forms (Lebesgue substitution in the pairing, and the real Rayleigh bijection).

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: - A Rayleigh trial must have h_s f^2 integrable. The condition keeps Lean's junk value 0 for a non-integrable integral out of the set. For the manuscript's h_s (Psi in CPos, s in [0,1]) it is automatic: VariationalMean.isRayleighTrial_mean_iff_paper proves that a trial is then exactly a unit f in L^2 with an L^2 weak gradient, because h_s is bounded and continuous (L:variational-global-mean, formalized in VariationalMean). - Psi is continuous; this follows from smoothness. - The identities hold for every real s, not only for s in [0,1].

Junk values. Every identity is an exact identity of Bochner integrals and of sSup. It would remain true if an integrand were not integrable, or if the Rayleigh set were empty or unbounded (Lean's value 0 on both sides). The companion does not exclude these junk cases. It proves only conditional transfers, in variational_control_dilation_integrable_paper: - every integrand in the definitions of h, v and I is integrable for D_r Psi exactly when it is for Psi; - the Rayleigh sets themselves scale, so a Rayleigh set is nonempty and bounded above for D_r Psi exactly when it is for Psi.

So if a quantity is a genuine integral or supremum for Psi, the identity relates it to a genuine integral or supremum for D_r Psi. For s in [0,1], VariationalMean proves that the integrand of h_s(x) is integrable and that h_s is bounded (L:variational-global-mean, variational_global_mean_paper), so the mean identity relates genuine integrals there. That the variance and rate integrands are integrable, and that the Rayleigh sets are nonempty and bounded above, is not proved in this module. For Psi in C_pos under the section's hypotheses these are proved in VariationalRate (rawCost_genuine, unmasked_rate); the identifications v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2 and lambda = sqrt(-E_s) remain outside Lean. The integrability equivalences are Lean-route auxiliaries: the TeX proof (lines 339-346) works with nonnegative integrands and Tonelli and states none of them. Their rows below say so.

The TeX's square-root step uses positivity of the rates. Lean instead uses sqrt(sSup(r^2 S)) = r sqrt(sSup S), which holds for every set S.

Hypotheses carried but unused: Gamma != 0, and every clause of H:homog except the set scaling. The general theorems assume only the set scaling SetScaling and continuity of Psi.

Not formalized: - lambda = sqrt(-E_s) (P:variational-unmasked-rate; positivity of the Rayleigh-form rate is in VariationalRate); - v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2 (L:compact-raw-profile; finiteness and positivity of the integral form are in VariationalRate); - the mixed-derivative bounds of L:variational-global-mean (its display is formalized in VariationalMean; the bounds are proved in VariationalMeanDerivatives, wave L13); - integrability of the integrands of v and I (that of h for s in [0,1] is in VariationalMean), and nonemptiness and boundedness of the Rayleigh sets (only their transfer under D_r is proved); - the TeX's side remark that U_r preserves H^2 and that H_{D_r Psi,s} U_r = r^2 U_r H_{Psi,s} (not part of the statement).

The auxiliary definition VariationalDilation.dilHomeo (the spatial dilation as a homeomorphism of R x R^d) only names a map used in the proof and has no row. The structure fields IsRayleighTrial.memLp_f, memLp_g, weakGrad, unit and integrable_pot are projections of IsRayleighTrial and have no rows either. Four refutations in refutations/variational-dilation/ prove that the following wrong variants are false: - the mean scaling with r in place of r^2; - the variance scaling without the Lebesgue factor (r^(d+4-alpha)); - the rate scaling with r^2; - the bijection with r > 0 dropped.

VariationalFloor (foundation: the variational floor)

Five deterministic foundations of wave L6 (item L6-d), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalFloor.lean. They carry no manuscript label of their own: they are the facts that the variational rates of notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex (Section S:unmasked-variational) and the spatial results of notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex (Section S:spatial-occupation-foundation) use, at revision 39f2597a. Every hypothesis is stated; nothing is supplied. They are consumed by VariationalRate, SpatialSmoothRatio, SpatialStaticControls and SpatialOccupationCompleted.

  • (F1) dilation_floor, rayleighSet_floor: the dilation floor. For a nonzero locally finite Gamma with the set scaling Gamma(c A) = c^(d-alpha) Gamma(A) of H:homog and alpha < 2, and a continuous, nonnegative, nonzero, compactly supported z with y -> z(x-y) Gamma-integrable for every x (so Gamma * z is a genuine integral, not Lean's junk value 0), one unit test f in C_c^infinity, an L^2 weak gradient g and one eps > 0 give eps <= int V f^2 - int norm(g)^2 for every potential V >= Gamma * z with V f^2 integrable. The test is U_l phi / norm(phi)_2 for a fixed bump phi and small l; the potential term is at least l^alpha (int z) Gamma(closed unit ball)/norm(phi)_2^2 (Tonelli in (x, y) and the scaling of Gamma on balls) and the gradient term is l^2 norm(grad phi)_2^2/norm(phi)_2^2. It is a pure inequality (no limit, no supremum). This is the elementary scaling principle behind the positivity in P:variational-unmasked-rate (TeX lines 203-208), which the manuscript obtains instead from the compact trial of P:compact-original-common-trial; it also discharges the input RayleighFloor of SpatialStaticControls.
  • (F2) measure_ball_pos, measure_closedBall_pos: Gamma(B_r) > 0 for every r > 0 when Gamma != 0 has the set scaling (exhaustion by balls and scaling: the argument of L:spatial-static-controls, occupation file lines 108-110).
  • (F3) autocorr_nonneg_of_posDef: for a real Q in C_c^infinity, int c_Q dGamma >= 0 when Gamma is positive definite in the sense of the field Gamma_posdef of H:homog, where c_Q = SpatialFourierBound.autocorr Q (c_Q(y) = int Q(x) Q(x-y) dx, the inner integral of B_Gamma(Q,Q) in E:spatial-physical-pair); route: HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap and the cast of the real pairing to C. autocorr_pos: int c_Q dGamma > 0 for continuous, nonnegative, nonzero, compactly supported Q and nonzero locally finite Gamma with the set scaling (no positive definiteness; TeX lines 107-110 and 247-250 of the occupation file).
  • (F4) hasWeakGradient_of_test, with the gradient field grad: a test function has its classical gradient as weak gradient (WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient).
  • (F5) ae_eq_zero_of_hasWeakGradient_zero: for d >= 1, an L^2 function with weak gradient 0 is 0 almost everywhere (half (b) of the D8-lite foundation; half (a), the density of test functions in the weak-gradient H^1, is H1Density.h1TestDense, wave L7). This is the fact used in P:spatial-smooth-ratio (occupation file lines 245-247); the Lean route differs from the TeX's Fourier-support argument: the mollifications rho_n * f are smooth with derivative (D rho_n) * f = 0, hence constant, they converge to f almost everywhere, and a nonzero constant is not in L^2(R^d) for d >= 1. The hypothesis d >= 1 is necessary (refutation ZeroDimension).

Also integral_pos_of_pos_zero and conv_pos (positivity of integrals against such Gamma, from F2), and exists_radius_fn. Junk values: the statements involving conv Gamma z assume the integrability of y -> z(x-y); the F3 integral is a genuine integral for locally finite Gamma (SpatialFourierBound.integrable_autocorr); the floor's conclusion is about the Rayleigh value of one explicit trial, not about a supremum. Lemmas labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve only the Lean proofs and are not TeX steps.

VariationalMean (narrower result: L:variational-global-mean without the mixed derivatives, which are proved in VariationalMeanDerivatives; L:variational-heat-envelope whole)

Formalizes Lemma L:variational-heat-envelope (Gaussian envelope for the original covariance; notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 28-40, proof 42-82) in full, and the display E:variational-global-mean of Lemma L:variational-global-mean (global regularity of the original mean; statement 85-95, proof 97-118), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalMean.lean. It reuses the definitions of VariationalDilation: the convolution conv ((Gamma * phi)(x) = int phi(x-y) Gamma(dy)), the mean mean (h_{Psi,s}, E:compact-raw-mean) and the control class CPos (E:variational-positive-class). The only new manuscript object is the heat kernel heatK eps x = (2 pi eps)^(-d/2) e^(-norm(x)^2/(2 eps)) (lines 30-31). Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.

The wrappers state the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-5: a nonzero covariance satisfying H:homog, with a = alpha0) as HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu and Gamma != 0; the mean is taken with exponent alpha0. variational_heat_envelope_paper (with eps > 0) gives, for every x, the integrability of y -> p_eps(x-y) against Gamma (so (Gamma * p_eps)(x), in particular the value at 0, is finite), the integrability of the spectral integrand against mu, the identity of E:variational-heat-envelope as complex numbers with no normalization factor, 0 <= (Gamma * p_eps)(x) <= (Gamma * p_eps)(0), and (Gamma * p_eps)(0) > 0. variational_global_mean_paper (with Psi in CPos) gives real M, C_Psi >= 0 with 0 <= h_s(x) <= M and |h_s(x) - h_t(x)| <= C_Psi |s - t| for s, t in I = [0,1] and every x (the sup-norm bound of the display, stated pointwise in x). It also gives the integrability of every integrand in the definition of h_s(x), the continuity of x -> h_s(x) and the integrability of h_s f^2 for every f in L^2. variational_global_mean_lipschitz_paper adds a joint Lipschitz bound on I x R^d; the TeX does not state it. isRayleighTrial_mean_iff_paper shows that the explicit side condition integrable_pot of WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial is automatic for h_s, s in [0,1].

General forms: heat_envelope assumes Gamma, mu tempered (IsTempered) and the spectral convention IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu, without Gamma != 0; heat_conv_pos assumes Gamma tempered and Gamma != 0; heat_identity assumes only the spectral convention; global_mean assumes Gamma, mu tempered, the spectral convention, Psi in CPos and a < 1.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: eps > 0. Finiteness of (Gamma * p_eps)(0) and of h_s(x) is stated as integrability of the integrands. A Lean Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0, so without these conclusions the bounds could hold through that junk value. M and C_Psi are nonnegative real numbers.

Hypotheses carried but unused. The wrappers use the H:homog fields Gamma_tempered, mu_tempered and spectral; the global-mean wrappers also use alpha0_lt_one. Gamma != 0 is used only for the strict positivity in L:variational-heat-envelope, and the global-mean wrappers carry it unused. The other fields (dim, alpha0_pos, Gamma_radon, Gamma_even, Gamma_posdef, mu_radon, mu_even, scaling, threshold, alpha_range) are carried, unused.

Proof-route differences. - The identity of E:variational-heat-envelope comes from MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectral_translated_gauss: the spectral convention applied to one Gaussian Schwartz test, with Mathlib's Gaussian Fourier integral. The TeX pairs with an arbitrary Schwartz test and uses uniqueness of continuous distributions (lines 68-77). - Integrability against Gamma and mu comes from the package's integral form of temperedness, not from polynomial ball growth (lines 54-60). - The bound by the value at 0 follows line 79 but does not use evenness of mu: the spectral integral is real because it equals the real left side. - For the mean, |Psi(u,z)| <= C e^(-norm(z)^2/2) (spatial support) and the envelope at eps = 1 (gauss_conv) bound Gamma * Psi(u,.) uniformly, as in lines 99-103 for the underived case. - The change of variables r = s - u (lines 105-109) is integral_sub_left_eq_self. The integral runs over (-1,1) rather than R, since the integrand vanishes outside (-1,1) for s in [0,1]. The time constant is int_(-1)^1 |r|^(-a) dr = 2/(1-a) (a < 1). - The Lipschitz bound in time does not differentiate under the integral (the TeX's route, lines 103-116). It applies the Lipschitz bound of the smooth, compactly supported Psi (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport) inside both integrals, dominated by the same Gaussian envelope.

Narrower conclusion and not formalized: - the first sentence of L:variational-global-mean, "every mixed time and space derivative of h_s is globally bounded in space, uniformly on compact time intervals", is not formalized in this module (only the display E:variational-global-mean on I = [0,1], plus the spatial and joint Lipschitz bounds); it is proved in VariationalMeanDerivatives (wave L13); - the smoothness of x -> (Gamma * p_eps)(x) mentioned in the proof of L:variational-heat-envelope (lines 60-62), which is not part of its statement.

Five refutations in refutations/variational-mean/ prove that the following wrong variants are false: - strict positivity of (Gamma * p_eps)(0) without Gamma != 0 (Gamma = mu = 0); - the identity with an extra factor (2 pi)^(-d) (d = 1, Lebesgue Gamma, mu = delta_0); - a strict peak (Gamma * p_eps)(x) < (Gamma * p_eps)(0) for x != 0 (same example, where the convolution is constant); - integrability of |r|^(-a) on (-1,1) with a < 1 relaxed to a <= 1; - the one-sided constant 1/(1-a).

VariationalMeanDerivatives (whole result)

Wave L13 item C4, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalMeanDerivatives.lean: the first sentence of Lemma L:variational-global-mean (global regularity of the original mean; notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 85-95, proof lines 97-118), "Every mixed time and space derivative of h_s is globally bounded in space, uniformly on compact time intervals" (lines 87-88), and the whole lemma.

  1. L:variational-global-mean: the section's hypotheses (H:homog, Gamma != 0, a = alpha0, lines 4-5) and Psi in CPos (E:variational-positive-class), every conclusion, nothing supplied (variational_global_mean_whole_paper). The first sentence (variational_global_mean_derivatives_paper): the map (s,x) -> h_s(x) on R x R^d is C^infinity; the integrand u -> |s-u|^(-a) (Gamma * Psi(u,.))(x) defining h_s(x) is integrable on (0,1) for every real s and every x (so h_s(x) is a genuine integral, not a junk value, wherever a derivative is taken); and for every order n and every compact K in R there is a finite C >= 0 with \|D^n h(s,x)\| <= C for all s in K, x in R^d, where D^n h is the n-th Frechet derivative in the joint variable (s,x). Its operator norm bounds every mixed partial d_s^j d_x^beta h of total order n (mean_partial_bound: \|D^n h(s,x)(v_1, ..., v_n)\| <= C prod \|v_i\| for arbitrary directions, in particular (1,0) and (0,e_j)). The display E:variational-global-mean on I = [0,1] (0 <= h_s(x) <= M, \|h_s(x) - h_t(x)\| <= C_Psi \|s-t\|, the sup-norm bound stated pointwise in x) comes from VariationalMean.variational_global_mean_paper.

Reading of the sentence: "every mixed time and space derivative" is every iterated Frechet derivative of the joint map, and "globally bounded in space, uniformly on compact time intervals" is one constant for all x and all s in a given compact set; existence of the derivatives (ContDiff R infinity) is part of the conclusion. Objects reused unchanged: VariationalDilation.conv, VariationalDilation.mean (h_s, E:compact-raw-mean, defined for every real s), VariationalDilation.CPos and VariationalMean.gMass.

Hypotheses. Of H:homog only Gamma and mu tempered, the spectral convention and alpha0 < 1 are used; Gamma != 0 and the other fields are carried, unused, in variational_global_mean_derivatives_paper; in variational_global_mean_whole_paper Gamma != 0 is passed to VariationalMean.variational_global_mean_paper, which carries it unused. Of the sign and nonvanishing conditions of CPos, only the nonnegativity is used, by the display (nonnegativity of h_s); the nonvanishing condition is carried, unused. The smoothness and support conditions of CPos are used in the regularity and derivative proofs. Nothing is supplied.

Lean route, as in the TeX (lines 98-116), in two "differentiate under the integral" steps through one engine tInt (p -> int w(y) Phi(p - tau y) nu(dy), with Mathlib's hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le as the TeX's dominated convergence): (1) F(u,x) = (Gamma * Psi(u,.))(x), each derivative of Psi bounded by C e^(R^2/2) e^(-\|z\|^2/2) (the TeX's \|D Psi\| <= C_D p_eps at eps = 1), integrable against Gamma by L:variational-heat-envelope (VariationalMean.gauss_conv); (2) h(s,x) = int \|r\|^(-a) F((s,x) - (r,0)) dr after r = s - u (lines 105-109), with \|r\|^(-a) integrable on bounded intervals for a < 1 (lines 111-113). Declarations marked "auxiliary to the Lean proof route" have no manuscript label.

Refutations (refutations/variational-mean-derivatives/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Lean-route-only controls (b): DominationNeeded (integrable_tInt without its domination hypothesis fails: Phi = 1 on R against Lebesgue measure; the engine has no manuscript label) and SlabBoundStrict (slab_bound with \|s\| <= T - 1 in place of the strict \|s\| < T - 1 fails at d = 1, T = 1, (s,x) = (0,0), r = -1; a boundary convention of the Lean truncation). Control of a broader Lean generalization outside the manuscript domain (c): KernelExponentOneBounded (abs_rpow_integrableOn_Ioo with a <= 1 in place of a < 1 fails at a = 1, outside alpha0 < 1 of H:homog).

VariationalRate (narrower result: Rayleigh-form rates and integral-form costs, their spectral and stochastic identification, the operator half of P:variational-unmasked-rate and Q_2 >= S_2^pos not formalized)

Formalizes the Rayleigh-form part of Proposition P:variational-unmasked-rate (the unmasked Rayleigh rate; notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 126-139, proof 141-217) and Proposition P:variational-positive-scores (intrinsic variational lower bounds; statement 370-384, proof 386-462) except Q_2 >= S_2^pos, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalRate.lean. The wrappers state the section's standing assumptions (line 4: a nonzero covariance satisfying H:homog, a = alpha0) as HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu and Gamma != 0. Reused definitions (VariationalDilation): the class CPos (E:variational-positive-class), the mean h_{Psi,s} (mean), the integral form v_Psi of E:compact-raw-cost (rawCost), the rate lambda_{Psi,s} DEFINED as the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum E:variational-real-rayleigh (rate) and I_Psi (integratedRate). New definitions: scoreSet a Gamma c = {c I_Psi - v_Psi/2 : Psi in C_pos}, the coefficient-one set score1Set (= scoreSet a Gamma 1), S1pos = sSup score1Set, the test radius r_0 (testRadius) and the named input S1Bdd. These are the package's only score set, S1Bdd and S1pos; SpatialSmoothRatio and SpatialStaticControls use them.

variational_unmasked_rate_paper (general form unmasked_rate): for Psi in C_pos and s, t in [0,1], the real Rayleigh value set of h_s is nonempty and bounded above with a uniform floor and ceiling eps <= lambda_s^2 = sup <= M (eps > 0 is the TeX's eps_0; -M <= E_s <= -eps_0 in the TeX's notation E_s = -lambda_s^2); |h_s(x) - h_t(x)| <= C |s - t|; |lambda_s^2 - lambda_t^2| <= C |s - t| (from abs_sSup_rayleighSet_sub_le, |sup R_V - sup R_W| <= norm(V - W)_inf, TeX line 209); sqrt eps <= lambda_s <= sqrt M; |lambda_s - lambda_t| <= C/(2 sqrt eps) |s - t| (line 211); lambda is integrable on (0,1); and sqrt eps <= I_Psi <= sqrt M, so I_Psi is a positive finite integral of an integrable function. variational_positive_scores_paper (general form positive_scores), with nothing supplied: the value sets are nonempty; for every Psi in C_pos the values are genuine (rate integrable, every variance integrand integrable, rawCost_genuine) with I_Psi > 0 and v_Psi > 0 (rawCost_pos); the positive test of lines 397-406, I - v/2 = r_0 I_0/2 > 0 at D_{r_0} Psi_0; E:variational-score-set-scaling (lines 412-418); the set identity scoreSet c = c^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha)) scoreSet 1 (lines 422-424); and BddAbove (scoreSet c) iff S1Bdd for every c > 0. variational_positive_scores_sSup_paper, on S1Bdd: S_1^pos > 0 and S_c^pos = c^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha)) S_1^pos > 0 (first identity of E:variational-score-homogeneity).

Supplied input (named, one): S1Bdd a Gamma, BddAbove (score1Set a Gamma), word for word the boundedness claim of TeX lines 372-374 at c = 1, and by positive_scores equivalent to the boundedness for any c > 0. Its manuscript proof (lines 430-446) is stochastic: T:full-upper for the same canonical solution and the point lower bound E:variational-unmasked-point-lower of P:variational-remove-mask. Because I_Psi and v_Psi are proved genuine first, no junk value enters it; it is used only by the supremum statements. In wave L8 S1Bdd is proved deterministically under H:homog and Gamma != 0 (OccupationCeilingFinite.s1Bdd_paper over SpaceTimeCS, discharged in L8Completed.s1Bdd_paper_completed); the theorems of this module still take it as a hypothesis, and L8Completed.variational_positive_scores_sSup_st_paper_completed states the supremum part with nothing supplied.

Narrower conclusions (not formalized): the operator half of P:variational-unmasked-rate (self-adjointness of H_s = -Delta - h_s on H^2, form domain H^1, the spectral bottom E_s with -E_s = sup R_s, and so the primary definition lambda = sqrt(-E_s); foundation D8); the second identity Q_2 >= S_2^pos of E:variational-score-homogeneity (the stochastic point liminf); the identification v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2 (L:compact-raw-profile). Implicit hypotheses made explicit: I = [0,1]; the side condition integrable_pot of WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial is automatic for h_s; finiteness is stated as integrability and as bounded nonempty sets. Hypotheses of H:homog used: Gamma_tempered, mu_tempered, spectral, Gamma_radon, scaling, alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one, threshold; the others are carried, unused.

Proof-route differences: the positivity floor uses h_s >= Gamma * Psibar for s in [0,1] (Psibar = int_0^1 Psi(u,.) du, since |s - u|^(-alpha0) >= 1 on [0,1]^2 off the diagonal u = s, which is Lebesgue-null and excluded almost everywhere in the Lean proof, and Fubini) and the dilation floor VariationalFloor.dilation_floor, not the compact common trial of P:compact-original-common-trial (lines 203-208); v_Psi > 0 comes from the positivity of the continuous integrand Psi(s,x) h_s(x) at a point, not from L:compact-raw-profile.

WaveGreen (foundation: the wave Green measures)

Defines the wave Green measures G_s of the main file (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a) and states L:damped-homogeneous-norms (lemma, lines 1010-1055; proof, lines 1056-1154) with nothing supplied, except its closing smoothing remark (lines 1052-1054), which is formalized in a narrower reading in DampedMultiplier and WaveGreenFourier (the spectral identification of the smoothed covariance is not formalized there; it is proved in wave L12, DampedSmoothing). Sources of the measures at 39f2597a: d = 1, G(s,y) = (1/2) 1_{|y|<s} (proof of L:white-test, line 952; again at lines 4913 and 8910); d = 2, 3, the proof of L:higher-riesz (lines 6124-6132), which quotes Chen (2.5), p. 7: G_h^(2)(dy) = 1_{|y|<h} dy / (2 pi sqrt(h^2 - |y|^2)) and G_h^(3)(dy) = sigma_h(dy)/(4 pi h), sigma_h the surface measure of the radius-h sphere, and states "Both have mass h and satisfy G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)" (lines 6131-6132). The list of notation (notes/index/list-of-notation.tex, lines 102-103) describes G_t as the "Wave Green measure, with mass t and support in the closed radius-t ball". The mass identity G_s(R^d) = s is the step of the proof of L:damped-homogeneous-norms at line 1104, which DampedNormsHomog took as the supplied input GreenMass G.

Definition. waveGreen d s is, for d = 1, (1/2) Lebesgue measure restricted to the open ball |x| < s; for d = 2, Lebesgue measure with density 1_{|x|<s} (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - |x|^2))^(-1) (inside the ball the root is of a positive number, so no sqrt or division junk value enters); for d = 3, (s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) volume.toSphere; for every other d, the zero measure. For d = 3 this is a DEFINITIONAL CHOICE (Le's decision 4 for wave L6): Mathlib's Measure.toSphere (which satisfies sigma(A) = 3 vol{r w : 0 < r < 1, w in A} for measurable A, the cone measure) is taken as the surface measure of the unit sphere, and sigma_s = s^2 map (w -> s w) sigma_1 as that of the radius-s sphere, so sigma_s/(4 pi s) = (s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) sigma_1. Neither identification with a Hausdorff or Riemannian surface measure is proved. The manuscript has d in {1,2,3} (H:homog) and s >= 0; the value zero for other d and for s <= 0 is a Lean convention (waveGreen_other, waveGreen_of_nonpos), and every mass and scaling statement carries d = 1 \/ d = 2 \/ d = 3, so no statement holds through it.

Formalized, all proved, nothing supplied: the mass G_s(R^d) = s for d in {1,2,3} and every s >= 0 (waveGreen_mass; s = 0 included, where the measure is zero); finiteness for every d and s; support in the closed radius-s ball, G_s((closedBall 0 s)^c) = 0, for every d and s; the scaling G_s(sA) = s G_1(A) for s > 0 and measurable A (waveGreen_scaling; the TeX does not say which sets A, and Borel sets are the reading used; for d = 1 it holds for every set, scaling_one, and d = 1 is included although the TeX states the scaling for d = 2, 3); waveGreen_paper bundles the four. waveGreen_greenMass proves GreenMass (waveGreen d) for d in {1,2,3}, so N0_waveGreen gives N_0(theta) = theta^(-2) with nothing supplied, and damped_homogeneous_norms_wave states every conclusion of DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper with G := waveGreen d under H:homog alone (HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu, temporal exponent a = alpha0, no Gamma != 0, as in the TeX; the dimension condition is h.dim). The hypotheses of H:homog used are those of damped_homogeneous_norms_paper (listed in the DampedNormsHomog section) plus dim, which that section lists as unused but which is used here by waveGreen_greenMass d h.dim; the carried-but-unused fields are that section's list without dim; nothing further is carried. In addition, waveGreen_fourier_one proves for d = 1 that int e^(i <xi,x>) G_s(dx) = G_s hat(xi) with G_s hat = WaveKernel.waveHat (lines 983-984), with integrability, so the d = 1 measure and the multiplier used in N_1, N_2 are linked in Lean; WaveGreenFourier (wave L9) extends the identity to d = 2, 3.

Proof route (the TeX quotes masses and scaling from the source, so there is no TeX proof to follow): d = 1 by EuclideanSpace.volume_ball and Gamma(3/2) = sqrt(pi)/2; d = 2 by polar coordinates (integral_fun_norm_addHaar) with the antiderivative -sqrt(s^2 - r^2)/(2 pi) of r (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - r^2))^(-1), and the scaling by the change of variables x = s y (Measure.map_addHaar_smul); d = 3 by Measure.toSphere_apply_univ (total mass 3 vol(B_1) = 4 pi) and the preimage identity {w : s w in sA} = {w : w in A}; the Fourier identity by transport to R along the coordinate map and int_(-s)^s e^(iat) dt = (e^(ias) - e^(-ias))/(ia) for a != 0, and = 2s for a = 0 (the TeX's value s of G_s hat at xi = 0, lines 983-984). The definitions radial2 (the radial density (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - r^2))^(-1), with Lean value 0 for s^2 <= r^2, in particular for 0 <= s <= r, never used there) and coordOne (the coordinate R^1 -> R as a measurable equivalence) only name route objects and have no row. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Narrower conclusions: the scaling for measurable A only (any set in d = 1); this module proves the Fourier identity in d = 1, and WaveGreenFourier (wave L9) proves it in d = 2, 3 for the same measures (in d = 3 for the toSphere definition). The identities are not needed for the conclusions of L:damped-homogeneous-norms about N_1, N_2, which are defined through waveHat directly; they identify the second norm of the Gaussian-smoothed wave Green measures with N_{2,m,S} (DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one in d = 1, WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave in d = 1, 2, 3). The lemma with nothing supplied, with its closing smoothing remark in the narrower reading of the DampedMultiplier section (covariance smoothing as multiplier membership only), is DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_full_wave (wave L8); the identification of the smoothed Green norm with N_{2,m,S} is not among its conclusions and is proved separately by the two Fourier wrappers above. The spectral identification of the smoothed covariance is proved in wave L12 (DampedSmoothing, with the whole lemma, over M1 and M3).
