WaveGreenFourier (foundation: Fourier identities of the wave Green measures)

The Fourier identities of the wave Green measures G_s in d = 2, 3, Archimedes' law for Mathlib's sphere measure, and the extension of the Green-smoothing identification of L:damped-homogeneous-norms to every d = 1, 2, 3, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveGreenFourier.lean. Sources (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a): G_s hat(xi) = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi), value s at xi = 0 (lines 983-984, before E:damped-norm-definitions); the display G_h hat(xi) = sin(h norm(xi))/norm(xi), G_h(R^d) = h (lines 5614-5618, in the proof of L:low-alpha-convolution, lines 5566-5631), which the TeX quotes from the source's (2.3)-(2.5), p. 7, without proof; the identity is also used as G_a hat in L:phase-contractions (lines 2518-2521, 2555-2556, d = 3) and in the proof of L:alpha-one-convolution (lines 5635-5708). The measures are WaveGreen.waveGreen (unchanged): in d = 3 the recorded definitional choice (s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) sigma with sigma = volume.toSphere (Le's decision 4 for wave L6); this module proves facts about that measure and does not identify sigma with a Hausdorff or Riemannian surface measure.

Formalized, nothing supplied. - waveGreen_fourier_two, waveGreen_fourier_three: for s > 0 and every xi, x -> e^(i <xi,x>) is G_s-integrable and int e^(i <xi,x>) G_s(dx) = waveHat s xi; waveGreen_fourier collects d = 1, 2, 3 (with WaveGreen.waveGreen_fourier_one), and waveGreen_fourier_paper states the display at lines 5614-5618 with the right side written as in the TeX (sin(h norm(xi))/norm(xi), value h at 0) together with G_h(R^d) = h. - sphere_fourier: int_(S^2) e^(i <xi,omega>) sigma(d omega) = 4 pi sinc norm(xi) with integrability, the d = 3 core. - archimedes: for a unit e, the image of sigma under omega -> <e,omega> is 2 pi Lebesgue measure on [-1,1], with the lower-integral, integrability and Bochner forms lintegral_sphere_inner, integrable_sphere_inner, integral_sphere_inner. It is the image law behind "direct integration over its normal coordinate" (lines 2573-2579, used in PhaseContractions) and "In dimension three spherical coordinates give" (lines 6134-6139, proof of L:higher-riesz, formalized in wave L10 by HigherRieszThree.F3w_eq through PhaseContractions.sphere_convolution). - greenFourier: DampedMultiplier.GreenFourier (waveGreen d) for d = 1, 2, 3 (wave L8 proved it in d = 1 only, greenFourier_one). - damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave: under H:homog alone (d from the field dim, no Gamma != 0), the conclusions of DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_paper with G := waveGreen d: the second norm of the wave Green measures is N2onSq alpha0 theta S mu and that of their Gaussian smoothing p * G (p = gaussKernel v, v >= 0) is N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 with m = e^(-v norm(xi)^2), with integrability and 0 <= N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 <= N_{2,1,S'}(theta)^2 (lines 1052-1054, proof 1150-1152). It generalizes DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one to d = 2, 3.

Proof route (the TeX has no proof; no Bessel functions). d = 2: rotate xi to norm(xi) e_0 by a reflection (Lebesgue measure is invariant under linear isometries), slice along x_0 (Fubini) and use int_(-a)^a (a^2 - u^2)^(-1/2) du = pi. d = 3: compute int_(norm(x) < R) e^(i <xi,x>) dx in polar coordinates (int_0^R r^2 Phi_xi(r) dr, Phi_xi(r) = int e^(i r <xi,omega>) sigma(d omega)) and by rotation and slicing (pi int_(-R)^R (R^2 - t^2) e^(i norm(xi) t) dt), and differentiate both in R at R = 1; no rotation invariance of toSphere is used (Mathlib has none). Archimedes: equality of characteristic functions (Measure.ext_of_charFun). The definitions splitFirst (R^(n+1) = R x R^n) and spherePhi (Phi_xi) only name route objects and have no row.

Hypotheses. Only damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave takes H:homog; it uses dim directly and passes the hypothesis to DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_paper (fields as recorded in DampedMultiplier). The Fourier identities and Archimedes' law are statements about the measures alone (d = 1, 2, 3, s > 0, or norm(e) = 1).

Junk values. WaveGreen.radial2 s r = (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - r^2))^(-1) is 0 for s^2 <= r^2, in particular for 0 <= s <= r (Lean's sqrt of a negative number and 0^(-1) are 0); it is used only where it is the density of waveGreen 2 s (waveGreen_two_eq, s > 0) or inside the slice integral, whose value (integral_slice_two) is stated exactly. Every Fourier conclusion includes the integrability of its integrand. Real.sinc 0 = 1 gives the TeX's value s at xi = 0.

Not in this module: the spherical computation of lines 6134-6139 (L:higher-riesz, in HigherRieszThree); L:alpha-one-convolution (in AlphaOneConvolution, completed in L10Completed, both wave L10). Narrower conclusions: none for the identities (the d = 3 measure is the recorded definitional choice). Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

WaveTwoVariances (narrower result: P:wave-two-variances for abstract variance and phase spaces, their identification with ell_R and the manuscript's spaces not formalized; named inputs; spectral core in full)

Formalizes Proposition P:wave-two-variances (Both variance directions) of S:wave-variance (notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex at 39f2597a: statement lines 452-467 with E:wave-input-variance at lines 458-460 and E:wave-output-variance at lines 461-463, proof lines 469-563 with E:variance-kernel-time-bound at lines 481-484 and E:variance-actual-row-bound at lines 489-492). It also uses the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-20: H:homog, a = alpha0, E:variance-gamma-range, E:variance-scale-profile), the kernel E:variance-normalized-kernel (lines 264-273), the right side of E:variance-normalized-covariance (lines 275-281), the mask zeta and the interval I = [t0, t0+h] (lines 219-222), C_nu of E:variance-actual-growth-constant (lines 239-242), the map J (lines 205-210) and E:variance-beta-range (lines 174-177).

What is formalized. (1) The purely spectral core, with nothing supplied (wave_two_variances, wave_two_variances_beta): for any measure nu on R^d with nu(B(y,r)) <= C r^alpha (open balls, C >= 0), any finite L^2(R^d; C^2)-orthonormal family U_k (standing for J e_k) and any V in L^2(R^d; C^2) (standing for J z), sum_k int ||int sum_ij 1_I K_ij(.; eta+lambda, eta) U_kj(eta) conj V_i(eta+lambda) d eta||^2_{H_a} nu(d lambda) <= 4 A_T K C h^(2-a) B_alpha(h) ||<xi>^(-gamma) V||_2^2 (InputBound), and, for even nu, the same with U = J z fixed and an orthonormal output family V_k (OutputBound); also with 4 A_T K_beta C h^(2 beta) for beta in the range of C:frequency-time. K is the constant of P:frequency-row, A_T = C1(a)(1+T)^4. (2) The same for the manuscript's nu_R = MaskedAuxiliaryNorm.nu mu zeta R with the section's hypotheses (wave_two_variances_core_paper, wave_two_variances_core_beta_paper), with C_T = 4 A_T K C_nu (line 530), uniform in R, I and the family. (3) The proposition itself (wave_two_variances_paper) with three named inputs (below).

Abstractions. H_a^C is the concrete completion TimeCompletion.Ha p of L:masked-time-completion; 1_I K_ij(.; xi, eta) is its element kerH, the image of the L^2(0,T) class of maskedKernel under the continuous inclusion TimeCompletion.extL2; c_r, b_r are those of L:masked-continuous-wave (MaskedContinuousWave.cFn, bFn). The TeX indices 1, 2 are Lean's 0, 1 (kernelEntry_matrix writes out the four entries). The phases are an abstract complex inner product space P (standing for the Schwartz phases with the complexified E inner product), and E|l_R(I; z, w)|^2 is an abstract number var R t0 h z w.

Supplied inputs (named hypotheses of wave_two_variances_paper only; the core has none). hlink: E:variance-normalized-covariance (the last claim of P:actual-wave-form, which needs the noise construction D1), ofReal(var R t0 h z w) <= int^- ||coef p t0 h (J z) (J w) lambda||^2 nu_R(d lambda), the TeX's display with U = J z, V = J w (its integral is of a nonnegative function, lines 503-504); no stronger than its source. hJL2, hJ (D8): J maps P into L^2(R^d; C^2) and preserves inner products, int sum_j (J z)_j conj((J w)_j) = inner C w z (Mathlib's inner C w z is linear in z, i.e. the TeX's <z, w>_E); the TeX's J is unitary onto L^2(R^d; C^2), so this is weaker. hnormSG (line 529, D8): ||z||^2_{E_{s-gamma}} = int <xi>^(-2 gamma) sum_i |(J z)_i|^2.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: the families and U, V are L^2 componentwise (MemLp 2) and orthonormality is PhaseBessel.IsOrthonormalL2; Bochner integrability of every H_a-valued eta-integrand is part of the conclusion (so the inner integral is never Lean's junk 0); the lambda integrals are lower integrals of nonnegative functions, as in the TeX; the weight integral is a real Bochner integral whose integrability is part of the conclusion; the general theorems need gamma >= 0 (the TeX has gamma > 0). In the general form nu needs no evenness except for the output direction, and no local finiteness (it follows from the growth bound, isLocallyFinite_of_growth).

Hypotheses carried but unused (wrappers): the mask properties of zeta (even, nonnegative, 1 on B_1, 0 off B_2; growth and evenness of nu_R hold for every real Schwartz zeta), 1/2 < beta, and the fields of H:homog other than mu_radon (for s-finiteness), mu_tempered, mu_even, spectral, scaling, alpha0_lt_one and threshold. Gamma != 0 is not assumed: the TeX treats Gamma = 0 separately (line 236), and here nu_R = 0 is covered by the same argument.

Proof route (differences from the TeX). Strong measurability of (xi, eta) -> 1_I K_ij(.; xi, eta) in H_a (lines 497-501) is proved by continuity (continuous_kerH): the entries are jointly continuous in ((xi, eta), t) (via b_r(t) = <r> t sinc(rt)), hence uniformly continuous on compact sets, hence continuous into L^2(0,T), and extL2 is continuous; no separability argument is used. E:variance-kernel-time-bound is MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted.masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper divided by <xi><eta> (norm_kerH_sq_le), as in the TeX. The fixed-lambda steps (input_fixed, output_fixed) apply L:phase-bessel (PhaseBessel.phase_bessel, phase_bessel_conj), the two-component Cauchy-Schwarz (sum_norm_sq_le; its constant 4 is sharp, see the refutation) and the translation xi = eta + lambda. The lambda integration uses lower integrals, superadditivity and Tonelli (total_of_fixed), so measurability of lambda -> int ... d eta is not needed; the row bound E:variance-actual-row-bound is the integral clause of FrequencyRow.frequency_row; the output direction reflects lambda by evenness of nu and uses rowKernel_symm, as at lines 546-550. The h^(2 beta) forms use the time-scale step FrequencyRow.scale_time_le of C:frequency-time (the same inequality as the TeX's use of the corollary). Rows labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve only this route.

Narrower conclusions. wave_two_variances_paper bounds the abstract var, which is tied to E|l_R|^2 only through hlink; l_R, the spaces E_r and the unitary J are not constructed, and the family is orthonormal in the abstract P. The core results are not narrower than the TeX's proof: they are lines 469-561 with nu_R generalized to any measure with the ball growth. Not formalized: P:actual-wave-form beyond its existing finite steps (DimensionalMatrix), E:variance-actual-row-bound as a separate statement for nu_R (it is used inside the core), and P:wave-square-columns.

WhiteClockLaplace (whole result)

Formalizes L:white-clock-laplace (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, section S:two-clock-screen; statement lines 8914-8940, proof lines 8942-8974) in full, with the manuscript's hypotheses and nothing supplied: the cross-pair transform E:white-cross-clock-transform (lines 8917-8928), the diagonal value K_x(theta,theta) = Gamma(1-a)/(4 theta^(3-a)) (lines 8929-8930) and the self-pair transform E:white-self-clock-transform (lines 8932-8939), together with the Green-factor steps of the proof. The section's standing case (lines 8908-8911) is d = alpha = 1, Gamma = delta_0, 0 < a < 1 and G_s(y) = (1/2) 1_{|y|<s} (green).

The wrapper white_clock_laplace_paper assumes 0 < a < 1 (line 8909), theta_1, theta_2 > 0 (line 8926) and eta_1, eta_2 > 0. The last is an implicit side condition made explicit: the TeX gives the damping parameters of the self transform no sign (line 8931, "independent gap damping"), and the integral converges only for positive eta. The integrands are the definitions crossIntegrand and selfIntegrand written verbatim, and the wrapper states their integrability on the open quadrant (0,inf)^2 and the values of the iterated integrals in the TeX order (ds dt and dr_1 dr_2). The quadrant-integral forms are cross_transform and self_transform. Every integral conclusion carries integrability, since a Lean Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0. At s = t Lean's |s-t|^(-a) = 0^(-a) is 0; the diagonal is a null set, so no stated value depends on it. The Lean route uses that value only to split the quadrant pointwise (crossIntegrand_split), and this is the only use of a > 0. The self transform needs only a < 1, and a > 0 is carried there for the section's range. The standing Gamma = delta_0 and d = alpha = 1 enter only through the Green-factor steps. In green_cross_factor the delta_0 pairing int int G_s(y) G_t(z) delta_0(y-z) dy dz is read, as in the TeX, as the diagonal integral int G_s(y) G_t(y) dy; Lean proves the remaining equality with min(s,t)/2. No covariance hypothesis (H:homog) is carried, since the displayed transforms are explicit real integrals.

Proof route: as in the TeX, the quadrant is split into s = t + v and t = s + v. In Lean the half {0 < t < s} (upperHalf) is the image of the quadrant under the measure-preserving shear (v,t) -> (v+t,t) (measurePreserving_add_prod). The half {0 < s < t} (lowerHalf) reduces to the first by the coordinate swap, which exchanges theta_1 and theta_2. Each product integral is computed by integral_prod_mul, which is the Tonelli separation of line 8963. The two elementary integrals of lines 8957-8962 are laplace_id and laplace_rpow, from Mathlib's integral_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_rpow. Although grouped in the Lean file under the Auxiliary heading, their doc comments and statements identify them as the two TeX proof steps (exactly those displays, with integrability), so the ledger labels them as proof steps. Every part of the lemma is formalized. The use of these transforms in the rest of S:two-clock-screen is outside this module.

WhiteCollapse (proof steps of P:white-four: the white-noise limit of every d = 1 diagram, for all chain lengths, on the registered model choice M4)

Wave L13 item D6 (part 1), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WhiteCollapse.lean: the analytic step of the proof of P:white-four (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at 39f2597a, proof lines 4982-5005: "identify its first pair's spatial positions with x and the other pair's positions with y. The two delta covariances have unit mass, so spatial integration leaves 1/16 times the area allowed by the four Green indicators" and "the distributional delta integrations can equivalently be obtained by convolution with the source's spatial approximate identity ... The resulting areas converge to the displayed areas", lines 4996-5001; "Integrability of the time weights follows from the disjoint-pair bound", lines 5004-5005). It is not a labelled result of its own; the whole result P:white-four is in the section WhiteFour.

What is proved, nothing supplied. For white noise in d = 1 (Gamma = delta_0, so p_eps * Gamma = p_eps) and alpha_0 < 1, for EVERY diagram (all chain lengths m, n and every pairing D of Pi, self-pairings included): the smoothed diagrams diagram (waveGreen 1) (covEps (dirac 0) eps) converge, as eps -> 0+, to whiteDiagram alpha_0 m n D t, the time integral of prod_(pairs) |s_j - s_h|^(-alpha_0) against the collapsed spatial factor whiteSpatial (the Green product with the two positions of each pair identified, one free position per pair), which is finite (tendsto_diagram_white, diagramLim_white, whiteDiagram_lt_top; wrapper diagramLim_white_paper with D in Pi2 m n and 0 < alpha_0 < 1, positivity carried and unused). The TeX proves this only for m + n = 4; the Lean statement is a generalization to every m, n (the TeX's approximate-identity remark applies verbatim), used by WhiteFour (the nine order-four integrals), by OrderTwoDiagrams (the white case of L:white-test) and by D1Upper.diagramLimits_white (the input DiagramLimits proved for white noise).

Registered model choice M4 (DiagramModel, see Scope): the TeX's J_(m,n,D)(t) of E:mixed-diagram (lines 814-824) for white noise is DiagramModel.diagramLim 1 (dirac 0), the limit at a common noise width eps of the increment-form diagrams with the smoothed covariance p_eps * Gamma, with the regularization convention of lines 825-832. M1 is not involved (d = 1).

Route (Lean's, following the TeX's approximate-identity remark): the positions integral with gamma_eps = p_eps is an integral over R^N (spatialPos_white, transport by DiagramBridge.eN); the volume-preserving shear (v_j = y_j at an opener, v_c = y_(D c) - y_c at a closer) makes the pair differences coordinates, and scaling the closer coordinates by sqrt(eps) gives p_eps(sqrt(eps) w) sqrt(eps) = p_1(w) (spatial_white_eq, eps > 0); dominated convergence in the positions with the bound 2^(-N) 1{|v_j| <= sum h} p_1 and the exceptional set {|L_i(v)| = h_i} null for positive increments (ae_good, tendsto_spatial_white); then dominated convergence in the times with the uniform bound 2^(-N)(2 sum h + 1)^N (spatialPos_white_le) and the disjoint-pair bound timeWeight_integral_lt_top (from TwoSimplexTime, alpha_0 < 1). The closer coordinates of whiteSpatial carry a standard Gaussian weight of mass one (lintegral_phi_one); WhiteFour.lintegral_A and lintegral_BC integrate it out for four labels.

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. Only alpha_0 < 1 is used (the manuscript's 0 < alpha_0 < 1, E:cov, lines 378-381); every limit is along eps -> 0+ (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)). The simplices are open and |0|^(-alpha_0) = infinity in [0, infinity] for alpha_0 > 0 (one for alpha_0 = 0, zero for alpha_0 < 0), which changes only null sets (ae_timeWeight_ne_top). Junk value: phi eps (a real power of 2 pi eps) is not a density for eps <= 0; every analytic density or limit use takes eps > 0 or the limit eps -> 0+ (the algebraic and measurability auxiliaries, such as heatDens_eq and covEps_dirac, use the totalized expression for every real eps). Lemmas with status internal serve the Lean route only. Five declaration names have namesakes or variants in other modules (heatDens_eq, lintegral_pi_prod, card_closers, sum_incr_le, spatialPos_white_le); they are listed for hygiene, not refactored.

Refutations. The module has no refutation directory of its own: the perturbations of its conclusions are the P:white-four refutations in refutations/white-four/ (section WhiteFour), which test the collapsed spatial factors, the area formula and the pairing count downstream of diagramLim_white (their proofs do not pass through it), and the Lean-route control refutations/order-two-diagrams/WhiteSelfZeroIncrement.lean (class (b), retargeted at L13 integration from a removed smoothed-limit lemma whose limit is now tendsto_diagram_white; section OrderTwoDiagrams).

WhiteFour (whole result)

Wave L13 item D6 (part 2), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WhiteFour.lean: one labelled result at 39f2597a, a whole result on the registered model choice M4.

  1. P:white-four (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, statement lines 4946-4971, proof lines 4973-5015): the proposition's hypotheses (d = alpha = 1, gamma = delta_0, with 0 < alpha_0 < 1 of E:cov, lines 378-381), every conclusion, nothing supplied (white_four_paper): the nine rows of E:white-four-table (lines 4950-4963; J_04A ... J_22C), "or by exchanging the two chains" (J_40_eq for every D in Pi2 4 0; J_31A_eq, J_31B_eq, J_31C_eq: J_(3,1) for A, B, C equals J_(1,3) for C, B, A), so with Pi2_04 ... Pi2_40 (every Pi_2 on four labels is exactly {A, B, C}, pairings_four: "no unlisted pairing or multiplicity", lines 4995-4996) every J_(m,n,D)(t) with m + n = 4 is covered; E:total-four (lines 4964-4969) for A_2(t) = coeffALim 1 delta_0 alpha_0 2 t (total_four); and the scaling J(t) = t^(6-2 alpha_0) J(1) for t > 0 (line 4970; diagramLim_four_scale, from the general whiteDiagram_smul). A table row (m,n), D, V, q_1, q_2 is the Lean statement diagramLim 1 delta_0 alpha_0 m n D t = int_dom q_1^(-alpha_0) q_2^(-alpha_0) V with the increment vector v = (a,b,c,d) for (0,4) and (2,2) and v = (r,a,b,c) for (1,3) (the letters and domains of lines 4930-4942), Lebesgue measure on R^4, and q^(-alpha_0) the power ofReal(q)^(-alpha_0) in [0, infinity] (infinity at q = 0 for alpha_0 > 0, a null set: "values on zero-gap sets do not affect these nonnegative integrals", lines 4942-4943). Labels are 0-based (pA = ![1,0,3,2] is A, pB = ![2,3,0,1] is B, pC = ![3,2,1,0] is C).

Registered model choice M4 (DiagramModel, see Scope): the TeX's J_(m,n,D)(t) for white noise is DiagramModel.diagramLim 1 (dirac 0); its value is computed through WhiteCollapse.diagramLim_white (section WhiteCollapse, proof steps). M1 is not involved (d = 1). Statements about E u^2 are not part of P:white-four; MixedMoment is not used.

E:interval-area (lines 4918-4928), used for the rows with F: volume_tri proves that for a, b, c > 0 the area of {|x| < a, |y| < b, |x - y| < c} is F(a,b,c) = 4ab - (a+b-c)_+^2 + (|a-b|-c)_+^2 (by integrating the overlap length of two intervals as four ramps; the TeX subtracts triangles); F_comm is the symmetry in the first two arguments. The TeX defines F for a, b, c >= 0 and also states that F is nonnegative and symmetric in all three arguments (lines 4922-4923); the boundary cases with a zero argument, the symmetry in the third argument and the nonnegativity are not separate Lean statements (none is used by P:white-four, whose increments are positive).

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. Only alpha_0 < 1 is used; 0 < alpha_0 is carried, unused, by white_four_paper. The table identities hold for every real t (for t <= 0 both sides are 0). The collapsed spatial factors (whiteSpatial_04A ... whiteSpatial_31C) are proved for positive increments, which is the domain of every row. The TeX's uniform-boundedness remark (lines 5001-5003) is the general bound WhiteCollapse.spatialPos_white_le. tacticTw_close is the syntax constant of a local tactic macro, with no mathematical content; it has no row and no claim. Lemmas with status internal serve the Lean route only. measurePreserving_incr and timeWeight_smul have namesakes or variants in other modules (listed for hygiene, not refactored).

Refutations (refutations/white-four/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbations (class (a)): AreaCorrection (the area formula of E:interval-area without the correction term (|a-b|-c)_+^2 fails at a = 3, b = c = 1: area 4, variant 3), CrossedWidth (the row (2,2), C with the strip width b + d in place of min(b,d) fails at h = (1,1,1,1): 3/16 against 4/16), PairingCount (a fourth pairing of four labels, or the identity as a pairing, is refuted: #Pi_2 = 3) and StripMinimum (the row (0,4), B with V = ab/4 in place of a min(b,c,d)/4 fails at h = (1,2,1,1)).

WhiteModel (foundation: the spatial white-noise model, H:homog with alpha = d = 1, and proof steps of T:white-moment-bounds)

Wave L10 (item L10-W0) in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WhiteModel.lean. It sets up the spatial white-noise model of Section S:intrinsic-white-evaluation of notes/integrated_white_evaluation.tex (at 39f2597a, lines 1-11: d = alpha = 1, Gamma = c delta_0 with c >= 0, temporal kernel |s-t|^(-a), 0 < a < 1) and proves the facts that the proof of T:white-moment-bounds (statement lines 140-151, proof 153-167) needs and that do not involve the value of the spatial energy. Nothing is supplied and no step of P:white-spatial-energy (lines 79-133) is used or proved.

New objects: whiteCov c = c delta_0 and whiteSpectral c = (c/(2 pi)) Leb, measures on R^1 = HomogHypothesis.Rd 1, with c entering as ENNReal.ofReal c (for c < 0, outside the manuscript's range, both are the zero measure; every statement meant for the manuscript carries 0 <= c or 0 < c). The TeX names Gamma only; mu is its spectral measure in the convention of H:homog (main TeX file notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, lines 388-391).

Proved, with nothing supplied:

  • H:homog for the white model (main TeX lines 384-400, whose lines 399-400 assert that spatial white noise is the case alpha = d = 1; the TeX gives no proof and the white section assumes it, lines 4-9): white_homogCovariance gives HomogCovariance 1 1 a (c delta_0) ((c/(2 pi)) Leb) for c >= 0, 0 < a < 1, field by field: both measures locally finite, even and tempered; c delta_0 positive definite (the pairing with phi * phi~ is c int |phi|^2); the spectral identity int phi d(c delta_0) = int (int phi(x) e^(i xi x) dx) (c/(2 pi)) d xi for every Schwartz phi; the scaling Gamma(lA) = l^(d-alpha) Gamma(A) = Gamma(A); alpha = d = 1; a + 1 < 2.
  • The spectral facts used elsewhere in the package: mu(lA) = l mu(A) and V = mu{|xi| <= 1} = mu{|xi| < 1} = c/pi (V as at main TeX line 5559, closed ball, and mu(B_1) as at line 1069). These are no labelled step of the white section; they are recorded for later use (rows "no direct label").
  • A_sp(f) = B_Gamma(f^2, f^2) = c int f^4 (line 9: A_sp(f) = cA), for the real pairing SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair (an identity of Bochner integrals, so no integrability is assumed or asserted; if f^4 is not integrable both sides are 0) and for the extended pairing OccupationKernelRow.pairing in [0, infinity] (no junk value).
  • The arithmetic of lines 154-161 at alpha = 1 (q = 3, k = 2, m = 3/2): F_0(c^2/6) = sqrt c/(3 sqrt 2) and 2^m F_0(c^2/6) = (2/3) sqrt c for c >= 0, and the two sides of E:intrinsic-spatial-bracket (notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex lines 323-327) at z = c^2/6, 2^m M_a^(-1/k) F_0(c^2/6) and 2^m K_0^(1/k) F_0(c^2/6), equal the lower and upper formulas WhiteRelativeWidth.lowerFormula c a and upperFormula c a of E:white-moment-bounds (lines 143-144), with M_a = TemporalEquilibrium.mass a and K_0 = WhiteRelativeWidth.boundK0 a. F_0 is evaluated at the NUMBER c^2/6, not at E_sp: the identification E_sp = c^2/6 is P:white-spatial-energy (reserved board item B9) and is used, as a named input, only in WhiteMomentBounds.

Exact-hypothesis wrappers: white_model_paper with the section's c >= 0, 0 < a < 1 (lines 4-5); white_pairing_paper with c >= 0 only (the pairing does not involve a); white_score_arithmetic_paper with c > 0 as at line 159 (the general lemmas hold for c >= 0, which covers the remark of lines 164-165 that both displayed formulas vanish at c = 0). They state setup facts and proof steps, not labelled results. Proof route (the TeX gives none for H:homog and the pairing): the inner integral of the spectral identity is a rescaled Fourier transform in Mathlib's convention (inner_integral_eq_fourier), and int Fourier phi = phi(0) by Fourier inversion; V through the coordinate isometry WaveGreen.coordOne. Not formalized here: P:white-spatial-energy (both R_sp = c/sqrt 3 and E_sp = c^2/6) and L:white-cdf-square.

Refutations (refutations/white-model/), all manuscript-domain perturbations (a wrong constant, normalization or exponent of the white model, refuted at c = 1); none relies on a junk value: BallLength (V = c/(2 pi)), F0Constant (F_0(c^2/6) = sqrt(c)/3), ScalingExponent (scaling exponent alpha = 1/2) and SpectralNormalization (spectral measure c Leb without 1/(2 pi)).

Wave L10 (item L10-W1) in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WhiteMomentBounds.lean. It states T:white-moment-bounds (Explicit white moment bounds; notes/integrated_white_evaluation.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 140-151, proof 153-167) for the variational value S_2^pos = sup scoreSet(a, Gamma, 2) on the white model of WhiteModel (Gamma = c delta_0, d = alpha = 1, lines 4-9). Class: inputs supplied, conclusion weaker.

Supplied input (named hypothesis, not proved): WhiteSpatialEnergy c, i.e. E_sp(c delta_0) = c^2/6, the energy half of P:white-spatial-energy (lines 79-133), reserved as board item B9. Each half of the bracket uses one inequality of it only, recorded by the one-sided theorems: the lower half (white_moment_lower_of_ge) uses c^2/6 <= E_sp (the sech profile, lines 106-124), the upper half (white_moment_upper_of_le) uses E_sp <= c^2/6 (the CDF square, lines 88-100 and 117-121).

Formalized: white_moment_bounds_paper (headline): for c > 0, 0 < a < 1 and WhiteSpatialEnergy c, the coefficient-two value set is bounded above and (2/3) sqrt(c/M_a) <= S_2^pos <= (2/3) sqrt(c K_0(a)) with K_0(a) = 2^a/(1-a) and M_a = Gamma_E((1+a)/2)/(Gamma_E(1+a) Gamma_E((1-a)/2)) written out as in lines 143-147, and M_a, K_0(a) and both formulas are positive (the TeX's "All Gamma factors are positive finite", lines 163-164). Route as in the TeX (lines 153-163): the bracket of C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket at the white model, from L8Completed.spatial_bracket_lower_sSup_paper_completed and L8Completed.spatial_bracket_upper_paper_completed (the standing assumptions alone; S1Bdd and OccupationCeilingK0 discharged there), with H:homog from WhiteModel.white_homogCovariance, Gamma != 0 from whiteCov_ne_zero, E_sp >= 0 from SpatialOccupationL7Completed.spatial_energy_value_paper_completed, the arithmetic WhiteModel.white_bracket_lower and white_bracket_upper at z = c^2/6, and monotonicity of F_0. An earlier draft of this item carried its own copies of the L8Completed bracket theorems; they were removed at integration and the module now calls L8Completed. In addition, white_moment_upper_exact_paper gives, on the upper half of the input, S_2^pos <= 2^m F_0(E_(1/2)^O) <= (2/3) sqrt(c K_0(a)) and 2^m F_0(E_(1/2)^O) < 2^m F_a(E_(1/2)^O) through the exact C_occ of OccupationCeilingExact (wave L9), over the class O modelled by joint representatives (its identification with the TeX's strongly H^1-measurable class is not formalized): the comparison of C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket (integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex lines 328-332) at the white model. It is at least as sharp as the upper formula; strict sharpness is not claimed (C_occ is not evaluated, only C_occ <= K_0 R_sp is used).

Side conditions proved in Lean, not assumed: Gamma != 0 (for c > 0) and E_sp >= 0. Every hypothesis is used: 0 < a, a < 1 enter H:homog and M_a > 0, c > 0 enters Gamma != 0 (module report). Narrower than the TeX: the bounds are for S_2^pos, not C_2(c,a); the identification C_2 = S_2^pos is T:intrinsic-second-moment (outside Lean), used at line 162 through C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket; the sentence "Its time exponent is (3-a)/2" (line 149) concerns C_2 and is not formalized; the case c = 0 (c delta_0 = 0 violates Gamma != 0; the TeX's lines 164-165 use T:intrinsic-second-moment) is not formalized (decision 4 of wave L10); P:white-spatial-energy is the supplied input above.

Refutations (refutations/white-moment-bounds/), classified; none relies on a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbations: EnergyNormalization (the closed form does not survive the energy c^2/3) and LinearInC (the upper formula is not linear in c). Lean-route-only controls: InputDirection (F_0 is increasing, so each bound needs its own half of the supplied input) and ZeroCovariance (c delta_0 = 0 at c = 0, which is why the wrapper assumes c > 0; the case c = 0 is in the manuscript's domain and is not formalized).

WhiteRelativeWidth (whole result)

Formalizes C:white-relative-width (notes/integrated_white_evaluation.tex at 39f2597a, statement lines 173-181, proof lines 183-204) in full, with the manuscript's hypotheses and nothing supplied. The two formulas it compares are those displayed in T:white-moment-bounds (E:white-moment-bounds, lines 140-150): K_0(a) = 2^a/(1-a) (boundK0) and M_a = Gamma((1+a)/2)/(Gamma(1+a) Gamma((1-a)/2)) (boundMass), with the lower formula (2/3) sqrt(c/M_a) (lowerFormula) and the upper formula (2/3) sqrt(c K_0(a)) (upperFormula). These four are definitions of real expressions only. Lean proves the identities and the inequality between the displayed formulas: that the intrinsic constant C_2(c,a) lies between the lower and upper formulas is T:white-moment-bounds; Lean proves it for the variational value S_2^pos with E_sp = c^2/6 supplied (WhiteMomentBounds, wave L10), not for C_2; it is not used here. Nothing of P:white-spatial-energy (the CDF square identity, H^1 profiles, the spatial energy constant; reserved package B9) is used or proved.

The wrapper white_relative_width_paper assumes exactly c > 0 (line 175) and the section's 0 < a < 1 (line 5). It concludes that the ratio of the upper to the lower formula is sqrt(K_0(a) M_a), that this is at most [sqrt(pi)/(2 Gamma(5/4)^2)]^(1/2), and that equality holds if a = 1/2. Gamma_E is Mathlib's Real.Gamma, 2^a is Real.rpow, and the square roots, including [.]^(1/2), are Real.sqrt. Every quantity under a square root or in a denominator is shown positive for 0 < a < 1 (boundK0_pos, boundMass_pos), so no statement relies on Lean's sqrt of a negative number or x/0 = 0. All hypotheses are used. Also proved: the closing remark of the proof that this ratio is symmetric under a -> 1-a (lines 201-202), and boundMass_eq_mass, which identifies the displayed M_a with TemporalEquilibrium.mass a, the mass of L:temporal-equilibrium (E:temporal-equilibrium-mass), for 0 < a < 1. That identification is not stated in the corollary.

Proof route: the duplication and recurrence steps (lines 184-190) are those of the TeX, taken from L:equilibrium-gamma-beta (TemporalEquilibrium.gamma_beta_duplication_general, gamma_beta_recurrence). The inequality Gamma(5/4)^2 <= Gamma(1+a/2) Gamma((3-a)/2) (with x + y = 5/2) is proved from the log-convexity of Gamma on (0, inf) (Mathlib's Real.convexOn_log_Gamma, through the auxiliary gamma_mid_sq_le), not by Cauchy-Schwarz in Euler's integral as in the TeX (lines 196-200); the inequality is the same. Every part of the corollary is formalized; P:white-spatial-energy stays outside, and T:white-moment-bounds is proved only for S_2^pos, with the energy value supplied (WhiteMomentBounds).

Not in Lean

The main analytic ingredients of the manuscript are not formalized here. In particular:

  • Existence of the canonical solution and its expansion, including self-pairings and fixed-order coefficients (P:mild-construction, of whose proof only the finite-coordinate multiplication bound E:occupied-multiplication is in FockForm; L:joint-fixed-order), and the crude bound T:crude. The deterministic two-chain diagram integrals are modelled in DiagramModel (registered model choice M4, wave L13); P:mixed enters as the named input MixedMoment, the common-width convergence of the diagrams of L:joint-fixed-order as DiagramLimits (proved for white noise in d = 1), the first-moment series as FirstMomentSeries, and P:three-transfer as ThreeTransfer (see the named-input list in Scope). Not proved for M4: the identification of its increment form with the TeX's positions form in d = 2, 3, and the identification of the TeX's joint limit at arbitrary vertexwise widths with the common-width limit.
  • The upper bound at the scale t^kappa (T:full-upper) and the spectral and operator estimates behind it: the identification of the Fourier-side model of FockColumnBound (where the spatial half of L:fock-form and E:interval-column are proved) with the physical-space operators (unitary Fourier conjugation) and of its modes with the Gaussian coordinates of W_eps (also for the operator form of E:fock-sandwich, which FockSandwichModel proves on that model, discharging FockSandwich of StaticInteractionCompleted there); the phase propagator of L:complex-phase and L:interval-complex, Crouzeix-Palencia E:cp-input, the inverse-root integral representation and the identification of the propagator with the weighted block map (their scalar, numerical-range and Banach-algebra steps are in ComplexPhaseScalar), the composition of the telescoping of E:interval-metric with the propagators outside L:fixed-split (the telescoping of the scalar conversion factors is in FixedSplitCore); the cutoff evolution of L:fixed-split, its propagators and coefficients, and the proofs of the inputs supplied to FixedSplit (SegmentBound, DysonCrossCube, BackgroundPreserves, EntireCoefficients); and the operator and Gaussian parts of P:static-phase-all-orders (its Cauchy, scalar and series steps are in StaticPhaseCauchy and SeriesType). The Hermite and Fock algebra, the Fock half of L:fock-form and the consequences in L:interval-contractions are in GaussianHermite, HermiteFock and FockForm; L:finite-word-cutoff is in FiniteWordCutoff (and its one-mode case in HermiteWordFock).
  • Equality in law under the exact scaling (L:exact-canonical-scaling), beyond the exponent arithmetic listed above.
  • Construction of the operator-valued driver and the Young-type evolution (P:actual-operator-driver); the free wave group S_E on E = H^(1/2) x H^(-1/2) (L:symplectic-free; its group law, velocity reversal and translations are supplied to SymplecticFree as FreeWaveData), the operator J_E and the preservation of omega by S_E on E (neither proved nor assumed), and the Young evolution on L(E) (P:constant-young-linear, supplied as LeftYoungSumsConverge).
  • Gaussian changes of measure, Cameron-Martin means and tube estimates (P:raw-block-gaussian-law, P:cameron-full-mean, P:tube-actual-law), and L:tube-closed-geometry (closed tubes, least-radius attainment and the Gaussian tail from the imported Borell theorem), whose two conclusions are supplied to SourceTube as TubeAttained and TubeTail for P:tube-rayleigh-transfer.
  • The variational lower bound and its constant (T:intrinsic-second-moment, so also C_2 = S_2^pos in C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket), the moment sentence C_2 <= U_2 of T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling, the restatement of L:occupation-raw-square on the class O itself (it is proved over joint representatives in OccupationCompletion, wave L14), the mean identity and the canonical versions of L:positive-raw-embedding, the direct zero case Gamma = 0 beyond the energies (C_2 = 0, S_c^pos = 0, the vanishing of the original means, Q = 0 and the reduction to the free moment model; the rest is ClassOBridge.zero_covariance_paper), the white-noise evaluation for C_2 (T:white-moment-bounds is proved for S_2^pos with the energy value of P:white-spatial-energy supplied, in WhiteMomentBounds; the identification C_2 = S_2^pos, the time exponent (3-a)/2 and the case c = 0 are not formalized; its displayed formulas K_0(a), M_a and their relative width C:white-relative-width are in WhiteRelativeWidth), and P:white-spatial-energy itself (reserved package B9).
  • The moment bounds for the operator paths (P:radius-actual-moments, C:radius-covariance-residuals), which RadiusMeanAnchor takes as a supplied hypothesis.
  • The identification of Ht (M5, OccupationCompletion) with the completion of C_c^infinity(I), and its complexification (TimeCompletion builds H_a directly over C, with the real tests' span dense).
  • L:signed-limiting-multiplier and the operator of P:signed-closed-form: the multiplier V, its pairing v_V and the self-adjoint operator H_V are not constructed. E:signed-multiplier-form is supplied as the named input SignedMultiplierForm, with the Hermitian pairing, for an abstract bounded operator on H^1, and only the form bounds and the bounded resolvent of the form are proved (ResolventForm); D(A^(1/2)) = H^1, E:signed-quarter-phase, the dual completion H^(-1/2) and the commutation with real conjugation are not formalized.
  • The identifications behind the registered model choices M5 and M6: of HK p G with a tensor product, of HI with the completion of smooth space-time tests and with the Hilbert tensor product of L:cameron-supported-tensor, an isometry between Hsp and HGamma (M5); that every real element of Mathlib's H^1 comes from ClassOH1.H1R d (M6).
  • In L:positive-physical-gram: the label row E:positive-label-row and the entrywise order 0 <= C^R_ij <= D_ij (out by wave L14 decision 5); the uniform mean T_R and the multiplier form v_L are not constructed.
  • The proof-internal finiteness and continuity of rho_R in the proof of P:masked-auxiliary-norm (lines 131-134), which the Lean route does not need (the clause for a real H after complexification is proved in MaskedAuxiliaryReal, wave L13).
  • The operator half of P:variational-unmasked-rate: self-adjointness of H_s = -Delta - h_s on H^2, its form domain H^1, the spectral bottom E_s with -E_s = sup R_s, and hence the identification of the Rayleigh-form rate with sqrt(-E_s) (needs unbounded self-adjoint operators, foundation D8; the Rayleigh-form part, with its uniform floor, Lipschitz bounds and 0 < I_Psi < infinity, is in VariationalRate); and the identification of the integral-form cost with E W(Psi)^2 (L:compact-raw-profile, needs Gaussian chaos).
  • The stochastic proof (TeX lines 430-446: the upper bound T:full-upper for the same canonical solution and the point lower bound E:variational-unmasked-point-lower) of the boundedness claim of P:variational-positive-scores (lines 372-374). Lean proves the claim, VariationalRate.S1Bdd, deterministically from the occupation ceiling (OccupationCeilingFinite.s1Bdd_paper, completed in L8Completed.s1Bdd_paper_completed).
  • Q_2 >= S_2^pos (the second identity of E:variational-score-homogeneity) and the original point lower bound E:raw-block-original-lower of P:raw-block-original-lower, from which RemoveMask derives E:variational-unmasked-point-lower as a supplied input (the masks and every rate statement of P:variational-remove-mask are proved in RemoveMask, for the Rayleigh-form rates); the compact ground rates of m_R h_s.
  • The ground family of S:compact-mean-family (flows, spectral projections, normalized complement, margins; interface C16), which IndexedCone takes as one supplied hypothesis structure.
  • The infinite-dimensional results of S:compact-gaussian (L:cutoff-factorization, P:cutoff-singular-values, P:compact-two-envelopes, L:compact-positive-order, P:localized-finite-variance, C:finite-gaussian-operators, P:cutoff-boundary-tests): they need Schatten classes, singular values of compact operators and torus Sobolev spaces.
  • The identification of Mathlib's Measure.toSphere with the surface measure of the unit sphere, which WaveGreen takes as the definition of the d = 3 wave Green measure (Le's decision 4, model choice M1); the identification of the density measure smoothedCov Gamma eps with Mathlib's Measure.conv of N(0, eps I) and Gamma (model choice M3; the spectral measure of that density measure, e^(-eps|xi|^2/2) mu, and its uniqueness are proved in DampedSmoothing).
  • The noise statements of P:masked-noise-completion: membership of mathcal D in the test-noise completion, E:masked-actual-noise-norm, the contraction extension of F -> W(zeta_R F) and its joint Gaussianity, and the identification of the masked covariance and auxiliary Gram matrices with the matrices of the finite comparison (GaussianComparison proves only that comparison, for every pair A <= B in positive semidefinite order).
  • The rest of S:wave-variance: the forms on the full phase and P:actual-wave-form beyond its finite steps (DimensionalMatrix), including E:variance-normalized-covariance, which enters wave_two_variances_paper as the named input hlink; the spaces E_r, the unitary map J and the identity ||z||_{E_{s-gamma}} = ||<xi>^(-gamma) J z||_2 (named inputs hJL2, hJ, hnormSG; D8); and P:wave-square-columns. The instance nu = mu, C = C_Gamma of P:frequency-row is not stated in Lean, although both its inputs, P:frequency-row and P:masked-spectral-growth, are formalized.
  • In P:wave-two-variances, the variances E|l_R(I; z, w)|^2 themselves: Lean proves the bounds for the right side of E:variance-normalized-covariance (no input) and transfers them to an abstract var through hlink.
  • In S:spatial-occupation-foundation, whose labelled results cited here are in Lean (L:spatial-static-controls and P:spatial-smooth-ratio in SpatialStaticControls, SpatialSmoothRatio and SpatialOccupationCompleted, with positivity by the floor lemma of VariationalFloor, a route different from the TeX's, and R_0 positive and finite by the deterministic bound of SpatialFourierBound, the TeX's L:spatial-fourier-bound; P:spatial-four-linear and P:spatial-energy-map in SpatialFourLinear, P:occupation-physical-class in OccupationPhysicalClass, both completed in SpatialOccupationL7Completed, and over the class O itself with topological joint continuity in ClassOH1 and ClassOBridge, wave L14): the exact value J_0 l^alpha A_sp(g) with J_0 in (0,infinity) (lines 568-570; Lean uses a lower bound); the reduction to the free moment model in the zero-covariance remark after P:occupation-physical-class (lines 581-582); the separability of H^1 (lines 356-358); and the extension of E:spatial-dilation to H^1 (lines 437-439), which the Lean route does not need. The supremum forms of E:spatial-static-score, E:spatial-smooth-score and E:spatial-static-energy-score and the bound on R_0 by S_1^pos (the manuscript's route before a284420) take the named input S1Bdd in those modules; it is proved in wave L8 and discharged in L8Completed.
  • The inputs of P:moment-growth-logconvex and C:static-moment-constant-continuity (TypeContinuity, supplied as TypeContinuityInputs): L:full-moment-coefficient-holder (the diagram limits behind E:full-moment-positive-series and E:full-moment-coefficient-holder), P:static-minorant-lower, the imported static law E:static-ratio-input (Chen-Hu), T:full-upper at each temporal exponent, and Cauchy-Schwarz for the solution's moments. The rest of S:near-static-lower (L:mean-coefficient-holder, P:near-static-mean-gap) is not formalized either.
  • The operator and stochastic inputs of C:static-interaction (IntervalScalar, StaticInteractionCompleted): the construction of the static interaction map (its identification with sum sigma^n Y_n and the order bounds are proved in StaticInteractionCompleted for abstract Hilbert-space quantities, from the inputs of P:static-phase-all-orders and L:complex-phase), the Gaussian parity (line 3293), the first-variance bounds of P:static-phase-variance (lines 3275-3280), and the L^2 extension of the block maps with tensoring with the independent past (lines 3332-3338).
  • The inputs of P:interval-coefficients (IntervalScalar): the inputs of L:fixed-split (lines 3675-3716; the lemma is assembled in FixedSplit with them supplied, see above), the coefficient existence and entire majorant (E:interval-entire-majorant, lines 4092-4136), the split identity E:interval-energy-splits and its parity (lines 4147-4157), the Duhamel word expansion of the ordinary coefficients (lines 4092-4097, 4166-4170; the named input DuhamelWords of FiniteWordCutoff.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_words, which replaces the added hypothesis hQ of FixedSplit.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_fixed; the identification of the cut-off coefficients is proved from it), the finite-interval model of lines 4239-4256, and the zero-noise case and the sign reduction (lines 4079-4085). L:inventory-product is in InventoryProduct, connected in IntervalScalarCompleted.
  • In L:terminal-wick (TerminalWick, TerminalWickInputs, TerminalWickRegularization, TerminalWickComplete; complex r and the comparison for second moments of partial sums are in TerminalWickComplete): the density g_n of E:expansion in d = 1, 2 (lines 4285-4287), the symmetrization paragraph, the identification of the regularized chain measure with the product of the factors p_eta * G_(s_(j+1)-s_j) beyond one factor and the clause on the source's fixed-noise convention; the identification of the L:uniform-series-tail family with the regularized terms of the solution and their fixed-order limits; and the lemma's applications in later proofs (lines 4676, 4730, 8341).
  • Fourier analysis of the covariance (beyond the wave-kernel and two-time Laplace transforms, the Gaussian transform of P:masked-spectral-growth, the auxiliary mask norm P:masked-auxiliary-norm, the spectral identity of Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2 (P:masked-quotient-obstruction), the spectral form of the autocorrelation integral (SpatialFourierBound), the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in d = 1, 2, 3 and Archimedes' law for Mathlib's sphere measure (WaveGreen, WaveGreenFourier), the Gaussian Fourier representations of the smoothed covariances (LowAlphaConvolution, PhaseContractions) and the spectral measure of the smoothed covariance with Fourier uniqueness of tempered spectral measures (DampedSmoothing) now in Lean), measure-theoretic constructions, and limits in time and in regularization parameters of the equation or its solution (the scalar and norm-tail limits stated in their sections, such as the tails E:damped-tail-norms as M -> infinity, and the abstract L^2 regularization limit of L:uniform-series-tail, are in Lean).
